Sorrowfulness, sadness, sorrow, pity, grief, compassion, sympathy. (subô; see kasubô).
Smart, ache, pain. (see hápdì).
Smart, pain, ache, chafing, fretting. (see hápdus, kahápdì).
Yesterday. (see hápon).
Yesterday (in (during) daytime). Kahápon nga ága. Yesterday morning. Kahápon nga (sing) hápon. Yesterday afternoon or evening.
Yesterday (in (during) daytime). Kahápon nga ága. Yesterday morning. Kahápon nga (sing) hápon. Yesterday afternoon or evening.
Yesterday (in (during) daytime). Kahápon nga ága. Yesterday morning. Kahápon nga (sing) hápon. Yesterday afternoon or evening.
Even-tide, evening. (see hápon).
Evening. (see hápon).
Ease, easiness, facility. (hapús; see kahulás).
See kahapús. Also: things that are easy, the easiest of a kind. Amó iní ang kahapusán sa tanán nga tulún-an. That is the easiest of all the (text) books.
Sharpness, pungency, acidity, acridity. (see hárang, kaárhang).

To hazard, dare, venture, be audacious, reckless, intrepid, impertinent, insolent, daring, bold, high-spirited, dauntless. Kinahásan níya ang paghinguyáng sang pílak nga ginpatágò ko sa íya. He dared to spend the money I had entrusted to him for safe keeping. Indì mo pagkahásan ang pagbukás sang ganháan kon walâ ka sing túgut sa pagsulúd. Don't dare to open the door, unless you have permission to enter. (see aháng, ahás).
The fourth part of a peso, twenty five centavos. (see manghátì, manghatión).
(H) Slavery, peonage, bondage, peonism, serfdom, villeinage, villenage, complete subjection. (see ulípon).
Amazement, awe, astonishment, surprise, wonder, admiration; things that amaze or astound, marvellous, amazing, astonishing, astounding, wonderful, wondrous, admirable, awful. (see urúng).
Desert, waste, wilderness, territory destitute of trees and shrubs; a lonely or isolated place. (see háwà).
State of being clear of encumbrance or obstruction, openness, clearness, freedom from impediments. (see háwan).
See kaháwan. Also: things that are free, unencumbered, unobstructed.

Clearness, plainness, distinctness, perspicuity, clarity, lucidity, brightness. Ang kaháyag sang kapáwà. The clearness or brightness of light. Ang kahayág sang íya nga katarúngan--. The lucidity of his argument (reasoning)--. (see háyag, hayág).

Clearness, lucidity, etc. See kaháyag. Also: What is clearly shown or easily understood, intelligible, comprehensible, visible, manifest. Sa siníng dibúho makítà nínyo ang kahayágan sang ákon nga ginsilíng. You can see from this drawing what I mean to say. (see háyag, hayág, kaháyag).
Live stock, cattle, domestic or farm animals. (see háyop).
(Sp. cajero) Cashier, treasurer, cash-keeper. (see kúymi, kwími, tesoréro).
Straits, difficulties, want, misery. (hi-ól; see kahil-ánan).
Depth, deepness, profoundness, profundity, deep or mysterious things. (see dálum, kadálum, kaidadálman).
Desire, longing, yearning, hankering, aspiration, craving, wish (to see absent friends, etc.). (see hídlaw).
(B) Foot. (see tiíl).
To remove, push or kick off as with the feet. Kahíga sang sílhig ang ití sang manók. Remove the chicken's excrement with the broom.

To scratch with the feet as a chicken. Ang manók nagakáhig sang dútà. The chicken is scratching the ground. Ginakahígan sang manók ang dútà. The ground is being scratched by the chicken. (see pangáhig).
(H) Corners, nooks, out-of-the-way places. (higád; see binít, bá-id, duók, suók, hilít).
Occasion, opportunity.
Dirt, filth, muck; dirtiness, filthiness, foulness, uncleanness, impurity, obscenity. (hígkò; see kaláw-ay).
See kahígkò. Also: depravity, immorality, moral filth, abomination, lechery, lewdness.
Envy, spite, grudge. (híkaw; see kahísà).
(Sp. cajel) A small orange indigenous to the Philippines.
Straits, hardship, weariness, misery. (hi-ól).
Hunger, exhaustion through lack of food. (hílab).
Connection, relation, interest, concern. (lábut).
See kahilábtan.
A refreshing drink made of water and sugar and mixed with the juice of the "kahíl" (Sp. cajel).
Longing, regret, fretting over past or lost things. (hílak; see kangílin).
(H) Neighbour; vicinity, proximity, region near, neighbourhood.
Nervous excitement, nervousness, nervosity; vexation, molestation, bother; uneasiness. (see hilás).
Rueful, woeful, piteous, pitiful, objects to be treated tenderly or to be sympathized with. (see hinóklog, hanóklog, makahanóklog).
Tenderness, sympathy, pity, mildness. (see hinóklog, kahinoklógon).
Seclusion, solitude, isolation, solitariness, retirement, state of being separate or far away from others. (see hilít).
Condition of being untrammelled or unobstructed, freedom, liberty.
Freedom, independence, liberty. (see kahílway).
Relations, relatives, kindred, kin, kith and kin, kinsfolk, kinship, offspring, progeny. (bátà, himatâ).
Bliss, blessedness, glory, happiness, felicity; blissful, felicitous; objects whose possession gives happiness. (see himáyà).

Deed, action, performance, doings; result, effect, issue, event; possibility of performance. Inâ walâ gid man sing kahimoán. That comes (came) to nothing,-cannot (could not) be done,-is (was) of no effect. (see hímò).
Perfection, completion, excellence, consummation. (see hímpit, kalántip).
See kahímpit. Also: Perfections, virtues, habits or actions that are perfect or praiseworthy. (see kalantipán).
Position, rank, state, station, condition, circumstances. (butáng; see kabtángan, kahamtángan).
Scarcity, rareness, rarity, fewness, dearth. (hínà; kaíwat).
Nephews and nieces. (see hináblus).
Pain, suffering, ache; feeling, sentiment. (see hinakít).

Slowness, deliberateness, dilatoriness, tardiness, sluggishness, gentleness, want of haste, lack of precipitation, quality of doing something without undue haste, slow and careful performance. (see hínay).
Slowness, etc. See kahínay.
Expenditure, outlay, waste; squandering, extravagance, wastefulness, prodigality. (see uyáng).
(H) Gloss, lustre, polish, shine, brilliance, brilliancy, brightness, sheen. (see híning, kasilíng, kasílì).
Cleanness, smoothness, neatness. (see hínlò, katínlo).
Kindliness, tenderness, mildness, pity, sympathy, commiseration. (see hinóklog, kahilinoklogán, kahanóklog).
See kahinóklog.
See kahi-ól, kahil-ánan.
(H) Slavery, etc. See kahaulipónan id.
(H) See kahiolípnan, kahaulipónan.
(H) Trimness, neatness, nattiness, dapperness, tidiness, state of being dressed or kept in becoming order and cleanliness. (see hípid).
(B) Neatness, trimness, cleanliness. (see kahípid id.).
Silence, stillness, muteness, reserve, reticence, taciturnity, quietness, noiselessness, absence of sound or noise. (see hípus).
Intimacy; intimate friend, crony, confidant. Kahírup ko siá. He is my intimate friend. (hírup; see kahámbal, kadágil).
Envy, spite, grudge, malice, resentment, rancour, venom. (hísà; see kahíkaw).
(Sp. cajeta) A little box; cash-box, jewel-case.
Height, exaltedness, loftiness, high position or dignity. (see táas).
See kahitaásan.
(Sp. cajetilla) Package, box, (as of cigarettes, matches, etc.).
Softness, pliability, plasticity, amenability to physical or moral impressions, impressionability. (hómok).
(Sp. cajon) Box, trunk, case; dam, dyke, ditch, bank, particularly applied to banks that inclose rice-fields. Also verb: Kahoní ang ímo talámnan. Put a bank around your field. (see sulúdlan).
Tree; wood.
Dim. of káhoy. Bush, shrub, undergrowth, scrub, brushwood, underwood, coppice, copse.
Drooping, limpness, hanging down loosely, dangling, the hang of wet clothes, etc. (see hóyhoy).
See kahi-ól id.
(H) Drunkenness, intoxication, inebriation, inebriety, state of being drunk. (hubúg).
Tardiness, lateness, backwardness (of ripening, etc.; see kaatrasádo).
Diligence, zeal, application, ardour, industry, assiduity, assiduousness, earnestness. (húgud; see kapísan, kaúkud, katándus).
Tightness, tautness, tension, tenseness, tensity, closeness, compression, lack of freedom to breathe or act; fervour, sincerity. (hugút).
Justice, jurisprudence, court of justice. Tiglikúm sang báhin sa kahukmánan. Secretary of Justice. (see hokóm, holokmánan).
See kahil-ánan. (hu-ól-hi-ól; see kalisdánan, kapipít-an, kalalát-an).
Unsteadiness, restlessness, instability, unstableness, fickleness, shakiness, lack of stability or firmness. (see húlag).
See kahulág. Also: Fidgetiness; unsettled manner of life.
Facility, ease. (hulás; see kahapús, kahapusán).
Ease, facility. See kahulás.
(H) Drunkenness. See kahubúg.
(H) Evaporation, loss of moisture, drying up, exsiccation. (see hubás).
Meaning, tenour, connotation, implication, sense, application, signification, significance, import, purport, interpretation, drift. Anó ang íya sinâ nga kahulúgan? What does that mean? (húlug).
(H) See kahulúbgon.
Shadow, shade, shadiness, umbrageousness, condition of plants, etc., that receive little sunlight. (hulúng).
(H) Shame, disgrace, disrepute, debasement, degradation, ignominy, humiliation; things or actions that are shameful, disreputable or disgraceful. (huyâ).
Completion, execution, fulfilment, accomplishment. (see humán).
Mildness, softness, tenderness, even temper, quiet, condition of one who says little and quietly goes his way. (húmoy).
Fragrance, perfume, aroma, bouquet, scent, sweet odour, pleasant smell, etc. See kahamút id.
Dampness, moisture, moistness, humidity, dankness. (húnog).
Neatness, closeness of weaving, etc.; tidiness. (hunápit; see kahúpit, kahípid).
Toughness, resistance, durability. (see húnit).
See kahúnit.
See kahunápit id. (húpit-hunápit).
Order, disposition, regulation, settlement, agreement, proper arrangement. (húsay).
See kahúsay. Also: A clearing up, a settling or adjustment of a dispute, quarrel, debt, etc.

Propriety, appositeness, correctness, accordance, aptness, rightness, conformity, suitability, fitness. Walâ sing kahustóhan ang ginsúgid níya. What he told was not correct (not in keeping with the facts). (hústo).
Shame, disgrace, debasement, degradation; remorse mingled with shame. (see kahuyâ, kahulúy-an).
Shame, confusion, mortification, abashment, sense of shame. (see huyâ, mahulúy-on, makahuhúyà).
Bent, inclination, leaning. (see húyug, huyúg).
Desire, longing, yearning, hankering, passion, craving, particularly with regard to material goods and pleasures, covetousness. (see íbug, kailíbgon).
Exactness, precision, preciseness, diligence, zeal, application, punctuality. (see íd-id).
Depth, etc. See kahidálman.

(B) To mend, repair, restore, do up. Sín-o ang nagkaídan sang baláy? Who repaired the house? Kaidána (kidána) ang ímo baláy. Repair your house. Kilidanón, kiridanón-things to be mended or needing repairs. May kilidanón kamó? Have you anything to mend? (see kaáyo, kaalayohón).
Fitness, aptness, suitability, propriety. (see ígò).
See kaígò. Also: things that are fit, proper or right.
(B) Shame; to be ashamed, etc. See huyâ. Naihâ (nagkaihâ) siá. He was ashamed. Ginkaihaán ko siá. I am ashamed of him. Indì ka maihâ (magkaihâ). Don't be ashamed. Don't be shy or bashful.
(H) Closeness, state of being close together or spaced only a little apart. (see íkit).
(H) Liking, longing, craving, fondness, desire. (see ílà).
Wildness, condition of an untamed animal; shyness, bashfulness, coyness. (ilá).
(H) Attraction, attractiveness, allurement, enticement. (see ílà).
Desire, instinct, passion, lust, appetite, prurience, cupidity, concupiscence, especially with regard to carnal emotions. (see íbug).
See kailíbgon id.
Wretched, miserable, poor, pitiable, woeful, unfortunate.
Darkness, blackness, brownishness, dun-colour. (ilóm).
(B) Liking, longing, craving, fondness, particularly for pleasant food, drink, etc. From íma. (see kaílà, kaíbug).
A kind of fruit tree.
Poverty, penury, want, destitution, deficiency, indigence. (ímol).
See kaímol. Also: Things that make life hard and poor, beggary, pauperism, impecuniousness.
See kaímol. (see kaimolán).
Jealousy, apprehension of rivalry, fear of being supplanted or superseded in love, esteem or rank. (ímon).
Stinginess, miserliness, closefistedness, meanness, niggardliness, parsimoniousness. (ímot).

(H) To go somewhere; to do, be, fare, come to, amount to, end, result. Makaín gid balá inâ? Where will it end? What will it finally come to or amount to? Makaín ka? Where are you going to? Ginkaín mo ang ákon lápis? Where did you put my pencil? (see anó).

A short while ago, some time since, a moment or a few hours ago (within the same day); formerly, previously. Kaína sang ága--. This morning--. Kaína lang siníng hápon naghalín siá. He left this afternoon. (see kunína-after some time).
Affability, amiableness, sociableness, sociability. (áblaw; see kaabiabíhon).
Tenderness, gentleness, softness, slowness, condition of anything done gently, quietly, softly, noiselessly or peacefully. (nanáy; see kananáy, kaananáy).

Practice and result of jungle-burning, burned clearing, clearing; to burn or fire a piece of grass-land, jungle or mountainside. Nagakaingín silá dídto sa bakólod. They are burning (or firing) the grass there on the hill. Kaíngna (kainginá) iníng talónan. Set fire to this jungle. (see tútud, súnug).

Nearness, proximity, neighbourhood, adjacency, state of being placed at the side of or near by; neighbour. Sa kaíngod sang ámon baláy. At the side of our house or near our house. Kaíngod námon siá. He is our neighbour. From íngod. (see kahilapít, kaíping).
Scarceness, scarcity, want, rareness, paucity, fewness, dearth. (íngol; see kaíwat, kahínà).
Heat, warmth, glow, fervour, ardour. (see ínit).
See kaínit. Also: The thick of a fight, heavy work during the heat of the day, etc. (see inítan).
Heat, especially the heat of the sun. See kaínit.
Economy, frugality, parsimony, niggardliness, thriftiness, meanness, closeness, miserliness. (ínot; see kakínot, kakinótan, kaímot).
See kaínot. (see kaímot).
China, the Chinese, Chinamen, the Chinese nation. (see ínsik).
(B) Smallness, littleness, diminutiveness. (see íntok, kagamáy, kadiótay, kaisót, katikî).
Neighbourhood, adjacency, proximity, nearness, state of being attached to the side of; neighbour. (see íping, kaíngod, kahilapít, kasilíngan).
(Sp. cairel) Appendage, fringe, silk-band, watch-chain.
See kairél id.
Once; sometimes. Kon kaisá--. Now and then, sometimes--. (see makaisá, kís-a).
Agreement, settlement, accord, union, pact. (see isá).
Oneness, union, unity, unification. (see isá).
Counting, reckoning, enumeration, telling, selfishness that counts up every little thing; fault-finding, carping. (see ísip).
Reckonings, thoughts, desires, plans, projects, designs, purposes, proposals, intentions. Ang Diós nagamándò sang áton mga hunâhúnà kag kaisipán. God directs our thoughts and intentions.
(B) Smallness, littleness, a small amount, especially of liquids. For solids "katikî" is more often used. (see isót).
Violence, vehemence, bravery, courage, hardihood, force, strength, severeness, severity, strictness. (see ísug).
Blackness, darkness, swarthiness, state of being dark coloured. (see itúm).
Scarcity, rarity. (íwat; see kahínà, kaíngol).

Full, stuffed, crammed, brimful, chockfull, chokefull, bulging; to be or become full, etc. Abáw, balíkda ináng bátà nga nagakâkâ ang íya bólsa sang kamúnsil. My! look back at that boy whose pockets are stuffed with camunsel-fruit. Kâkâ ang íya púyo. His purse is full. (see bát-al, punô, báknal).

To collect, gather, scrape or rake together with the hand, as things lying on a table, earth from a hole, etc. Kakáha ang dútà. Scrape the earth together. Kakáhi ang tabungós sing humáy. Take some rice from the tabungos-basket (with your hands). Ikáka akó ánay siníng maís. Gather, please, these maize-seeds (maize-cobs) with your hand. Diín akó makakáka sing pílak? Where can I scrape together some money? (see típon, tingúb).
Cackle, cackling; to cackle; to talk or shout much. (see kákak).
Toughness, insensibility to pain. (see kabalán).
Pungency, sharpness, hotness, acidity, acridity, (kádat; see kaádat).
Greediness, gluttony, voraciousness, voracity; desire for honour or excellence, ambition. (kágud).
Pungency, acerbity, sharpness, hotness, piquancy of taste. (káhang).
Audacity, boldness, hardihood, temerity, insolence, venturesomeness, rashness, cheek, impertinence, daring, intrepidity. (see káhas).
Forest, wood, coppice, copse; collection of trees, wood, timber, lumber. (see káhoy).
Cackling; to cackle. Ang mungâ nagakákak. The hen cackles. (see kakáak, kurukutúk-to cluck).
Ticklishness, sensation produced by tickling. (see kalám).
Uncouthness, unsightliness, ungainliness, boorishness, clumsiness, awkwardness. (see kaliwâ, baksiwâ, bikwálon).
Brightness of colours, conspicuousness, condition of one dressed up in bright colours. (see kánang).

Slowness, retardation, a slow, tedious process. Ang pagkakúlang sang kasangkápan amó ang nanginkabangdánan sang kakánat sang íla pagpangabúdlay. Lack of tools was the cause of the slowness of their work. (see kánat).
Brightness, shine, lustre, polish. (see kánaw).
Leanness, thinness, meagreness. (see kandínggal, kaníwang, kahágpis, kakanít).
(B) Leanness, thinness, skinniness, emaciation, lankness, gauntness. (see kanít, kaníwang, kakandínggal).
(B) Staleness, insipidity, insipidness, tastelessness, mawkishness, condition of cold cooked food, especially applied to rice. (see kápog, kabáhaw).
Exhaustion, tiredness, weakness, fatigue, languor, lassitude. (see kápoy, kabúdlay, kaálay, kapául, kalúyò, kalúya, kakúlì).
(H) See kaádat, kakádat.
Hustling, speeding-up, haste, despatch, dispatch, expedition, hurry; volubility (of speech). (see karókaró, kadásig, kadalî, kagarógaró).

To wash away-, take out-, dissolve-, a stain, or the like. Butangí sing agás, agúd makakás ang pínta. Apply some kerosene to remove the stain of paint. Anó balá ang maáyo nga ikakás ko sa siní nga bulíng? What is the best for removing-, taking out-, this stain? Kakasá ang mga dágtà nga tínta sa ímo kamót. Wash the ink-stains off your hand. Indì akó makakakás siníng bulíng (índì ko makakás iníng bulíng) sa túbig. I cannot get this stain out with water. Kakasí akó sináng mga dágtà sa ákon delárgo. Wash those stains out of my trousers. Ikakás akó sináng hígkò sa ákon báyò. Please wash that dirt off my jacket.
Leanness, meagreness, thinness, condition of one who is as lean as a casag-crab. (kaság; see kaníwang, kakanít).
Spain; Spaniards; the Spanish Nation. (see Katsílà).
Itchiness. (katúl).
(Sp. cacao) The cacao-tree and its fruit; cocoa.
Clumps of bamboos; bamboo in general. (see kawáyan, kawayánan).

Sneak, trickster, tricksy, sly, wily, clever, cunning (used only-and mostly humorously-of females). Ay, si tíyà kákay man--! Oh that wily aunty--! Oh that tricky (cunning, sly, clever) good soul--! (see kákoy).
Khaki.
Savouriness, tastiness, toothsomeness (of eatables that are neither too soft nor too hard, but just right). (see kíd-ol).
(H) Relations, relatives, family connections, friends. (see kílid).
Economy, retrenchment, thrift, etc. See kaínot, kakinotón. (kínot-ínot).
See kakínot, kaínot. Also: Collective of all things that bring about economy or frugal living.
See kakínot.
Quick movement, agility, litheness; sudden jerk. (kisáy; see kapágsik, kalígsi).
Often stands for makakítà, nakakítà from kítà-to see.
(B) Narrowness, tightness, little breadth or width. (see kitíd).
(H) See kakitidón.

Nearness, proximity (of time); narrowness (of mind); tightness (of clothes, belts, etc.). Kakóg-ong na sang Simána Sánta! How near Holy Week is! Kakóg-ong sang íya ísip! How narrow-minded he is! Kakóg-ong sang ákon wáklos; laboyán ko. My belt is too tight; I am going to loosen it. (see kógong, lapít, gutúk).
Place where much cogon-grass grows; mountain side or field covered with cogon-grass. (see kógon, kakogonán).
See kakógnan.
(H) Pottery, pots and jars. (see kólon).
A sneak, trickster, cheat; fool; to fool, cheat, trick. Ginakákoy lang níya siá. He is just fooling him. Indì mo akó pagkakóyon. Don't fool, trick or cheat me. (see búang, hásò, lágit, agóng, etc.).
Lowness, lowliness, humble station or position; meanness. (see kubús).
See kakubús. Also: the humble, poor, low caste, low class, Pariah.
Diligence, assiduousness, assiduity, industry, application, care. (see kúgi).
Fright, alarm, fear, terror, panic, dread. (see kúgmat).
Want, need, lack, insufficiency. (see kulábus).
Shortcomings, lack, want, insufficiency. (see kúlang).
Shyness, fear, trepidation, apprehension, nervousness, nervous excitement, trembling. (see kúlbà).

(H) Slowness, arduousness, hardness, laboriousness, irksomeness, toilsomeness, condition of something that is achieved only step by step with hard work or great patience, (kúlì; see kahínay, kabúdlay, kakánat).
(H) See kakúlì. Also: Difficulties, hardships, things requiring hard work or great patience.
(H) Laboriousness, etc. See kakúlì.
Partner, associate, fellow-member, stockholder, shareholder (of a firm or company). (see kumbúya, kumbuyahán).
Shrinkage, contraction, dwindling. (see kúpus, kupús).
Strength, force, power, vigour. (see kúsug, kusúg).
Shakiness, unsteadiness, weakness, feebleness, debility. (see kuyúg, kalúya, kalúyò, kakúlì).
A croak, the hoarse, harsh cry of a frog; to croak (as a frog). Ang mga pakâ (pánkà) nagakálà. Frogs croak. N.B. The Dim. and Freq. kalâkalâ is more in use.
Shell, tortoise shell; made of tortoise shell (or an imitation of it); comb (of tortoise shell). Ang íya husáy kála. Her comb is made of tortoise shell.
Dim. of kálà-croaking; to croak.
(H) A field planted one year which without additional planting yields its produce the following year also, (especially applied to sugar-cane fields). (see dáan).
(H) Things to be mended or standing in need of repair. (áyo, kaáyo; see kilidanón, kiridanón).
(H) Length of objects, extent from end to end. (lábà; see kalabaón, kalábug, kalabugón, kadúgay, kabúhay-length of time).
(H) Cloth to be worked up, or fit to be worked up, into farmers' shirts called "kába".
The greater part or number, majority. (labán; see kadám-an).
(Sp. garbanzo) A kind of chick-peas.
(H) Length. See kalábà.

(Sp. calabaza) Squash, pumpkin, gourd; failure, mess, fiasco; to make a mess of, meet with failure, commit a great blunder. Nakalabása (Nagkalabása) ang íla tábad. Their banquet was a failure. Ginkalabása lang akó níya. He left me in the lurch, tricked or cheated me, made a fool of me, caused my plans or intentions to miscarry.
Common or joint property. (see karabátan).
Excess, haughtiness, great ambition to exceed others. (see labáw).
The larger or greater share, more than others, or more than is left; excess, superfluity, superabundance, redundancy, what is beyond due limits. (see labáw).
(Sp. calavera) Skull. (see bagól).

Preference, preponderance, excellence, privilege, value or esteem set upon one thing rather than another. Ang mga kalabihán sang Mahál nga Bírhen. The excellences or glories of the Blessed Virgin. (see labí).
Anything liable or exposed to being undermined or having its foundations sapped by the action of water; hen-nest. (see kábkab).
Eggs to be hatched. (see kalabkában).
That is to be, or can be, touched; tangible. (see káblit).
Tastiness, savouriness (of squashes, tubers, etc.; see labó).
(Sp. calabozo) Prison, jail, dungeon, calaboose. (see bilanggóan).
Relations, connection, interest, implication, participation, share, interference, meddling. (see lábut, kalabútan).
(B) See kalábà.
(B) See kalabaón.
(H) Astonishment, amazement, wonder, surprise; wonderful, astounding, amazing. (búlung). (see kahaurungán).
Prison, gaol. (see kalabóso, karsíl, bilanggóan).
Connection with, relation, etc. See kalabtánan.
Tallness, large size (when age is considered). (see lábwak).
A kind of "dágmay". (see gládì).

(H) Fun, funniness, drollery, ludicrousness, laughableness, ridiculousness, pleasantry, anything that excites laughter (with or without contempt); ridiculous, funny, droll, etc. (see kádlaw, kalaham-után).
(H) Laughter, act of laughter, inclination to laugh. Ginkagát níya ang íya bibíg sa pagpugúng sang íya kaladláwon. He bit his lips to check (restrain) his laughter.
(Sp. calado) Draught of a vessel; fretwork. (see dágpak).
(Sp. cuadrado) Square. (see kasílo).
(H) Place to go to or arrive at. (kádto; see kadtoán).
(B) Intelligence, sensibility, sensibleness, sense, reasonableness, judiciousness, understanding, prudence, common sense, wisdom, sagacity, sagaciousness. (see ísip, ihibaló, kalibútan).
Soul, spirit, moral and spiritual nature of man; a disembodied spirit; vitality, moving spirit. (see kálag, láwas-body, matter).
Cunning, craftiness, knavery, double-dealing, trickiness, cheating, artfulness. (see lág-it).
(B) Dim. of kálag. Sense, wit, understanding, intelligence.
(B) Sensible, intelligent, prudent, reasonable, wise, docile, sagacious, judicious, obedient. (see kálag, kalág, but-ánan).
Slowness; gentleness, tenderness. (see lágday, kalágway).
(H) Mourning, grief, sorrow; what is to be mourned over or grieved at, lamentable. (see kághà, makakalágha).

To arrange, dispose, marshal, array, regulate, put in order; prepare well, drill, make ship-shape. Kalagínga ang mga tulún-an, bánkò, láta, botílya, etc. Set in order the books, benches, tins, bottles, etc. Kinalagíngan akó níya sang mga galamitón sang ákon balatonán. He arranged for me the furniture of my reception room. Ginkaláging sang mananábang sing maáyo ang mga sáksi. The lawyer drilled (prepared) the witnesses well. (see káging, húsay, hímos, áman, híwat).
Destruction, perdition, ruin. (see láglag).
Of, or pertaining to, the soul or spirit, spiritual, immaterial. (see kalág, espirituhánon).
(B) Dirt, dirtiness, filthiness, condition of being dirtied, foul, soiled, tarnished, particularly applied to soiled clothes. (see lagô, lagôlagô).
(H) A rasp, a kind of coarse file. (see kagót, kágot).
Freshness, vigour, vigorousness, floridness (of plants). (lágtom).

(H) Noise, commotion, stir, excitement, disturbance, riot, sensation; making a stir, causing or exciting a commotion, etc. Kalagulaán iníng mga balítà sa dílì madúgay. These reports will soon cause a sensation. (see makagulúlà, gúlà, gamó).
Slowness, etc. See kalágday (lágway-lágday).

To deteriorate, degenerate, become less productive. Nagakalágyan ang mga ságing, kapáyas, etc. sa ámon hardín. The bananas, papaws, etc. in our garden are deteriorating, are giving less fruit than formerly.
(H) Black spots on the skin.
(H) Pan, frying pan.
(H) Things that excite fear or terror; fearsome, fearful, terrible, awful, horrible, dreadful, frightful, alarming, appalling. (see hádluk, kahadlukán).
To touch, feel. (see káham, láham, ipangaláham).
(H) Merriment, pleasure, pleasantry, fun, mirth, drollery, buffoonery, things that excite laughter and merriment. (see hám-u, kahám-ut, kaham-útan, kaham-utánan, makahalám-ut).
(H) See kalaham-után.
(H) Fear, apprehension, etc. See kahalangáw-an, kahangaláw-an, kahangáwà.

(H) Grief, sorrow, pity, commiseration, sympathy; things that excite pity or compassion, pitiable, woeful, lamentable, sad, distressful, deplorable, pathetic, touching, affecting. (see subô, hanúsbò).
Rake, anything that is used for raking. (see káhig, kahíg).
(H) Things to be-cherished,-desired,-regretted (when lost); desirable, lovely, highly praised or esteemed; regrettable. (see hílak, makahihílak, makahilílak).
Poisonous, venomous, baneful, noisome, noxious. (see hilô, makahihílo, karahílo).

The liquid obtained from the tapican-fruit and used to spite others by spirting it on them by means of a tube, the liquid causing great itch and pain, more even than "nípay"; to use or apply "kalahós". Kalahosón níya ikáw, konó. They say, he will treat you to a dose of "kalahós". Ginkalahós níya siá. He was treated by him with "kalahós". (see nípay).
(H) Attraction, attractiveness, fascination, winsomeness, allurement, enticement, charm; attractive, seductive, winning, captivating, charming, fascinating, bewitching. (see ílà, makailílà).
(B) Disagreeable to sight or taste, distasteful, revolting, noisome, disgusting, repelling, ugly, bad; quality that excites disgust or aversion. (see límnan, laímnan).
(H) Badness, maliciousness, malignity, malevolence, hurtfulness, harmfulness, perniciousness, noxiousness, wickedness, noisomeness. (see láin).
Difference, diversity, dissimilarity. (see laín, kalaínlaínan).
To be different, dissimilar, diverse, unlike; to differ one from another. Nagakalaínláin silá sing duág. They are different in colour-or-of different colours.
Difference, diversity, variety, unlikeness, dissimilarity.
Badness, etc. See kaláin. Also: evil, harm, hurt, mischief, prejudice, drawback, disadvantage.

(H) Jungle or grass to be burned or fired. Siá amó ang tag-* *íya sang madámù nga kalaíngnon. He is the owner of many parcels of land that can be cleared by fire and made fit for the plough. (see kaingín).
(B) See kalaímnan.
Excess, extreme, radicalism, extravagance, intemperance. (lakás).

To throw about one's arms and legs in gaiety and merriment, to jump, frolic and play like children, to be full of mirth and hilarity. Ang mga bátà nagakalakatád. The boys are frolicking. (see karakatád, tiríktirík).
Treacherousness, insidiousness (of diseases, etc.). (see lála, malála).
Men, males, menfolk. (see laláki).
Means, ways, device, contrivance, appliance, resource that is employed to bring about something. (see laláng).
Evils, harm, injury, affliction, disaster, misfortune. (see láut).
(H) A flat-bottomed sieve or low-brimmed basket mainly used to separate freshly pounded rice from the chaff. (see karáraw).
(B) Sea, ocean. (see lawód, kalaláwran, kadagátan).
(H) See kalaláwdan.
(H) See kalaláwdan.
Road, line, limit, boundary; to lie athwart, lie across, be in the passage of. (see lábang, labangán, kalbangán).
(H) Taste, flavour; tastiness, savouriness, toothsomeness; ingredient, admixture; element. (see lalím).
What is to be wound on a bobbin, as a thread, etc. (kalíngyas).
(H) Pleasure, things that give joy or pleasure; pleasant, pleasurable, enjoyable, gratifying. (see lípay, kalípay, makalilípay, malipáyon, malipayón).

(H) Superfluous, redundant, exaggeration, what is to be or should be removed, taken away or left out, or, "taken with a grain of salt" (not to be fully believed). Kalalíson na gid ang amó nga mga punípúni. Those flourishes (or little decorations) should be removed or left out. Ang íya nga pagpakigsúmpung sa kay Fuláno may katarúngan nga dakû, ápang kalalíson gid man ang ibán nga ginsilíng níya. His opposition to N.N. is perfectly justified, but some of the things he said must be taken with a grain of salt. (see kalís).
(H) Promptness, despatch, expedition, first opportunity; anything that does not suffer delay or should be done quickly. (see kalít).
(H) Pitiableness, anything that excites pity or compassion. (see kalalóy-an, makaloló-oy).
(H) Nail, claw or anything else used for scratching, scraping, digging out earth, etc. (kálot; see karalót id.).
Things to be scratched or dug out, as roots, tubers, etc. (kálot; see talangkónon).
What is to be scratched, rubbed or soothed, as an itch; trial, hardship, difficulty; hard to bear or suffer. (see kálot, kalalóton).
See kalalo-oyán id.
Loveliness, attraction, charm; likeable, lovely, charming, pleasing, captivating, anything that excites a liking, affection or passion for. (see lúyag, makalulúyag, maluyagón, pangaluyág).
Place where digging is done, a mine, or the like. (see káli).
To tickle, itch, irritate, titillate. Ginakalamán akó. I have a tickling feeling.
Doubt, suspense of judgment, uncertainty, indecision, hesitation. (see lamá-lamá, kaduháduháan).
(H) Novelty, modernity, novel or new-fangled things. (see bág-o, kamág-o, kamag-ohán).
Anything that crawls or creeps, as snails, crabs, shrimps, etc. (see kámang).

Lean, thin, emaciated, gaunt, spare, skinny; to become lean, etc. Iníng báboy kalamanít kaáyo. This pig is very lean. Nagkalamanít ang karabáw kay nabugtasán sa pangabúdlay. The buffalo became lean, because it was overworked. (see kanít, maníwang, níwang).
To die (of many). (see kamátay, patáy).

(H) Deadly, fatal, mortiferous; a fatal spot. Awát na lang ang pagbulúng sa íya, kay ang íya pilás sa kalamatáyan gid. He was past cure, for his wound was mortal, for he was wounded in a vital spot. (see patáy, kalamátyan id.).
(H) See kalamatáyan id.
Sugar.
To sugar, to flatter, to "soft soap". Indì mo siá pagkalamayón. Don't flatter him. Ginkalamáy níla siá. They flattered him-or-They "soft-soaped" him. (see unís, utís, odót, paayónáyon).
A sweet dish of crushed or pulverised rice mixed with sugar and the juice of coconut-meat.

To get bad, fester, mortify, gangrene (applied especially to wounds becoming worse through the influence of heat). Kinalamáyo ang íya nga pilás. His wound got bad (through exposure to heat). Also: erysipelas, St. Anthony's fire.

Healthy growth, quality of-growing well,-thriving,-flourishing. Ang mga tanúm nga waláy kalámbò dápat nga bunyagán kag sagurón. Plants that do not grow well or thrive should be watered and taken care of. (see lámbò).
A guard-ring, made as a rule thinner than the ring it guards.
See awóáwo id.
A kind of river-crab. (see kaság, kágang, pangalámpay).
Tripod, especially a small iron one for use in the kitchen.
(H) Dining table, dining room, refectory, restaurant, eating place. (see káon).
(H) Food, especially rice. (see káon).
(H) Sweets, sweetmeat, pastry, cakes, biscuits, bread, etc. (Almost any side-dish may be called "kalan-ónon", except rice, meat, fish and vegetables). (see káon).
(H) To shine, glisten; fill (with tears). (See kánaw, kanáwkanáw).
A kind of very sticky, viscous rice; it is particularly used for making "íbus" and "alopí". (see arabón, pilít).
Unsymmetrical, awry, unequal, lop-sided, disproportioned, queer, odd, strange. Ang íya bísti kalandrákas. Her dress is unsymmetrical. She is dressed in an odd style.
(H) Ladle, scoop, shovel for dry or liquid things. (see kándus, luág, garaló).
A covering or protection for wounds. Also verb: Kalángi ang pilás-or-butangí sing kálang ang pilás. Put a covering over the wound.
Braided straw, twigs, mat, or the like used to place pots upon to prevent them from coming into contact with the floor. (see likín).
Jocoseness, jocosity, jocularity, waggery. (see langás).
(H) Abomination, frightfulness, repulsiveness, something shocking or terrifying, things awful to look upon, filthy stench. (see ngíl-ad, kangíl-ad).
Rottenness, rancidness, condition of being spoilt (of coconut-meat, copra, etc.). (langís).
The disagreeable sensation produced by strident sounds, as by a saw encountering a nail or stone, etc. (langís).
Heaven; the heavens, firmament, welkin (poetical). (see lángit).
Impatience, uneasiness, weariness, worry; longing, expectancy, desire. (see lángkag).
(H) To stretch out one's hand with fingers apart, as when catching a ball, etc. Kalangkangá ang kamót mo, ang túdlò mo. Stretch out your hand, spread your fingers.
Ripeness, fulness (of grains, nuts, etc.). (see lángking).
Stop, pause, interval, rest. (see langán).
A strong fishy taste or smell (said of fish in a raw as well as in a cooked state). (lángsa).
A bad, vapid, insipid nauseating taste, disagreeable flavour, particularly applied to raw or half-raw or green peas and beans. (see lángto).
That is to be pitied or regretted. (see kanógon).
State of being over-ripe, rotten-ripeness. (see lanóng, katanáng).

Hardness, fulness, ripeness; to be full and ripe, applied especially to kadiós-beans. Nagaamátamát na ang kadiós sang kalánsan. The kadiós-beans are beginning to get full and hard. Nagkalánsan na ang kadiós. The kadiós beans have become full and ripe. (See kadiós).
(H) A song, lay, ballad, ditty, what is to be sung, a hymn, chant, canticle. (kánta; see ambahánon, ambáhan).
Perfection, excellence. (see lántip).
Perfection, quality of the highest worth, excellence, first class, supreme, things of the highest standard. (lántip; see kahimpitán).
To fill with water, mortify, get infected or purulent through the action of water, said of wounds, etc. Kinalantubíg ang ákon pilás. My wound mortified (through contact with water).
Associate, companion, cooperator, collaborator; at the side of, near-by, adjacent. (see tupád).
Breadth, width, extensiveness, wideness, extent. (lápad).
See kalápad.
(H) See kalápad.
Omission, neglect, negligence, failure to comply with orders, duties, etc. (see lápas).
A tick, a kind of mite (very small insect). (see galapáta).

To caulk (a boat, ship); to knead, mix; to besmear, plaster. Kalapatíhon mo ang lúnang kag iháplas sa kólon, agúd índì magtúlò. Knead the mud and plaster the rice-kettle with it, that it may not leak.
(H) Nearness, proximity, short distance. (see lapít).

Tendril of a vine, etc.; to encircle, wind around, cling to, entwine. Ang búyò nagakalápkap sa búgsok. The "búyò" is winding itself around the post. Iníng mga bató ginakalapkapán sang kadenadeamór. These stones are entwined with the vine called "cadena de amor". Pakalapkapá ang kalubáy sa palápála. Make the "calubay" cling to the trellis or lattice work. (see kápkap, kabúd).
Plaster, any kind of sticky or viscous material. (kápol).
(H) To be-castrated,-gelded, fit to be made-a "capon",-a eunuch (especially said of cocks). (see kapón).
(H) Handle, haft, grip; anything to be grasped or held. (see kapút).
(H) Place where animals are castrated. (see kapón).
(H) Anything used for grasping or holding. (kapút).
To adhere to, stick together. (see kápot, dokót, pilít).
(H) Thickness, consistence, coherence, density, condensation, inspissation (of liquids). (see lapúyut).
Tiredness, fatigue, exhaustion, feebleness, weakness. (see lápyò, kabúdlay, kalúyà).
Handle, grip, grasp, hold, haft; influence, power, sway. (see kápyot).
A harrow. (see pakalás, pakarás-to harrow).

To rustle (as dry leaves in the wind). Nagakálas ang lukáy. The dry coconut-leaves are rustling. Ang mga dáhon nga kigás ginapakálas sang hángin. The dry leaves are being rustled by the wind-or-are rustling in the wind.
Tastelessness, mawkishness, insipidness, vapidity. (lás-ay).
See kalás-ay. Also: Things that are insipid or cause nausea or aversion.
Shield, cover, protection, defense; escutcheon.
(H) Bride, bridegroom, a couple to be married. (see kasál).
Foolishness, folly, stupidity, silliness, shallowness, stolidity, fatuity, nonsense, condition of one who talks foolishly or has silly ideas. (see lásang).
Folly, stupidity, twaddle, silly talk. (see kalásang).
(H) See kalasálon.
Rope, thick string, line, cord. (see lúbid, písì).
Condition or state of food cooked overmuch or overdone. (see latâ).
Snare, trap, net; difficulty, trial. (see káti, katián).
(H) Meeting, assembly, club, club-house, society. (see típon).
A kind of cactus-tree with beautiful white flowers.
Evil, badness, wickedness, malice, malignity, maliciousness, malevolence, banefulness, balefulness, perniciousness, noxiousness; misery, wretchedness, misfortune. (see láut, kaláin).
See kaláut. Also: Harm, injury, bad things, wicked deeds.
(H) Ugliness, hideousness, unsightliness, unseemliness, nastiness, unbecomingness, impropriety, indecency. (see láw-ay).
(H) See kaláw-ay. Also: Things that are ugly, unbecoming, dishonest, indecent, filthy, improper.
A kind of plant. It is used as a remedy for painful or decaying teeth.
Body, materiality. (see láwas).
Body, the main or principal part of a dress, the contents of a letter (as distinct from the address), etc. (see lawás, ináng).

To receive Holy Communion, communicate. Nakakaláwat na ikáw? Have you been to Holy Communion? Sín-o ang ginakaláwat? Who is received in Holy Communion? Buás magakaláwat akó. To-morrow I will receive Holy Communion. Mangaláwat akó karón. I am going-to receive Holy Communion now. Ang masakít nga táo ginpakaláwat sang Párì. The sick man had Holy Communion administered to him by the Priest. The Priest gave the sick man Holy Communion.
Such as to be reached or grasped; within reach, near, easy to obtain, obtainable. (see káwhat).
(B) Length, duration of time. (see kaláwig id.).
(H) Length, duration of time. (see láwig).
Length; distance. (see kaláwig, kalayoón).
(H) Pleasure, enjoyment, delight, satisfaction. (wíli; see kalawilihán, kawilihán).
(H) See kalawilián, kawilihán id.
(H) Anything used as a hook, as a stick or pole with a hook attached to it and the like. (kawít; see síngit, singít).
(B) Bigness, hugeness, condition or quality of being-very tall,-of more than ordinary size, especially applied to animals. (lawóg).

To jingle, chink, tingle, tinkle (of coins, iron chains, etc.). Nagakálay ang kwárta sa íya bólsa. The money is jingling in his pocket. Indì mo pagpakaláyon ang pílak mo. Don't jingle your money. (see kálas, lágting).
Dryness, exsiccation. (see láyà, layâ).
Exsiccation, withering, fading, drying up. Búlak nga walâ sing kalayaán. A flower that never withers. (see kalayâ).
(B) Looseness, bagginess, wideness (of clothes that are too large and the like). (see layáng, kasángkad).
Aridity, dryness; dry or arid soil. (see layóng).
(H) Farness, distance, remoteness, far away. Anó ang kalayô sinâ? How far is it?
(H) To be on fire, to flame or flare up (of fire; see hingaláyo, kaláyo).
Fire; flame.
See kaláyngan-aridity, etc.
(H) See kalayô.
(B) Main road, principal way or passage.
See kalabása. Ang kalbása kon malabó maáyo nga utánon. The squash, if just right (i.e. neither too hard nor too soft), is a nice vegetable.
(Sp. calvo) Bald, hairless. (see bungád, upáw).
(Sp. caldera) Kettle, cooking pot (of metal).
(Sp. caldero) A large kettle, bucket or tub (of metal).

(Sp. caldo) Broth, beef-tea, bouillon, sauce, gravy, a stew, a mixture of meat, potatoes, onions, sausages, etc. Also verb: Kaldohán mo akó sing kárne. Make me a dish of "káldo" from meat. Also: A large bowl or cup; saucepan. (see kaldóhan).
Pot or kettle for making "káldo". (see káldo, tasón).
(Sp. calendario) Calendar, almanac. (see almanáki).
(Sp. calentura) A cold, fever. (see lágnat, hilánat).
(Sp. calesa) A kind of two-wheeled vehicle, covered-in buggy or gig.
(Sp. calesin) A small kalésa.
To dig. Kalíha (kálya) ang dútà. Dig up the ground. Kalíhi (kályi) ang halígi. Dig up the ground around the post. Ikáli akó ánay sing kamóti. Please dig up for me some sweet potatoes.
Discordance, dissonance, flatness (of sounds, voices, music, etc.). (libágon).
Occupation, task, business, work, preoccupation preventing one from attending to something else. May kalibángan pa akó. I have still some work to do-or-I am still occupied or busy. (see libáng).
Squinting, squint, condition of one who is cross-eyed. (see libát).
(B) The youngest (a younger) brother or sister; the last or youngest child of a family. Si Pédro amó ang íya anák nga kalibáynan. Peter is her youngest child. (see libáyon, kamanghóran, mánghud).
Confusion, dizziness, perplexity, giddiness, vertigo. (libúg).

See kalibúg. Also: Mixture as between Visayans and Negritos, Visayans and Europeans, etc.; Mestizo, half-breed, hybrid. Ang mga bumulúthò nga tumándok nagpakigáway sa mga bumulúthò nga katsílà kag kalibugán. The native students fought against the Spanish and half-caste students.

World, earth, visible creation, universe; the world as opposed to moral and spiritual forces; reason, intelligence. Walâ na siá sing kalibútan. He is unconscious. (Literally: "There is no world for him"). Walâ siá sing kalibútan. He knows nothing. May kalibútan pa siá. He is still conscious. Ang lángit kag ang kalibútan. Heaven and earth. Dirí sa ibábaw siníng kalibútan--. Here on the face of the earth--. Ang kalibútan kag ang íya sinâ nga kadayáwan umalági man lang. The world and its vanities are but passing. (líbut).
How is it possible to know, etc. See pamál-i, panghimál-i.
Worldly, earthly, materialistic, sensuous, sensual. Ang mga táo nga kalibutánon. The worldly minded. Kalípay nga kalibutánon. Worldly or sensual pleasures.
Firmness, stability, security, durability. (see líg-on).
See kalíg-on. Also: Security, bond, bail, anything that makes for stability or freedom from danger and apprehension.
(B) Forgetfulness, carelessness, negligence, disregard, slight, unmindfulness, heedlessness. (see lígà, kalipát, kalipátan).
(B) See kalígà. (see kalipátan).
Modesty, propriety, correctness of conduct, self-respect. (lígdong; see kaúgdang).
Laziness, indolence, idleness, sloth, inaction. (ligóy).
Laziness. (see kaligóy, ligóy, katámad).
Swiftness, speediness, celerity, rapidity, fleetness, nimbleness, agility, quickness of movement. (lígsi; see kalíksi).
(H) To stir, loosen up earth, rice in a kettle, etc. Kalikáda (kalikára) ang tiníg-ang. Loosen up the cooked rice. (see hakíd, súkad).
Anything used for cleaning out liquid waste matter from narrow tubes or holes, as from the ear, the nose, a wound, etc. (see kilikóg).

To clean out with a feather, cotton, stick, etc. a narrow aperture, wound, hole, etc. Kalikóga sang búlbul ang ímo dulúnggan. Clean your ear with a feather. Kalikógi ang ilóng sang bátà. Wipe the baby's nose. Ikalíkog akó ánay sang ákon pilás. Please cleanse my wound. (see kilíkog).
See kalígsi. (see líksi-lígsi).
(H) Preoccupation, distraction, state or condition of being much upset or distracted by cares, etc.; things that make one's head swim, perplexity. (libúg; see kalibúg).
(H) See kalilíbgan.
Hardships, troubles, difficulties, stress, straits. (see lisúd).
Fifty. (see limá).
For makalimóg, nakalimóg. (see limóg, katingúg).
(H) Forgetfulness, oblivion. (límot; see kalígà).
The eyeball, the apple of the eye; the pupil of the eye. (see taótáo).
Calm, quiet, tranquillity, calmness, stillness, smoothness, quietness, state or condition of being unruffled. (see línaw).
See kalínaw. Also: Things that insure peace and tranquillity.
Plough-handle, plough-tail.
Folly, foolishness, stupidity; a stupid fellow.

Distraction, diversion, inattention, condition or state of being distracted. Támà gid ang íya kalingáw (pagkalingáw) nga walâ siá makabatî sang lágpok sang íya bátà nga nahúlug sa hágdan. She was so distracted that she did not even hear the noise made by her child when it fell down the stairs. (see lingáw).
Distraction, diversion, relaxation, entertainment, things apt to distract the mind and provide amusement. (see lingáw).
Distraction, diversion, amusement, pastime, relaxation, recreation. (see lingáw, kalingáw, kalingáw-lingáwan).
Confusion, perturbation, embarrassment, distraction, worry. Dakû ang kalíngin sang íya ólo. His mind is greatly perturbed, worried, upset. (see língin, lingín).
Doubt, hesitation, questioning, incertitude, misgiving, distrust, suspense, indecision, vacillation. (see lingólingó, kalamalamahán).
Apprehension of danger, hesitation, wavering.
See kalínyas-to wind on a bobbin, etc.
Peace, order, quiet, quietude, tranquillity, calm. (see linóng).
Bobbin; to wind on a bobbin. Ang bunáng ginakalínyas. Yarn is wound on a bobbin. Kalinyasá iníng isá ka labág nga kósta. Wind this hank of yarn on bobbins.
(H) Shortness, briefness, brevity, small extension from end to end. (líp-ot).
(H) Oblivion, forgetfulness. (lipát; see kalímot, kalígà).
(H) Forgetfulness, etc. Ang kalipátan unáy sa láwas. Forgetfulness is a common failing of man. (see kalipát, kalígà, kaligáan).
Joy, gaiety, pleasure, cheer, entertainment, gladness, delight, glee, cheerfulness, mirth, merriment, hilarity, bliss. (see lípay).
See kalípay. Also: Things that give pleasure, happiness or enjoyment.
Swoon, faint, fainting-fit, syncope, fit, unconsciousness. (see lipóng).
(H) Anus. (see áno, kagalán, ipotán).

(Sp. calero, calera) Lime-kiln, lime-burner; faggots or wood used in burning people at the stake; to burn at the stake. Ginkalíro níla ang buyóng. They burned the robber at the stake. Ang maáyo sa íya kaliróhon. It would be best to burn him at the stake. (A saying used in anger and passion).
Lime-kiln; furnace. Ginbutáng siá níla sa kalirohán. They put him into the furnace (lime-kiln). (see kalíro).
(Sp. caliz) Chalice.
(Sp. cris) The Malayan dagger, creese or cris, a sword as used by the Moros.

To even out, strike or level off what is above measure or superfluous, especially in measuring out grain. Kalisá ang gantángan. Strike off the heap on top of the gantángan-measure. Ikalís akó ánay siníng paníga. Please level off this fanega. (paníga; (Sp. fanega)-half a pásong (bushel)).
Horror, terror, fear, panic, fright, frightfulness. (see lísang).
Tastelessness, insipidness, unsavouriness, usually applied to stale tubers like "úbi", "banáyan", "kamóti", etc. (see lísaw).
Difficulties, distress, etc. See kalilísdan, lisúd, kalisúd.
Tilt, slant, leaning, inclination. (see lísding).
See kalísding. Also: liability to tilt, possibility of tilting. Dílì ka mahádluk sináng bayóng, kay walâ gid inâ sing kalisdingán. Have no fear about that bamboo water-tube, for it cannot tilt over.
Backwardness, dulness, stupidity, condition of a person whose mental faculties are below normal. (see pungág, tampuháw, pákok, búngaw).
(From the Sp. listo) Cleverness, sharpness, intelligence, quickness, capacity, sagacity, brightness, resourcefulness, gumption, capableness; trickiness.
Hardship, trouble, cross, adversity, affliction, visitation, bad-, ill-, fortune or luck. (see kalisdánan, kalilísdan, lisúd).

To anticipate, do promptly, take the first opportunity. Ginakalitán sang mga buyúng ang kadudúlmon sa pagpangatí. The brigands are prompt in making use of the darkness for their depredations. Kalití ang ímo pagpaúlì, kay básì maulanán ikáw. Go home quickly, or the rain may overtake you.

A kind of binding or fastening together with spaces between the pieces fastened together, as in the making of a "lág-i", of split-bamboo flooring, etc.; to tie, fasten or bind together after the manner of "kalítgit".
Clumsy, awkward, ungainly. (see baksiwâ, bikwálon).
See kaliwâ.
Stock, family, inheritance, heredity. Nagasándig gid siá sa kalíwat. He is a chip off the old block. (see liwát).
Generation, progeny, offspring, descendants. (see kalíwat).

A non-liquid enema, an introduction into the rectum of kalawág-roots or the like in order to relieve constipation. Kaliyáhi siá sing upús kag sibúyas. Give him an enema of the remnants of a smoked cigar and of onions. (see ayúda, labatíba).
Dried hipon-fish; to become as dry as dried hipon-fish. Nagkálkag na ang bagáso. The bagasse has become as dry as dried hipon-fish, i.e. is quite exsiccated and brittle or friable.

To remove, get or take out, as bones from a mortuary niche, to dig out, look-, hunt-, up, data from a register or the like. Kalkalá ang linubúng. Disinter the buried corpse. Ginkálkal sang piskál ang sertipíko nga kinahánglan ko. The parish-clerk dug out from the register the certificate I needed. Kalkalí akó sang ákon sertipíko sang bautísmo. Look up and copy for me my baptismal certificate. Ikálkal akó ánay siníng panteón nga dáan. Please open and clean out this mortuary niche for me.
(B) To stir, turn about. Kalóa ang túbig. Stir the water. Sín-o ang nagkálò sang áwang, kay malubúg ang túbig? Who stirred up the well, for the water is dirty (turbid)?
Hat, cap, head-dress; anything in the form of a hat.

Cold rice warmed up and stirred in a pan either with or without lard; to warm up rice in the manner described. Kalókalóha ang kán-on. Warm the rice and stir it in the pan. Kalókalóhi akó sing kápog. Make me a dish of "kalókálo" from cold rice. Ikalókálo akó ánay siníng báhaw. Kindly prepare me a dish of kalókálo from this cold rice.
Mercy, pity, compassion, clemency, forbearance, lenity, lenience, leniency, indulgence, pardon, sympathy, complaisance, toleration. (see lóoy).
Ditch, channel, trench, gutter.
(B) To slide, glide, slither, slip down. Nagkalóg-og siá sa bintánà. He slipped down from the window. (see alóg-og).

(H) To tuck or turn up (trousers and the like). Kalokúsa ang delárgo mo. Tuck up your trousers. Nagalakát silá nga kinalókus ang íla mga delárgo. They are walking with their trousers tucked up. Pangalókus ka, kay matabók kitá sa subâ. Tuck up (your trousers), for we are going to cross the river. (see baláking-to tuck up skirts, sotanas, and the like).
(H) Tenderness, affection, mildness, amiability, gentleness, affability, mansuetude. (lolô; see kalólot).
Any sticky, viscous juice.
See kalolô. Also: A lover, paramour.
To apply any sticky, viscous material. Ginakalólot sa ápal sang binángon ang tagók sang kamánsi. The juice of the bread-fruit is used for fastening the handle of a bolo.

(B) To compress, press together, squeeze between the hands. Angay gid nga kalomóon ni nánay ang úlo mo, kay nagsinutíl ikáw. It is quite right for mother to squeeze your head, for you have been naughty. Ginkalómò níya siá. He squeezed his head. (see kulámò).
Softness, flaccidness, flaccidity, pliability, limpness, flabbiness, floppiness, condition of wet clothes, etc. (lomó; see kahómok, kalúm-ok).
Dry, exsiccated, empty, applied particularly to pods and husks; to be or become dry. (see kagúng).
One, one piece (of dry fruit enclosed in a pod or husk). Hatági akó sing isá ka kalóng nga kamúnsil. Give me a pod of camunsel-fruit.
Dim. of kalóng. Ripe and dry (of fruit enclosed in a pod or husk).
Wart, wart-like excrescence.
To carry in one's arms. Kalongkongá ang bátà. Carry the baby in your arms. Ikalóngkong akó ánay siníng bátà. Please carry this baby in your arms. (see kúgus, kólkol).
To scratch (with the nails, claws, etc.). Kalosá siá. Scratch him. Ginsúmbag ko siá, kay kinalós níya akó. I struck him, because he had scratched me. (see karós id.).
To glide, slide, slither, slip down, as down a pole, rope and the like. Nagkalós-os siá sa lapgósan. He slid down the maypole. (see alóg-og, dalús-us).
See salók, kándus-to scoop up (out), draw water, etc.

To scratch softly (to ease an itchy feeling). Indì mo pagkalóton ang arikís mo, kay básì magadúgang. Don't scratch your rash, for it may become worse. Nagdágsang ang íya katúl, kay kinálot níya. His skin-disease "katúl" began to fester, for he scratched it. Ikálot akó ánay sang ákon likód, kay indi akó makadáb-ot. Please scratch my back for I cannot reach it.
(Sp. calzada) Road, highway, street, causeway, row, walk. (see dálan).
(Sp. calzon) Drawers, pants, underwear, short trousers.
(Sp. calzoncillo) Drawers, pants, underwear.
Freedom, independence, liberty, delivery, escape. (see luás).
A kind of rice. (see arabón).
A kind of elongated gourd, white squash.

(H) Coconut-grove, coconut-plantation; self-praise, boastful language, bragging about one's accomplishment, etc. Nagasúgid siá sang íya nga kalubihán. He is boasting of his accomplishments, etc. (see lubí, kaniogán, agrót).

To scratch in the meaning of "kálot" but with this difference that "kalúbkub" indicates a swifter motion to and fro of the hands and fingers. Kalubkubá ang ímo katúl. Scratch your itch. Kalubkubí siá. Scratch him. Ikalúbkub akó sa ákon likód. Kindly scratch me on the back. (karúbkub, id.).
Youthfulness, tenderness, softness, weakness. (see lúbud).
Turbidness, turbidity, muddiness, dirtiness, uncleanness (of liquids). (see lubúg).
A wicker-basket with lid, often used for carrying food to workmen in the fields, etc.
Fiasco, failure, frustrated efforts, baffled hopes. (see lugáw-an).
Sinking. (see kalugdángan).
Sinking, foundering, going down, submersion, drowning. (see lúgdang, kalúgdang).
To cover or enwrap oneself, put a blanket, etc., round one's body. (see kalúmbut, pangulúmbut, panimúlon).
Treason, treachery, perfidy, perfidiousness, betrayal. (see luíb, kabúdhì).
See kaluíb. Also: Treacherous deeds, treasonable proceedings, traitorous actions, cheating.
To roll up, wrap up; to gag. Kinalúkud níla siá. They gagged him. (see panimúlon, tágpò, tágpon).
Solution, act or process of solving; explanation. (see lubád).
Drowning, death by drowning. (see lumús).
Softness, pliability, plasticity, compressibility, impressibility. (lúm-ok; see kalomó, kahómok).

To swing, hang, dangle by the hands, with the feet off the ground. Ang mga amô nagakalumbítà sa sangá sang káhoy. The monkeys are hanging by their hands from the branch of the tree. Ang káhoy ginakalumbitá-an sang mga amô. The monkeys are dangling from the tree. (see kábit, kabítkábit).

(H) Cloak, coat, cover, wrapper; to cover or protect oneself against the cold, against blows and thrusts, etc., by wrapping a blanket, or the like, around one's body. Magkalúmbut ka sing hábul. Wrap a blanket around you. Ginkalúmbut níya ang hábul. He protected himself with a blanket. Ginkalumbután siá níla sing hábul. They wrapped a blanket around him. (see pangulúmbut which is more in use as a verb).
Weakness, debility, feebleness. (lumíng; see kalúya).
Lodger, guest, boarder, fellow-lodger. (see lúmon).
(H) Withering; destruction, ruin, perdition. (see lúmpag).
A kind of rice. (see arabón).
Drowning. See kalulúmsan id.
(H) Vulgarity, commonness, condition of being common, vulgar or used by many. (see lunák).
Mud, mire. (see lúnang).
Softness, compressibility, impressionableness, impressibility, plasticity, pliability; tenderness. (see lúnay).
(B) Fool, ass, idiot; foolish, half-witted, not quite normal. (see pángug, pángog).

The sinking, foundering, going down or disappearance beneath the waves of a vessel, etc.; fellow-passenger in a shipwreck. Sín-o ang áton sumaláon sang pagkalúnud sang sakayán? Who is responsible for the sinking of the boat? (see lúnud, katugdángan, katúgdang).
(B) Grounds, fields, lands. (lúpà-dútà; see kadutáan).
Ripeness, maturity, particularly applied to fruits. (lútò).
Tiredness, exhaustion, weariness, fatigue. (see lúyà).
Weakness, debility, frailty, feebleness. (see lúya).
See kalúya. Also: Things that are tiresome, exhausting or wearying.
Liking, love, fancy, leaning, partiality, relish, inclination, desire, passion. (see lúyag).
See kalúya. Also: Things that cause weakness or that are debilitating.
Weakness. See kalúya.
Companion, associate, comrade; condition of being at the side of, or near, another. (see luyó, kalúyo).
Neighbour, friend, partner. (see kaluyó, kaíping, kasilíngan).
Slowness, condition of one who loiters or jogs along slowly due ta exhaustion, natural debility, old age, etc. (see lúyò).
Pan, frying pan. (see kaláhà, karuágan, karwágan).
A little, small amount, trifle, bagatelle, insignificant, of little moment, of no importance. (see púdyot, diótay, tikî, ikî).
A kind of plant. (see talyákay id.).
See káli.
(Sp. calle) Road, way, street, causeway, walk, row. (see dálan, kalsáda).
(Sp. callo) Callus, callosity, corn, wen. (see kíbul).
Cant hook, peavy; barb, hook.
A large, thick bowl as used in Philippine households.
(Sp. cama) Bed, couch. (see higdáan, higdaanán, balatángan).
Often used instead of pagkama-for the formation of abstract nouns from ma-adjectives, e.g. kamaulínggon-concern; kamatinatápon-attention; kamaabí-abíhon-friendliness, etc. etc. (see ka-).
The felloe of a wheel, felly, curved section of the rim of a wheel.
Pygmy, dwarf, fairy, pygmean ghost; dwarfish.
(Probably from the Sp. cama) A stack, heap, pile; to stack or pile wood, etc. Kamadáha ang káhoy. Stack the wood. Ikamáda akó sináng gatóng. Please pile up that fire-wood for me.
Lightness, levity, airiness, state of being easy to lift or carry. (mág-an; see kabúg-at-heaviness.)
See kamág-an.

Novelty, newness, freshness, something new or strange noticed or experienced for the first time. Kamág-o iní sa ákon. This is new to me. (I have never seen or experienced it before). Nagmasakít siá sang íya pagabút sa Mindanáw tungúd sang kamág-o. He became sick when he arrived in Mindanao, because he was not accustomed to conditions there. (see bág-o).
See kamág-o. Also: Things that have only lately been introduced, new fashions and styles and the like. (see kalamág-ohán id.).
The string with which a spinning top (kasíng) is spun.
A hardwood tree and its timber, related to ebony; mahogany.
(H) The eldest brother or sister; the eldest (first-born) son or daughter. (see kagulángan, maguláng).
Dearness, costliness, preciousness, value, high price, exorbitant price. (mahál).
See kamahál. Also: Preciousness; dear, precious things.
See kamahál.
Friendship, friend, intimate acquaintance, attachment, mutual esteem or assistance. (Often used rather humorously instead of the Sp. amistád).
(H) Dryness, lack of moisture, aridity. (see malá, kalayâ, kalayaán).
(H) Suspense, doubt, hesitation. (see kalamalamahán).
Proportion, symmetry, harmony (of a man, clothes, a building, etc.). (see balántang).
A kind of wasp with a very painful sting. (see mangaláyo, alingáyo).
To err, mistake, misunderstand, misinterpret, misapprehend, misconceive, misconstrue. Nagkamalí siá sang íya nga nabasahán. He misunderstood what he read. ("kamalí" appears to be of Tagalog origin).
Hut, shed, hovel, granary, storehouse.
The little finger. (see kumalíngking, tingayón, tingáy-tíngay).
A kind of edible beans.
A tree whose leaves are often boiled and used as a vegetable. (see balúnggay id.).
A kind of plant similar to "kásla", but with a reddish stem and dark leaves.
Prostrate, inclined, lying down, bent towards the ground, chiefly applied to sugar cane of the second crop (kalaánan) that frequently does not grow erect as in the first crop.
Dim. of kámang. To creep, crawl, jog along.
To creep, crawl, walk on hands and feet (knees).
Hone, whetstone. (see bairán).
Magnet. (see batóbalánì).
Youngest (younger) brother or sister. (see mánghud).
See kamanghúdan id.
A kind of incense.
Openness, spaciousness; freedom to get a living and make progress. (see manháwà, kamanwaháan).
The Philippine breadfruit.
(From the Sp. manso) Tameness, gentleness, submissiveness, mildness. (see kahagúp).
A beautiful flowering plant.
A kind of Philippine dance.
A kind of grass.
Prosperity, welfare, progress, success, well-being. (see manwáhà).
See kamanhawáan id. (see manwáhà-manháwà).
Thoughtfulness, regard, consideration, sympathy, kindness. (see pasunáid).
(Sp. canapé) Sofa, settee, lounge, couch.
(Sp. cámara) Hall, chamber, house (of a legislative body). Kámara álta. Upper House. Senate. Kámara báha (Sp. baja) Lower House. House of Commons.
(Sp. cámara) The cabin of a "lorcha".
(Sp. recámara) Mortar, shooting mortar, detonator.
(Sp. camarín) Barn, shed, outhouse, storehouse, go-down.
(Sp. camarote) State-room, berth; cabin (of a steamship, etc.).
Fight, scuffle, scrimmage; any limb, as an arm, leg, tentacle, etc., used in a fight. (see kámas).

To fight using hands and feet as in wrestling or as horses when fighting, to rear up, clamber, climb a steep mountain-side using hands and feet. Ang mga kabáyo nagakamasáy. The horses are fighting each other. Kamása siá. Fight him tooth and nail, (with hands and feet). Figuratively: Maáyo ang íya kamás (kámas) sang kadiós nga ginútan ko. He is greedily eating the kadiós-peas I prepared as a vegetable dish.
To waste, squander, throw away. Dì mo pagkamasáan ang kwárta, kán-on, kinitáan, etc. Do not waste money, rice, earnings, etc.
Trustworthiness, faithfulness, strength of character, reliability. (see sálig).
(B) The last child in a family, the baby of a family; youngest brother or sister. (see kalibáynan, libáyon).
Eyes; source, beginning; centre. Ang kamát-an sang subâ. The source of the river. The central or deep channel of the river. (see matá).

Many dying at one time, great mortality, frequency of death; to die in great numbers. Ang pagkamátay-or-ang kamátay nga nagagíkan sa pamalatián--. The mortality from sickness--. Madámò ang nagkalamátay gíkan sa pamalaúd. Many died of dysentery. (see patáy).
Death, termination, end, dissolution, decease, demise. see patáy).
Tomato.
(H) Truth, verity, rightness, correctness; truthfulness, veracity, frankness, candour. (matúod).
Greed, voraciousness, passion for. (see maóg).
Fertility (of soil); plenty, galore. (see maúya).
Hand, arm; the legs of a crab, spider, etc. (see kamóy).
To beckon. Ginkamayán níya akó. He beckoned me. (see páypay).
To throw about one's arms, as in swimming. Magkámay ka, kay kon dílì masálup ka. Use your arms, or you will sink.
Dim. of kamáy. To beckon repeatedly or in quick succession; swing the arms or throw them about as in swimming. (see kapáykápay).

To encircle, wind around, entwine. Ikámbad mo sa ákon bútkon iníng tinábas. Wind this piece of cloth round my arm. Kambarí (-adí) ang bútkon ko sang bínda. Bind up my arm with the bandage. (see kámbat, kámbod, sabúd).

Variegated, motley, marked with various colours, spotted, dapple, dappled, mottled, brindled; to be or become variegated, etc. Ang tínday nagkámbang na. The calf has become spotted. (see bolók, pintókpíntok: the difference is that "kámbang" is used of variously coloured surfaces with spots of a larger size than implied by "bolók" or "pintókpíntok").
See kámbad. (see kambatí-kambarí).
To twist round the legs or feet as in wrestling, etc. Kambirí (-idí) siá. Entwine your legs around him. Ikámbid sa íya ang ímo tiíl. Twist your foot around him. (see sálbid, lákwid).

(Sp. cambio) Change, exchange, barter; to exchange, barter, swop, swap, change. Ikámbio ko iníng báka sa ímo karabáw. I will exchange this ox for your buffalo. Kambiohí iníng papél nga sínko písos sing sensílyo. Give me change for this five-peso bill. Nagkambiohánay silá sang íla mga baláy. They swopped houses. Ikámbio mo akó ánay siníng kwárta. Please give me change for this money. (see báylo).
See kámbad-to encircle, etc.
Stomach-or chest-protector, abdominal belt; cholera belt; armour, cuirass.
(Sp. cambray) Cambric; gauze, fine or transparent linen.

Unseemly, unsightly, slovenly, not well done (of sewing, etc.). Kambúsà (Nagakambúsà) ang ági siníng mákina, siníng talahían, etc. No good sewing is done with this machine,-in this tailoring shop, etc. Also: A kind of small dog with curly hair.
See kambúsà.

(From the Sp. compañía) Partner, participant, share-or stock-holder; to combine, form a partnership, company or society. Nagakambúya silá. They are partners. Ginkambuyáhan níla nga duhá ang pahunán sang íla nga negósyo. The two of them contributed the capital of their business. Kambuyáhi akó sa pangomérsyo. Form a partnership with me for a commercial enterprise. Kambúya ko siá. He is my partner. (see kumbúya).
Change, exchange. See kámbio.
(Sp. camello) Camel.
We, excluding the person addressed or spoken to. See kamihánon, kamíkámi.
Dim. of kamí. (see kamihánon).

Tap, light stroke, gentle slap; to tap, slap, strike with the finger-tips. Kamiasá ang íya ilóng. Tap his nose. Indì mo siá pagkamiasán sa íya guyá. Don't tap him on the face. (see káblit, kúhit, kámlot, kámlò, tándog, kámlas, tápdas).
We among ourselves. (see kamí).
Capsized, overturned; to turn turtle, overturn. (see túmba, sulî, balískad).
(Sp. camino-road) Road-mender, street-cleaner.
Loneliness, solitariness, dreariness, glumness, moodiness, dejection, sadness, gloom, sentimentality, melancholy, emotional feelings. (see míngaw).
See kamíngaw. Also: Things that make life lonely, sad, etc.
Loneliness, dejection, etc. See kamíngaw.
(Sp. camino) Road, way, street, causeway, walk, row. (see dálan, kalsáda).
(From the Sp. menos) Something that does not come up to expectations, a falling below the standard or requirements, anything far below what is due.
A kind of fish. See tamínsot id.

(Sp. camisa) Shirt (for women). Kamísa déntro. A shirt with long sleeves worn under a coat or near the skin. Kamísa tsína or kamísa de tsíno. A jacket or shirt-like upper garment worn by men without a coat. The kamísa tsína is made in various designs, often decorated with embroidered flowers, etc., and is frequently made of very light and transparent fabrics, as jusi, piña, etc.
(Sp. camiseta) Shirt-like blouse, spencer, short shirt, worn by men (without a coat).
(Sp. camisola) A shirt-like upper garment worn by women leaving the neck free; ruffled shirt, dicky. Also: night-shirt. (see báta).
(Sp. camisón) Long shirt, night-shirt, chiefly worn by women. (see báta).

To touch, nudge, bring one's hand in contact with. Ikámkam ang ímo kamót sa dalúnggan sang bátà. Touch the baby's ear with your hand. Kamkamá siá. Touch him. Kamkamí siá sa íya bútkon. Touch him on the arm. (see híkap, tándog, kámlot, etc.).
See kámias.

To nudge, touch momentarily. Kamloá siá. Nudge him. Kamloí siá sa kamót. Touch him on the hand. Indì mo pagkamloón ang líbro, kay básì mamansahán. Don't touch the book, for it may get soiled. (see kúhit, káblit, kámkam, etc).
(H) See kámlò. (kamlotá, kamlotí-kamloá, kamloí).
You, the plural of ikáw. (see kamókámo, kamohánon).
(B) To fight hand to hand, to grapple. Kamóga siá. Grapple him. Anó ang ginkamógan nínyo? What are you fighting about?

(B) To grasp, clutch, clench, grapple with, as in wrestling, etc. Nagakamogoláy silá. They are grappling with each other. Kamagóla siá. Grapple with him. Ginkamógol níya akó. He held me in a clench. Siá gid lang nga isá ang nagakamógol sang íya trabáho. He grapples with his work quite alone. (see kámog, gahús, gakám).
You among yourselves.
Botched, bungled, not well done or made, badly wrought; to botch, bungle, do something badly or carelessly. Dílì nínyo pagkamôkamoón ang ínyo trabáho. Don't perform your work carelessly.
Dim. of kamó. (see kamohánon).

To encircle or span around with thumb and middle-finger. Indì siá makakamól sang ákon liwatán. He cannot span my wrist with his thumb and middle-finger. Tilawí kag kamolón ang ákon bútkon kon makasaráng ikáw. Try to encircle my arm with your thumb and middle-finger, if you can. Also: A handful, as much as one can grasp with thumb and middle-finger. Hatági akó sing isá ka kamól nga humáy. Give me a handful of rice. Metaphorically: Walâ gid sing nakadimól, kay gínúrut lang níya sang kamól. Nobody had any benefit of it, because he grasped (or took) everything for himself. (see gamól).
Dim. and Freq. of kamól. Also: to settle amicably, come to terms, make an agreement. (see kapánkápan, tapáltápal).
The thumb. (see kumalagkû).
Profoundness, soundness, deepness (of sleep). (see kahamúok).
(H) The hand. (see alíma).
(Sp. camote) Sweet potato.
A plant with edible roots.
See kamotikáhoy.
The legs of a crab, spider, shrimp, etc. Nakuháan siá sing kamóy. He was deprived of his legs (i.e. he lost his support).
(Sp. campana) Bell. (see bágting, linggánay).
(Sp. campanario) Belfry, bell-tower. (see lingganáyan).
(Sp. campanilla) A small bell, altar-bell.
(Sp. campanero) Bell-man, bell-ringer; bell-founder.
A large, long kind of sword; hanger, cutlass.
(Sp. campo) Field, open ground, camp, campus. (see umá, patág, halampángan, halampangánan).

(B) To include all, embrace all, comprise all, take in all, leave out none or nothing; equipped, provided or dealt with, in an equal manner. Nagakámpod silá nga tanán sang páyong, sang kálò, etc. All of them have umbrella's, hats, etc. Ikámpod mo sa íla ang mga lápis sa látok. Distribute to them the pencils that are on the table. Kampodán mo silá sing bíntay nga mútyà. Give them all ear-rings made of pearls. Pakampodán mo silá nga tanán sing bág-o nga mga tulún-an. Procure new books for all of them. Kámpod (magkámpod) kamó nga tanán sang binángon kag maglakát. Take (all of you) your boloes and go. (see tápud, túptup).
(Sp. campeón) Champion; hero.
See kámara.
See kámlas, kámros id.
To tap, stroke, slap, etc. See kámlas.
Increase, multiplication, propagation, procreation, augmentation, production, growth, increment. (see búad, múad).

An equal, one of the same blood, condition or position; to be partners, help or stick together and never fight each other. "Nagakamúkhà silá" may mean "They are idiots or half-fools" or "They are partners and will not fight against each other". (see kaángay, kasúbung). (N.B. kamúkhà seems to be a Tagalog word).
Not quite normal, half-witted, fool, softy. (see kulángkuláng, buangít, tampuháw, etc.).
Apprehension, fear, misgiving, suspense, doubt. (see kalamalamahán, kamalamalahán, kahangáwà).
A kind of flower.
A kind of plant with very odoriferous leaves.

Beginning, start, commencement, first stage, introduction, initiation, preface. Sa kamunóan, kag (sa) katapúsan--. At the beginning, and at the end--. At any rate--. When everything is said--. Under all circumstances--. (see púnò).
A very common tree whose fruit is edible and whose wood supplies many a house with posts.
A kind of tall grass.
A creeper with beautiful leaves. It mostly climbs large trees.
(B) To lead in work, direct work and take the chief hand in it. Sín-o ang nagakamúros sa ínyo nga pangabúdlay? Who is your leading workman? Or: Who is your boss?
Living from hand to mouth, etc. See abátabát.
Destitution, poverty, misery, penury. (músmus). (see kaimolán).

(Sp. como está) How are (you)?; to greet, salute, shake hands, inquire after another's health, etc. Kamústa ka man? How do you do? How are you? Kamustahánay kitá ánay. Let us shake hands first. Nagkamústa siá sa ákon. He asked me how I was. He saluted me. He shook hands with me.
(From the Sp. mucho) Much, a large amount. Abáw, kamútso sang ímo kináon! Goodness, what an amount of food you have taken! What a lot you have eaten! (see kadámù).

To strive, exert oneself, strain every nerve, do one's best, make great efforts; to fight, wage war, join battle, enter into conflict, engage in a fight. Nagakamútut (nagakinamútut) silá sa pagdaúg. They are making great efforts to win. (see pamurúg-ot, himúd-os, paningúhà, panikasúg).
A flowering plant.
(B) Article for the dative and accusative. (see sa, kay, sang, kang).
(B) When, at what time, (always with reference to the past). (see sán-o, pa, id.).
Food, especially cooked rice. (see káon).
(B) Him, her, it; to, at, from, by, etc. him, her, it. (see íya, sa, íya).
To test, try, examine, probe. (see tiláw).
(B) Lowness, shortness in height. (nabâ; see kanobô).
(B) See kanabâ.
Shallowness, little depth. (see nábaw).
Test, trial, probe, examination, contest, competition. (see kaná).
(B) To me, etc. (see sa, ákon).
(Sp. canal) Channel, ditch, trench, conduit. Also: Verb. Kanalí ang higád sang dálan. Make a ditch at the side of the road. (see kalóg, ililigán).
A large-sized, very savoury banana.
To do quickly, thoughtlessly, absentmindedly, unawares. Nakanalî lang akó sa paghámbal sinâ. I uttered that thoughtlessly. (see tabinás, dalî).
Sweetness, deliciousness; nicety, niceness, beauty, comeliness. (námì)
Tastiness, toothsomeness, savouriness. (see námit).
See kanámit id.
A kind of rice. (see arabón).
(B) To us, etc. (see sa, ámon id.).
An exclamation of joy and pleasure: Oh, how nice! How lovely! What a beauty! This is fine! (see aráw, aráwaráw).
Flavour, tastiness, agreeableness, especially applied to nuts. (see nanám).
Softness, mildness, gentleness, condition of things done gently, quietly, noiselessly or peacefully. (see ananáy, kaananáy).
(B) To them, etc. Maágda akó kanánda ni Pédro. (--sa íla ni Pédro). I will invite Peter and his family or his friends. (see sa, íla id.).
(B) To them, etc. Itúgro iní kanánday Pédro. Give this to Peter and his family, to Peter's household. (see kánday).
To be bright, conspicuous, to shine, glisten; be dressed in bright colours. (see kánaw).
(Sp. canario) Canary (bird); yellow.
(Sp. canasto, canastro) Basket, hamper, crate, used for marketing fruits, vegetables, etc.

Slow, tedious, tardy, flagging; to be slow or tedious. Nagkánat ang ámon trábano sa umá sa karón nga túig, kay nagmasakít ang ámon mga háyup. Our farmwork has been slow this year, because our animals are sick. (see kúnat).
(B) To us, etc. See sa áton id.

To shine, glisten, sparkle; to fill, brim, become full to bursting or overflowing, cram-, chock-, full (of tears). Nagakánaw ang íya mga matá sang (sing) lúhà. Her eyes are glistening (brimming) with tears.
Dim. and Freq. of kánaw-to glisten, etc. Nagakanáwkanáw ang íya mga lúhà. His tears are ready to flow. His eyes are brimming with tears.
The north-west wind; a sea-gull.
The North-West.
To grow less, lessen, abate, relax, calm, grow calm, subside (said of wind, waves, passions, etc.). Ang mga balúd nagakánay na. The waves are now lessening.
Dim. of kánay. To blow softly or gently (of wind); to become calm, mild, gentle, good-tempered, etc. (of persons).
Great distance, farness, far away. (see nayóknáyok, nayópnáyop).
See kanáyok.
A cotton-plant with reddish or light brown flowers. (see búlak-a cotton-plant with white flowers).
(Sp. candado) Lock, padlock. (see pamakúd).
(B) To, for, towards, etc. them. (see sa, íla, kanánday, kanánda).
(Sp. candidato) Candidate, aspirant; one offering himself for an elective office. (see palapilián).
(Sp. candela) Candle, taper.
(Sp. candelero) Candlestick.
Candlestick. (see kandiléro id.).
Goat. Kánding nga laláki. Buck, goat. Kánding nga babáye. Nanny goat.
Dim. of kánding. Also: Women of loose or evil habits, concubine. (see alaasáwa, babáe).
Lean, meagre, spare, emaciated, thin. (see kalamanít, maníwang).
A kind of melon, or cucumber similar to the "atímon".
To form into lumps or balls. Ginakándol níya ang samblági. She is forming tamarind into balls. Kandolá ang tsokoláte. Make the cacao (cocoa) up into balls.

To shovel, scoop, spoon or ladle out dry and liquid things. Kandusá ang humáy, sópas, etc. Scoop out the rice, ladle out the soup, etc. Kandusí akó sing isá ka kándus nga sópas. Give me a ladleful of soup. Ikándus akó ánay sing duhá ka gántang nga humáy, kay ipíslong ko sa lusóng kag bayohón. Kindly scoop out two gantas of rice for me, because I am going to put it into the mortar and pound it. (see sarók, galó).
(Sp. canela) Cinnamon.
(B) See sang id.

(B) To engage, hire, invite, usually with the promise of pay. Ginakángay si Fuláno, ang músika, ang manugsírko, etc. N.N., the band, the circus-man, etc., are being invited (or engaged). Kinangáyan níla ang pándut sing orkésta. They hired an orchestra for the feastday. Ikángay akó ánay sang orkésta sa Miagáw. Please engage for me the Miagao orchestra. Kangáya ang kosinéro ni Fuláno sa áton tábad. Engage N.N.'s cook for our banquet. (see ágda, hágad).
Wagon, cart, with or without a roof and usually provided with wooden wheels. (see káro).
Driver of a wagon or bull-cart, waggoner, carter. (kángga).
(B) Mercy, compassion, sympathy, clemency. (see kaló-oy, kaáwà).
Terror, horror, frightfulness; terrible, horrible, frightful, awful, shocking. (see ngídlis).
Nausea, loathing, detestation, abomination, shrinking from, sickening at. (see ngíl-ad).

(H) See kangíl-ad. Also: Things that are loathsome, sickening, noisome, abominable, detestable, nauseating, nasty, filthy, shocking to look upon or to hear of, the abomination or aversion produced by evil or by things of a very disagreeable smell. (see kalangil-arán).
Regret, sorrow, unwillingness to part with, a pining for lost or absent things. (see ngílin, kahílak).
Setting one's teeth on edge. (see ngílo).
(B) See kanghír-o.
Heartache, desolation, compunction, sorrow, pain, darkness, distress. (ngítngit).
See kangítngit. Also: Things that cause heartache, etc.
See kalángkang. Kangkangá ang kamót mo. Spread out your fingers.
(Sp. cangrena) Gangrene, mortification. (see dágsang).
(Sp. canguro) Kangaroo.
Surprise, shock, etc. See kahanguyús, kuyús.
(B) You, to you, etc. See sa ímo, id.
A dribbling, trickling, oozing, sending forth of a small stream. (see ninít).
(B) You, to you, etc. See sa ínyo, id.
(B) Coconut-grove, coconut-plantation. (nióg; see kalubihán).
Nípà-swamp, nípà-plantation. (see nípà).
Thinness of a sheet, board, paper or the like. (nipís; see kadámol-thickness).
See kanipís.
(H) Roundness, spherical shape, sphericity, rotundity, circularity. (tipólon; see katipólon).
Small, dwarfish, undersized, stunted in growth. (see koridíg, daúldaúl, aríarí, agílagíl).
A kind of small-leaved "búyò" used for betel-nut chewing.

Lean, gaunt, thin, spare, emaciated; to be or become lean, etc. Nagkanít siá, kay nagmasakít. He got lean, because he was sick. Pakán-a siá sing maáyo, índì mo siá pagpakanitón. Feed him well, don't allow him to become thin. (see níwang, kalamanít, kandínggal).
Leanness, thinness, spareness, skinniness, emaciation, gauntness. (see níwang, kakanít).
See kaníwang.
