To do, spend, eat, etc., to one's heart's content, because there is so much (to do, spend, eat, etc.). Ginkankanán gid lang níla ang mga pagkáon. They ate to their heart's content. (see patúyang, pasamíyang, údak, pagústo).
(B) They say, it is said, rumour has it, it is reported, etc. See konó, id.

To be or sound hollow, empty, loose, shrivelled, shrunk, said of the contents of bottles, tins, nuts, shells, etc. Iníng ítlog, lubí, etc. nagakanô. This egg, coconut, etc. sounds hollow. Also: dull, foolish, doltish, stupid. (see búngkag, búngaw, pákok, etc.).
To get yarn or thread ready for weaving. Nagakáno siá sang háblon. She is getting the yarn ready for weaving.
Contr. of Amerikáno-American.
(H) Lowness, of little height, shortness. (nobô; see kanabâ, id.).
(H) See kanobô.
An exclamation expressive of regret for something lost or spoilt. A, kanógon inâ! Oh, that's a pity! What a pity!
To fray and break easily, said of threads and yarn in clothes, etc. Nagakanótnot gid lang ang báyò ko. My jacket is just fraying away. (see nátnat, nútnut, tâtâ, sarabusáb).
A kind of tree whose reddish seeds are used for medicinal purposes.
Dry leaves of the sugarcane.
(Sp. cancel) Screen, (upright frame). (see biómbo).

(Sp. canción) A song, lay, ballad, ditty; to sing, to troll. Kansyoná ang "Adiós". Sing the song "Adiós!". Kansyoní akó sing bilyansíko. Sing me a Christmas carol. (see ambahánon, ambáhan, ámba, kalantáhon, kánta).
(Sp. cantar) To sing, troll, chant, warble. Kantahí kamí sing isá ka matahúm nga kalantáhon. Sing us a nice song. Kantahá iní. Sing this. (see kansyón).
Diaphragm, midriff.
(Sp. cantero) Mason, stone-cutter, stone-dresser, bricklayer, builder in stone and brick.
Dog-vane, weather-cock; to call-, summon-, invite-, the wind (at sea, at winnowing rice, etc.).
(Sp. cantidad) Quantity, amount, sum. (see pilá, kapíd-an).
(Sp. cantil) A steep, precipitous rock. (see píl-as).
(Sp. canto) Edge, rim, brim, corner, margin, bevel, cant. (see binít, hamitán, bígki).
(Sp. canto) Song, hymn, chant. (see ambahánon, kalantáhon, kansyón).
Yarn. (see bunáng).
Cantonese, pertaining to-, made in-, from-Canton in China, applied to a variety of textiles, silk-fabrics, poultry, etc., coming from China, especially from Canton.
Singer, cantor, chorister, choir-boy, especially one who sings in church. (see manugámba from ámba).
(Sp. cantora) A female singer, cantor, especially one who sings in Church.
Repentance, contrition, compunction, sorrow for past mistakes or for wrongs committed. (see núlsul, hinúlsul).
Sixty. (see ánum).
A kind of bird.
Friend, intimate, companion; friendly, affectionate, sociable. Kanúnay nga hángin. A favourable, steady breeze. (see kahírup, mahírup, maabiabíhon).
Often, continual, frequent. (This seems to be a Cebuano term; see masamí, masúnsun, himánhimán, imánimán).
(Sp. cáñamo) Jute, hemp; jute-cloth, sail-cloth, hemp-cloth.

(Sp. cañon) Cannon, gun, field-piece; cannon-ball; the benches in a prominent part of the Church for the accommodation of the Authorities and principal Catholics are also called "kanyón" in some places. Also: Ravine, gorge, canyon.
(Sp. cañuto) A small pipe or tube, as the tube through which the wick passes in a lamp.
Midday, noon. (see ódto).
The end, last things, latter happenings, final outcome. (olíhi; see katapúsan).
(H) Tardiness, lateness. (olíhi; see kaatrasádo, kahudyánan).
(H) See kaolihánan.
Young men, bachelors, youth. (olitáo).

To eat, take food, feed, fare, devour, despatch, mess. Kán-a iní. Eat this. Kán-i iní sing diótay. Eat a little of this. Pakán-a siá sing maáyo. Feed him well-or-Give him good food. Pakán-a siá sa pínggan. Let him eat off the plate. Pakán-i sa íya iníng mga páhò. Let him eat some of these mangoes. Indì ka magkáon siníng búnga, kay línghod pa. Don't eat this fruit, for it is not ripe yet. Anó ang kináon mo? What kind of food did you take? Ipakáon ko sa íya iníng kabúgaw kon makaúyon siá. I will let him eat this pomelo if he likes it. Walâ akó makatupús sang ginpakáon níya sa ákon. I could not stand the food he gave me. Iníng kalán-an ginakán-an sing duhá ka púlò ka táo sa tágsa ka ádlaw. Twenty men take their meals-, mess-, are fed-, in this dining room every day.
Hour, time. (see táknà, óras, orasón).

To stick or adhere to; to paste, smear, put on powder, etc. Nagapakáp-al silá sing pólbos sa íla nawóng. They are powdering their faces. Nagakáp-al ang pólbos sa íya nawóng. Her face is thickly covered with powder. (see ápol, kápol, pilít, pálhit).
(Sp. capa) Mantle, large cloak; cope used at religious functions.

To cover as with a mantle; to grasp, seize, take possession of, appropriate. Daw buút níya kapahán ang tanán nga mánggad sa kalibútan. It seems as if he would like to seize all the wealth of the world. Ginkapahán níya ang tanán nga pílak nga nagsulúd. He appropriated all the money that came in. (see karipón, ángkon).

To droop, hang down, be full of-, covered with-, laden with-, weighed down with-, fruit, be enshrouded as with a mantle. Nagakápà ang mga sangá siníng káhoy. The branches of this tree are weighed down, (being covered with fruit as with a mantle). Nagakápà gid lang sang búnga iníng páhò. This mango-tree is covered with and bending under the weight of its fruit. (see gápà).
See kapa-ít. Also: Things that are bitter or difficult to bear, crosses, trials, hardships, sufferings. (see kalisdánan, kalalát-an, kapipít-an, kalilísdan, kahil-ánan).
Dim. of kápa. Also: To slap the water with the hands as in swimming, flap the wings, throw about one's hands and the like. (see kapáykápay).

To perish, disappear. Nagakapáas na ang mga talonón sa talónan. The wild pigs are disappearing from the forests. Tungúd sang madámù nga mga mangangáyam nagkapáas na ang talonón sa sinâ nga búkid. On account of the great number of hunters the wild pigs have now ceased to exist on that mountain. (see pápas, púas, pánas).
Firmness, security, durability, stability, state of not being shaken easily. (see pág-on).
See kapág-on. Also: Things that are stable or give stability.
Corals, coral reef. (see pagáng).
Strength, robustness, vigour, health. (see págrus).
Swiftness of movement, speediness, quickness, nimbleness, etc. (see kalígsi, págsi-lígsi). Also: activity, energy, agility, etc. (see kaábtik).
Low or mean station (position); low estimate, contempt, contemptibility, despicableness. (see hámak, pahámak).
Rest, repose, quiet, peace. (see pahúay).
See kapahuáyan.
Competitor, rival, contestant. (see paindísíndis).
Bitterness. (pa-ít).
Slowness; dulness. (pákok).
Slowness; dulness, stupidity, ignorance. (see pákok).
See kapákok, kapakokán.
Fate, chance, fortune, luck, happiness, blessedness. Maáyo nga kapaláran. Good luck. Maláut nga kapaláran. Bad luck. (see pálad, sukúd, swérte).
The closing or healing of a wound, etc. (see pinalían-the mark of a healed wound or ulcer, scar, cicatrix). (see pálì).
(Sp. capa magna) Prelate's mantle, called Capa Magna, a dignitary's long gown.

To overflow, swamp, cover, pass over. Ang subâ nagkápan sang ámon umá. The river overflowed our farm-land. Ang pángpang nakapánan sang túbig. The banks were covered with water. Ginkápan sang mga balúd ang sakayán. The waves passed over the boat-or-The boat was swamped by the waves.
A wiping-, rubbing-, out, erasure, deletion, abolishment, destruction, disappearance. (see pánas).
(H) Clouds. (ánod; see pangánod, gál-um).
Of the same skin or color or complexion. Kapánit ko siá. He is of the same complexion as myself. Ang íya mga kapánit. Those of his race. (see pánit).

Dim. and Freq. of kápan. Also: To be about equal, be a draw, be quits, square, neither winning nor losing; to settle in peace, make mutual concessions, square or settle accounts, smooth differences. Kinapánkápan lang kamí. We were about equal, (none of us won or lost). (see pátas).
Noise, uproar. (see kagánsal, gáhud).
Smell of urin. (pánsot).
Tranquillity, repose, peacefulness, stability. Walâ gid sing kapantagán ang ámon pangabúhì. Our life has no peace. We can never rest at ease. (see pántag).
Application, industry, assiduity, diligence, zeal. (see pántok).

Army, large crowds or numbers, hosts, great multitude assembled, throng; shoal (of fish); herds (of sheep, cattle, etc.); numerous army (of soldiers); any great assembly or collection of things or persons. (see panóng).
Great-grandfathers; forefathers, forebears, progenitors, ancestors. (see pápò).
The priesthood (in the concrete, priests, clerics). (see párì).
(Sp. capaz) Capable, ingenious, clever, learned, fit, suitable. (see makaákò, batíd, sagád, sámpaton, may-igkasángkol, -ikasárang, -ikatakús).
Failure, setback, drawback, fiasco, disappointment, want of success. (see páslaw).
Punctuality, fixedness, fixity, stability; certainty, sureness, exactness, preciseness. (see pát-ud).
Plain, campus, wide valley or open country. (see pátag, patág).
Forty. (see ápat).
(Sp. capatáz) Foreman, one who has charge of a gang of workmen on a road, a farm, etc.
Forgiveness, remission, pardon, amnesty, absolution, acquittal, acquittance. (see patáwad).
Friend, chum, "pal". (see atíd, akíd, idól, kahírup, ábyan).
Strength, firmness, determination. (see pátol, kabákud, kahúnlit, kahúnit).
Fatigue, tiredness, weariness. (see pául, kahiól, kaálay, kabúdlay).
Light, illumination, luminosity, gleam, glow, brightness. Ang kapáwà sang ádlaw. The light or brightness of the sun. Ang kapáwà sang Pagtóo. The light of Faith. (see páwà, kasánag, íwag,
(B) Blanket; to use a blanket, cover with a blanket, to blanket. Kapáyi siá. Put a blanket on him. Pakapáyi siá. Have him covered with a blanket-or-Provide him with a blanket. (hábul).
Fin (of fish). (see sílik, sírik).
The wing of a bird. (see pákpak).

To flutter, flop, slap, clap, flap the wings, strike the water with the palms of the hands as in swimming, to swing or vibrate (said of anything with a broad surface). Nagakapáykápay lang ang píspis sa hángin. The bird is flapping its wings in the air. (see kapákápa).
Youthfulness; childishness, silliness, foolishness. (see payâ, kaalangón).
The papaw and its fruit. (see papáyas).
(Sp. café) Coffee.
(Sp. cafetéra) Coffee-pot.
Twin, twins, (said of men, animals, plants and things in general); grown together, joined side to side, double. (see dungán).
Number, quantity, amount, an undetermined aggregate of individuals, that may be either few or many. (see pilá-how many).
Fastidiousness, daintiness, overniceness, squeamishness (particularly with regard to food). (see pidâ).
Frailty, feebleness, debility. (see pígaw).
Half, one half, moiety. Kapíhak siá sang ákon tagiposóon. He is (forms) one half of my heart; i.e. I am very much attached to him. I love him very much. (see píhak, pihák, tungâ).
Tightness, closeness. (see pikít).
Tiredness, exhaustion, stiffness of limbs. (see píl-ay, kaálay, kapául).
Fastidiousness, squeamishness, condition of one who is difficult to please. (see pílì, kapíslì).
Compulsion; to be compelled or forced. Nagkapilitán siá sa-. He was compelled (forced) to--. (see pílit).
(Sp. capilla) Chapel, small church, village chapel. (see ermíta).
Condition of one who is "pílyo", mischievousness, naughtiness, shrewdness, roguishness, artfulness, tricksiness, cunning, cheating. (see kalág-it, kasutíl).

More, over, above; to be more etc. Kapín kon kúlang--. More or less, about, nearly, approximately--. Kapín pa--. Moreover, besides, especially yet--. Magakapín áyhan ang bilí sa napúlò ka mángmang, índì gid magkúlang. The price will probably exceed (or be over) ten pesos, certainly not less. Kapín sa duhá ka líbo ka táo ang nagtalámbong-or-Duhá ka líbo ka táo kapín ang nagtalámbong. More than two thousand men took part or attended.
Cruelty, harshness, brutality, inhumanity, truculence, ferocity. (see píntas).
Pressure, strait, strictness, condition of being squeezed into a tight corner. (see píot).
See kapíot, kapipít-an.
See kapíot. Also: Crosses, troubles, difficulties, trials, straits. (see kalilísdan, kalisdánan, kalalát-an, kapa-itán).
Diligence, application, activity, industry, assiduity, laboriousness, energy, zeal. (see písan, kaúkud, kapántok, kabákas, katándus).
See kapísan.
Fastidiousness, overniceness, over-indulgence; wastefulness, prodigality. (see píslì, kapidâ, kabuhahâ).
Birds. (see píspis).
(Sp. capital) Capital, chief or principal town; capital, principal, money invested or set apart for an enterprise. (see úlo-bánwa, pahunán, prinsipál).
(Sp. capitán) Captain; mayor, burgomaster, municipal president (in Spanish times).
Completeness, totality, extreme point, climax, height of, midst of (distress, darkness, etc.); utter, consummate, absolute, complete. (see pitípit).
See kapílya.
To feel one's way, grope. (see híkam, etc.).
To twist or twine round, encircle, entwine, cling to (as ivy). (see kalápkap).
Poverty, penury, misery, impecuniousness, pauperism. (see póbre, kaimolón).
(B) Cold cooked rice. May kápog kamó sa baláy? Have you any cold rice in the house? (see báhaw).
Stumpiness, stockiness, condition of being thick-set. (see póktol).

Plaster; to plaster, cover with a plaster, mend, repair, seal or stop leakages or small holes with thick paint, mortar, cement, etc. Kapóli sing pínta ang mga úlo sang mga lánsang sa atóp nga sin. Cover the nail-heads on the zinc-roof with paint. Sín-o ang nagkápol sang tohók sang alhíbi? Who plastered up the hole in the water tank? Ipilák na lang iníng pínggan, kay índì na makapólan ang íya sirâ nga balanâ. Throw this plate away, for it is so cracked that it cannot be mended. (see pálhit, ápol).
Dim. and Freq. of kápol. Also: to patch, mend, repair, make things up, settle amicably or peacefully. (see kapánkápan, tapántápan).
To crumble, fall to pieces, said of clods of earth, or the like. Nagakapólpog ang pugá. The clod of earth is crumbling. (see pólpog).

(Sp. capón) Capon, gelding, any castrated animal, but particularly applied to cocks, pigs and dogs; to emasculate, castrate. Ginkapón níla ang mga báboy nga palatambókon kag ilihawón. They castrated the pigs that are to be fattened and slaughtered. Kaponá ang idô. Castrate the dog. Nakabakál akó sing tátlo ka manók nga kinapón. I succeeded in buying three capons.

The marriage ceremony; the bride and bridegroom giving their mutual consent and pledging conjugal fidelity and immediately after joining hands, before the priest who solemnizes their marriage. Bagtingán mo silá sa kápot. Ring the bells when they clasp hands. Nagpakápot lang silá, ápang walâ pagbilóhi. They went through the marriage ceremony, but did not receive the nuptial blessing during the Holy Mass.
To stick or adhere to, paste, glue. (see dokót, pilít).
(Sp. capote) Overcoat, raincoat, mackintosh, macintosh. (see kúmbut, kúnup, kulámbot).

Select tobacco leaves used as wrappers for cigars. Dálhi akó sing maáyo nga dáhon sang tabákò, kay ikapóte ko sa ákon piokós. Bring me a choice tobacco leaf, for I am going to use it as a wrapper for my home-made cigar.
Tired, exhausted, weak, worn out, done up, fatigued, weary, knocked up, jaded, spent. Kapóy na siá. He is tired out. (see paúl, luyâ).

To tire, fatigue, weary, knock up, wear out, exhaust, weaken. Nakápoy (kinápoy) siá. He was exhausted (tired). Ginakápoy (ginakapóyan) akó. I am getting tired. Ang amó nga pagpangabúdlay nagpakápoy sa íya. That drudgery wore him out, knocked him up. (see lúya, lúyà, pául, álay, búdlay).
(Sp. cafre) A ghost or monstrous being alleged by the superstitious to take the form of a horrible giant.
(Sp. capricho) Caprice, whim, fancy, fad, craze, quirk, crotchet. (see luyáglúyag, lubá).
(Sp. cápsula) Capsule; metal cap on a bottle or the like.
From kapút-to grasp, take hold of, etc.
Cold (cooked) rice. See kápog.
Redness, reddishness, rosiness. (see pulá, mapulá).
Exhaustion, inanition, frailty, feebleness, faint. (see púnaw).
Isolation, loneliness, solitariness, desolation, dreariness, dejectedness. (see púng-aw, kamíngaw, kasím-ong).
Nations, powers, states, governments. Ang mga kapungsurán sang kalibútan. The nations of the world. Ang katilíngban sang mga kapungsurán. The league (society) of Nations. (see púngsud).
Archipelago, island-group. (pulô). Ang Kapupúd-an nga Pilipínas. The Philippine Islands.
Islands, isles, archipelago. (see pulô, kapupúd-an).
Fulness, plenitude; abundance, plenty, affluence. (see punô).
Dearth, misery, stress, hard lines, difficulty. Ang kapuráut sang pangabúhì. The difficulties of life. (see hiwáos, kalisúd).
Anger, excitement, exasperation expressed in strong language. (see púsa, pamúsa).

Profit, utility, use, gain, avail, benefit, good, advantage, behoof, boot. Ang tanán náton nga mga paninguhâ manginwaláy kapuslánan, kon walâ kitâ pagabulígi sang Diós. All our efforts are in vain-or-of no avail, unless God assists us. (see pulús).

To grip, grasp, seize, clasp, grab, get-, lay-, catch-, take-, hold of. Kápti iní. Take hold of this-or-Grasp it. Kináptan níya akó sa kamót. He took me by the hand. Ginkáptan níya ang tulún-an kag ginlámba sa salúg. He seized the book and threw it on the floor. Buót silá magkapút sang uluyatán sang kaláhà. They like to hold the handle of the pan (i.e. wish to have power, influence and especially a large share in the division of the spoils). (see kápyot).
Condition of being a prostitute. (see púta).
Whiteness, fairness, blondness. (see putî).
The white race, the whites, Caucasians. (see putî).
Bankruptcy, liquidation, failure, insolvency. (see púto).
A kind of maize with black and white kernels mixed on the same cob.
Irritability, fretfulness, hotness (of temper); narrowmindedness. (see putóng).
Sleepiness, drowsiness, tiredness; condition of one who sleeps long,-awakes or rises late. (see púyat).
To grip, grasp. See kapút. Kapyotí, kinapyotán-kápti, kináptan. (see úyat).
(B) See karón.
(B) Of that, etc. (see sinâ id.).
(B) See kála. Also: A kind of hard stone variously coloured.

(B) To scold loudly, abuse in strong language, shout at, rail at. Karái siá. Give him a good scolding. Ginkaráan níya kamí. He shouted and railed at us. Dílì ka magságad pangárà. Don't be always scolding so loudly. (see ákig, pamúsa, pamúrag, pamulúgso).
(Sp. cara) Head, face. (see úlo, nawóng).
A hustler, driver, one who urges or impels others; to hustle, hurry, be very energetic, work with despatch, do something-quickly,-carelessly,-thoughtlessly. (see tarátará, tarágtarág, garógaró).
To come and go, visit frequently, go to and fro. (see karâ).

(H) To go there, denoting a shorter distance than when "kádto" is used. Kumarâ ka dirâ. Go over there. Indì pa akó makadalikát sa pagkarâ dirâ sa ínyo. I cannot go away at once to visit you there. (see kádto).

To burn lustily, crackle and spread (of fire). Ang kaláyo nagakarábkárab. The fire is burning lustily, is spreading, is increasing (with a crackling sound). Agólagól (kirótkírot) gid lang iníng kaláyo; butangí sing paámak, agúd magkarábkárab. This fire is burning low; put some kindling on it, that it may burn bright.
Common or joint property. (see guráptan, garapátan).
Buffalo.
(B) See kalabó-tastefulness, etc.
(B) Long ago, in olden times, once upon a time, a long time since, in the past, of yore. A, inâ sa karádto pa! Oh, that was in the good old times! Karádto ánay--. Formerly--. (see sádto).
To run-, rush-, push-, against something with some impetuosity. Karagmangá ang nagakatulúg. Run and shake the one who is asleep. (see kurágmang which is the more usual form).
(B) See karádto.
(B) See kaláhà-pan, etc. (see karuágan).
To take another's "hand", or cards, or place, in card-playing; one who temporarily takes another's place at the card-table.
(B) See kalahílo.
(B) Repairs, etc. See kilidanón, kaalayohón.
(B) Multitude, etc. See karakoán.
(B) Badly done, botched, bungled, clumsy, desultory, careless work. (see bástos, bául, patarásak).
To be a loafer, roam about, idle away the time, etc. See lagáwlágaw, landólándo, tiyógtiyóg, taratalánda.
Uneasy, nervous, excited; to be excited, nervous, etc. See darabáhan.
To rustle (of dry leaves, starched clothes, etc.); to jerk, jump, make a sudden movement, be in a hurry. (see kólas, líktin, kuratán).
(B) See kalakatád.
To cluck (of a hen). (see kurukutúk, katákkaták).
A kind of banana. (see lakatán).
(B) Many, plenty, multitude, much. (see rakô, dakû, kadakû).
(B) Multitude, great number, many, plenty, crowd. Ginpakahúy-an akó níya sa karakoán (karák-an). He put me to shame in public. (see rakô).
(B) See kalalót.

(Sp. carambola) A carom shot at billards, a carambole, a cannon; quarrel; to quarrel. May karambóla kaína sa bulangán. Nagkinarambóla silá kaína sa bulangán. A short while ago there was a quarrel (row, fight, scuffle) in the cockpit. (see áway, súay, gamô).
(Sp. caramelo) Caramel, unrefined sugar, usually of a brown colour and sold in square tablets that readily dissolve in water, etc.

To scuffle, scramble, fight, to compete eagerly for the possession of something. Nagakaramútot silá sa pagágaw sang mga bukáka-or-ginakaramutótan níla ang pagágaw sang mga bukáka. They are scrambling for the ripe camunsel-fruit. Indì kamó magkaramútot. Don't scuffle (scramble, fight). (see ális, árnis, áway, kámas).
To be in a stir, excitement or hubbub on account of a fire, a sudden inundation or the like. Nagakinaránkáran silá. They are in a state of great excitement.
(B) To perform with despatch, expedite, do quickly and hence carelessly. Karandahá lang ang panápton. Be quick with the clothes (in dressing, washing, etc.). (see dalî).
Restless, fidgety, unsteady. (see matínong-steady).
See kadapâ, kurapâ.

To hang down, fall down loosely (of clothes that are too large, etc.). Nagakarápà lang ang íya bistído. Her dress falls down loosely (like a mantle-kápa), being too long and too wide, etc. (see kápa, kápà).
See kalapól.
(B) Taste, etc. See kalalím.
(B) See kalalóton, kalalotón.
To tear-, scratch-, pull-, off quickly vines, creepers, an old thatched roof or the like; to tear the ground (of a galloping horse); to perform with despatch, do quickly. (see káskas).
(H) Pungency, etc. See kádat, ádat id.).
To be in a hurry, have to do quickly; to hasten, urge. Ginakarát akó sa pagpaúlì. I am in a hurry to go home. (see alipasá, kalít, dalikát, dalî).
One who is in a hurry, who "sits on needles", etc. (see kuratán).
(Sp. carretel) Spool, reel; rope-walk reel, rope-maker's twisting machine, rope-wheel, cable-wheel; to twist, make ropes. (see lúbid).
To punish severely, chastise. Ginkaratíl níya ang íya bátà, kay nagsinutíl. She punished her child severely, because it was very naughty. (see baká-báka, tarítári, kátad).
Dim. and Freq. of karát. (see kurátkurát).
(Sp. carátula) Pasteboard, label, sign-board, advertisement.
Tortuous-, winding-, zigzag-, movement, twist, contortion, convolution; to crawl, creep, twist, contort, writhe, move along, as snakes, or the like. (see isíísi, tikô).
A kind of bird.
(B) Deviation, digression, winding, turning aside, going out of one's way (of speech, walking, etc.). (see ráwit).
(B) Hook. (see kalawít).
Dry coconut leaves. (see lukáy).

To scratch and scatter (rice, corn, etc. as chickens, rats, etc. do); to bring into disorder, disarrange by trampling upon, by shuffling or stirring levelled off grains, peas and beans, sand or the like. Ginakaráykay sang mungâ ang humáy. The hen is scratching in the rice, scattering it with her claws. Indì mo pagkaraykayón ang humáy. Don't stir the rice.
(B) Buffalo. (karabáw id.).
Pertaining to a buffalo; like a buffalo. (see kinarabáw).
(Sp. carbón) Coal; papel de carbón-carbon paper.
Restaurant, eating-house; a small shop. (see karihán, tiénda, tiánggi, talangwáyan, pansiteríya).
(Sp. carrera) Career, profession; run, race; to race. Nagakaréra na ang mga kabáyo. The horses are racing, (are off), already. (see palangitánan, kabuhián, palúmbà).
(Sp. carretela) Cart, bus, two-wheeled vehicle for passengers and freight.
(Sp. carreton) Wagon, cart, go-cart; wheel. Butangí sing karetón ang sibáy. Put wheels (or rollers) on the baby's chair.

(Sp. carga, cargar) Burden, load; to load, burden; to transfer, enter. Iníng kárga lakás kabúg-at sa ákon. This burden is too heavy for me. Ikárga iní sa ímo áwto. Put this in your auto. Ikárga akó ánay siní sa ímo karósa. Please put this on your cart. Pilá ang hinákay kon kargahán ko ang ímo káro sing napúlò ka pásong nga humáy? How much will the freight be, if I put ten bushels of rice on your cart? Ikárga sa libro ináng mga binunyagán. Transfer to the register the names of those baptized. Dílì mo siá pagkargahán sináng sáko, kay támà kabúg-at sa íya. Don't burden him with that sack, for it is much too heavy for him. Nalúnud ang sakayán, kay kinargahán sing támà. The boat sank, because it was overloaded. (see lúlan).
(Sp. carga, burro) A game at cards.
(Sp. cargador) Porter, carrier.
(Sp. cargamento) Luggage, baggage, goods, load, freight, merchandise, cargo.
(Sp. cargo) Office, duty, responsibility, charge; income, receipts. Kárgo y dáta. Receipts and expenditure.

(H) To come here, approach. Karí ka dirí-or-Kumarí ka. Come here. Walâ pa siá makakarí, or: makapakarí. He hasn't been able to come here yet. Pakariá siá sa madalî. Order him to come here at once. Indì siá saráng makakarí-or-makapakarí. He is unable to come here.
A kind of dish. (see karihán).
Of that, etc. See sinâ, kará, id.
One who steps into-, walks into-, interferes with-, meddles in-, something carelessly or thoughtlessly; to be careless, etc. (see tarádag, túdag, tádag, lúdag).
Revolution, upheaval, violent change (of government, etc.), war, strife, commotion. (see ribók).
Short and stout, stocky, stumpy, stubby, thickset. (see kiribúd, tipúngkò, búdul, pudól, karibudó).
(B) See karibúd.
(B) Sultriness, stuffiness, mugginess, closeness (of heat or weather). (see kagín-ot, kabóhot).
Inn, restaurant, rest-house. Place where "karí" is made or sold. (see karí).
(B) See kalíkad-to stir or loosen up rice, earth, etc.
(Sp. caricatura) Caricature.
Intricacy, complication, complexity. (see rikót).
(Sp. carril) Rail-rut, rail, cart-way, furrow.
(B) Sweetness. See katám-is. (see rímis).
A kind of banana. (see kúndal, túndal, térna).

(B) Small, little, tiny things, tots. Pulús mga karintukáy ang mga nagaeskwéla sa ákon kláse sang toksóan. The children that come to my catechism-class are all very small. (see íntok, magágmay, magágming).

To gather, collect, bring together, join or associate with, mingle, mix, put together. Indì mo pagkariponón ang mga kabatáan nga magamáy kag dalágkù. Don't put the small children together with the big ones. Ginkaripón níla ang mga báka kag karabáw. They put the cows with the buffalloes. Kariponá silá nga tanán. Put them all together. (see símpon, dápon, upúd, abáy).
Dirt, filth, stain. (see rísmò, kahígkò).
A kind of plant.
Stunted, backward, kept back in growth. (see aríarí, agíl-agíl, daúldaúl).
(Sp. carrillo) A small cart; toy-cart.
A small lobster. (see koritót, kiritót).
(Sp.) Carmel; Carmelite nuns; Carmelite monks.
(Sp. carmen) Carmelite order; scapular, scapulary. (see eskapuláryo).
(Sp. carnaval) Carnival.
(Sp. carne) Flesh; meat. (see kusúg, unúd).
(Sp. carnero) Sheep; mutton. Karnéro nga babáe. Ewe, a female sheep. Karnéro nga laláki. Ram, a male sheep.
(Sp. carro) Cart, wagon, wain.
Dim. of káro. A child's toy-cart.

To do something with great speed, to scamp work, perform in a hurry; hasty, careless (of work). Karó-karó nga pagtrabáho. Careless, hasty work. Indì kamó magkarókaró sa pagóbra sinâ. Don't scamp that work-or-Don't be hasty and careless in doing that. (see karógkárog, karótkot).
To rub or scratch with some force. Karobkobá ang batíis mo kon magkatúl. Rub the calf of your leg if it itches. (see kalúbkub id.).
To rub, rasp, scratch (one's hair, head, etc.); to scrape, scoop out, shell (coconuts, gourds, etc.). (see kódkod, kokód).
(B) To hurry, hustle, urge on. Karóga tána nga magpánaw ron. (padaliá siá sa paglakát). Urge him to go quickly.
A hustler. (see karóg-károg).
To do with great despatch, perform quickly, hurry. Karóg-karóga ang ímo trabáho. Hurry on with your work, (be quick about it). (see karókaró).
A wide-meshed basket, usually hung up on a wire or string and used for carrying various provisions.
See kalókos.
To rumple, tousle, tumble, jumble, put-, throw-, bring-, in disorder; rumpled, jumbled, complicated. Indì mo pagkarókosohón ang lánot. Do not tumble the hemp-fibers. (see gómon, gomón, korokosó).
(Sp. carromata) A two-wheeled vehicle, bus.

(H) Now, at present, at the present-time,-day,-moment,-juncture,-occasion, presently, immediately, shortly, forthwith, anon, nowadays; before long, soon; adj.: present, current. Lakát kitá karón. Let us go now. Mapailóngílong akó karón. I am going to Iloilo soon. Sa súbung siní walâ akó sing tinión, ápang karón ugáling tatápon ko ang ímo kinahánglan. Just at present I have no time, but before long I will attend to your need. Sa karón nga mga tinúig--. At the present time, in the times we are living in--. Ang karón nga túig. The present or current year.

To scratch, claw. Indì mo siá pagkarosón. Don't scratch him. Ang kinarosán sang kuríng sa bátà nagdugô. The scratch made by the cat on the baby was bleeding. Ang mga kuríng nagakarosánay. The cats are fighting (are clawing or scratching at each other). (see kalós).
(Sp. carroza) Cart; sledge, sled, as used by farmers over rough road.

To scratch (one's head or the like). Ginkaróskos níya ang íya úlo sa kaákig, sa kabúlung, etc. He scratched his head in anger, in astonishment, etc. Dílì mo pagkaroskosón ang úlo mo. Don't scratch your head. (see kalós, karós).
To rub, stroke, scratch. (see kálot).

To scratch or rub against a door (as cats and dogs do); to scamp work, perform carelessly, hurry, hustle, do something by tearing and pulling, by leaps and bounds. Ang idô nagakarótkot sang ganháan, kay malúyag siá magsulúd. The dog is scratching at the door, for he wants to come in.
To starch yarn or thread previous to weaving. Karoyí ang bunáng. Starch the yarn. Bunáng nga kinaroyán. Starched yarn.
(Sp. cárcel) Prison, jail; to imprison, confine. Karsilá siá. Put him in prison. (see bilánggò, pahúnong, bilanggóan, kalabóso, kalabús).
(Sp. cartera) Portfolio, writing case, pocket book, note book, letter case.
(Sp. cartero) Letter-carrier, postman, one who carries or distributes letters.
(Sp. cartilla) Primer, first book for children. (see katón).

(Sp. carton) Card-board, paste-board; paste-board cards as used in various games. Malúyag akó maghámpang sang lóte, ápang walâ akó sing kartón. I would like to play the game called "lote", but I have no cards for it.
(Sp. cartucho) Cartridge, cartouch.
A pan. (see kalwágan).
(Sp. carruaje) Equipage, coach, four-wheeler, usually drawn by horses.
(Sp. casa) House, abode, dwelling, domicile, residence, habitation. (see baláy).

To wager, bet, stake, lay, lay a wager, make a bet, put one's money on. Kasahí siá sing duhá ka mángmang. Bet him two pesos. Pilá ang ikasá mo sa íya? What is your wager with him?-or-How much did you bet him? (see kási).
(Sp. caza, cazar) Hunting; to hunt. Kasahí ang báboy nga talonón. Hunt down the wild pig. (see pangayám).
Banana-plantation, collection of bananas called "sáb-a". (see kasagíngan).
Lawsuit, question or case before a court; to have a case in court; sue by legal process, institute legal proceedings. May kasábà silá-or-nagakasábà silá. They have a case in court.
Impediment, let, check, hitch, obstacle, hindrance. (sáblag).
See kasáblag. Also: a person or thing that is an obstacle, that prevents, etc.
Voraciousness, greediness, gluttony, state of being greedy or gluttonous, (sáblok; see kadalók, kakágud,
(Sp. casada, casado) A married woman, a married man.

Good cheer, glee, enjoyment, gladness, gaiety, merriment, merry-making, revelling, rejoicing, joy, pleasure, celebration, solemnity, entertainment, applied to any religious, social or political gathering, where good feeling and cheerfulness abound. (sádia, sádya).
See kasádia. Also: Things that are cheerful or that provide enjoyment and diversion.
See kasádia id.
See kasádia, kasadiáhan, kasadiahón id.

A kind of crab. As this crab is usually rather lean it has become a synonym for thinness, leanness, emaciation. Kaság nga táo. A man as lean as a casag-crab. Kakaság siníng táo! How scraggy this man is!
(H) Banana-plantation, collection of bananas. (ságing; see kasab-ahán).
Liking, attachment to, affection for. May kasahô akó sa íya nga batásan. I have a liking for his ways and manners. (sahô).
To cut up meat into strips, etc. See kusáhos id., and more commonly used.
Concern, regard, attention to visitors and the like. (sahót; see kasinahóton id.).
Passenger, fellow passenger. (see sakáy).
Grief, mourning, pain, sorrow, affliction, woe, heartache, unhappiness, infelicity, anguish, pang, agony, interior or spiritual suffering, dolour, dolor. (see sákit).
Pain, painfulness, suffering, pang, anguish, agony, torture, torment, ache, smart, bodily illness, injury or ailment. (see sakít).
See kasakít. Also: Torture, martyrdom, bodily pains or punishments, things that inflict great bodily pain.
See kasákit. Also: Troubles, worries, anxieties, trials, ordeals, crosses, mental sufferings.
Resentment, ill-feeling, dislike, sense of injury, condition of one who is offended or takes things amiss. (see sáklaw, ákig).
See kasáklaw. Also: things that are irksome, unpleasant, irritating.
Hustle, bustle, press of work, much work, much to do, condition of one who is very busy or much occupied. (see sákò).
See kasákò.

To marry, bless or solemnize a marriage. Sín-o ang nagkasál sa ínyo? Who married you? Who solemnized your marriage? Sín-o ang nagpakasál kaína sang ága? Who was married this morning? Sín-o ang ginkasál sang Párì kahápon? Who was married by the Priest yesterday? Mapakasál kamí buás. We are going to be married to-morrow. Nakasál-or-nagpakasál na kamó ukón walâ pa? Have you been married yet or not? Indì mo pagipakasál ang ímo anák sa kasamiénto sibíl. Don't permit your son (daughter) to contract a civil marriage. Ang mga Kristiánhon nga nagapakasál sa sibíl nagapakasalâ sing dakû sa atubángan sang Diós. Christians that contract a civil marriage sin grievously in the sight of God.
Grudge, spite, anger, resentment, aversion, antipathy, difference, quarrel, condition of one who is at variance with another. (see sál-ag, ákig, aligótgot, gulut-ánon, kasíb-ot).
Sins, faults, errors, offences, transgressions, trespasses, wrong-doing, slips, mistakes, blunders. (see salâ, kasáypan).
Incongruity, discrepancy, inconsistency, awkwardness, inharmoniousness. (see salangiság).
A messmate; friend, companion. (see sálo, kahámbal, kahírup).
Sunset, west, Occident. (see sálup, katúndan, katulúndan).
Injury, damage, destruction, harm, havoc. (see samád, sámad).
(Sp. casamiento) Marriage, wedlock, wedding. Kasamiénto sibíl. Civil marriage. (Sp. casamiento civil). (see mínyo, pangasáwa, kasál).
Disturbance, commotion, mix-up, hodge-podge, miscellany, medley, jumble, disorder, confusion. (see sámok).
Goal, end, result; benefit, advantage; consummation. (see sámput, alapután, kapuslánan, kahimoán).
Mixture, blending; common, joint. Dútà nga kasamwánan. A field that is the joint (common) property of several persons or of a whole community. (see sámò, salamuánan, salamuanán).
Progress, continuity, prosperity, solidity, stability. (see sámwad, kauswágan).
When, at what time (of the past). (see kán-o, sán-o, pa).
Dimness, twilight, the light of the early morning or evening. (see sanáaw).
Clearness, brightness, lucidity, light. (see sánag).
Explanation, exposition, clearing-up, a clear proof of, manifestation, publication, explication, the unfolding of the facts or throwing light on something obscure, etc. (sánag).
Daybreak, peep of day, dawn, first blush-, prime-, of morning, morning light, aurora, daylight in its initial stages, the time preceding sunrise. (see sánag, kasánag, kasanagán, kasanagón).
See kasánag.
A partner at play, especially in a game of cards. (see sángga, dápig, kadápig, kadámpig).
Opponent, contestant, adversary, antagonist. Kasánggà níya siá sa pagkapangúlo-bánwa. He is his opponent for the office of Municipal President. (see kasúmpung, sánggà).
(B) The day before yesterday. (Kang isaráng hápon, sang isá ka hápon).
Trial, probation, examination. (see sánghid).
Width, breadth, wideness, latitude, amplitude, expanse. (see sángkad).
Width, etc. See kasángkad, kasangkarón.
Equipment, outfit, gear, tools, furniture, the collective name for all the things required for a certain purpose. (sángkap; see galamitón).
(H) Width, etc. See kasángkad, kasangkadón.
Capacity, capability, preparedness, ability, fitness, proper preparation for an undertaking, etc. (sángkol; see takús, ikatakús, kaákò).
Companion, equal, one of the same class, example, type. (see sánglit, panánglit, pananglítan, pananglitánan).
Formerly, in times past, long ago. (see sádto, ánay, sang, úna).
Exactness, fitness, harmoniousness, good proportion, symmetry, harmony. (sántò; see kasíbò).

Continuance, continuation, durability, permanence, persistence, lastingness, quality of lasting long, decision, determination. Ang katin-arán kag kasanyogán sang bánwa--. The prosperity and stability of the town, commonwealth, etc. Isilíng mo na ang kasanyogán. State now your final decision or determination. (sányog).
Animals in general, the animal kingdom, fauna, brute creation, beasts. (see sápat).
Thorns, briars; place overgrown with thorns or briars. (see sapínit).
Skim, that which is taken off or removed as by skimming; gain, profit, emolument, benefit, advantage, interest. (see sáplid, latáb, gáhi, gáhab, láhab, túbò).
See kasaplídan.
See kasaplídan. (see ganánsya).
Roughness, ruggedness, unevenness, opposed to smoothness and slipperiness. (see sápnot).
One who is a party to an agreement or contract, a member of a meeting or board, a councillor. Kasápulbánwa. A municipal Councillor. (sápul).
A meeting, assembly, board; council. Kasapulán-bánwa. Municipal Council. Kasapulán-puód. Provincial Board.
See kasapulán. Also: agreement, accord, resolution.
Possibility, potentiality, practicability, feasibility. Walâ na sing kasarangán sa paglikáw sinâ. There is now no possibility of avoiding it. (see saráng, ikasaráng).

Temperance, moderation, sobriety, soberness, restraint; enough, not too much and not too little. Ang kasarángan. Temperance. Ang birtúd nga kasarángan. The virtue of temperance. Kasarángan gid lang ang íya nga pagkabutáng. He has just sufficient property to live on. He is neither poor nor rich. (see saráng, kasarangán).
Bad luck, evil fate. (see sarót).
Ugliness, plainness, hideousness, repulsiveness (of face); cursedness, curstness. (see sárot).
To fray, become useless, run to seed. Nagakasâsâ ang ákon panápton sa kagabúk. My clothes are getting frayed through rottenness. (see katâtâ).
Disgust, aversion, loathing, antipathy. (see sáw-a).
Impropriety, indecency, unbecoming conduct, unsuitability. (see sáw-a).
Fault, blame, mistake, blunder, slip, error that needs correction. (sawáy).

To recuperate, recover, get slowly better and stronger, improve in health and strength after an illness, be convalescent, convalesce. Nagakasáykásay na ang masakít nga bátà. The sick boy is now slowly recuperating, (improving, moving about again).
Errors, mistakes, fallacies, blunders, oversights, slips; faults, shortcomings, defects, imperfections, deficiencies. (sayóp; kasáypan id.; see kasal-ánan, kakulángan, katalángan).
(H) Explanation, exposition, elucidation, explication, meaning, interpretation; knowledge, understanding. (sáyod; see kasaysáyan).
See kasayopán.
See kasayopán.
(H) See kasayóran.
(H) See kasayóran.
Explanation, exposition, elucidation, explication, clear statement, interpretation. (sáysay; see kasayóran).

(Sp. casera) Mistress of the house, housewife, landlady, housekeeper; to be a housekeeper, etc., accept boarders and lodgers. Nagakaséra siá sang mga bumulúthò sa matáas nga buluthóan. She accepts High-School students as boarders and lodgers.
(Sp. caserola) Pan, saucepan. (see kaláhà, kalwágan).
(Sp. casi) Nearly, about, somewhat more or less, almost. (see bílang, daw).
To bet, lay, lay a wager, put one's money on, wager, stake. See kasá id. Kasíhi siá sing pilô. Bet him double the amount. Pilá ang ikási mo? How much is (was) your wager? (see patád, tayâ).
A small flag, banner or signal.
(H) Denseness, thickness, condition of ground cumbered with high grass, brush or undergrowth. (sí-ot; see kasiók).
Ninety. (see siám).
Disgust, grudge, displeasure, annoyance, angry feeling, vexation, irritation, chagrin. (síb-ot).
Quarrel, a falling-out, disagreement, difference, disaccord, dissidence, variance, dissension, misunderstanding. (see síbag).

Divergence, difference, opposition, disunion, disharmony. Nagaabyánay silá sa gwâ, ápang may ginahúptan silá sa dúghan nga kasibágsíbag ang isá sa isá. They are friends outwardly but in their hearts they oppose one another. (see síbag-to disagree, etc.).
Fitness, exactness, accuracy, suitability, quality of fitting precisely. (see síbò).
See kasíbò. Also: Things that fit or suit exactly.
Courage, strength, bravery, valour, intrepidity, dash, pluck, mettle. (see kaísug, kabáskug).
Brilliancy, brightness, gleam, shine, resplendence, effulgence, refulgence, glitter, lustre, sheen, shimmer. (see sídlak).
Radiance, dazzling brightness. (see kasílaw, sídlaw-sílaw).
Hiccough, hiccup. (see sidô).
Light, brightness, gleam, illumination, visibility, luminosity, luminousness, irradiation. (see síga).
See kasídla id.
Horribleness, dreadfulness, horridness, frightfulness, fearfulness, hideousness, repulsiveness, awfulness, state of being shocking to look upon or to hear of. (see sígne, makasisígne).
Anger, spite, grudge, ill will, hatred, detestation, dudgeon, spleen, acrimony, aversion. (sílag; see dumút).
See kasídlak.
See kasídlaw.
A kind of fish.
Brightness, gloss, lustre, shining surface, glistening. (see sílì, kasilíng).
(B) Gloss, shine, sheen, gleam, glint, brightness, brilliancy. (silíng; see kahíning, kasílì, kasídlak).
(H) Neighbour; neighbourhood; grounds at the side of a house. (silíng; see kaíping, kaíngod, etc.).
Square, having four equal sides; carpenters square. (see askwála, eskwála, kaládo).
(Sp. casillas) Lavatory, privy, closet, latrine, jakes, W.C. (short for water-closet). (see lubô, komún).
Loneliness, solitariness, isolation. (see sím-ong).
Co-citizen, fellow-countryman, citizen, resident. (see bánwa).
Feeling, sentiment, regard, consideration; to have regard or consideration for. (see patugsíling, pasunáid, balatyágon).
To fool, cheat, play a trick to. Dílì mo pagkasináhan ang ímo isigkatáo. Don't cheat your neighbour. (see dáyà, límbong, lág-it).
See kasahót.
See kasántò.
Limpidness, limpidity, pellucidity, clearness, transparency, translucence, translucency especially of liquids. (sínaw; see katín-aw).
Spinning top. (see trómpo).
To spin a top. Ikásing ang kasíng mo. Spin your top. (see kasíng).
Heart, affection, heart as the seat of love and tenderness. (see tagiposóon).
Very great heat, torrid heat, hot weather, torridity, torridness, state of being very hot; heat (of anger or passion).
A knob or protuberance on the neck of some horses (as a distinctive horse-mark).
(Sp. casino) Clubhouse for social or political reunions. (see tilipunán).
A hollow sound, quality of sounding hollow, as a half-empty coconut or the like. (see sinô).
(B) See kasí-ot. (siók-síot).
(B) Eventide, nightfall, evening twilight. (sírum; see kasisídmon).
See kasírum.
See kasírum, kasisídmon.
Straitened circumstances, difficulties, troubles. (see síot, kapipít-an, kalalát-an, kalisdánan).

To tear or pull off as an old thatched roof, vines or the like. Kaskasá ang dáan nga atóp kag ilísan mo sing bág-o. Tear off the old roof and replace it with a new one. Ikáskas akó ánay sináng mga balágon. Please pull off those creepers. (see karáskas).
(Sp. casco) Hull, hold of a ship, hulk. (see dágpak).
A kind of plant much used for hedges and fences. (see kamándag).
Imperative passive of kasál.
Marrying, marriage, the celebration of marriages or nuptials; to marry, get married (of many). (see kasál, pangasáwa).
(Sp. caso) Case, cause (legal); result, event, occurrence, contingency. Walâ man sing káso. There was no result. Nothing happened.
Nearness, proximity (of time, as of a feast, etc.). (see sóbol, kakóg-ong).
Commandment, order, injunction, law, prescription, rules; testament. Ang dáan kag bág-o nga kasogoán. The Old and New Testament. Kasogoán-bánwa. Municipal ordinance. (see sógò, pagbulút-an).
(H) Beginning, opening, outset, inception, start, commencement. (see súgud, ginsugúran, kamunóan).
To tousle-, rumple-, tumble-, the hair, grasp and shake by the hair, or the like. Indì mo pagkasókasóhon ang íya bohók. Don't rumple his hair. (see karokosó),
A kind of tree with an edible fruit. The stone protrudes from the ripe fruit.
A Philippine folk-dance.
Roughness, hardness, callosity, callus, harshness, asperity (of skin); to be or become rough, etc. (see gáspang, gúphal).
(B) Once. See makaisá.
(Sp. casta) To mate, pair, cover (of animals). Kastahí ang kabáyo. Bring the mare to the stallion. Pakastahá ang kabáyo. Let the stallion cover the mare.
(Sp. castañas). Chestnuts, chesnuts.
(Sp. castañetas) Castanets, castanettes.

(Sp. castigo) Punishment, chastisement, correction, castigation, penalty; visitation (of God); to punish, chastise, castigate, penalize. Kastígo inâ sang Diós. That is (was) a visitation of God. Kastigóha siá. Chastise him. Ikastígo mo sa íya iníng múlta nga duhá ka písos. Punish him with this fine of two pesos. (see sílot, gábà).
(Sp. castillo) Castle, fortress; imitation of a bombardment by letting off detonating fireworks tied to a bamboo-erection.
(A corruption of castañetas) Castanets. (See kastanyétas).
(Sp. castor) Castor, small vessel with a perforated top for sprinkling pepper, etc.; beaver (animal so called). Aseite de kastór. (Sp. aceite de castor) Castor oil.
(Sp. castoreño) A derby hat, felt hat, any hat made of cloth.
Quarrel, dispute, brawl, contention, disagreement, discord, difference, squabble, altercation, dissension, tiff; an opponent in a quarrel. (see súay, kasuáyan).
Quarrelling, bickering and biting; things fought or quarrelled about. (súay; see kasúay, kasuayón).
Cause or origin of a quarrel, quarrelsomeness. (súay).
Sorrow, grief, sadness, distress, woe, affliction, mourning, bitterness, heart-ache, dolour, dejection, care, dole, fret. (subô).
See kasubô. Also: Things to be grieved over; that causes affliction or sorrow; sorrows.
Rivers, river-system. (see subâ).
(H) An equal, one in the same predicament as another; sameness, equality, like, as, similar to. (súbung).
Entrails, bowels, guts, viscera. (sulúd).
See kasúdlan. Also: Contents; vessel, container, receptacle.
Exhaustion, inanition, starvation. (see súgpay, súp-ay).
Continuation, prolongation, lengthening, production, protraction, extension, accession, addition; continued (of serials). (see súgpon).
Party, partner; agreement, compact, pact. (see sugút).
Anniversary, annual or yearly celebration. (sukát).
Writings, books, works, writ, scripture. (see sulát).
Cocks. (sulúg).
Current, torrent, flow, race, course, swift motion of water. (sulúg).
(H) Exciting nausea, loathing, aversion, turn, queasiness, qualm, repugnance, antipathy. (sumó, makasolómo, kataláka, kataká, kangílad).
Swiftness, velocity of a current. (see sulúg, kasúlgan).
See kasúlgan.
(Sp. casulla) Chasuble, vestment used by a priest at Mass.
Nausea, loathing, queasiness, qualm. (súm-od).
(H) Loathing, aversion; abomination. (see kasúm-od, kasulómo).
See kasúm-od.
Plaintiff, accuser, prosecutor, complainant, arraigner. (súmbung).
Opponent, enemy, adversary, antagonist, assailant. (súmpung).
Intimacy; near relationship. (see súod, kahírup, kahámbal, kadágil, pariénte).
Nooks, corners, out-of-the-way places, secluded places. (see suók).
Daring, recklessness, boldness, hardihood, rashness, cheek, frowardness, dash, impertinence, audacity, temerity. (see súpug, kakáhas, kaaháng).
Inquisitiveness, curiousness, curiosity. (see súsi).
(Sp. sústo) Shock, surprise, trepidation, turn, a strong and sudden agitation.
Badness, naughtiness, wickedness, disobedience. (sutíl).
See kasutíl. Also: Naughty behaviour, wicked deeds, naughty practices, bad manners.
See kasutíl.

(B) To be full, brim-, chock-, choke-, full, replete, replenished, crammed, stuffed. Nagakátà ang túbig sang ísdà, ang bólsa sang tinápay, etc. The water is full of fish, the pocket is crammed with bread, etc. (see punô, butâ).

To manage-, distribute-, portion out-, well, apportion, assign; to spend little, be economical, live frugally, be thrifty. Katákatáha ang humáy, agúd índì kitá makulángan, kay dílì gid maáyo ang áton pinatubás sa karón nga túig. Portion out well the rice or we may run short, because this year's harvest was far from good.
To prattle, prate, talk much and flippantly, be a noisy or idle chatterer. Anó na man ang ínyo nga ginakinatâkátà? What are you talking about so much? (see búrà, ngálngal, ngásal, etc.).
Height, tallness, loftiness. (see táas).
See katáas. Also: High dignity, things that are lofty or sublime.
See katáas.
Excellences, prerogatives, high perfections, privilege, exaltation, elevation (in rank, etc.), great dignity. (see táas, kalabihán, kamahálan).

To stretch on a frame or rod, as yarn previous to weaving; to stretch on the rack, figuratively or literally. Katáda (-ára) ang bunáng. Stretch the yarn. Ginkátad níla siá. They put him on the rack. They punished him severely.
See kalakatád, karakatád.
A frame to stretch yarn on, etc. Walâ ko makátad ang bunáng, kay walâ akó sing katadán. I cannot get the yarn ready for weaving, because I have no stretching frame.
Straightness, directness, rightness. (see tádlung).
See katádlung. Also: Straight-forwardness, honesty, rectitude, uprightness; honest and upright dealing.
Retiredness, shyness, bashfulness, coyness; to be shy, etc. May katág-an siá-or-nagakatág-an siá sa paghámbal. She is too bashful to speak. (see tágò).
Hearts; kind, sympathetic people, tender-hearted folks. (see tagiposóon).
Fog, mist, cloud; darkness. (see ámbon, alopóop, gál-um, pangánod, dámpug).
Respect, reverence, awe, fear, veneration, regard, consideration, deference. (see tahâ).
Fear, alarm, dismay, consternation, apprehension; shyness, respect. (see táhap).
See katáhap. Also: Danger, things that cause fear or apprehension.
Loss of strength, defection, deterioration. (see táhaw).
See katáhaw. Also: Things that cause loss of strength, etc.
Beauty, loveliness, comeliness, fairness, good looks, goodliness, pulchritude, niceness, pleasing appearance, handsomeness. (see tahúm, katahumán, kagayón, kaányag).
See katahúm. Also: Objects that are beautiful or pleasing in appearance.
See katahúm.
Reverence, deference, respect, veneration, esteem; distinction, glory, honour, dignity. (see táhud).
To cackle. Ang mungâ nagakatákkaták. The hen cackles. (see kákak, kurukutúk).
Nausea, surfeit, loathing, queasiness, qualm, quality that excites a loathing or aversion. (see taká).
Dimension, size, bulk, volume, extent, measurement, measure. (see takús).
See katáksan.
Hanging down freely, dangling loosely in the meaning of "kátal".
To hang down freely, dangle loosely, (particularly applied to the male organ of generation of a horse or other animal).
Danger, apprehension, peril, risk, hazard, jeopardy, liability. (tagám).
(H) See makataláka. Kataláka iníng kalán-on. This food is loathsome, sickening, nauseous. (see taká, kataká).
(H) Attention! Observation, notice. (see tamúd, talámdan, katámdan, pahibaló, abíso, patimáan).
Mistake, blunder, slip, missing one's way, deviation, swerving, declination, going astray, wandering, error, deception, illusion. (tálang).
(H) One of the same class or condition. Si Fuláno katalarúngan ko sa pageskwéla. N.N. is my classmate at school. (see dungán).
Cowardice, faint-heartedness, funk, timidity, poltroonery, weakness. (tálaw).
See katálaw.
Quality of wood, or the like, that is easy to split. (tálhà).
(Sp. catalina) A wheel with teeth, cog-wheel, sprocket-wheel, spur-wheel.
The last part or stage of a thing, end, termination, condition of approaching ripeness, completion or termination. (see tápus, talipuspusón).
(H) Pointedness, acuteness, sharpness of a point or pointed instrument, as of a needle, awl, thorn, etc. (see talíwis).
(H) Sharpness of an edged tool, keenness, quality of cutting well, said of a knife, bolo, etc. (see talúm).
See katalúm.
Jungle, deep forest, bush, wild country, uninhabited territory. (see tálon, katalunánan, )
See katalúnan.
Sweetness, deliciousness, exquisiteness, condition of being sweet, agreeable, exquisite, delightful to sense or feeling. (see tám-is).
See katám-is. Also: Objects that are sweet, etc.
See katám-is.
Laziness, sloth, indolence, idleness, slowness, remissness. Katámad sa ímo! How slow or lazy you are! (see támad).
See katámad.

Condition or quality of being adjacent, adjoining or contiguous, especially said of grounds that border on each other; neighbour, one whose land is adjacent to another's. Katámbi ko siá. He is my neighbour, his field borders on mine. (see támbi).
Fatness, obesity, stoutness, corpulence. (see támbok).
Field, cultivated land, farm, especially rice-land. (see tánum, tanúm, palangúmhan).
Wickedness, depravity, maliciousness, insulting behaviour. (see tampálas).
Sound, echo, noise (of a cry, voice, etc., heard from a distance).
Condition of being overripe, rotten-ripeness, very soft and rotten (of fruits), (see tanáng, kalanóng).
Accuracy of aim, unerring aim, sure or good aim, hit, pointing well, taking good aim, certainty of hitting. (see tándà).
Dexterity, adroitness; application, zeal, diligence, assiduity, industry. (see tándus, kapísan).
A kind of crab.
Wonder, miracle, prodigy, marvel; wonderful, marvellous, miraculous, extraordinary. (see tanhágà, katingaláhan,
(B) Straightness, straight growth (of trees, etc.). (see tanús).
Reach, scope, extent, stretch (of one's power, influence, etc.). Ang katányog sang íya nga tíngug. The reach of his voice. (see tányog).
To be born. See táo. Sa adláwádlaw may nagakatáo kag may nagakamatáy. Every day-some are born and others die,-there are births and deaths.
To live independently, have a household of one's own, live together with others. Pilá kamó nga nagakataó sa ínyo baláy? How many are you living together in your house? (see táo).
Men, mankind, humanity, the human race, man (taken collectively). (see táo).
Dirtiness, uncleanness, impurity, foulness, filthiness, filth. (see táp-ing).
See katáp-ing.
Weakness, feebleness; dulness, stupidity. (see táp-ol).
Evenness, smoothness, levelness, flatness, quality of being even or level (of a floor, road, plain, etc.; tápan).
Associate, member of a society or club, share-holder, stock-holder; mate, companion, fellow, partner, confederate, colleague. (see tápù).
Fragility, frailty, brittleness, weakness, flimsiness, quality of-being easily broken or torn,-having neither strength nor solidity. (see tapúk).

End, finish, completion, termination, expiration, wind up, consummation, denouement, limit, stoppage, close, conclusion, finale, finis, period, term, terminus, last. Sa waláy katapúsan. Endless, for ever and ever, in perpetuity, evermore, aye for aye, for evermore, without end, eternal, everlasting. (see tápus, katalipuspusán).
Thoughtlessness, carelessness, imprudence, lack of circumspection or consideration. (see tarág-tarág).
(B) Jungle, bush, forest, wild country. (see tángkal, katalúnan).
(Sp. catarata) Cataract, cascade, waterfall; cataract of the eye. (see busáy, kúlap, bítlig).

Justice, equity, justification, righteousness; argument, reason, contention, reasoning, argumentation. Ginpaháyag níya ang íya nga katarúngan. He gave his reason. He explained his argument. (see tárung).
(B) Often stands for makatarús. See tarús-to accomplish, perform, etc.
To fray, etc. See kasâsâ id.
Mermaid, naiad, siren, water-nymph.
Tranquillity, peace, peacefulness, freedom from worry, obstruction or opposition, calmness. (táwhay).
See katáwhay. Also: Things that make for a tranquil life, for peacefulness, etc.
See katáwhay.
See kataóhan. (see táwo-táo).
A parade, procession. See kátay.

File, line, parade, procession; row (of houses); to follow in line, file, line up, parade, walk in Indian file. Pakatáya ang mga táo sa prosesyón. Marshal the people in orderly lines for the procession. Buás, konó, may kátay sang mga salín sang kagúbut. To-morrow, it is said, there will be a parade of the war-veterans. Magkátay kamó. Line up-or-Form in line. (see ídas, kóro).
Farness, etc. See katayogón).
Farness, distance, remoteness. (see táyog, kanáyop, kanáyok).
(Sp. cate) A measure for sugar, etc., equal to about two thirds of a kilo. (gm. 632.60). One hundred "káte" make a "píko" or "píkul" (Sp. pico).
(Sp. catedral) Cathedral.
(Sp. catequista) Catechist.
(Sp. catecismo) Catechism, christian doctrine. (see toksóan).
To decoy, catch birds by a decoy; to provoke, excite, induce, lure, allure, draw, draw on. Amó inâ gánì ang ginakáti (ikáti) níya sa ákon. That is exactly what he is enticing me with. (see katián).
Dim. and Freq. of káti. Katíkatihá siá. Provoke (induce) him. Ginkatíkatí (kinatíkatí) níya akó sa pagpakigáway. He challenged me to fight. (see ákyat).
Small, very itchy eruptions, pustules or boils in various skin diseases.
Glass, crystal. (kátyà id).
Lure, bait, decoy, especially a bird used to lure other birds into a trap. (káti).
Spouse, husband, wife, love; betrothed, lover. Katiáyon níya siá. She (he) is his (her) wife (husband). (see tiáyon).
Freedom, liberty, independence. (see tibáwas, kaluásan).
Roundness, plumpness, etc. See katibúnog. (tíbsol, típsul).
Stockiness, stumpiness, stoutness, plumpness. (see tibúdol, búdul, katipúngkò).
Roundness, plumpness, stoutness, fleshiness, beefiness (of arms, legs, etc.). (see tibúnog, katipólon, kanipólon, katíbsol, katámbok, kabahúl).
To be narrow, etc. See kitíd id.
Outrigger, usually made of bamboo-spars. Its purpose is to steady a boat.
(H) Hardness, solidity, quality of great resistance to pressure or of being unyielding to physical or moral agencies. (tíg-a).
Possibility, feasibility, facility, occasion, opportunity (of obtaining or procuring a thing). (see katigayónan).
Procurement, preparation, effectiveness; capacity or ability to bring something about or to get results. (see tigáyon).
Place overgrown with tígbaw-reeds. (see tígbaw).
Clearness, distinctness (of pronunciation, etc.). (see tígdà, kaáthag).
See katíg-a. Also: hardness, toughness (of food that is underdone); harshness, roughness, abruptness, bluntness, brusqueness (of speech).
Scarcity, rarity, dearth, lack, want, scantiness. (see tigô, kaíwat, kahínà).
(H) The old, aged, superannuated, old folks, old people, parents advanced in age, forefathers, ancestors, ancients, by-gone generations. (see tigúlang).
Old age, oldness, senility, advanced age, superannuation. (see tigúlang, kagulangón).
Lure, bait, etc. See katián.
(H) Union, gathering, collection, assembly, meeting, society, resume, selection, anthology. (see tingúb).
Freedom, liberty, independence; the common people, ordinary folks. (see timáwà).
Balance, scales, counterweight, counterpoise; partner, mate, assistant. (see tímbang, kabúlig, binangî).
Reaching to below the knees, but above the ankles, short (of dress); a few inches above the ground, not reaching to the floor (of curtains, or the like).
(H) Prosperity, economical independence, stability, durability, progress. (tín-ad).
(H) Limpidness, limpidity, perlucidness, lucidity, pellucidity, clearness, transparency. (tín-aw; see kasínaw).

To squat down in such a way that one does not quite sit on the ground. Indì ka magkatínkátin sa simbáhan. Indì mo pagkatínkatínan ang simbáhan. Don't squat down in church. Indì ka magkatínkátin, kóndì magtíndog ka kon may bisíta. Don't squat down, but stand up, when visitors are present.
Wonder, astonishment, marvel, amazement, wonderment, admiration, surprise; to wonder, etc. Nagakatingála akó. I am astonished. Punô siá sa katingála. He is full of wonder. (see tingála).
Wonder, marvel, miracle, prodigy, phenomenon, things that are astonishing. See katingála. (see katanhagáan).
Union, reunion, etc. See katilíngban. (see tingub).
See katíngban, katilíngban.
For makatingúg, nakatingúg. See tingúg.
Cleanness, cleanliness, spotlessness, purity, freedom from dirt or stain. (see tínlò).

Bond, agreement, covenant, compact, bargain, engagement; lover, affianced, fiancé, fiancée, paramour. Ang Dáan (Bág-o) nga Katípan. The Old (New) Testament. Katípan níya siá. He is her-lover,-intended,-betrothed. He is engaged to her. (see típan).
(H) Roundness, spherical shape. (see tipólon, kanipólon).
Meeting, gathering, congress. (see típon, katipúnan, tilipunán).
Plumpness, etc. (see típsul, katíbsol, katibúnog).

Union, society, association, assembly, meeting, gathering, club. Ang Katipúnan. The revolutionary society founded by Filipino Patriots during the latter part of the nineteenth century and directed against the Spanish colonial Government. (see katípon, katilíngban, tilipunán, tinipóntípon, talapuán, talapuánan).
Stumpiness, stockiness. (see tipúngkò, katibúdol).
Stiffness, rigidity, inflexibility. (tískug; see kabáskug).
Spitefulness, malevolence, malice, maliciousness, spite. Patúga inâ kag búnga sang katístis sang ákon kaáway. That is the work and result of my enemy's spite. (see tístis).
A kind of coarse native cloth made in various colours that soon fade.
Undersized, dwarfish, little, petite, diminutive, less than medium size, applied especially to women.
Small, insignificant, worthless. (see katitíya).
Dangers, perils, jeopardy, hazard. (see tiwálwag).

To find out about other people's affairs, to fish-, worm-, ferret-, out secrets and reveal them, to disclose, lay open, divulge. Katkatá ang sekréto ni Fuláno. Try to fish out N.N.'s secret. Kinátkat níya siá. He wormed out his secret. Sagád gid siá magkátkat sang mga tinágò sang ibán. He is an adept at worming out the secrets of others (and revealing or telling them to others).
Thirty. (tátlo).
Pertaining to or affected by the skin-disease "katúl". Ang may katúl ginatawág nga kátlon. One who has the skin-disease "katúl" is called "kátlon".
(Sp. católica, católico) Catholic. Ang Iglésia Katólika. The Catholic Church. Ang mga katóliko. Catholics.
(Sp. catón) First spelling and reading book for small children, Primer.
(Sp. catre) Bed, couch. (see higdáan, balatángan).
A large, thick kerchief used for wrapping up things brought to or from the market, etc.
(Sp. cachil, castilla) Spanish; Spaniard. Sang tiémpo sang mga Katsílà. In Spanish times. (see Kakatsiláan).
A kind of banana.
Spanish, Iberian. (see katsílà, kinatsilâ).
A kind of field-mouse with a long, pointed snout and a very offensive smell; a kind of rice that when cooked and stirred emits a very strong odour.
A kind of plant; it is poisonous.
Place where toddy is produced or sold. (see tubâ).
Harvest-time, rice-harvest, season for gathering in the crop, the season following immediately after harvest-time. (see tubás, tagaláni, tigaláni).
Sugar-cane field, sugar plantation. (tubó).

Quality or condition of being of equal age with another or of having grown up together with another; contemporaneousness, contemporariness, coexistence. Katúbò ko siá. He is of the same age as myself. (see kadúngan, tubô).
See katúbhan.
Delivery, salvation, redemption; freedom. (see tubús, katibawásan, kaluásan).
Goal, end, termination, limit (of time or place). Sa waláy katubtúban. Without end or limit, endless, eternal, boundless, everlasting, immense. (túbtub).
Delivery. See katubsánan.
See katúbhan, katubohán id.
Force, impetus, vigour in the use of one's hands, as in striking, boxing, throwing, etc.; harshness, roughness, abruptness (of speech). (see katígdas, kaábtik).
Sinking, submersion, foundering, disappearance under water, drowning. (túgdang).
See katúgdang. Also: Danger of sinking; jettison, the throwing of goods overboard to save a ship.
Order (s), comand (s), injunction (s), errand (s). (see tógon, túgon, bílin, kasogoán).
(H) Freshness, coolness, coldness, cold, chill, keenness, bleakness, bitterness, chilliness, rawness, frigidity. (túgnaw).
(H) See katúgnaw. (see kabúgnaw).
An adviser, counselor, reminder. (see túgon).
Difference, dissimilarity, distinction, quality of not being the same or not belonging to the same class or kind. (see túhay).
See katúhay. Also: things that are different. (see kinatuháyan).
Years, time, centuries, ages, aeons; yearly obligation, Easter-duty. (see túig).
Time, year, season. (see katuigán, panuigón).

A kind of skin-disease, producing a very itchy rash that soon forms painful pustules, scabs, etc. It often takes many months to cure; pruritus, itch; to itch, cause the skin-disease katúl. Ginakatúl siá. He is affected with "katúl". Kinatúl man akó sádto ánay. I also once had the skin-disease "katúl". Pakátli siá sing nípay, kalahós, etc. Give him a painful itch by means of "nípay, kalahós", etc.
Bones, skeleton, collection or heap of bones. (túl-an).
Exactness, preciseness, punctuality, exactitude, zeal, diligence, application. (see túl-id, kaíd-id, kapísan).
Dim. and Freq. of katúl. To itch a little, have or cause an itchy feeling.

Loose, not firm or tight, not well joined or adapted and hence creaky, squeaky, emitting a harsh or grating sound (said of tools, knives (not well joined to the handle), of cart-wheels, etc., with loose parts); to be loose; to creak, squeak. Nagakatúlkatúl ang kaláptan sang súndang. The handle of the knife is loose, creaks (not being well joined to the handle). Indì mo pagpakatúlkatulón ang káro, kóndì pisákan mo. Don't rattle the cart, but steady it by means of wedges. (see lágtok, palágtok-to creak, crack (of bones, fingers, etc).
Similarity, equality, likeness, example, like. (see túlad, kaángay, pananglítan).
Sugar cane fields. See katúbhan, tubó.
Sleep, slumber, nap, snooze. (see túlug, tulúg).
(H) West, sunset; going down, disappearance. (see túnud, tunúd, katúndan, katúngdan).
Sleep, sleepiness, drowsiness, somnolence, heaviness, torpidity. (see tuyó, ginatuyó).
Sarcastically used for: Obstinacy, wilfulness, self-will, heedlessness. Ay katumanán siníng bátà! Oh, the obstinacy of this boy! How obstinate this boy is!
Fulfilment, execution, accomplishment, performance, observance, discharge, acquittal, satisfaction. (see túman).
Chili, a species of capsicum, red pepper, Cayenne pepper, Guinea pepper.
Purity, genuineness, solidity, quality of being unmixed, unadulterated, etc. (see túnay).
West, etc. See katulúndan.
Western, occidental, European. (see katúndan).
The midst, middle, centre, middle part, central portion; the heart (of trees, etc.). Ang katung-ánan sang káhoy. The middle part (the heart) of the tree. (see tungâ, alibútud).
Half, moiety. Isá ka katungâ. One half. (see tungâ).
West, etc. See katulúndan, katúndan. Also: relation, etc. See katungdánan.
Relation, connection with, reference to; duty, obligation. (see tungúd).
Western. See katundanánon.
Swamp, bog, nípà-swamp, morass.
Swampy, marshy, fenny, boggy; growing in swampy soil. (see katúnggan).
(H) Thorns, briars; place where thorns and briars grow. (see tunúk).
(H) Sinking, setting, the going down (of a vessel, etc.), disappearance; crash, smash, failure, bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation, closing down, wind-up. (see tunúd).

State of being over against or at the side of, opposite, facing, vis-a-vis, over the way, nearby, in a line with; neighbour, one living over against or at the side of another. (see túpad, luyó, kaluyó, kaatúbang).
Equality, sameness, identity, similarity, condition of being of equal size, influence, attainments, etc., with another; an equal, compeer. (see túpung, tupúng).
Injustice, malice, wickedness, guile, cheating. (see tóso).
Courage, bravery, fidelity, trustiness, allegiance, loyalty, fealty, devotion. (tútum).
Sleep, disposition to sleep, sleepiness, somnolence, drowsiness, heaviness. (tuyó).
Sleep, act of sleeping, slumber, nap, snooze.
(B) See katutúyhan.
(B) See katutúyhon.
Sleepiness, somnolence, drowsiness, heaviness. (tuyó).
Scheme, plan, intention, design, project, proposal, measure, course, things intended to be carried out. (túyò).
Glass; crystal. See kátià.
Vineyard. See ulubásan.

Companion, helper, assistant, help, attendant, associate colleague, one at the side of another; company, companionship; friend, adviser. Ang Diós nga Espiritú Sánto kaúbay sang Iglésia Katólika. God the Holy Ghost is with (Holy Church) the Catholic Church. Hukóm nga kaúbay. An assistant judge. (see kabúylog, kaluyó, kaúpud, kadámpig)
(Sp. caudal) Stock, capital, funds, assets, property, wealth. (see pahunán, mánggad, pagkabutáng, pílak).
Waste, prodigality, wastefulness, unthriftiness, lavishness, profusion, squandering, extravagance. (see údhà, kabuhahâ).
Own, proper, private, personal, independent, peculiar, particular.
Blood-vessels, veins, arteries; muscles, tendons. (see ugát).
Modesty, reserve, decorum, decency, delicacy, pudicity, correct behaviour. (see úgdang, kalígdong).
Abatement, alleviation, mitigation, decrease. (see úgdaw).
Thirst, thirstiness, drought, drouth, dryness. Dakû ang íya nga kaúhaw. He is very thirsty. Kaúhaw sa ímo! How thirsty you are! (úhaw).
Diligence, industry, assiduity, ardour, earnestness, sedulity, laboriousness, zeal for acquiring knowledge or experience, application, inquisitiveness. (úkud).
(English: caucus) Caucus; party conference, political meeting; gathering, meeting (in general). (see katilíngban, katipúnan).
Stiffness of joints, etc. (see úl-ul, ól-ol, kaálay).
Impurity, lasciviousness, lewdness, uncleanness, impudicity, pruriency, lechery, carnality, lubricity, immodesty, indecency, obscenity, bawdry, unchastity. (see úlag).
Grandparents; forefathers, ancestors, progenitors, forbears, forebears. (úlang).
Hindrance, obstacle, impediment, obstruction, let, check, hitch. (uláng).
Purity, virginity, maidenhood, integrity, continence. (úlay).
Fields, tillable soil, plantation, arable land, farmland. (umá).
(B) Foolishness, folly, absurdity, nonsensicality, nonsense, bosh, twaddle. (úmang).
(B) Folly, nonsense, craziness, twaddle, bosh. (see kaúmang, kabuangán).
See kaúmang. State or condition of one who is a fool, idiot, lunatic, madman; lunacy, idiocy, foolishness, insanity, madness.
Fields, etc. See kaumahán id.
Shake, jolt, jolting, bump, jerk, shock, joggle, jounce, a jerking motion. (see úndag, kagúnda).
Flesh, meat, the fleshy parts of a slaughtered animal, etc., as distinct from the bones. (see unúd). Also: The prominent, wealthy, influential people.
See kaúndan.
Obstacle, hindrance, objection, impediment, obstruction, let, check, hitch, stoppage, interruption. (see upáng, kaulángan).
(H) Company; companions, associates, comrades, friends, chums, intimates, acquaintances. (upúd).

(H) Companionship, intimacy, acquaintanceship, fellowship, association, comradeship, the going with, companion. Kaúpud (sa) sang-together with, in company with. Nagabút siá dirí kaúpud sang íya mga útud. He arrived here in company with his brothers. (upúd).
(B) Good management, carefulness, circumspection, acuteness, keenness, penetration, shrewdness, sharpness, discretion, wisdom. (uríka).
Advance, progress, getting on, making headway, extension, improvement. (úswag).
See kauswágan. (see úswad, úswag, kasamwáran).
Debts, obligations, what one owes to another. (see útang).
Activity, diligence, application, zeal, assiduity, sedulity, ardour, earnestness, laboriousness. (kautihón id.).
Industriousness, attachment to work, assiduousness, activity. (úti; see kaúti).
(H) Care, solicitude, concern, zeal. (see utitíd).
One half-, one side-, of a thing. Ang kautúd sang láwas. Half the body. One side of the body. (see utúd, útud, kapíhak).
(H) Brothers and sisters, brethren, brotherhood, sisterhood, all near relations in general. (see útud).
The link of a chain, loop, ring; to link. (see káwad).

To hook in, insert a hook, take hold of by means of a hook. Kawití ang sangá sang káhoy kag uyúgon mo. Get a hook on the tree-branch and shake it. Ginkaw-itán níla ang lángkà kag ginbútong túbtub nga nadágdag. They hooked the jack fruit and pulled till it fell down. (see káwit).
The small rope connecting the trace-beam with the plough, etc.
A boiler, large pan or cauldron of metal, as used in sugar-milling. (see kináwà).
A link; to link, connect as by a link, to unite or join. (see káw-id).
Lack, need, want, loss, privation; things that are lacking or whose want is felt, destitution, deprivation. (see walâ, kawád-on, kinawalâ, kinawád-on).
Deprivation, bereavement, lack, want, loss, poverty, destitution. (see kawád-an, etc.).

To hang down, depend from, be suspended from, stick out, dangle. Nagakáwal ang pányo mo sa bólsa. Your handkerchief is hanging out of your pocket. Pakawála ang koréa sa kílid mo, dílì sa atubángan. Let your girdle hang down at the side, not in front. (see kábit, káway, gáway).
Left handedness, awkardness, clumsiness. (see walís).
Eighty, four score. (walô).

To go or step over a fence, pass out over the side of a vehicle instead of leaving it by the ordinary way of exit, etc. Nagkáwas lang siá sa bíntana. He simply went out by the window. Dílì mo pagpakawáson ang mga karabáw sa kodál. Do not let (make) the buffaloes step over the fence. Kinmáwas ang kabáyo sa kwádra. The horse escaped from its fenced-in stable. Ang kalámpay nagkáwas sa kólon. The calampay-crabs escaped over the rim of the kettle. Pataáson mo ang díngding sang tángkal agúd índì na makakáwas ang báboy. Make the sides of the pigsty higher so that the pig cannot get out again. (see áwas, sagáhay).

(H) Stealth, secrecy, wiliness, slyness, craftiness; to steal, rob, commit theft, take, pilfer, filch, pinch, nab, prig, appropriate unlawfully. Sa káwat. Secretly. On the sly. Stealthily, craftily, cunningly. Sín-o balá ang nagkáwat sang ákon taknáan? Who has stolen my watch? Indì ka magkáwat (mangáwat). Don't steal. Kinawátan si Fuláno sing duhá ka mángmang. N.N. had two pesos stolen from him. Indì mo pagbáklon ang mga butáng nga nahibál-an mo nga kináwat. Don't buy things you know are stolen. (see tákaw, káwtì, tíkas).
A thief, robber, stealer, burglar, gangster. (see makáwat).
Correspondent, lover, paramour (particularly said of one who has illicit relations with a married woman). (see kalólot, kahagúgma, banábána).
Anything that dangles or hangs down freely as a tassel, fringe, hair, rope, string, etc.; to dangle, hang down, protrude and shake in the wind, etc. (see gáway, káwal, kábit).
To dangle, swing in suspension, etc. (see káway, kabítkábit, kabílkabíl, gawáygáway).
Bamboo.
Place where bamboo grows; clumps of bamboo. (see kakawayánan).
A large plain, extensive grounds, extended level land fit for cultivation. (wayáng).
To wound, tear, scratch, lacerate. (see pílas, píla, gádras, karós, bákris).

To reach for, stretch out the arm after something, make a long arm. Kawhatá ang ákon báyò nga yárà sa salab-ítan. Take down my jacket from the peg there. Ikáwhat akó ánay sang ákon kálò. Please reach up and take down my hat. (see káb-ot, dáwhat).
Earpick; to use an earpick, pick out the earwax. Kawhihí siá. Scoop out his earwax. Nagapangáwhi siá. He is taking out earwax with an earpick. (see gómi).

Attractiveness, charm, winsomeness, pleasantness, delightfulness, agreeableness, quality of an object that is pleasing or attractive; liking, attraction, delight; to like, be pleased with. Nagakawíli siá sinâ (Ginakawíli níya inâ). He likes it. He is pleased with it. (see wíli, kawilíhan, makawiwíli).

See kawíli. Also: Things to be liked, attraction, attractiveness. Ngáa man nga nagwíli ka dídto nga walâ man sing kawilíhan? Why did you like it there where there is no attraction? (see kalawilián, kalawilihán, kawilihánan).
Attraction, objects that give pleasure or enjoyment. (see kawilíhan, wíli, kawíli).
Junction, copulation, articulation; to join, copulate, articulate.
Hook; a receptacle for palm-wine made of bamboo and having a hook attached to it for carrying over the shoulder. (see káwit).

To hook, pluck or gather with pole and hook, pull or shake down with a hook. Kawíta ang dúldul. Shake (pull) down the (ripe) pods of the kapok-tree with pole and hook. (see síngit, dágas, dúgus, paníngit, pangáwit).
Dim. and Freq. of káwit; Dim. of kawít.

To touch with the hands, handle, grasp, take hold of (somewhat roughly or violently). Indì ka magkáwkaw (magpangáwkaw) sang súd-an, kóndì kuháon (galohón) mo sang kutsára. Don't touch the side-dish with your hands, but take it with the spoon. Kawkawá lang inâ. Seize it-, catch hold of it-, with your hands. (see kámkam, kámlò, kapút, hámò, búklas, sábnit).
Band, rope, satchel-string, wallet-strap, basket-sling and the like.

A small quantity of yarn or thread, a skein. Ang isá ka ágpang may napúlò ka maréhas kag ang isá ka maréhas may napúlò ka kawól. A large hank of thread has ten small hanks and each small hank has ten skeins.
Dim. of káwat. To pilfer, sneak, steal a little, be a thief in a small way, to commit a petty theft.
Thief, sneak-thief, petty thief, pilferer. (see makáwat, kawatán).
(H) For, because, on account of, for the reason. Indì akó magkádto dídto, kay nagaulán. I am not going there, because it is raining.
Particle denoting dative or accusative of persons. Ginhátag níya iníng líbro kay Pédro-or-sa kay Pédro. He gave this book to Peter. Nagsúmbag siá kay Pédro-or-sa kay Pédro. He struck Peter.
To lie supine, etc. See kayáng, kayâ.

To spread, scatter; disorder, dishevel. Kay-agón mo silá sing alalángay. Spread them out-equally,-evenly,-in groups of equal size. Ang íya bohók ginakáy-ag sang hángin. Her hair is fluttering in the wind. (see báhin, bahínbáhin, bulád, búkag).
For kayaán from kayâ.
To glide, slither, slide down a tree, pole, rope, steep incline, etc. Nagkáy-us siá sa pángpang. He slid down the bank. (see alóg-og, dáhog, dalóhog, dalús-us, kalós-os).

To delight, please, attract, cause a liking for (especially for money). Sang pagkakítà níya sang madámù nga pílak nga ginpamakál sing magáy nagtoón siá sa paghabúl, kay nakáya siá sang báyad. When she saw the large amount of money paid for magáy-cloth, she learned to weave, because she was attracted by the (high) price (pay). (see ílà, íma, íbug, lúyag).

To lie on one's back, to lie supine, lie face upward. Nagakayâ silá sa lándong sang páhò. They are lying on their backs in the shade of the mango-tree. Pakáy-a (pakayaá) ang pínggan. Put the plate face upwards. Pakáy-i akó siníng pínggan. Turn this plate face upwards for me. (see kayáng).
Dim. and Freq. of kayâ. Ang bátà nagakayâkayâ sa salúg. The baby lies on its back on the floor.
Sometimes used for "kuyáb", which is the proper and more usual expression. To fan.

To ascend, rise, go up on high. Nagkáyab-or-kinmáyab sa lángit ang Aton Ginóo. Our Lord ascended into heaven. Ginpakáyab sa lángit sang Mahál nga Diós ang Ilóy ni Hesukrísto. God caused to ascend (assumed) into heaven the Mother of Jesus Christ.
To seize, snatch greedily or selfishly. Kayabáha lang tanán. Just seize everything-or-take all for yourself.
A kind of fishing net. (see pókot, sálap, láya, sápyaw).
Maize cob, corn cob.
To float, hover, drift. Ang mga sakayán nagakayánkáyan sa túbig, ang mga píspis sa hángin. Boats float on water, birds in the air.
Also: the border of a roof, the eaves. (see balísbísan).
Shed, hut, kiosk, tent; tabernacle (of the Old Testament). (see kamálig, hayúbháyub).
To lie on one's back, to lie supine, lie face upward. Pakáynga ang bátà. Turn the baby face upwards. Lay the baby on its back. (see kayâ).
Shock, start, surprise; to be shocked or surprised. (see kibút, pamalúng, hanguyús, búlung, tingála).
Exposed to the wind, open. (see ábong).
