To be taken by surprise, be startled, be taken aback, receive a shock. Nakayás siá. He was taken by surprise-or-he was startled. (see kuyús, hanguyús, kibút, pangyós, panglígbos).
To trail, sweep the floor, be dragged along the ground. Ang íya sáble, sáya, etc., nagakáyat. His sword, her skirt, etc., is trailing on the ground. (see gánoy, gúyud).
Devils, hell; devilish-, diabolical-, acts or behaviour; great hardship, distress, anguish, torture, torment. (see yáwà).

To scratch and scrape like chickens, to use one's fingers in a similar way. Kaykayá ang dútà. Scratch and scrape the earth together. Kaykayí ang kamóti. Dig the sweet potato out with your fingers. Ikáykay akó sang gamót siníng tanúm nga himulák. Please dig out with your fingers the root of this flowering plant for me. (see karáykay).
A beggar, petitioner, haggler, one who always asks for some privileges, gifts, discount or the like. (see ayô).
See kayót.
Rice-cutter, sickle, reaping-hook, a small semicircular knife used for cutting off ears of rice.
Small, little. (see diótay, isót, ikî, tikî, magamáy).
A small young pigeon or dove.
To shrink, shrivel, contract; shrug (the shoulders); cross one's arms, cover (the chest, etc.). (see kúpus, panimókò).
Softness, tenderness. (see yúm-uk, kahómok, kalum-ok).
A young louse, the young of "kúto" or "botól". (see kúto, botól, lusâ),
Dark, darkish brown, dun, tanned, sunburnt. (see ilómilóm).
To shrivel, etc. See kayúgpus.
A kind of creeper.
To crawl, creep, wriggle, move along the ground on hands and feet. (see káyus-a kind of creeper).
A moan, groan, sigh. (yuyó).
Sweetness, tenderness, mildness, kindheartedness, evenness and mildness of temper. (yúyum).

(Sp. quebra, quiebra) Breakage, breaking loose or asunder; loss, shrinkage; failure, bankruptcy; to break asunder, be severed from; to become less, shrink; to fail in business, become bankrupt. Indì mo pagkebrahón ang kinitáan sang mga tápì. Don't force asunder the joints of the planks. Nagkébra ang íya komérsyo. His business failed. Nagkébra ang humáy sing tagisá ka gántang ang pásong. The rice shrunk one ganta to the bushel. (see púto, ángkat, kúpus, kúlpà).
(Sp. queja, quejarse) See under kíha.
(Sp. querida,-o) Beloved, sweetheart, liked; love, lover, love-partner; paramour, concubine, correspondent.
(Sp. querida,-o) Beloved, sweetheart, liked; love, lover, love-partner; paramour, concubine, correspondent.
(Sp. querida,-o) Beloved, sweetheart, liked; love, lover, love-partner; paramour, concubine, correspondent.
(Sp. queso) Cheese.

Gentle, soft, slight, little; to do gently, tease slightly, make another a little angry or the like. Maunáuná kiámpaw, bálus matámà. (Proverb) Such a beginning such an end. Some who mean only to warm, burn themselves. (Literally: At first a little (quarrel or the like), then as a result very much trouble).
See luát. Walâ gid níya pagkiáni kon walâ níya makúhà inâ. He would not have-yielded,-been satisfied, if he had not succeeded in getting that (it).
To limp, hobble, walk lamely, trudge. (see ikángíkang, kunád).
Dead branches and roots, drift-wood, weeds, debris, rubbish piled up or swept along by a current of water; dry stalks of sugar-cane. (see siápò-Bagasse).
To take or cut off a little. Kiási akó sing kalabása, lángkà, tosíno, etc. Cut off for me a piece of squash, jackfruit, bacon, etc. (see kíyas id.).
Dim. and Freq. of kías. To cut off piece by piece or little by little.
Kitten, young cat, kitty.

To move the shoulders up and down, to rock, undulate, pulsate; a rocking motion or movement. Ang kiáy sang túbig sa baybáyon. The rise and fall of the water on the sea-shore. Nagakiáy siá sang íya abága. She moves her shoulders up and down. (see kiáy-kíay).
To walk about or promenade ostentatiously moving the body and buttocks in an affected manner.
To tremble, be shocked; to astonish, surprise, take aback. Kiníbang siá. He was taken by surprise, was taken aback. (see kibút, tingála).
See kíbyas.

To be supported insecurely on a narrow ledge, be but slightly connected, hang by a thread, be in danger of having the connection severed. Nagakibít na lang iníng págbo sá halígì, sa baláyan, etc. This rafter rests only on a narrow ledge of the post, girder, etc. Indì mo pagpakíbton ang baláyan sa halígi, kóndì pasámlon mo gid. Don't permit the girder to rest on the edge of the post, but put it on far enough to secure it well. Walâ man mabálì ang íya bútkon, kóndì nakíbtan lang. His arm was not entirely broken, but only dislocated.
To fly to a great distance, be hurled (flung) far away. (see tisíl, táyog).
To nibble, gnaw. Ang ilagâ nagkíbkib sang tinápay. The rat nibbled at the bread. Ginkibkibán sang idô ang túl-an. The dog gnawed the bone to bits and devoured it. (see ót-ot).
Callous, hard, leathery, horny, thick-skinned, having the skin hardened or thickened by constant pressure or friction like farmers, etc. (kíbul, kibúlon).
A throb, pulsation, beat (of the pulse, the heart, etc.); to throb, etc. Malúya na ang kibô (pagkibô) sang íya nga púlso. His pulse is weak.
Dim. and Freq. of kibô.
See kibít.
A callus, thick or hardened skin, to be or become callous. Nakíblan (nakibúlan) ang íya mga kamót sa dáyon nga pagpangabúdlay. His hands became horny from constant work. (see kíblon, kibúlon).
See kíblon id.
To surround, besiege, beleaguer, blockade, shut up in, enclose, encircle. (see líkup, kabán, líbut).
(H) To get a shock, be surprised, be startled, to start, jump. Nakibút siá sang pagkabatî níya siná. He got a shock when he heard that. (see kayás, panguyús, pangyós, kuyús).
To mutter, murmur, utter indistinctly. Nagakíbut siá sing mga palangadíon. He is muttering some prayers.
To pout, murmur, complain. (see kúmud).
Dim. and Freq. of kibút. Also: To quiver, tremble, move in agitation. Nagakibútkíbut ang íya bibíg. His lips are quivering.

To strike at a tangent, miss the centre, hit only the edge or corner, graze; missing the centre, grazing, hitting or cutting the edge. Indì mo pagpakibyasán sang binángon ang kawáyan, kóndì biálon mo sa tungâ. Don't strike to one side the bamboo with the bolo, but split it in the middle. Nagkíbyas lang ang bála sa íya bútkon. The bullet merely grazed his arm. Ginlabô nía siá sang binángon, ápang kíbyas lang ang pagtupâ. He struck him with the bolo, but it was only a glancing blow.
(B) To mend, repair, set to rights. (see kaáyo, kaídan).
Cooked to a turn, neither too hard nor too soft, but just right, well-done, said of eatables; to be or become nice, tasty, etc.
To recline or sit comfortably in an arm-chair, etc. Kidángi lang ang butáka kag magtúlug, kon malúyag ka. Just make yourself comfortable in the arm-chair and go to sleep, if you wish.
Dim. and Freq. of kídang.
To cut in thin slices, to slice very thin and fine. Kidkirá (-idá) ang támbò. Slice the bamboo-shoot very thin. (see kíhad, ád-ad, kías, kíyas).
To spark, emit sparks, twinkle, sparkle, scintillate. (see ídlab, kídlas).
See kídlab.
See kídlab, ígpat, ínggat.

To go about peering, as when looking for something lost, to move, stir, be restless. Anó ang ginakídos mo sa plása? what are you looking for on the public square? Hinúgay sang kídos. Be quiet. Don't keep moving or stirring. Don't fidget. (see lághap, húlag, etc.).
Dry, etc. See kigás

Very dry, hard, exsiccated; to be or become very dry. Pahalmokí ang tabákò nga kigás. Soften the dry tobacco-leaves. Nagkigás ang tabákò, kay walâ mo pagbalahósi sing maáyo. The tobacco-leaves became quite dry, because you did not wrap them up well. (see layâ, layóng, báskug, kusúg).
See kibút, kíbut.

To tear asunder, separate the fibres, strip hemp, etc. Kigihá-or-kígya ang lánot, magí, pínya, etc. Strip the hemp, maguey, pine-apple leaves, etc. Kigií (kígyi, kigihí) akó siníng lánot. Strip this hemp for me.
etc. From kigí-to strip (hemp, etc.).

(Sp. queja, quejarse) Accusation, complaint, charge, imputation, inculpation, denunciation, citation, arraignment, impeachment, indictment; to accuse, bring before a court or judge, institute a lawsuit; to complain, express dissatisfaction. Ikíha siá sa hukóm. Accuse him before the judge. Kiháhi ang hukmánan sang maláin nga ginbúhat ni Fuláno. Lodge a complaint with the court against N.N.'s evil deed.

To cut into slices, to slice, carve. Kihára (-áda) ang kapáyas, kalabása, lángkà, tinápay, etc. Slice the papaw, squash, jack-fruit, bread, etc. Mansánas nga kiníhad. Sliced apples. (see ád-ad, kídkid, gulút, láplap).
See kíhad.
Tartar, the film that collects on the teeth and which is easily removed by cleaning the teeth frequently.

Cicada, cicala; grass hopper, cricket. Ang kíkik nga maitúm nagahuní sa gáb-i, ang maputî sa ikapúlò ka táknà sa ága, ang borók sa kaagáhon. The black cicada chirps at night, the white one at ten o'clock in the morning and the speckled one early in the morning.
Pertaining to or covered with "kíkì".
A flash. See kiráb.
A dish of coconut-meat mixed with toddy; the verb is "pangilábò"-to eat coconut-meat mixed with palm-wine. (see kulábò).

(B) To look about curiously or searchingly. Anó ang ginakílag mo? Why are you looking about so curiously (or distractedly)? Indì ka magkílag sa simbáhan. Don't look about in church. Nagkílag siá sa mga baláy nga dalágkù kag sa hinálì nadalasâ sang trak. He was looking curiously at the large houses and suddenly he was run over by the truck. (see lísi, língas).
The pomelo with reddish pulp. Dálhi akó sing kabúgaw nga kilála. Bring me a pomelo with reddish pulp.

To know, recognize, recollect, be acquainted with; an acquaintance, a person known. Kilála ko siá. I know him-or-He is an acquaintance of mine. Nakakilála ka sa íya? Do you know him? Ginakilála mo si Fuláno? Do you know N.N.? Kilaláha siá. Make his acquaintance. Magkilalaháy kamó. Get to know each other. Nakakilála siá sing madámù nga mga tanúm. He knows many plants. Kinilála nga táo. A man well known. Ipakilála ko sa ímo si Fuláno. I am going to introduce you to Mr. N.N. May nakilál-an siá sa amó nga bánwa. He has some acquaintances in that town. Indì akó magkilála sa íya. I do not wish to recognize him-or-I'll give him the cold shoulder.
To sparkle, etc. See kilángkílang.
To shine, glisten, twinkle, sparkle. (see igpátígpat, kipát-kípat, ínggat).

A sudden movement, start or jerk; electricity; electrical; to give a sudden start or jerk as if shocked by an electrical current. Nagkilás ang íya láwas, kay nangilát. He gave a sudden start, because it lightened. Ang síya nga kilás-or-Ang síyang-kilás. The electric chair, used to execute criminals. Kakilás sang íya mga matá! How shifty his eyes are! His eyes seem to be always moving as if he were in danger. (Said of murderers and other criminals or the like).
Unsteady, easily upset, said of small boats without outriggers, or the like.
Lightning, bolt, flash of lightning. (The verb is pangilát.

To eat raw fish or meat. Malúyag ka magkílaw sing ísdà? Would you like to eat some raw fish? Sa dakû nga kadalók kinílaw níya ang báboy. Very greedily he ate some raw pork. Kiláwa lang ang gunô. Simply eat some raw "gunô".
To burn dimly, give but little light. (see kíraw, kiráwkiráw, kírot, kirótkírot).
A young hen beginning to be broody. (see sumaláyhaw-a young cock; pisô, sulúg, agák, mungâ, manók).
The edge of a sickle or scythe.
The eyebrows. (see amimilók-eyelashes; pangiláy, pinangiláyay).
Nervous, excitable, easily upset; surprising, shocking, startling. (see kibút).
Side, flank, beam, quarter. Sa kílid sang baláy. At the side of the house. Ari siá dirí sa ákon kílid (luyó). He is here at my side. (see luyó).
To lean against, have the back supported by pillows, etc.
Things to mend or in need of repair. (see kaídan, kíd-an, kaalayohón, kiridanón, kalaayohón).
A feather or any other similar instrument used for the operation of "kilíkog". (see kolikóg, kililikóg, kirilikóg).

To clean a small hole or aperture with a feather, etc.; to clean the ears, nose, wounds by means of a cotton-probe or the like. Kilikóga ang ilíg sa dulúnggan sang bátà. Clean the flow from the child's ear. Kilikógi ang dalúnggan sang bátà. Clean the child's ear. (see kolíkog, kolíkot).

(H) To scratch gently (the edge of a wound, of an itching eruption or the like). Indì mo pagkilikóton ang ímo katúl. Don't scratch your "katúl". Ginakilíkot nía ang íya pilás. He is scratching the edge of his wound. (see kálot, kolíkot, kilíkog).
(H) See kilikóg id.
(H) Wants, needs, necessaries, requirements, what is lacking, required or necessary. (see kinahánglan).
The month of April. (see abríl).
The ring attached to the traces and through which ring the rein or nose-rope is passed; a steadying device put on a kite, so that it may fly straight and smooth.
To tinkle, tingle, jingle, ring (said of small bells).
(H) Closure; constrictor ani. (see kípot).
(H) To wash or clean hulled rice previous to boiling it. (see balónas id.; kísli, kiníslan, etc.-balonási, binalonásan, etc.).
Calesa, rig, cab, a two-wheeled and one-horse vehicle for the conveyance of passengers.
(H) Juncture, junction, meeting, juxtaposition, seam, joint, coming together, position side by side. (kítà; see kinitáan).
(H) Place of meeting, trysting-place, rendez-vous. (see kítà).

(H) What is to be joined, connected or brought together. Kilitáon pa iníng mga tápì. These boards have to be joined yet. Kilitáon pa si Hosé kag si Andres. José and Andres are to meet still, have to be brought together yet. (kítà).

A rough fish-skin, usually of the pági-fish, used to rub and smooth wood, etc. after the manner of sand-paper; to clean, smooth, rub boards, etc. with fish-skin or sand-paper. Kilkigí ang tápì, agúd magtínlò. Rub the board with fish-skin to make it smooth.
To gnaw, nibble, bite to pieces. See kíbkib.
Side, border, brim, edge, flank. (see kílid, kólod, bíbì, bígki).

Tiny, small, diminutive, slender, applied to roundish and oblong objects like bananas, fingers, etc. Kímay ang íya mga túdlò-or-kímay siá sing túdlò. He has very small fingers, his fingers are too slender in proportion to his size. Also verb. Nagkímay ang isá níya ka bútkon sang pagbutí sa íya. One of his arms has become quite thin since he had small-pox.
To eat slowly and little, take food leisurely and in small quantity.
Dim. and Freq. of kimít. Indì mo pagkimítkimitón ang pagkáon. Dont eat so slowly and so little.

(Sp. quimón) Kimono, Japanese garment for both sexes resembling a lady's dressing gown; a short-sleeved, buttonless woman's upper dress with just a hole for putting the head through and reaching down to the waist, as often worn by Philippine women.
To move to and fro or up and down, fluctuate, undulate, pulsate, oscillate, rock or pitch. (see linggílinggi).
Dim. and Freq. of kímpa.
See kímpa.
Dim. and Freq. of kímpang. (see lumpálúmpa).
Maimed, mutilated, etc. See kímpul, kúmpul.
A pair of pincers, pliers, nippers, tweezers; to use or apply pincers; to pinch. Kimpíton ko ang ímong ilóng. I'll pinch your nose.

Mutilated, maimed, having parts, ends, corners or edges broken or cut off; to break off ends, etc., to mutilate or become mutilated, to dock. Nagkímpul ang íya túdlò. His finger is mutilated. Kimpulá ang íkog sang idô. Dock the dog's tail. Kimpulí ang manók sang íya íkog, agúd makilála nga áton. Cut off part of the cock's tail, so that it may be recognized as ours. (see kúmpul).
(H) To frown, sulk, be offended, take ill, murmur, complain, pout, scowl, fume, resent, take-ill,-to heart,-amiss,-umbrage,-offence,-exception,-in bad part. (see kúmud, kósmod).

A prefix frequently used to form (abstract) nouns and (intransitive) verbs, e.g. kinabúdlay-toil; to toil (budlay); kinasádya-mirth, merriment, celebration; to make merry, etc. (sádya); kinagánsal-noise, boisterousness; to be noisy, etc. (gánsal), etc. etc.
Learning, knowledge, wisdom, education, cleverness. (álam; kaálam, kinaálam).
(H) See kinaádman-learning, etc.
(H) Habit, custom, practice, manner, behaviour, usage. (see ánad, batásan, kinabatásan).
Goodness; benefit, advantage. (see áyo, kaáyo).
Like-, in the form of-, a kabásì-fish; sharppointed. Bángkaw nga kinabasî. A lance with a straight, sharp point. (see kabásì, pinángdan).

Childhood, pertaining to childhood or to children, childlike, childish, silly; from childhood, since one's birth. Ang pagkasungî sináng táo kinabátà níya. That man-is hare-lipped from his birth,-was born hare-lipped. (see bátà, bataón).
Custom, manner, habit, behaviour. (see kabatásan, kinaanáran).
Tribe, bunch, crowd, troop, company, flock, herd; by tribes, etc. (see kabón).

Life, mode or manner of one's life, living conditions; to live, remain, stay, reside, lead a-, pass one's-, life. Nagakinabuhî silá sing matáwhay. They are leading -a tranquil life, -a happy life. Magbuligáy kamó, agúd magtáwhay kag maglinóng ang ínyo pagkinabuhî. Help each other, that you may live a tranquil and peaceful life. (see buhî, búhì, pangabúhì, kabúhì).
Life, period from birth to death. (see kabúhì).
Noisy shouting, disturbance, confusion. (burígal). Kinaburígal kag linabugáyay. Confused noise and melée.
Boisterousness; to be noisy, rowdy. See kinaburígal.
Excitement, stir, disturbance, trouble; to be excited, be in commotion. (see buróka).
Oldness, antiquity; old, ancient, of old, of yore, of long ago, bygone. Batásan nga kinadáan. An old custom. (see dáan, dumáan).
Multitude; many. (see dámò, madámò, kadámò).
Bite, wound from a bite, place where one has been bitten. Ang kinádtan sang idô sa bátà naghubág. The place where the child was bitten by the dog has swelled. (kagát).
Commotion, disturbance, trouble, uproar, riot. (gamó; see kagamó, kagarokán).
Stir, commotion, uproar, confusion, excitement; to make an uproar, be excited. (see gúbot).
Noise, uproar, commotion, boisterous proceedings, row; to be noisy, excited, rowdy. (see gúlà, kinagamó, kagarokán, kinagúbot).
Seniority, priority of birth, state of being older. (see kinamagulangán, kinagúrang id.).
(B) See kinagúlang.
The end, termination or last of anything, as the last grain of rice, the last centavo, etc. (see hiringítyon, katalipuspusán, katapúsan).

Need, lack, want, indispensability, necessity; to have need of, stand in need of, be necessary, require, entail, call for. Anó ang kinahánglan mo? What do you want?-or-what is it you need? Kinahánglan gid nga magkádto ka dídto. You must go there-or-it is necessary for you to go there. Pilá ka butáng ang kinahánglan sa ...? How many things are required for...? Kon magkinanánglan ka sing kwárta--If you need some money--.
Tree-like; to develop into a tree-like shrub. Iníng sibúkaw nagakinahóykáhoy na. This sebucao is developing into a tree. (see káhoy).
One's own affairs, proper to oneself, selfishness, individualism, egotism. (see íya, kaugalíngon).
Cheating, trickery; tricksy; hypocrite; to cheat, trick, defraud, obtain by fraud or foul play. (see kákoy).
Superiority, advantage, preeminence, predominancy, advance over, odds. (see labáw).
Disadvantage, drawback, hindrance, damper, wet blanket, objection. (see láin, kinaáyo-advantage, etc.)
Worldly, earthly, earthy, secular, natural and carnal as opposed to the supernatural and spiritual. (kalibútan).
Mercy, pity, compassion, ruth, clemency, commiseration, tenderness of heart. May kinaló-oy siá-or-nagakaló-oy siá sa napílas. He has pity upon the wounded man. (see ló-oy, kaló-oy).
To taste, try the taste of. Nagakínam siá sing páhò, ginakínam níya ang páhò. He is trying the taste of a mango. See kinámkínam which is more in use.

Dim. and Freq. of kínam. Kinámkináma iníng ságing, kon malúyag ka sang íya sabór. Try the taste of this banana and see whether you like its flavour. Kinámkinámi (tilawí) sing diótay iníng súman. Taste a little of this suman-dish. (see tiláw).
Seniority, etc. See kinagúlang id.
Justice, right, reason, argument, proof. (see katarúngan).
The cause of death, what kills or causes death. Ang ános amó ang íya nga kinamatáy. Consumption was the cause of his death. (see patáy).
The place or reason of one's death. (see patáy).
Fight, quarrel, row; to fight, etc. (see kinaburúka, kinagamó, kinagúlà, áway, sinambúnut).
Like a buffalo; a kind of "úbi" with a covering like the skin of a buffalo. (see karbáwon).
To behave like a buffalo; buffalo-like, according to the ways and manners of a buffalo.

(B) Past events, past time, the past, things of long ago, of yore; old, of old, bygone, ancient, out of date. Ang kinarádto--. Things or events or customs, etc. of long ago. Sa kinarádto nga batásan--. According to an ancient custom--. Sa kinarádto--. Formerly, in former, olden or bygone days--. (see sádto, sinádto, karágto, sinágto, tinó-o).
(B) See kinarádto id.
(B) See kinarabáw-buffalo-like, etc.
Litigation, legal contests, disputes, etc.; to litigate, etc. (see kasábà).
Married, wedded; wedlock, nuptials, matrimony, marriage, wedding, wedding-feast, marriage-feast. (see kasál, kalasálon, kasamiénto, pangasáwa, mínyo).
Worthiness, excellence, dignity; capacity, capability, quality of being up to the standard of. (see takús, kasángkol).
The nature of man; natural, human, pertaining to-, referring to-, man, from birth, congenital; parts-, organs-, of generation, genitals, sexual organs. (see táo, kinatúbò, taohánon).
Birth-day. (táo).
Human, pertaining to human nature. (táo).
etc. See kinatáo, kinataóhan, etc. (táo-táwo).

Nature; natural, growing or developing naturally. Labáw inâ sa kintúbò sang táo. That is beyond or above the nature of man, that is preternatural. Kinatúbò (kinaugálì) sang táo ang pagsayúp. To err is human, is natural to man. (see túbò, kinaugálì).
Difference, etc. See katúhay, katuháyan.
Natural peculiarity, nature, idiosyncrasy, personal or individual characteristic; habit, custom, manner. (ugálì).
A banquet, feasting, conviviality, eating in common, mess; to feast. (see káon,
To glisten, sparkle, shine. (see kánaw).
Dim. and Freq. of kínaw-to glisten. (see kanáw-kanáw).
A kettleful; by the kettle or cauldron. (see káwà).
Lack, need, want, what one needs or lacks. (walâ).
(H) See kinawád-on.
Stealing, robbing, burglary; to steal, rob (of many). (see káwat).
To glisten, sparkle, shine, twinkle. (see kídlab, ídlab, ínggat, ígpat).
(Sp. quinque) Lamp, table-lamp, light. (see sugâ, solô, paról).

To grasp or take hold of very carefully with two or three fingers for fear of soiling one's hands, etc.; to be averse to touching unclean things, be fastidious. Indì ka magkíngking sa pagpúlut sinâ kay dílì man makalolóod. Don't be afraid to pick that up, for it is not at all loathsome.
To lift-, raise-, one's leg (as if to give a kick); to hop, jump, stand (on one leg).
To hobble along, limp, halt, walk lamely. (see kunád, íkang).
To shrug, jerk one's shoulders, give a start as one tickled. Itíka siá, agúd magkínhol. Tickle him and make him jump. Pakinholá ang íya láwas. Startle him.
To economize, stint, be niggardly, live very frugally. Indì ka magkínì sing lakás sang ímo pagkáon, kay magalúya ang ímo láwas. Don't live too frugally, for you will become weak. (see kínot, kínit).
Dim. and Freq. of kínì.
The waste or useless remnants of stripped fibre, as of hemp, maguey, etc. (see kigí).
The water in which hulled rice has been washed. (kilís; see balinónas).
(Sp. quinina) Quinine. (see bitâ).
Savings, something saved or hoarded (through economy, frugality, etc. see kínot).
To sparkle, twinkle. (kipátkípat; see igpátígpat).
Life; breath of life; stomach. (cf: tirúsdak, tinúsdak, hinurángus, gináhab, ginháwa, solóksolók, kabúhì).
See kínì, kínot.
Dim. and Freq. of kínit. Kinítkiníti sing mantékà ang manók. Use only little lard for the chicken. (see kinîkínì, kinótkínot).

Earnings; junction, juncture, seam, joint, joining, meeting together. Ang kinitáan sang mga mamumugón mapúslan sang búg-os nga bánwa. The earnings of the working population are of advantage to the whole commonwealth. Ang kinitáan sang tápì. The board-seam. (kítà; see kilitáan).
To play the "kiyánò-game".
See kíngke-lamp, light.
(Sp. quino) Kino, cinchona, peruvian bark.
To be noisy, boisterous, rowdy, (of movements like running, stamping, rushing, etc, but not of voices). Indì kamó magkinólas. Don't make so much noise. (see kólas).
To brag, boast, praise oneself and one's own. Pamatíi, nagakinolás na man siá. Listen, he is boasting again.

Stir, movement with some noise; to stir, move rather noisily. Nagahinulághúlag kag nagakinolás-kólas na ang mga nagapapílì. The candidates for election are already on the move and making some stir. (see kólas, koláskólas).
Comical, ludicrous; to play a comedy, trick, make a farce of. (see komédya).
To economize, etc. See kínì.
Dim. and Freq. of kínot. (see kinîkínì).
(Sp. quinto, quintar) The law of requisition for military purposes; to draft men for-, press into-, service. Nakintosán siá sídto ánay. He was drafted for military service in bygone days.
Made as pointed or as sharp as cogon-grass; the point of a spear, lance, arrow, etc. (see kógon).
The cry of a large bat, as of the fruit bat or flying fox. (see kúkik).
Relationship through affinity or affiliation. (kumpári).
Crease fold, wrinkle, plait. (see kunút, piníd-an).
Wrinkled, creased; miserly, stingy, close-fisted. Kinuripót nga batásan. A miserly habit. (see kuripót).
The place or part that has been stung or bitten by a mosquito or the like. (see kútut).
Stir, movement, noise. Silá íla walâ gid sing kinuyúng-kúyung, kóndì naghípus lang silá. They for their part did not make any stir, but remained silent or quiet.
To abstract, purloin, filch, pinch, pilfer, steal, (see tíkas, takáb, tákaw, káwat, káwtì, kúhà).
To twinkle, shine, glitter, sparkle, emit flashes of light. (see igpátígpat, bádlak, ínggat, kídlab, kíndab).
See kitáw-kítaw, kitáw-kitawón.
To cross the legs; to sit or stand with crossed legs.
Dim. and Freq. of kípì. Also: to gather one's dress, etc. See kupîkúpì.
To close, shut, draw together, pull tight (by means of a running string or the like. (see kípot).
To shut, close. Kipóta ang matá, bâbâ, ganháan, bintánà, baúl, etc. Close the eye, the mouth, the door, the window, the trunk, etc. (see kíum).

Maimed, mutilated, docked, having a part cut off or shortened as feathers, hair, tails, arms, legs or the like; to be or become maimed; to maim, cut off a piece, etc. Kipoyá ang íkog sang manók. Cut off part of the cock's tail. (see kímpul).
See kíd-ol.

To flash, emit a flash or spark of light; a flash or spark. Ang kilát nagakiráb. The lightning flashes. Sang pagtupâ sang wásay sa bató nagkiráb ang kaláyo. When the hatchet hit the stone, it struck fire from it. Pakirabá ang isá ka asúgi. Strike a match. Nakítà ko ang kiráb sang sugâ. I saw the flash of the light.
A sudden flame or light, spark, flash, flare-up; transient, transitory, momentary, ephemeral, not lasting or enduring, passing quickly, soon over, (as the burning of cogon-grass).
Spark, flash, sudden flame or light; sparking, flashing, as lightning, a gun, a flash-light, etc.

To burn dimly, give but a dull, feeble, low light, to glimmer. Nagakíraw ang kíngke. The lamp burns but dimly. Pakiráwa ang sugâ. Dim the light. Make the light shine less bright (by turning down the wick, etc.). (see kírot).
Dim. and Freq. of kíraw. (see kirótkírot).
See kiláy, kílay.
(B) To quiver, tremble, shake, shudder. Nagkiréu ang íya láwas. His body trembled. Nagakiréu ang íya matá. His eye is quivering. (kíryo id.).
See kiréu.
Open-eyed, wide-eyed, having wide open eyes as a natural peculiarity. Kírhat siá sing matá. He has wide open eyes.

Small, undersized, dwarfish, below standard size (of fruits, etc). Báklon ko iníng mga páhò, ápang kuháon ánay ang mga torakón kag kiribúd. I am going to buy these mangoes, but the rotten and undersized ones must first be taken away. (see kímay-small, slender, (of fingers, etc.).
(H) See kilidanón (see kaídan, kíd-an, karaidanón, kaalayohón).
See koridíg-stunted, etc.
A pin. (see sibít, turúbok, alpilír).
A small lobster. (see karitót, koritót).
See kilíkot id. Kirikóta ang hígkò sa kinitáan sang tápi-or-kirikóti ang kinitáan sang tápì sang hígkò. Pick the dirt out from between the board-seams.
Wrinkled, shrivelled, creased; a wrinkle, crease. (see koritót).
See kilikóg, kililikóg.
To slice, cut off a piece. Kirisá ang kárne. Slice or cut the meat. Kirisí akó sing duhá ka kirís sa páa sang báka. Cut for me two slices off the leg of beef. (see gulút).
To wrinkle, shrivel, shrink, form creases, said of skin, leaves, fruits, clothes, etc. (see korítot).
See kíraw. Pakiróta ang kíngke. Dim the light of the lamp.
Dim. and Freq. of kírot. (see kiráwkiráw).
(Sp. querubin) Cherub.
To tremble, quiver. See kiréu.
Also: gingerly, bashful, shy, timid; to move about shyly or timidly, etc.
Dim. and Freq. of kíryo.
(H) Once in a while, sometimes, now and then. Kon kís-a--. Now and again--. (see kaisá).
(Sp. quizame) Ceiling, plafond.
Gold beads, sequins (usually flat and thin). Kilála mo yanáng babáe nga nagapangolíntas sang kisáp? Do you know that lady that wears a golden necklace-or-that has gold beads in her necklace?
To open and shut the eyes rapidly, to blink, twinkle. (see pisók).
Dim. and Freq. of kísap. (see pamisókpisók).
Nimble, lithe, agile, quick, swift (of movement); to be nimble, etc.
Dim. and Freq. of kisáy. Also: to trip, skip, move with light quick steps. (see págsi, líksi).
(H) To frown, sulk, pout, look cross or angry. (see lárong, ariwaróng, kósmod, kúmud, kolisáw, súnggud, súngon).
A very fine awl, drill or bit, any thin and sharp-pointed tool.
To rub (between the palms of the hand) rice before boiling or the like. (see pilípis).
To scrape, rub with something sharp. Kiskisá sang kotsílyo ang hígkò sa látok. Scrape the dirt off the table with a knife. Kiskisí ang báboy sang íya búlbul. Scrape the pig clean of its bristles.
etc. From kilís-to wash (clean) rice, etc.
Plait or fold in a garment, loop, ornamental doubling in fringes, various decorations made of paper, ribbons, etc.
See késo-cheese.
A kind of grass often fed to pigs.
(B) Sour; to be or become sour. Nakisomán akó siníng ísdà, kay napatám-an (natám-an) sing lánggaw. I find this fish very sour, for too much vinegar has been put into it. (see áslum).
(Sp. sacristan) Sacristan.
See kisólkísol.
(B) See kisóm.

To see, behold, discern, perceive, descry, sight, make out, discover, distinguish, spy, espy, set one's eyes upon; to meet, find. Nakakítà ka na sa íya? Did you see or meet him? Hóo, nakakitaáy na kamí. Yes, we met or saw each other. Ang alipokpokán sang búkid índì makítà kay natabúnan sang gál-um. The top of the mountain cannot be seen, because it is covered by the cloud. Nakítà-or-nakít-an ko siá dídto. I saw him there. Dílì na siá makakítà sa pagbása. He can no longer see to read. Ang íya nga balatían daw sa índì na makitáan sing bulúng. It will be almost impossible to find a remedy for his disease-or-his sickness is, I think, past cure. Diín mo inâ makíta?-Kinítà ko inâ sa dálan. Where did you see or find it?-I found it there on the road. Ang nagapangítà makakítà. He who seeks shall find. Sa yanáng bakólod kitáon mo túbtub ang simbáhan sa Ogtón. From that hill yonder you can even see the church of Oton. (see tán-aw, túluk-to see, inspect, look at).

Trial, hearing (of a case in court); to try, hear (a case in court or the like). Buás kitáon ang íya nga kasábà. His case will be tried tomorrow. Ang pagkítà sang kasábà. The hearing (trial) of the case.

We; including the person or persons spoken to. Kitá áton-or-kitá sing áton-or-kitáy áton-We for our part--As far as we are concerned--. Kitá nga tanán. All of us. Sa katapúsan kitá gid kag dílì silá ang nakadaúg sa kasábà. The upshot is that we, and not they, are the ones that have won the case (or lawsuit).
Visible. (see kítà).

(Sp. quitar) To remove, take away, separate, put aside. Sang pagísip níla sang mga ságing nga íla baláklon ginkitár níla ang mga sinipî nga magágmay. When they counted the bananas they were going to buy, they put the small clusters apart. (see kúhà, bulág, báhin).
To be dim, hazy, in the far distance, indistinct (of sights and sounds).
Scarcely perceptible, dim, hazy, indistinct, visible-in the far distance,-in contour,-in indistinct outlines; not clear or distinct (of sounds), scarcely audible.
Narrowness; narrow; to be or become narrow. Nakitirán (-idán) akó siní. This is too narrow for me. This seems to be too narrow.
See kilíkog, kilíkot-to clean a hole, a wound, etc. by means of a feather, a small stick or the like.
The very small chili with an exceedingly hot taste. Dinálhan níya akó sing katúmbal nga kitikót. He brought me very small and hot chilis.

To grumble, croak, clamour, mutter, growl, murmur, complain in the hope of getting redress. Ginkitíkot níya ang ákon báhin, kay, konó, labán ang ákon báhin. He complained about my share, for, he said, my share was larger than his. (see yámo).
The chief tendon connecting the calf with the heel; to cut that tendon, to hamstring. Kitiní ang karabáw sang binángon. Cut the buffalo's tendon with the bolo-or-Hamstring the buffalo.
To gnaw, nibble, bite to pieces. (see ót-ot, kíbkib, kílkil).
To shut, close. Kiúma ang bábà mo. Shut your mouth. (see kípot).
To raise with a lever, crowbar, spar of wood, etc. Kiwáli sang bára ang bató. Raise the stone with the crowbar. Ikíwal ang báhì sa halígi. Use your dibble to lever the post.
Awry, twisted, etc. See kiwî.
Turned or twisted aside, awry, oblique, inclined, sloping, slanting, leaning, canting, crooked. (see hiwî, sambigî).
A kind of squirrel. Ang kiwíg amó ang isá ka sápat nga malábà sing pangolíhi kag malíp-ot sing pangúnhan. The "kiwíg" is an animal with long hind-legs and short fore-legs.
(B) To move or bend the body sideways, to twist and turn (as in many folk-dances), to bend, curve. Ikiwô ang láwas mo. Bend your body sideways.
A kind of game that is usually played with nuts of the "dalógdog" and "búgtong". (see kiniyánò-to play that game).
To slice, etc. See kías id.
To steal, pilfer, rob. See kiô. (see káwat, tíkas).
(Sp. clavetes) Small nail, tack, brad.
(Sp. clara) The white of an egg, albumen. (see bátog-the yolk).
(Sp. clarinete) Clarinette, clarinet; clarinet-player.
(Sp. clase) Class, kind, sort, species, brand, variety; class, class-room work, school-hours.
(Sp. clero) Clergy, priesthood. Ang kléro nga sekulár kag regulár. The secular and regular clergy. (see kaparían).
(Sp. clima) Clime, climate. (see hángin, kahangínan).
Mine, of me, etc. (See ákon, nákon).
Curve, fold, plait; enclosure, entrenchment, fence. (see kobál).

To form curves, waves and creases as a mat, an uneven ground or the like. Anó na man ang sa idálum sang mantél, kay nagakobál sa tungâ? What is lying under the tablecloth, because there is a bump in the middle?
To scratch lightly with the finger-tips not using the nails. Kobkobá ang likód ko, kay makatúl. Scratch my back, for it itches. (see kálot, karós).
To flap the wings and splash or bathe as a bird in shallow water. Ang mungâ nagakóbo sa talámnan. The hen is flapping its wings and splashing in the rice-field.

Dim. and Freq. of kóbo. To flutter, flap the wings, move with quick vibrations or undulations. Ang mga gánsa, bíbi, etc. nagakobókóbo sa lúnang. The geese, ducks, etc. are bathing (or splashing) in the mud. Pakobókobóha ang manók sa túbig. Let the chicken splash in the mud (flapping its wings and shaking itself).

To hold on to by the teeth, stick or cling to as a leech, a pair of pincers, the claws of a lobster, etc. Ang katáng nagkóbot sa ákon kamót. The crab held on firmly to my hand. Ang bintósa nagakóbot na sa likód sang masakít nga táo. The cupping glass is now firmly attached to the sick man's back. Pakobóta ang tándok sa bútkon sang bátà. Apply the cupping glass to the child's arm. Pinakóbot níla ang tándok sa páa sang bátà, agúd makúhà ang dálit sang kinádtan sang idô. They put a cupping glass on the boy's leg in order to draw off the poison from the place bitten by the dog.
(Sp. cobre) Copper.

(Sp. cubrir) Cover, protection; to coyer, shield, protect. Ipakóbre sa kapitán iníng napúlò ka soldádo-or-kobrehí ang kapitán siníng napúlò ka soldádo. Protect the captain with these ten soldiers. Ang mga soldádo nagakobrehánay. The soldiers are covering each other.
Kodak, a small photographic apparatus.

(Sp. corral) Fence, hedge, inclosure, yard, corral, pen, fold; to fence or hedge in. Kodalí ang ímo pamulákan. Fence in your garden. Pakodalí ang ímo pamulákan. Have a fence made around your garden. Ikodál mo iníng kawáyan sa ímo pamulákan. Use this bamboo to make a fence for your garden.
Dim. and Freq. of kodál.
To scrape, shred, grate, rasp, scoop out with some sharp tool. Kodkorá (-dá) ang sulúd sang lubí. Scoop out the meat of the coconut. (see kokód id).
A grater, shredder, scraper, scoop, any tool or instrument used for the action of "kódkod."
(H) See kodkódan.
A game played with six stones and a ball.

To play with stones, throwing them up and catching them in falling down, picking up meanwhile some more lying in front of the players; small gravel is commonly used by children for the purpose of this game. Ang mga bátà nagakodô. The children are playing the game called "kodô". Pakodoá lang ang mga bátà, agúd nga índì maggamó. Let the children play with stones, that they may not be troublesome. (see korô id.).
Dim. and Freq. of kodô.

Uneven, not level, not quite plain or smooth; to be or become uneven, have or form some little prominencies or reliefs. Nagakodól-kodól ang alpómbra. The floor carpet is not quite smooth, has some raised figures or relief-work.

A cloth to cover the head with, head-cover; to cover the head with any kind of cloth. Kodóngi ang úlo mo sang pányo. Cover your head with the kerchief. Kodóngi ang bátà. Cover the child's head. Pakodóngi ang bátà. Have the child's head covered. Ipakódong sa íya iníng tuálya. Cover his head with this towel. (see tákdong, takuróng).

(B) To pinch, compress between thumb and fore-finger, to nip with the finger-nails. Kódta siá. Pinch him. Ginkodót nía akó. He pinched me. Ang kinódtan sa bátà masakít. The place where the child was pinched is painful. (see kosî).
(B) See kodót.
To tie up short, put near, fasten with a short tether. Ikóg-ong ang karabáw sa káhoy. Fasten the buffalo to the tree with a short rope.
A kind of bird.
Bareheaded, uncovered; to walk about bareheaded. Daw kógkog gid lang iníng táo. This man is accustomed to walk about bareheaded.
A kind of long grass, much used for thatching purposes.
(Sp. cojin) Hassock, cushion, pillow, especially one for kneeling on.

Bow-legged, bandy-legged; to be or become bow-legged. Koíng siá. He is bandy-legged. Ang kapitán nagkoíng tungúd sang lakás níya nga pagpangabayó. The captain became bow-legged through too much riding on horseback.
Short-sighted, near-sighted. (see kortabísta).
The cooing of doves; to coo.
A kind of cheap white cloth, white cotton-stuff.
Catarrh, cold with running at the nose. Also verb. Ginakókò siá. He has a cold.
Nail, hoof, claw, talon.
To stoop, bend down. (see kuúb, sungúk, súngroy, sikóktot, dúkoy, dúroy, súngkok).
Hoof, claw, pig's foot. (see kokó).
To grate, scrape, rasp, shell, shred, scoop out. (see kódkod id.; kokorá (-odá)-kodkorá (-oda).
A kind of snail with a white shell. It is often found on trees.
Grater, scraper, rasper, any tool used for shredding or scooping. (see kodkóran id.).

To rasp or rub off with some sharp instrument, to shell, husk, shuck beans, peas or the like. Kokotá ang maís. Scrape off the maize (from the cob). Shuck the corn. Kokotí akó sing kadiós, mónggo, etc. Shell for me some cadiós-peas, monggo, etc. (see kódkod, kokód).
To bathe; to take a bath. (see dígos, palígos).
etc. From kolô-to expand and contract.
(Sp. cola) Glue, mucilage, paste.
(Sp. cola) Tail, train (of a gown, etc.).
(Sp. encolar) To glue, stick, paste; to be (lie, stand, sit) closely attached to. (see kóla, dokót, pilít, kupô).
(H) Coconut-meat mixed with toddy. (see kilábò).
(Probably from the Sp. cola-paste, glue) Cigar, tobacco rolled for smoking. (see abáno, piokós).
Bat. (see kolápnit, kololáknit, kolonáknit, múrtik).
To place, put, lay. Ginkólan níya siá sa isá ka pasungán. She laid him in a manger. Ikólan ang bátà sa duyándúyan. Put the baby in the hammock. (see butáng, pahígdà, tángday, pahámtang).
Bat. See koláknit.
(Sp. collar) Collar. (see kolyár, kwélyo, kolíntas).

To make a noise by walking to and fro, to move audibly or noisily. Ang mga ilagâ, haló, etc. nagakólas sa ibábaw sang kisamí. The rats, iguanas, etc. are moving about noisily above the ceiling. Indì kamó magkólas. Don't be noisy. Indì nínyo akó pagkolásan. Don't disturb me with your noise. Kagáhud sang kalóng sang sibúkaw nga nagakólas sa hángin. What a noise the dry sebucao-pods make rustling in the wind. (see gáhud, galúng).

Dim. and Freq. of kólas. Ginapakoláskólas sang hángin ang mga kawáyan. The wind is stirring and rustling the bamboos. Nagakoláskólas silá dirâ. They are rather noisy over there. (see hulághúlag, gahúdgáhud, litóklitók, etc.).
(Sp. colación) A light repast, collation, snack, bite. (see pamáhaw).
(Sp. culata) The butt of a musket or rifle; to strike with the butt-end. Kulatáha siá. Strike him with the butt.
(Sp. cólera) Cholera.
(Sp. colgadura) Drapery, embroidery, light decorations, hangings, festoons.
(Sp. colegio) College. (see buluthóan).
Anything used for the operation "kolíkog". (see kilikóg).
To bore or clean one's ears, etc. with a feather, the finger or the like. (see kilíkog).
(H) See kolíkog. (see koríkog, kotíkot).
(H) See kolikóg. (see korikót, kilikóg).
(Sp. colindante) Neighbour; adjacent, near, hard-, fast-, by, adjoining, neighbouring, bordering, contiguous. (see katámbi).
(Sp. collar) Necklace, string of pearls; rosary.
(Sp. col, pl. coles) Cabbage.

To twist one's face, wrinkle the brows, make grimaces as if tasting something very sour or sharp. Nakainúm siá sing lánggaw, kay nagakolisáw siá? Has he drunk vinegar, that he makes such a face? (see korisáw).
See kolisáw. Also: To pucker one's lips in anger or passion.
To carry in one's arms. Kolkolá siá. Carry him in your arms. Ikólkol akó ánay siníng bátà. Kindly carry this baby for me in your arms. (see kúgus, kalóngkong).
(B) Fool, ass, idiot, simpleton. (see búang, úmang, tampuháw, hángà, búngaw, pákok, lóko).
A kind of tree.
A large bundle, a load (of cogon-grass, etc.). Katloán ka búgkos manginisá ka kólo. Thirty bunches make a load (of cogon-grass).
To carry something Negrito fashion by means of a string around the forehead. Kolohá-or-kólwa lang ang pinutús. Just carry the parcel in Negrito-fashion.
To expand and contract; to squeeze, compress. Ang lástiko nagaúnyat kag nagakolô. Elastic bands expand and contract. Kól-a ang lubí nga inurá-od. Compress the coconut-meat taken from the shell.
Dim. of kólò-fool, ass, etc. (see buangít).
Side, edge, rim. (see kílid, kílod).
Uneven, hilly, not quite level, plain or smooth, etc. See kodólkodól, boklódbóklod.
(Sp. colocación) Position, employment, service, place, job. (see alagarán, palamúgnan, palangitán-an, pangítà).
To move about fluttering or flapping the wings, take a dust-or water-bath, said especially of geese, ducks, hens and the like. (see kobókóbo, kobókobó).
A kind of plant with very odoriferous flowers.

To tuck up one's trousers, sleeves or the like. Kolokósa ang delárgo mo. Tuck up your trousers. Nagalakát siá nga kinolókos ang pakô sang íya báyò. He walks with the sleeves of his jacket tucked up. (see baláking-to tuck up skirts, sotanas or the like).
The gizzard, principal stomach of a bird. (see batikólon).
What is to be rasped, scraped, shelled, husked, shucked as corn, peas and beans, etc. (kokót).
Bat. (see koláknit).
See koláknit, kololáknit, múrtik.
(Sp. columpio) Rocking chair.
An earthenware pot, especially a rice- or cooking-pot. (see kóron).
(H) Bat. See koláknit, etc.
(H) Curly, woolly, crinkly. Kolóng ang íya bohók. His hair is curly. Ang mga áti kolóng sing bohók. The Negritoes have woolly hair.
(Sp. color) Colour, hue, tint, shade, tinge, dye, complexion. (see duág).
A primitive brush made of half a coconut-husk with the shell removed and used especially for brushing yarn previous to weaving. (kúskus). Also: to rub rather violently, brush.
What is to-, should-, be dug out; tubers, roots. (see kótkot).
(B) See kólò-fool, etc.
(B) See kolôkolô-fool, etc.
(Sp. colchon) Mattress.
etc. From koló-to carry by means of a string round the forehead.
(Sp. collar) Collar. (see kolár, kolíntas, kwélyo).
(Sp. coma) Comma.
(Sp. comadre) The relationship of the godmother to the parents of her godchild and to the godfather.
(Sp. combate) Combat, fight, war, skirmish, battle, fray, encounter. (see áway).
(Sp. convidar) Feast, celebration, banquet, repast, entertainment. (see tábad, punsyón, pagkáon, bádù).
Also: an invited guest.
See kombidádo.
(Sp. comedor) Dining room, refectory, dining hall, mess-room. (see kalán-an).
(Sp. comedia) Comedy; any stage-play.
(Sp. comediante) Comedian; player, actor, actress.

(Sp. comerciante) Merchant, shop-keeper, tradesman, trader, chandler, retailer, hawker, huckster, higgler, pedlar, colporteur, any seller of goods even in a small way, dealer, salesman, chapman, costermonger; cheapjack, caterer. (see pumalatíkang).
(Sp. comercio) Commerce, business, trade, traffic, lucrative enterprise. (see palatikángan, palangitán-an).
(Sp. cometa) Comet.
(Sp. comida) Dinner, meal, repast, feed, spread, fare; food, comestibles, eatables, victuals, viands; eating, feeding. (see pagkáon, kináon, kalán-on).
(Humorously) Committee; member of a committee, a stuck-up fellow, big gun; self-important, overbearing, proud.
(B) Silent, reserved, retired, uncommunicative, reticent, taciturn, not talkative.
To grumble, murmur, sulk, pout, complain. Indì ka magkómod. Don't murmur. Indì mo akó pagkomóran (-ódan). Do not grumble at me-or-in my presence. (kúmud id.).
Dim. and Freq. of kómod. To grumble a little, or have a habit of grumbling and complaining on every occasion.
(Sp. cómoda) Chest of drawers, bureau, night-commode.
See kamústa. Nagkomostahánay silá. They saluted each other, they shook hands.
(Sp. compañia) Company, society, concern, firm; troop, body of soldiers or the like. (see kumbuyahán, hubón, kabón).
(Sp. acompañar) To accompany, attend, convoy, bear-, keep-, company, join, go along with; join in, play an accompaniment. (see upúd, tawás, búylog).
(Sp. compadre) The relationship of a godfather to the parents of his godchild and to the godmother. (see komári).
(Sp. compas) A pair of compasses, callipers, measure, time (in music), rule, standard (of life). (see solóndan).
Also: to beat time; to lead, be boss or master; to gesticulate, move or wave the hand.
(Sp. componer) To put together, compose, do up, repair, mend, put to rights. Komponehá inâ. Put that together, put it to rights, mend it. (see kaáyo, kaídan, búhat, hímò).
(Sp. composición) Composition, repair, mending, make, making, putting to rights. (see búhat, binúhat).
Also: Note book, composition book.
(Sp. comun) In common, common to. Iníng dútà komún námon. This land belongs to us in common. (see guráptan, garapátan).
(Sp. comun) Privy, water-closet or (abbreviated) W.C., lavatory, public lavatory, jakes, latrine. (see lubô, kasílyas).
(Sp. comunicación) Communication, intercourse, converse; means of communication, connection.
(Sp. compañero) Companion, partner, friend, fellow, associate, curate, assistant, mate, consort. (see kaúpud, kadámpig, kabúylog).

Particle: If, when, whether; or. Kon magabút siá-. When he comes-. Usisáon mo sing maáyo iníng mga kasangkápan kon mapúslan pa ó kon dílì. Examine these tools well, whether they are still of some use or not. Padálhi akó sing duhá kon tátlo ka páres nga sapátos. Send me two or three pairs of boots. Kon maáyo ang tiémpo magadúaw akó sa ímo. If the weather is fine I will pay you a visit. (see ó, ukón,  N.B. ukón is now mostly used in the meaning of "or" and kon in the meaning of "if, when, whether", "ukón" is a contraction of "ó, kon").
(Sp. convención). Convention, congress, assembly, meeting, caucus. (see sinápol, tinipóntípon, katipúnan).
(Sp. convento) Convent; Parish Priest's house, presbytery.
(Sp. conde) Count; aristocrat.
(Sp. condenado) Condemned, sentenced; damned, the soul of a damned person. (see tinagudilían).

But, if not, unless, except; really, surely, certainly. Iní dílì matúod, kóndì butíg gid. This is not true, but a downright lie. Waláy saráng makabúhat sináng mga kalatingaláhan, kóndì ang Diós. No one, except God, can perform such miracles. Abáw, kóndì kahalamútan gid inâ. Now, if that isn't funny! ("kóndì" is a contraction of "kon dílì").
A kind of rather rough red cloth used chiefly for pillow-cases and for decorative purposes; a native song and dance. (see kundíman).
(Sp. conejo) Rabbit.
To carry at the side or astride the hip as small children are often carried. Kongkongá ang bátà. Carry the baby on your hip.
Sometimes, occasionally, from time to time, now and then, repeatedly, but not very often. (kon kaisá, kon kís-a).

They say, it is rumoured or reported, it is said, the story goes, rumour has it, etc. Maáyo siá nga táo, konó. They say that he is a good man. May súnug, konó, kagáb-i sa dálan Rizál. There was a fire, last night, in Rizal-street, they say.
Dim. and Freq. of konó. Ginakonókóno nga--. It is being rumoured that--. (see hudínghúding).
(Sp. confencia) Conference; consultative meeting. (see sinápul).
(Sp. confesar) To confess, go to confession, receive the Sacrament of penance. Sán-o pa ikáw magkonpesár? When did you go to confession? Pakonpesará siá. Hear his confession. (see túad).
(Sp. confesor) Confessor.
(Sp. confesión) Confession, the sacrament of Penance; sick-call.
(Sp. confesionario) Confessional, confessional box.

(Sp. consabido, consaber) Confabulation, collusion, agreement, understanding. Konsábo níla iní. There is an understanding between them as regards this-or-They jointly contrived this. (see kasugtánan, kasapulán, húmon, hinubónhúbon, pahítò, padúgi, patúga, etc.).
(Sp. consagrar) To consecrate. Konsagrahí iníng mga pórmas. Consecrate these hosts. Pilá ka pórmas ang nakonsagrahán kaína sang ága? How many hosts were consecrated this morning?
(Sp. consagración) Consecration.
(Sp. concejal) Councillor, member of a council, municipal councillor. (see kasápul).
(Sp. concejo) Council or board, especially a municipal council. (see kasapulán).
(Sp. consejo) Advice, admonition, monition, counsel, opinion. (see láygay, túdlò, panúgyan).
(Sp. considerar) To consider, take into consideration, have a heart, show sympathy. Konsiderahí ang ákon mga kalisúd. Take into consideration my difficulties. (see pasunáid, patugsíling).

(Sp. consideracion) Consideration, commiseration, fellow-feeling, humanity, sympathy, compassion, forbearance. De konsiderasyón-worthy of consideration, to be reckoned with, having influence, standing or property. Táo nga walâ konsiderasyón. A man without consideration or pity. Táo nga de konsiderasyón. A man of influence or good standing. (see pasunáid, patugsíling, kaló-oy, kaáwà, dawâdawâ, dirâ-dirâ).
(Sp. conciencia) Conscience. (see ipalatugsíling, tagiposóon).
(Sp. cónsul) Consul.

(Sp. consultar) To consult, ask advice, take counsel, take counsel with. Magkonsúlta-or-magkonsultár ka sa manugbúlung. Consult a doctor (physician). Ginkonsultahán ko siá. I asked his advice. Ikonsultár mo sa íya kon mapamanílà ikáw ukón índì. Ask his advice whether you should go to Manila or not. Also noun: Consultation, conference, a question proposed and the answer given. (see pamángkot, pakigkítà).
(Sp. consuelo) Consolation, relief, condolence, solace, encouragement, comfort; joy, cheering up, mirth, gaiety, merriment, merry-making, pleasure. (see kalípay).

(Sp. contra) Against, in opposition to; to oppose, resist, go against, counteract, run counter to, clash with, cross, conflict with, beat-, run-, militate-, against, withstand, antagonize; opposition, objection; opponent, enemy. Ang kaálwan kóntra sa kaímot. Liberality is opposed to niggardliness. Indì ka magkóntra (mangóntra) sa mga sógò sang ímo ginikánan. Do not go against the orders of your parents. Ang mga nagakóntra (magapangóntra) sa pagbulút-an magabatás sang sílot. Those that go against the law will be punished. Nagakontrahánay silá. They are opposed to each other. They are quarrelling or fighting. Madámù ang íya mga kóntra. He has many enemies. (see bátok, bátò, kasúmpung, kaáway).
(Sp. contrario) Contrary; opponent, enemy, antagonist, contestant. (see kóntra, etc.).
(Sp. contrata) Contract, agreement, bargain; deed, document (containing the terms of a contract, etc.). (see kasugtánan, katípan, kaligonán).
(Sp. contratista) Contractor; one who gathers workmen or farm hands.
(Sp. contrato) Contract, stipulation, pact, agreement. (see kontráta, kasugtánan).
(Sp. contrincante) Opponent, competitor, rival, antagonist, adversary, contestant. (see kasúmpung, kaáway, kasánggà, kóntra).
(B) Say, speech, utterance; to say, tell, utter, speak. Nagkoón tána (ginkoón na) nga--. He said that--. Ikoón mo kaná nga--. Tell him that-. (see silíng, hámbal, púlong, súgid).
See kúut-to grope, etc.
(Sp. copa) Cup, goblet, wine-glass, vase, tea-cup, coffee-cup, drinking cup, glass (of wine, etc.).

Lies, tales, inventions, stories, fibs, falsehoods, prevarications, fabrications, untruths, fiction; to tell lies, make up stories, utter untruths. Ginkópal lang níya inâ. He simply invented that story or he told a lie. Kópal gid lang ang súgid nga iní. This tale is a mere invention, or lie. Indì ka magkinópal. Don't tell lies. (see butíg, bákak).
Lying, telling stories, false, mendacious, deceptive, misrepresenting, exaggerating much. (see butigón, bakákon).
(Sp. copa) Hearts, one of the four suits in card-playing.
(Sp. copeta) A small cup or drinking vessel, liqueur-glass, thimble-glass.
(Sp. copón) A large cup, goblet; ciborium.
(Sp. cupón) Coupon; cheque, draft, note, voucher.
(Sp. copra) Dried coconut-meat, copra.
See kóprak.
(Sp. copia) A copy; to copy. Ikópya-or-kopyahá iní sa líbro. Make a copy of this in the book-or-transfer this to the register. (see huád, sáylo).
(H) (Sp. corral) Fence, etc. See kodál.
(Sp. coral) Coral. (see pagáng, kapagángan).
(Sp. corales) A string of corals.
(Sp. corazon) Heart. (see tagiposóon, kasíngkásing).
See kalabása.
(Sp. corbata) Cravat, tie.

To do something with sudden jerks, get restless with excitement, to puff, pull, draw, jump, curvet, etc. with quick movements. Nagkórbot ang kabáyo sang paglágpok sang láta. At the sound of the tin-can the horse suddenly began to jump. Kinórbot ang karabáw sang paglubás sang áwto. The buffalo stampeded when the automobile passed. Pakorbotá ang abáno mo, agúd índì mapatáy ang kaláyo. Puff your cigar quickly, or it will go out. (see hubót).
(Sp. cordero) Lamb, lambkin, young sheep.
(Sp. acordeon) Accordion.
(Sp. corredizo) Groove, rut, canal, especially the groove along which push-and-pull shutters move; a grooved beam or spar.
(Sp. cordon) Cordon, line of posts or guards, military or otherwise, watching a certain district in time of public calamities, revolutions, infectious diseases, or the like.
(Sp. correa) A girdle, belt, sash, cincture, surcingle, especially one worn by a religious society or confraternity.
(Sp. correo) Post, mail; post-office.
Half of a gantang. Fifty kórha make a bushel (pásong) of rice.
Stunted, undersized, dwarfish, kept down in growth. (see arí-arí, agílagíl).
Anything used for the operation "koríkot". (see kolikót).

To stir, twitch, bore with the finger, etc. Indì mo pagkorikóton ang búhò sang ulúnan, agúd índì magdakû kag maggwâ ang búrak. Don't bore your finger into the hole in the pillow, lest it should enlarge and the cotton come out. (see kotíkot, kitíkot, kolíkog, etc.).
To wrinkle, form creases or lines. Ang pánit siníng tigúlang nagakorítot. The skin of this old person is full of wrinkles. (see kurínot).
Cat, puss, pussy, grimalkin, mouser. (see kutî).
To call a cat. Korínga ang koríng. Call the cat-or-shout "kóring" to bring the cat here. (see míming).
See kolisáw.
See kolisóng.
A kind of small lobster. (see karitót, kiritót).
Wrinkled, creasy, creased, lined; twisted, curled, (as a pig's tail). (see kurinót).
(Sp. coronel) Colonel.
(Sp. cornetin) Cornet; cornettist.
(Sp. cornisa) Cornice.
(B) Curled, curly, woolly, crinkly (of hair; see kolóng).
(B) To contract. See kolô.
(H) To play with stones. See kodô.

(Sp. coro) Choir; line, row, tier, file, circle; to form a line or circle, arrange in a line or circle. Magkóro-or-kumóro kamó. Form a line or circle. Koróha ang mga bátà. Form (arrange) the children in line. Make the children stand in line (in a circle). Pakoróha ang mga bátà. Make the children line up. (see andána, ídas).
Dim. and Freq. of kóro.
To rumple, etc. See karokosó.
(B) See kolokotón. (see batikólon).

(Sp. corona) Crown, corona, coronet, fillet, diadem, circlet, chaplet, garland, wreath; tonsure; to crown. Koronáhi ang hárà. Crown the queen. Ginkoronáhan níla ang réina sa Flores de Máyo. They crowned the queen of the "Flores de Mayo"-or-queen of the May. (see púrung, purúng).
See kórnel.
(Sp. corpiño) Shirtwaist, short shirt or waist as worn by women. (see kimóno).
(Sp. corsé) Corset, stays for women.

(Sp. cortar) To cut (clothes, etc.); to cut, chisel, fashion, carve (wood or stone); a fringe or indentation, cut in a zigzag or roundish pattern along the edge of a sleeve, etc., goffer, gauffer; to curdle, coagulate. Nagkórta ang gátas. The milk curdled. Nagkórta ang pásta, lúnang, etc. The paste, mud, etc. has become dry and friable. (see básbas, bórlas, bágtik, gréka).
Dim. and Freq. of kórta. Nagakortákórta siá sing bató. He is cutting stone. Maálam siá mangortákórta. He knows how to cut or carve (stone, wood, etc.).
(Sp. cortaplumas) Knife, penknife, pocket-knife. (see lansítas, igulúlut, íwà).

(Sp. corte) A cut, fit, the stuff necessary for a garment; to cut, cut out, fit (in tailoring). Maáyo ang kórte sang íya mga panápton. The cut of his clothes is good. Ang manugtábas nagakórte na sang ákon delárgo. The tailor is cutting out the cloth for my trousers. Iníng manugtábas maábtik mangórte. This tailor is an expert cutter. (see tábas).

(Sp. corte) Court, tribunal, judgment-seat; a king's or monarch's residence or retinue. Ang Kórte de Priméra Instánsya. The Court of First Instance. Ang Kórte Supréma. The Supreme Court. (see hokmánan, holokmánan).
A piece of cloth measuring 2.50 m in length and sufficient for an ordinary pair of trousers.

(Sp. cortina) Curtain, blind; to curtain. Kortináhi siá. Draw his curtain. Curtain him off. Pakortináhi siá. Provide him with a curtain. Nagapangortína siá kon magtúlug. He uses a curtain, when he goes to sleep. Ginkortináhan níya ang bátà, kay may hángin. She drew the curtain on the baby, because there was a draught. (see kúmbung).
(Sp. corcho) Cork; clogs. (see bakiâ, kótso).
(H) A little, a pinch, a small piece or amount.
(H) To pinch, press or nip between the finger nails. Kosiá siá. Pinch him. Kosií siá sa bútkon. Pinch his arm. Gindúmpug ko siá, kay ginkosî níya akó. I hit him, because he pinched me. (see kodót).
(H) Dim. and Freq. of kosî. To tease and pinch each other in play as children do.

To strip, divide or tear into thin strips, shred, decorticate. Kosî-kosía ang páklang sang burí. Strip the burí-stalk. Kinosîkósì na ang páklang sang burí. The burí-stalk is now torn into strips. (see láknit).

(Sp. cocina) Kitchen; to make or provide a kitchen. Kosináhi ang baláy mo. Get a kitchen built for your house. Kinosináhan na man ang bág-o níla nga baláy. Their new home is now provided with a kitchen. (see digamohán).
(Sp. cocinero) Cook.
To pinch, twist or tweak, nudge, poke (another's legs, ears, etc.). Kosipára (-áda), ang íya dalúnggan. Pinch and twist his ears. (see kulípat, gurípat, guránit).
To shell, shuck beans. (see kokót).

To sulk, pout, frown, be sullen, look offended. Indì ka magkósmod. Don't frown, sulk or pout. Ginkosmorán (-odán) níya akó. He looked sullenly at me-or-he frowned at me. (see súngon, kolisáw, súnggud, kúmud).
Dim. and Freq. of kósmod.
To rend, tear to pieces, pull apart by force, rip. Kosnitá ang papél, hénero, etc. Tear the paper, cloth, etc. to pieces. Kinósnit níya ang ákon báyò. He tore my jacket. (see gísì, kosîkósì, láknit).
Torn, rent; ripped. Kosnít na galî ang ákon báyò. Sín-o ang nagkósnit siní? Why, my jacket is torn! Who tore it? (see gisî).

To rub, apply friction, abrade, massage, chafe, fret. Kosóa sing maáyo ang ákon panápton sa (sang) habón. Rub my clothes well with soap. Kinósò níya ang duhá níya ka dalúnggan. He rubbed both his ears.
To rub, rumple, tousle. Nagakosôkosoáy silá sang íla bohók. They are rumpling each other's hair.
(Sp. costa) Cost, price, expense; coast, seashore; red yarn or thread. (see bilí, baybáyon, bunáng).
Constabulary.
(Sp. costoso) Costly, dear, expensive. (see maámbas, gastóso, mahál).
(Sp. costumbre) Custom, habit, manner, usage. (see kinaanáran, kinabatásan, batásan).
(Sp. costura) Suture, seam; sewing. (see tinahián).

Throb, beat, pulsation; to throb, heave, palpitate, pulse, to twist and wriggle as a worm, to throb with pain as a boil, etc. Nagakotíkot ang sulúd sang ákon hubág. The inside of my boil is throbbing with pain.
To clean a hole, aperture, etc. by means of a small stick or the like. (see kolíkog, kitíkot).

Hole, cavity, grave, sepulchre; to excavate, dig-, scoop-, out earth, etc. Akó ang makáli, ikáw ang makótkot. I will do the digging and you will take out the earth. Imo kotkotón ang binayó sa lusóng, kay ákon pagatáphan. Scoop out the pounded rice from the mortar, for I am going to sift it. Kotkotá ang balás sa búhò. Take out the sand from the hole. (see káli, búhò, lulúbngan).
etc. From kotól-to pluck, cull.
Louse. (see botól, kúto).
To be dense, thick, crowded. Nagakótò lang ang táo sa punsyón. There is a dense crowd at the banquet. (see kútò, gutúk).
A louse-like insect living in loose sand.
See bilógbilóg. Madámù ang kotókotó siníng bunáng. This yarn is not smooth, is full of little lumps or knots (nodes).
To pick, pluck, gather, cull. Kótla ang búlak. Pluck the flower. Kótli akó sing búlak. Pluck me some flowers. Ikotól akó ánay siníng búlak. Please pick this flower for me.
(Sp. cotonia) A kind of rather rough cloth, dimity, fustian.
To ache, pain, be painful. Nagakótoy ang tiyán ko. I have stomach ache.
To tire, exhaust; tired, exhausted, stiff as from walking, etc. Ginakotóy akó. I am tired. (see kápoy, kapóy, álay, pául, paúl).
(Sp. coche) Coach, carriage, omnibus, tramcar, autobus, motor bus.
(Sp. cochero) Coachman, driver.
(Sp. cochillo) Knife, table-knife. (see súndang).
See kórtso.

To disparage, criticize adversely, detract, censure, speak ill of, exaggerate wrongs or injuries suffered, belittle benefits received, complain to others. Indì ka magkotsókótso. Don't speak in disparagement of anybody. Indì mo akó pagkotsókotsohán. Don't censure me-or-don't make unreasonable complaints about me to others. Anó na man ang ginakotsókótso mo? What are you complaining about now?
A kind of rice. (see arabón).
(Sp. credencial) Credential; certificate of cattle-registration.
(Sp. cristal) crystal; glass. (see kátyà).
(Sp. cristiano) Christian. (see kristohánon).
(Sp. Cristo) Christ.
Christian. (see kristiáno).
(Sp. cruz) Cross; trial, suffering, difficulty. Pagpangurús-to make the sign of the cross. (see sáng-an).
(Sp. cruzar las manos) With hands or arms folded or crossed; to cross or fold one's hands or arms. Krusamanóha ang ímo mga bútkon. Fold your arms. (see panimókò).
(Sp. crucifijo) Crucifix.
What d'ye call them, etc. See kwan.
See kwan.
(H) To throb, beat, palpitate, pulse. (see kumbákúmba, tumbôtúmbò, kotíkot).
To float, swim on the surface. Ang tápas nagakubág sa túbig. Coconut husks float on the water. (see kutáw, lutáw, utáwútaw, kubáw).
Cowardice; to be or become a coward. (see tálaw).
Coward, poltroon; cowardly, pusillanimous, timorous. (see matálaw).
To float, swim, drift, move on the surface of. (see kubág, kutáw).

To form in line, file or row, line up; line, row, file, tier. Magkúbay or simply kúbay kamó. Form in line. Nagakúbay ang mga baláy sa siníng báryo sa toó kag sa walá sang dálan. The houses in this village form rows (are in rows) to right and left of the road. Kubáya ang mga bumulúthò. Line up the school-children. Pakubáya ang mga bumulúthò. Make the school-children form a line. (see ídas, kóro).
(Sp. cubierta) The deck of a ship.
(Sp. cubiertos) Table-cutlery, spoons, knives and forks.
See kóbkob.
To bow down, incline, bend over, stoop, dip. (see kuúb).

To hollow out, undermine, wash away, said especially of water. Ginkubkubán ang bató sang túbig. The stone was undermined by the water. Ginkúbkub sang túbig ang balás. The water washed away the sand. (see áb-ab, kábkab, kádkad).
(Sp. cubo) The handle of a chisel, hammer or other tool; socket, shaft- or axle-case; hub, nave of a wheel.
(Sp. cubrecama) Coverlet, counterpane, bedspread. (see sobrekáma, tabón).
etc. From kubús-to be low, etc.

A game in which two grasp each other's hand and try to inflict pain by pressing the finger-nails into the flesh; he who gives way first loses. Nagakubungáy silá nga duhá. The two of them are busy at the game called "kúbung". (see ógbo-another game, where the contestants try to bend down each other's arm; pákil-where they try, in a sitting position, to bend the outstretched leg; tornílyo-where the middle finger is made the victim). (see pangúbung).
Full of creases, creased, puckery, puckered, corrugated, wrinkled, gathered, contracted into folds; to be or become creased, etc. (see bokóng).

Low, mean; sorry, poor, petty, paltry, unimportant, insignificant, nonentity, inferior, not up to the standard, of-little-, -small,-no-, -account,-importance. Kubús nga táo. A man of mean origin, of little worth or influence. Sín-o sa íla nga tátlo ang kubús sa pagdúmug, sa pagkabutáng, sa kataasón, sa kaálam, etc. Which of the three is the least in wrestling, in wealth, in height, in wisdom or learning, etc.? (see kulábus).
See kubyál-to struggle, etc.
To struggle, rear up, jump, curvet, make frantic efforts (as a horse trying to get loose, etc. (see húblag).
To give a jerk, make a swift movement, step aside quickly. (see págsi, dalî, líktin, líksi, likáw).
Fence, etc. See kodál.
Screen, awning, shelter; umbrella. Kúdang sa ínit. Parasol. (see páyong).
The red blossoms of the dápdap-tree.

To walk abroad under difficulties, as at night, during pelting rain, in a raging storm or the like. Ngáa nga ikáw gid ang nagkúdaw sa siníng óras? Why have you ventured to walk out by yourself at such an hour? (see dúkaw).
A kind of plant, whose leaves and shoots are edible.
Pertaining to kudiápa; as plain or as flat as the leaves of the kudiápa-plant; snub-nosed, flat-nosed. (see dapâ, kurapâ).
See kuríng-cat.
Fool, ass, idiot, (see kólò, etc.); ugly to look upon. (see sárot, laímnan, maláw-ay).
Of little use or value, poor, paltry, sorry, not worth much, useless. Kudís siá nga táo. He is a worthless fellow. Kudís siá nga pánday. He is of little use as a carpenter,-not much of a carpenter.
Dim. of kudís.
To pretend to be against, refuse outwardly, object to outwardly, professedly, apparently, seemingly, ostensibly, etc. See bisyóbísyo, indîíndì, istíísti, etc.

Line, stroke, mark; to strike, line, mark, rub against. Kudlisá ang pósporo sa káha. Strike the match on the box. Kudlisí ang pápel sang lápis. Mark or line the paper with the pencil. (see kúlit, kúdlit).

Line, stroke, mark made with something sharp or pointed; to line, mark, sign with a chisel, pencil, brush, etc. Kudlití ang tápì sang lápis. Mark the plank with the pencil. Ikúdlit ang pósporo sa káha. Strike the match on the box. (see kúdlis, kúlit).
Dim. and Freq. of kúdlit. Indì ka magkudlítkúdlit, kóndì magsulát ka sing maáyo kag maáthag. Don't scribble, but write well and clearly.

(B) To tremble, shiver, quake, quail, shake with fear, cold, etc. Ang báka nagakúdug sa katúgnaw. The cow is shivering with cold. Pakudúga siá sang ímo sáble. Make him tremble with fear of your sword. (see kúrug).
See kudiápa-a plant.
Pertaining to "kudyápa". See kudiapáhon.
A musical instrument, a lyre. (see sísta, banduríya, rabél, etc.).
To throttle, strangle, choke, suffocate, garrote, compress one's throat. Kugaá-or-kúg-a siá. Throttle him. Gintámpà ko siá, kay ginkugâ níya akó. I slapped him, because he seized me by the throat.
A scab, scar, cicatrix, cicatrice. (see pálì, pinalían).

A noisy, impolite preparation for spitting; to hawk, i.e. to force up phlegm (spittle) from the throat and eject it, to cough in preparation for spitting. Indì ka magkúghad. Don't hawk (spit) with unseemly efforts. Indì mo siá pagkugharán (-adán) sa íya pagkáon, kay básì magalaút ang íya ginháwa kag magasúka siá. Do not hawk during his meal, for he may be sickened and vomit. Nagkúghad siá sing dugô. He coughed up blood. (see úghad, súgpà).

Care, carefulness, heed, heedfulness, attention, zeal, diligence; to do with care, diligence or circumspection, be careful about, to take pains, perform-, carry out-, attend to-, with care. Kugíhi iní. Do this with care. Ginakugíhan níya ang tanán nga mga butáng sa sulúd sang baláy. She takes great care of everything in the house. She is diligent in all her household duties. (see baláka, ámlig, tátap, písan, úkud, íd-id).
Octopus; vampire, shark, cheat.

Fright, terror, dread, fear, dismay, scare, alarm; to alarm, strike terror into, frighten, scare, dismay, affright, terrify, cause great fear or consternation. Ginakúgmat akó kon dumdumón ko inâ. I am quite frightened when I think of it. Nagakakúgmat siá. He is alarmed, scared, frightened. Amó ang naghátag sa íla sing kúgmat kag kúlbà. That frightened and scared them. That struck terror into them and filled them with a feeling of uneasiness. (see hádluk, hanguyús, kuyús, lísang, makakulúgmat).
Octopus. (see kugíta). Also: a kind of fierce shark, more dangerous than the "bagís".
To rasp, scrape, shred or scoop out. Kugurá (-udá) ang lubí. Scoop out the coconut-meat. (see oráod, kódkod, etc.).
To bear, hug or carry in one's arms. Kugúsa siá. Carry him in your arms. Ipakúgus sa íya iníng bátà. Give her this baby to carry in her arms. (see kólkol, kalóngkong).

(H) To take, take-away,-from,-away from,-off, remove, fetch, seize, abduct, subtract; gain, get. Kuháa iníng mga pínggan sa lamésa. Take these plates off the table. Kuháon mo ang ákon kálò sa kwárto kag dálhon dirí. Fetch my hat from the room and bring it here. Ginkuháan-or-kinuháan akó níya sing tátlo ka písos. He took three pesos from me. Kuhái iníng tabungós sing ápat ka gántang. Take five gantas out of this rice-basket. Anó gid man nga kapuslánan ang saráng náton makúhà sinâ? What advantage can we gain from that? What is the use of it? (see buúl).
(B) Fool, ass, simpleton. (see kolôkolô, etc.).
(H) Dim. and Freq. of kúhà.

To nudge, touch, pull slightly and withdraw the hand at once, tear or strain at gently. Kuhíta siá. Nudge him. Kuhíti siá sa íya bútkon. Pull him slightly by the sleeve or arm. (see káblit, tándog, híkap).
Dim. and Freq. of kúhit.
The cry of a flying fox, of a fruit bat or the like.
See kókok-a kind of snail.
The cry of pigeons; to coo. (see kók-kok).

Bad, poor, unsatisfactory, not up to the standard or reasonable expectations; to be or become bad, etc., chiefly applied to crops. Kúl-aw ang pinatubás ko sa siníng túig. I had a poor harvest this year. Nagkúl-aw iníng humáy. The rice turned out poorly, yielding e.g. less than half a ganta of "bugás" for every ganta of unhulled rice.
Softness, flabbiness; to be or become flaccid.
To eat coconut meat mixed with toddy. See kilábò.
Soft, flabby, flaccid, tender, not strong. (see mahómok, malúm-ok, tabonánà).

Insufficient, inadequate, deficient, wanting, skimpy, scant, stinted, not enough, lacking, short, too little or too small; to be insufficient, to not suffice, to come short of, etc. Kinulábus kamí sing kwárta. We were short of money. Nagkulábus ang súd-an. The side-dishes were too few or insufficient. Kulábus gid ang íya ikasaráng sa amó nga palangakóan. He has far too little ability for such an office. Kon kulabúson siá sang pálad--. If fate is against him--. If he is unlucky--. (see kabús, kúlang).
Superficial, pretended, sham, not hearty, not open or honest, insincere, dissembling. (see pakuláhaw, pasamústra, alakápa).
See kalahós.
Bat. (see koláknit, etc.).

(H) Cloak, mantle, covering, cover, wrapping; to cover or wrap oneself up, inwrap, enwrap, envelop, roll up in, swathe, swaddle, lap, fold, muffle up. Kon magtúlug siá nagakulámbot sing kápay. When he sleeps he wraps himself up in a blanket. Mangulámbot ka sing hábul. Wrap yourself up in a blanket. Cover yourself with a blanket. (see kúmbot, kulúmbot).

To sneak, to take away by stealth, filch, purloin, appropriate secretly. Sín-o ang nagkulámi sang ákon líbro? Who took away my book? Kinulámi níya ang ákon kálò, bastón, etc. He took away my hat, stick, etc. Kulamíha lang iníng páyong. Just take this umbrella. Ginkulamíhan akó níya sang ákon báyò. He took away (appropriated) my jacket. (see kúhà).
To hurt, cause physical pain by pushing, grasping tightly, striking, boxing, pinching, etc. Indì ka magkulámò sa íya. Don't hurt him (physically). Kulamóa siá. Let him feel it (physically).
Also: the outer and less oily portion of coconut meat.

The filmy formation of new skin around the edges of a wound or boil, when it is beginning to heal and before a scab is formed; to skin over. May kulámog na ang íya hubág-or-nagakulámog na ang íya hubág. His boil is beginning to heal or skin over.
See kólan id.

(B) To fell, hew down, cause to fall, lay low, throw down. Kulangá ang káhoy. Fell the tree. Nakuláng na ang káhoy sa dútà. The tree is now laid low on the ground. Ginkuláng sang bágyo ang dìmaísip nga mga káhoy. The storm laid low innumerable trees. (see púkan).

Less than required or expected, short, insufficient, inadequate, not enough, too little, deficient, deficit; to lack, fall short, be inadequate, etc. Kúlang iní. This is short-or-This is too little. Kúlang gid inâ sa íla nga tanán. That certainly is not enough for all of them. Nagkúlang ang bíno. There was not enough wine. Nakulángan akó sing kwárta. I ran short of money. Pakulángi siá sing limá ka dakû. Give him five centavos less. Pinakulángan níya ang bilí sang líbro sing napúlò ka dakû. He lowered the price of the book by ten centavos. Kúlang karón ang ísdà. There is at present a dearth or scarcity of fish. (see kabús, kulábus).
Now and then, but rarely, used for kúlang. Ginakuláng ang íya kinitáan. His earnings are not sufficient (for his needs).
Dim. of kúlang.
Fool, foolish, half-witted, mentally deficient or underdeveloped, not all there.
Lean, thin, frail. (see kanít, kalamanít, níwang, hágpis).
(Sp. culantrillo) A kind of plant, maiden-hair fern.
(Sp. culantro) Coriander, a plant with aromatic seeds.
A film on the eye; cataract. (see bítlig).
Flatnosed, snubnosed. (see dapâ, kurapâ).

Fine earth, slime, sediment, deposit; to deposit, cover with sediment (as inundated fields, etc.). Kon may bahâ, pagakulapohán gid iníng umá kag magaáyo ang dútà. If there is a flood, this field will be covered with sediment and the soil will improve. (see láy-on).
Having a cataract or film on the eye. (see bitligón).
Also: A meeting in honour of a person that has recently died; a wake. (see belasyón).

To interrogate, question, examine, investigate. Ginkulasisíhan níya ang íya mga sinákpan kon sín-o sa íla ang nagbúhat sinâ. He examined his subjects to find out who had done it. (see pangusísà, pángkot).
See kolata.
To call the chickens together. (see kurátay).
Nervousness, shyness, timidity, fear; to be nervous, shy, timid, afraid, etc. Ginakulbaán siá. He is upset, unnerved.
Dim. and Freq. of kúlbà. Indì ka magpakulbâkúlbà. Don't be shy or afraid. Don't get nervous.
etc. From kulúb-upside down.
(Sp. culebra) A sudden collapse or attack, often ending in death.

(H) To be slow, do slowly, weakly, with difficulty. Nagkúlì siá maglakát, kay matámbok siá. He was slow in walking, for he is so fat. Kon pakiáw ginadásig níla ang trabáho, ápang ginakúlì kon sa inádlaw. They are quick at work when paid a lump sum, but slow when they are paid daily wages. (see kúrì).
Young, tender, thin, in the first stage of development, applied particularly to the camunsel-fruit, peas and beans.
(B) See kuliápis. (see kupús).
See kulihót.
Late, tardy, too late, behind time, not in time, after or beyond the usual (proper) time, coming after the expected time; to be late, etc. (see kuligót, atrasádo, hudiánan).
To pinch, squeeze, twist (the ears, etc.; see gulínat, gurípat, guránit, kulípat).
To squeeze, pinch, twist, nudge, poke; to strike, beat, thrash. Kinulípat ang bána sang íya asáwa. The husband was pinched by (got a beating from) his wife. (see gulínat, gurípat, kosípad, guránit).

Worn out, old, useless, without value, fake, sham, bogus, counterfeit, false (of money). Kulirô nga kwárta. False money, money that is not accepted as legal tender, being counterfeit or too much worn. Kulirô nga balóta. A false ticket or vote.
(H) See kúdlit. Walâ siá magpadalá sa ákon bisán sing isá ka kúlit. He did not send me as much as one line.
A kind of bird. (see kurít).
A kind of thorny plant with edible leaves.
Wrinkled, etc. See koritót.
(Sp. culpa) Guilt, sin, fault, culpability, blame, crime, wrong. (see salâ, sayúp).

To shrink, shrivel, contract, diminish, condense, reduce, wane, settle, become small or smaller, lessen, decrease, grow less, dwindle. Kinmúlpà ang humáy. The rice shrank. Nagkúlpà ang dútà sa búhò. The earth in the hole settled, became compact and consequently apparently less. (see kúpus).

Upside down, wrong side up, bottom up, face downwards, topsy-turvy, inverted; to turn upside down, etc. Kulúb ang pínggan. Sín-o ang nagpakulúb sinâ? The plate is turned upside down! Who turned it over? Pakúlba ang báso. Turn the glass bottom up. Ginpakulúb níya ang baúl. He turned the trunk upside down. Kinúlban siá sang íya sakayán. His boat turned turtle. (see sulî, balískad, hayáng, kayâ-to face upwards, etc.).
Strangling, throttling, choking, suffocating; garrote (capital punishment); the neck, throat. (see kugâ).
(H) Anything made use of for the action of "kúhit"-to nudge, etc.
A kind of mollusk resembling a snail; a kind of a flowering plant.
Cradle, crib. (see kúlan).
See kulámbot.

(H) Murmuring, grumbling, complaining, complaint; to murmur, complain. Anó na man ang íya kulumúron? What complaint has he to make now? Nagkulumúron siá sinâ or tungúd sinâ. He grumbled or murmured at that. (see kúmud).
Curled; to curl. (see korô, kolóng).
(B) To shrink, shrivel, become compact, settle, pack, grow less in bulk. Nagkulús ang kóprak. The copra shrank. (see kúpus, kúlpà).
(H) Place or point of a stem or stalk where a flower, etc. has been, or is to be, plucked. (From kotól). (see ilipoán).
(H) A fan, anything used to fan a fire, etc. (see kuyáb, táyhop, taláyhop).
The sharp, fine steel edge of a knife or weapon; to make very thin, to sharpen, hone, whet. (see báid, kulyápis).
See kuliápis-thin.
(H) The thumb. (see kamomóo).
The little finger. (see kamalíngking, tingayón, tingáytíngay, atingayón).
See komári.
To throb, palpitate, beat fast. Nagakúmba ang íya tagiposóon. His heart is throbbing.
Dim. and Freq. of "kúmba"-to throb, etc. (see kubákubá).

A weave, a particular method of weaving wickerwork, especially applied in weaving small plates, sieves, etc. of bamboo splints; to weave, interlace, intertwine, entwine. Kinúmbis nga pagrára (paglála). Weaving according to the kúmbis-method. Metaphorically: Walâ sing madámù nga kúmbis. Easy. Without much ado. Without-fuss,-many requirements. Isá ka buluhatón nga madámù sing kúmbis (kulukúmbis). A difficult, intricate piece of work. (see lála, rára, habúl, pahitôhítò, rikobíkos).
A cake made of flour mixed with sugar and then fried.
