To guess, conjecture, surmise, suppose, think, imagine, judge, opine. Sa ákon pagmái-om--. According to my opinion or guess--. Anó, ang namai-omán mo sa íya nahanungúd sang pagkasúnug sang íya baláy? What is your conjecture about him as to the burning down of his house? Mai-omá sing maáyo, básì malagpatán mo ang matúod. Make a good guess, perhaps you may hit on the truth. (see bánà, bántà, hunâhúnà, pakót, lágpat).
(H) Sack, bag especially one made of buri-leaves and used to pack sugar. (see bayóong).
Covetous, ambitious, etc. See maíbug, maibugón.
Covetous, ambitious, passionately desirous of, craving for, avid, greedy, fond of, eager for, hankering after. (see íbug).
See maíbug.
Exact, precise, diligent, punctual, painstaking, wary, circumspect, careful, with application or zeal. (see íd-id).
See maíd-id.
Sparkling, glittering, sending off sparks, twinkling, flashing. (see ídlab, maídlak, maígpat).
Twinkling, sparkling, glittering. (see ídlak, maídlab).
Flashing, twinkling, sparkling, shining. (see ígpat, maídlab).
Close together, close set, thickset, dense, serried, crowded, narrow-spaced, with but little interval or interstice between. (see íkit, magarót).
(H) Desirous, covetous, wanting very much, avid, fond of, having a liking for. (ílà).
Sensual, sensuous, lustful. (see íbug, maíbgon, maíbug).
(H) See mailáon id.

A prefix used in the following ways: 1) To form the potential future tense of the active voice (see ma- for the passive voice), e.g. Makabúhat ikáw sinâ? Are you, or shall you, be able to do that? Makadángat siá sang íya nga ginatúyò, kon mapísan siá. He will be able to obtain his desire, if he is earnest about it. Makabáyad na siá sang íya útang, kay dakû ang sináplid níya sa pangomérsyo. He can now pay his debt, for he has made a large profit in business. Walâ siá makaabút, kay madámol ang ulán. He could not come, for there was a heavy rain. Indì siá makahalín. He cannot leave or get away. N.B. Quite frequently this "maka-", particularly in verbs expressive of any mental or sensitive operation, has the meaning of the present, e.g. Makahibaló ka siní? Do you understand this? Makabatî ikáw sang túnug sang linggánay? Do you hear the sound of the bell? Makakítà na akó sa íya dirâ. Now I see him over there. (see naka-).  2) to form adjectives meaning "able to, capable of, giving rise to or causing" what the root implies. "Maka-" is either simply prefixed to the root, e.g. "makaákò-powerful, mighty (ákò) or, as is more frequently the case, the first syllable of the root is reduplicated and then "maka-" prefixed, e.g. "makalilípay-causing joy or pleasure, joyful, pleasing (lípay); makalilísang-inspiring terror, causing great fear, terrible, shocking (lísang); makangingíl-ad-exciting nausea, loathsome (ngíl-ad), etc.  3) to form multiples corresponding to the English -times, e.g. makalíbo-a thousand times; makaduhákapúlò-twenty times; makaisá-once, etc.

(B) Old, adult, advanced in age, frequently applied to people of about sixty years of age. (see mál-am). Also used as a verb. Nagmál-it siá. He has become old. Namal-itán akó sa íya. I consider him old. N.B. Mál-it is often used in contempt. Mál-it nga táo (babáe). An old fogey (hag).
(B) See mál-am, mál-it, málmal.
(B) Pillow, cushion. (see ulúnan).

A diminutive particle: Like, as, like to, about, somewhat similar to, resembling, nearly, almost, as (large, small, thick, thin, good, bad, etc.) as-. Malakárbaw, malakarabáw-somewhat like a buffalo; malabitík-like a flea; as small as a flea; malapásì-as, like, about as large as, unhulled grains of rice; malabínlud-very small, as small as fine particles or fragments of hulled rice; malabaláy-like a house, almost as big as a house; malapálad-as large as the palm of a hand, very little; malakalibútan-as large as the world, nearly (almost) everywhere. Ginhatágan níla akó sing tinápay nga malatingá (Gintáw-an nánda akó ti tinápay nga malatingá). They gave me just a very little (a bite of) bread. Ang lúpà (dútà) námon malapálad. Our farm-land is as large as the palm of the hand i.e. it is very small. Ang íya dungúg malakalibútan (daw kalibútan kadakû). His reputation (fame) is spread all over the world. (see daw, súbung, oloánggid).

Dry, exsiccated, drained, seasoned; to be or become dry, arid, desiccated, parched, drained, sear; seasoned (of timber). Malá nga káhoy, tápì, etc. Dry wood, seasoned boards, etc. Nagmalá na ang ákon panápton nga ginbulád ko. My clothes which I spread in the sun are dry now. Ang pawíkan nga namálhan. The turtle deprived of water. The stranded turtle. Pamalahá (pamálha, pamál-a, pamád-a) sa ínit ang linábhan. Put the wash out in the sun to dry. Namád-an sing túbig iníng mga ísdà kag dinakúp ko. These fishes were stranded (ran aground) and I caught them. Namalahán-namálhan-namál-an-namád-an. (see ugá, láyà, layóng).
A kind of insect that in size and appearance somewhat resembles a cricket; a mole-cricket. It never appears to be wet, even in rain. Hence the name (malá-dry).
Long, lengthy, extended, extended in length. (see lábà, malábug, láwhan).
Dim. of malábà. Malabâlábà siá sing pangguyáhon. He is rather long-headed, has a long face. (see mabayóg).
Lukewarm, tepid, slightly warm, pleasantly warm, not hot. (see maalabáab).

Well cooked, properly cooked, done to a turn; very soft boiled (of rice). (see balatanóg-insufficiently cooked; alibútdan-underdone, still hard inside; lágdos-hard-boiled; basâ-soft-boiled, boiled in too much water; buád-ad-split, burst in boiling, overdone).
Weak, feeble, flabby, flaccid, flimsy, drooping. (see lábtoy, malúya, malumíng, mahúyang, mapígaw).
(B) Long, lengthy, elongated, extended in length. (see lábug, malábà).
Obscure, dim, not clear, not bright, weak-eyed, dim-sighted, half-blind, purblind. (see búlan, mabinulánon).
About as thick as an arm. (see bútkon).
Tasteless, insipid, mawkish, flat, neither sweet nor sour; like the taste of búyò-leaves. Ang tubâ karón nga hápon malabúyò. The toddy this evening tastes flat.
Tasteless, insipid, stale, flat, vapid. (see lád-ang, malás-ay).
Roaming, roving, wandering, rambling, loafing, travelling about; a loafer, vagabond, idler, tramp, hobo. (see lágaw, landólándo, haráyháray, tiógtióg).
Long, etc. See malábà.
Slow, leisurely, deliberate, plodding, jogging, tardy, laggard, dawdling. (see lágday, malágway, mahínay, pákok, lamínday).
Resembling-, like-, as fine as-, as small as-, fine or small chaff called "gílok", etc. Walâ siá sing bisán malagílok nga salâ. He is not at fault at all. He does not deserve the slightest blame.
(H) Slightly feverish, sickly, having a cold, suffering from a sore throat, a catarrh or a slight headache. (see lágnat).
Wide, broad, etc. See malápad.
Shrill, loud, resounding, piercing, lusty, penetrating, sonorous, far-reaching, carrying far, said of sounds. (see lágsing, masílik, masulánting).
Ticking, clicking. (see lágtik).
Strong, firm, hard, tough. (see lágting, mabákud, matíngting, mahúnit, mapág-on, hámrus, purús).
Tinkling, tingling, jingling, clinking, clanking, chinking. (see lágting).
Cracking, crackling, crepitant; falling with a bang, thud, thump or crash. (see lágtok).
Dark black, dark green, very pronounced, deep, decided (of colour); lusty, flourishing (of plants). (see lágtom).
See malábtoy-weak, etc. (lágtoy-lábtoy).
Slow, etc. See malágday.
(H) Precious, dear, costly, high-priced, highly priced, valuable, highly esteemed, expensive, of great price, priceless. (see mahál, hamílì, bilídhon).
Joking, jesting, rallying; jester, joker, clown. (see lahóg).
Bad, wrong, wicked, evil, noxious, injurious, disadvantageous; ill, sick, infirm; unwholesome, bad for one's health. (see láin, maláut, kinaláin).
Corn-field; fit-, suitable-, for growing or planting corn. (see maís).
Spaced wide apart, thin, not dense or near together, far between. Talágsa sa malakâ--. Few and far between--. Very rarely--. Scarcely ever--. (see lakâ).
Insidious, cruel, treacherous (of diseases, etc.). (see lála).
A run-away, one who shuns work, escapes from confinement, etc. (see lágyo).
(H) Cunning, plotting, resourceful, adept at contriving ways and means to gain one's end. (see laláng).
Infectious, contagious, spreading, catching, epidemic. (see latón, manlaláton).
Mourning, mournful, sad, in grief or mourning, wearing mourning dress. (see laláw).
(H) Tasty, delectable, savoury, toothsome, dainty, nice, palatable. (see lalím, manámit).

Disobedient, rebellious, neglecting to comply with orders or precepts, unruly, disregarding restraint, disposed to violate laws, ungovernable, unsubmissive, undisciplined, insubordinate, lawless, wicked, bad. (see lális, malinapáson).
Receptacle containing materials for chewing betelnut; a morsel (mouthful), of betelnut, etc., sufficient for one chewing. (see mamâ).
Materials for chewing betelnut, including betelnut, lime, búyò-and tobacco-leaves. (see mamâ, malám-an).
To grasp, etc. See marámad, marásmas.
Growing well, thriving, flourishing, growing luxuriantly, (see lámbò).
Cool, cold, frigid, keen; raw, sharp, piercing, cold and stiff. Malamíg nga bángkay. A corpse cold and stiff. (see lamíg, matúgnaw, maramíg).
Somewhat like a hen; the larynx, windpipe. (see mungâ).
Foul, stale, rotten, vapid, insipid (of water, coconut milk, etc.). (see lán-o).
Fat, oily, yielding lard or coconut oil, etc. (see lána).
Shining, shiny, lustrous, glossy. (see lánay).
Smelling of fish. Ang mga ginabaligyáan sang mga ísdà maláng-ig. The fish-market smells of fish. (see hurô-smelling of rotten fish).
Tourist, traveller; emigrant, home-seeker. (see mangangályaw).
Covetous, desirous of, ambitious, wishful, avid, eager for, avaricious, wishing or anxious for. (see lánggab, maibugón).
Fluid, liquid, flowing freely, thin, said of liquids. (see lángiaw, maátoy, malapúyut-thick, condensed).
Harsh, grating, squeaking, setting one's teeth on edge, said of sounds like the filing of a saw, or the like. (see langís).
Anxious, desirous of, expectant, worried, weary, disappointed, tired of waiting. (see lángkag).
See malángkag, malinangkágon.
Stale, tasting or smelling of fish, fishy, mawkish, insipid. (see lángsa, maláng-ig).
Nauseating, insipid, tasting or smelling offensively so as to make one vomit, said of badly cooked peas and beans, etc. (lángto).
See malángiaw id.

(H) Reappearing after death; to reappear or haunt after death. Si Fuláno, konó, nagmalánhig. N.N. they say, has risen from the grave or reappeared in the flesh. Ginamalanhigán, konó, ang íla baláy. Their house, it is said, is haunted by a ghost. (see maránhig, amamánhig, amaránhig).
High, tall; high-pitched. Malániog nga tíngug. A high-pitched voice; falsetto. (see lániog, lányog).
Tender, fresh, green, soft, young, impressionable; loud, high-pitched, far-sounding (of voices, music, etc.). (see lánoy).
Dim. of malánoy. Rather soft, etc.
That is to be tamed or broken in. (see mánso).
High, tall, large. Malántiog nga táo. A tall man. (see lántiog, malániog, maláyog, matáas).
See malántiog, id.
See malániog id.
Vagabond, loafer, tramp. (lá-og).
Loud, strong, far-reaching, sonorous, stentorian, resounding, noisy, ear-splitting, deafening, obstreperous (of sounds). (see laúy-láuy, malániog, sílik, sulánting, singgítan).

Wide, broad, extensive, expanded, large, vast, ample, spacious, wide-spread; free from narrowness or bigotry; covetous, greedy, avid. Malápad ang íya nga palangúmhan. He has a large farm. Malápad siá sing panghunâhúnà. He is broad-minded, liberal-minded. Malápad siá sing matá. He is covetous, greedy, ambitious. (see lápad, maálway, mahanáhay).

Trespassing, unobservant, unobserving, non-observant, lawless, unduteous, undutiful, neglecting, neglectful, heedless, failing to comply with, omitting the fulfilment of a duty or precept. (see lápas, malinapáson, malalíson).

By, near by, hard by, close by, fast by, nigh, near, near at hand, close at hand, in the proximity of, in the neighbourhood of, neighbouring, adjacent, adjoining, close to, approximate, about. Malapít sa simbáhan. Near the church. Malapít sa duhá ka líbo. About (more or less, approximately) two thousand.
Ghastly, wan, pale, blanched, gaunt, lean, bloodless, anemic. (see lápsì, malúspad, malún-ad).
(H) Thick, thickened, condensed, stiff, viscous, viscid, inspissated, treacly (of liquids); severe, heavy, vehement, violent (of fighting, or the like). (see lapúyut, malásaw, sugúng, masángsang).
Insipid, nauseous, nauseating, mawkish, tasteless, revolting, loathsome, disgusting, unappetizing, uninviting, vapid. (see lás-ay).
Soft-boiled. Itlog nga malasádo. A soft-boiled egg.
What is to-be kneaded,-be made or pressed into dough. (see mása).
Thick, stiff, treacly, as molasses, etc. (see lasáw, malapúyut).
Ghastly, wan, pale, etc. See malápsì. (láspì-lápsì).
(H) Bad, wrong, evil, wicked, ill, sinful, criminal, unprincipled, vicious, depraved, malignant, malevolent, malicious, base, mean. (see láut, maláin).
(H) Ugly, forbidding, repulsive, nasty, hideous, improper, indecent, dirty, unclean, impure, immodest, unchaste, obscene, foul, lewd, pornographic. (see láw-ay, mahígkò, kadû).
Long, large. See láwhan, malábà, malápad.
Long, etc. See maláwig.
Long, lasting a long time, kept up, enduring, sustained, prolix, continued, prolonged, protracted, extended. (see láwig, mabúhay, madúgay).

Long (of space and time); loose, not fixed, equivocal (of a word, speech, or the like); protracted, prolonged, confused (of thinking conjecturing); patient, forbearing, prudent, considerate, liberal, broad (of mind). Maláwlaw nga pagpainóíno. A prolonged-, protracted-, confused-, way of thinking. Maláwlaw siá sing hunâhúnà. He is broad-minded, liberal-minded, patient, prudent, or the like. (see láwlaw).
(B) Large, big, above the ordinary size. (see lawóg).
Conjecturable, what is to-, can-, should-, be guessed. (see máy-om).
Wide, spacious, extensive. (see layáng).
Dim. of malayáng-wide, spacious.
Scarce, rare, seldom, difficult to obtain. (see maíwat, mahínà, tumalágsa).
(H) Far, far away, far off, a great or long way off, remote, far distant. (see layô).
High, tall, lofty, towering. Maláyog nga lubí. A tall coconut palm. (see láyog, matáas, malántyog, malányog).
(Sp. malvavisco) The marsh-mallow.
(Sp. malva) Mallow.
(Sp. maldición) Malediction, imprecation, execration, curse, malison. (see panghimaláut).

(Sp. maldita, -o) Accursed, cursed, damned; to curse, damn, imprecate, wish evil upon. Ginsilíng (Gintawág) níya akó nga maldíta. He called me accursed. (see gátud, tinagudilían, panóloy, panghimaláut, maldisyón).
(Sp. maleta) Valise, handbag, suitcase, portmanteau, grip, bag.
See mád-an, mál-an, malahán, from malá-to be dry, etc.

(B) Advantage, benefit, profit; good, well; maybe, perhaps. Warâ ti málhas kon ikáw ang silótan tungúd kang salâ ni Fuláno. It's bad enough, if you should be punished for the fault of N.N. (Literally: There is no advantage in it, if-). Warâ ti málhas kon índì tána magabút. Perhaps he is not coming. It would be too bad, if he were not coming. Indì ikáw magpanúgid nga nagasugál kamí adláwdlaw; bokón ti (warâ ti) málhas kon idakúp (dákpon) támon kang polís. Don't tell (anybody) that we are gambling every day; it would be hard lines for us, if we were caught by the police. (see águd, agúdagúd, pulús, áyhan, torán, básì, dámlag).
In order that not, so that not, lest. (see agúd índì, agúd (nga) dílì).
Excuse, pretence, appearance, make-believe, trap; to put forward (as a pretext, etc.). (see pasúnì, balíbad).

Dim. and Freq. of malí. Also: to insinuate, hint at, use indirect language, enlighten another's mind by allusions, speak in parables, often practised by one who wishes to obtain a favour from another or to come to an agreement, to throw out a "polite hint" in a round-about way. Ginmalímalíhan níya kamí nga ang íya nónoy buút mangasáwa sa ámon índay. He politely insinuated that his son wants to marry our daughter. Malímalíha ang paghámbal mo sa íla. Talk to them with polite insinuations or allusions. Nagamalímáli silá nga buút magsímpon sa ámon sang íla anák. They are insinuating their desire or wish of having their boy stay with us. Masúnsun ang hámbal sang Aton Ginúo malímáli. Our Lord often spoke in parables.
Detracting, disparaging, backbiting, scandal-mongering, talebearing, talking evil of one's neighbour. (see libák).
Confusing, confused, bemused, perplexed, distracted, perplexing, worried, upset. (see libúg).
See malibúg.
Passing, transitory, quick. Sa labíng malídan--. Very quickly--. In a short while--. (see madalî, tióntión).
Stable, firm, solid, durable; lasting, resolute, determined. (see líg-on, mapág-on, mabákud, mabáskug).
Modest, self-respecting, formal, proper, unassuming, honest, decent, tactful. (see lígdong, maúgdang).
(Sp. maligno) Malign, malignant, wicked, evil, perverse. Ang espiritú nga malígno. The devil. (see maláut).
Short, brief (particularly in the plural). (see malíp-ot).
Swift, quick, agile, nimble, lithe (of movements). (see lígsi, madásig, mapágsi).
(Sp. legua) A mile off, a mile distant, a mile far, rather far in general; wide, spacious, extensive, broad. (see lígwa).
Pointed, spiky, sharp. (lígwis; see matalíwis).
Forbidding, abstaining from, having an objection to. (see lihî, mainumúron).
Portentous, dangerous, difficult (of times, places, situations, etc.). (see maríit).
See malígsi.
Secretive, concealing, keeping the truth from, doing something on the sly. (see likúm).
Nervous, excited, irritable, easily upset or flurried. (see libúg).
(H) Deceiving, tricksy, cheating, defrauding, fraudulent, overreaching, cunning, sly, tricky, tricksey, tricksome, trickish. (límbong).
Sheltered, quiet, free from wind, not exposed to the wind. (see límbong).
(H) See malímbong.
Giving alms, open-handed, free in giving, bounteous, bountiful, generous, munificent, liberal, charitable. (limós).
(H) Forgetful, absent-minded, unmindful, oblivious. (see límot, malipáton).
(H) Overbearing, excessive, extreme, abusive, one who over-steps the bounds or does something to excess; radical. (see lakás).
Disappointing, wearying, worrying. See malangkágon.
See malapáson id.
Hopeful, confident, sanguine, full of expectation. (see láum).
Calm, quiet, still, smooth, tranquil, peaceful, unruffled. (línaw).
A large rice-container of woven bamboo, capable of holding as much as thirty bushels or even more, but mostly of a size to hold about ten bushels.
Noisy, boisterous, obstreperous, tumultuous, clamorous, vociferous, rowdy. (see líng-og, magáhud, magáhud, magamó, magalúng, magarók, makagulúlà).
Confused, perplexed, giddy, swimming, dizzy; fuddled, drunk, dazed. (lingín).
Shiny, shining, bright, polished. (see línis, mahíning).
Peaceful, quiet, calm, tranquil, undisturbed, noiseless. (see linóng, matáwhay, matínong).
(H) Short, brief, curt, curtailed, abridged, laconic, concise, reduced (of length of time as well as of linear extension). (see líp-ot, malígpot, mabugô).
(H) Forgetful, oblivious, unmindful, absent-minded. (see lipát, malimóton).
Cheerful, glad, jolly, joyful, merry, happy. (see lípay).
Pleasure-loving, addicted to-amusements,-diversions,-entertainments. (see malipáyon).

Watery, insipid, flat, vapid, tasteless, unsavoury, said especially of stale tubers that, having been dug out, are not boiled within a reasonable time and in consequence have lost their flavour. (see lísaw, kalísaw, maganás).
Turning round, revolving, swinging, oscillating, turning in all directions. Síya nga malisôlísò. A swivel chair. (see lísò).
Troublous, troublesome, irksome, hard, difficult to bear or suffer; very ill, at death's door, dying. (lisúd).
Changeable, variable, fickle, not-steady,-reliable,-firm; retracting, repenting. (see liwán).
Full-grown, grown-up, strong; to become full-grown. Málmal siá nga táo. He is a full-grown man. Nagmálmal na siá. He is now full-grown. (see dakû, hámtong, hánggud).
Full-grown, etc. See málmal.
(Sp. malo) Bad, wicked, evil. (see maláin, maláut).
Rice-flower; to flower (of rice). (see marô).
Mild, tender, kind, benevolent, benign, benignant, gracious, affectionate, sympathetic, full of kindness, mild-tempered. (lolô).
Tender, affectionate, kind-hearted. (lólot; see malolô).
Merciful, compassionate, pitiful, having pity on, condoling, commiserating. (ló-oy).
Soft, softened, tender, yielding, impressionable, impressible, giving way to pressure. (lomó; see mahómok, malúm-ok).

(B) See pamulúng-to stare or gape at with open mouth (in disappointment, failure, or the like). Namalóng akó, kay walâ akó makadayón pakádto sa Ilóngílong. I am (was) greatly disappointed, because, after all, I could not go to Iloilo (as intended). Namalóng akó, kay walâ akó makatámbong dídto tungúd sang madámol nga ulán. I was sorely disappointed (I could go and whistle for it), because the heavy shower of rain prevented me from being present there. (see gamón).
Fading, changeable, changing, fickle, not steadfast, not reliable. (see lubád).
Young, tender, soft, impressionable, impressible. (see lubáy, línghod, lanúbò, mahómok, malúm-ok, malomó, bataón).
Dim. of malubáy. Rather young, etc.
Treacherous, cheating, insidious, mean, worming out secrets and then publishing them abroad. (lúbhà).
See malúbhà.
Turbid, impure, dirty, especially said of water. (lubúg).
Faded, pale, light, faint (of colours; see malús-aw).
Emaciated, lean, haggard. (see mahágpis).
Fragile, weak, easily broken or snapped, brittle, said of thread, strings, rattan, etc. (see lúgtì).
Selfish, covetous, cheating, violent, applying force to gain one's end. (see lúgus, mahákug, makágud, dingót, maímot).
See malúgus. Also: oppressing, harsh, cruel, tyrannical.
Traitorous, treacherous, betraying, untrustworthy, disloyal, perfidious; a traitor. (see luíb, mabúdhì, malubhaón).
(H) See malolô.
(H) Liking, desirous of, pleased with. (lúyag; maluyagón id.).
Soft, pliable, tender. (lúm-ok; mahómok, malomó).
New, fresh, young, tender, supple, flexible, said of leaves and shoots of plants. (lúmbay).
Weak. (lumíng; see malúya).
Pale, pallid, blanched, bloodless, wan, sallow, ghastly. (lún-ad; see maláspì, malúspad).
Soft, melting, pliable, tender, supple, yielding, impressible, impressionable. (see lúnay, mahómok, malúm-ok).
Dim. of lúnay, malúnay. Malunáylúnay siá sing tagiposóon. She is tender-hearted, soft-hearted.
Oppressive, arbitrary, masterful, tyrannical, tyrannic, tyrannous, cruel, severe, dour, despotic, dominating, domineering, harsh. (see lúpig, mapigusón).
See malúpig.
Pale, pallid, wan, blanched, bloodless, white, sallow, colourless. (see lúpsì, malúpsì, maláspî, malúspad, malún-ad).
Itch, pain; to itch, hurt, pain (of a healing wound).
Faded, fading, of a fading colour. (see lús-aw).
See malús-aw.
Wan, pale, pallid, etc. See malúpsì.
Dark, deep, pronounced (of colours). (see lútò, tagúngtung).

Weak, frail, feeble, nerveless, enervated, debilitated, unstrung, strengthless, powerless. Malúya ang íya láwas. Malúya siá sing láwas. He is weak. His health is impaired. Malúya siá sing buút. He lacks will power. He is weak-kneed. (see lúya, malumíng, mapígaw).
(H) Fond of, liking, having a liking or passion for, desirous of, etc. See maluluyagón id.
(B) For malúyag from lúyag-to like.
For mamaón from mamâ-to chew betelnut.
(B) To chew betel-nut; betel-nut chewing. Malúyag ka magmamâ? Do you like to chew betel-nut?

(B) To flatten, make flat (by pressure or by pounding), to crush or beat flat. Mamáa (lubáka, báyha) ang ságing, kay láktan ko sing kalámay. Pound the bananas soft (flat), for I am going to mix them with sugar. Mamái siá sing búnga, kay índì siá makadulút. Crush the betel-nut for him, for he is unable to bite it through. Imámà akó ánay siníng mga ságing nga tinanók. Please pound these boiled bananas for me. (lumâ, pusâ, lúbak, bayó).
(Sp. mama) Mother, mama, mamma; a wet-nurse. (see nánay, ilóy, yáya).
Old man, father.
Wet nurse. See mamá.
(H) Strong, stiff, fresh, fierce, violent, rushing, blustering (of wind; see mádlus).
(Sp. mamador) The nipple of a baby's feeding bottle; nursing bottle; instrument to draw off milk. (see beberón, lulutgútan).

Light, airy, easy to bear or carry, not heavy or weighty. Mamág-an ang íya lúlan, pagbátyag, panghunâhúnà, etc. His burden is light, he is much better or feels only a slight pain, his mind is at ease, etc. (see mág-an, mabúg-at-heavy).

Perfect, entire, whole, blameless, without blemish or defect, particularly applied to tobacco-leaves, etc.; good-looking, handsome, nice, attractive, beautiful, comely, pretty (of face, etc.) (see mahî, bilóg, maáyo, maányag, magayón, matahúm, maámbong).
Dim. of mamahî. Rather well developed, not much torn or fissured, pretty well, etc.

Dry, exsiccated, desiccated, arid, waterless, parched, free from moisture, drained; seasoned (of wood). Mamalá nga pagkádlaw. A dry laugh i.e. not a hearty smile, not an honest laugh, but a forced smile. (see malá, mabasâ-wet).
Mortal, subject to death. (see patáy, palátyon, namátyan).
Payer, one who pays. (see báyad).
Poet; poetical, imaginative. (see baláybay, binaláybay).
A kind of shrub with clusters of flowers and berries.
Seller, merchant, vender. (see balígyà).
Bogey, imp, sprite, goblin, elf, hobgoblin, bad fairy, wicked spirit; scarecrow; phantom. (see báhoy, pamáhoy).
Lying in wait for, ambushing, waylaying; robber, brigand. (see bángan).
Saviour, redeemer, liberator. (see báwì).
A ghost, shade, spectre, disembodied spirit, apparition, wraith, soul appearing after death, etc. See malánhig.
Publisher, reporter, journalist, publicity agent, disseminator of news, correspondent, (see bantálà).
A writer of history, historian, historiographer, chronicler, annalist. (see marágtas).
Elf, goblin, sprite, fairy, ghost, etc. (see mamamáhoy, tamáo, tumáo, kamâkamâ, etc.).
Wet nurse. (see máma).
A kind of tree with edible fruit. (see támbis).
Fold, kilt, plait; to fold, kilt, plait. Butangán sing mámbis-or-mambisí ang íya bestído. Plait her dress.
(Sp. mameluco) Mameluke; dolt, simpleton; half-breed; a kind of rompers or underwear for small children.
One who chooses or selects something; voter, elector. (see pílì, pamílì, pumilílì, palapilián, piniliáy).
Dreary, lonely, sad, dismal, dejected, doleful, sentimental, melancholy, mournful, gloomy, depressing, cheerless, joyless. (see míngaw).
One peso each, a peso for each. Nabayáran ko silá sing mamísos ang inádlaw. I paid them each a peso a day. Mamísos karón ang kílo sang kapé. A kilo of coffee costs one peso now. (see písos).

(B) A contr. of mamun-á-from munâ-to tarry, loiter, remain a long time, protract one's stay; to be at ease, be calm or tranquil. Indì ka mámnà dídto. Don't stay there a long time, don't loiter there. Indì gid mámnà ang íya hunâhúnà túbtub nga masayóran níya kon nakadángat na sa Manílà ang íya anák nga bág-o pa lang magsakáy. She cannot rest at ease till she knows whether her son, who a short while ago embarked for Manila, has safely arrived there. (see munâ, dúgay, lúsgò).
(Sp. mamon) Cake, tart, sweet bread, sponge-cake.
Thick, stout; heavy (of rain). (see madámol, madákmol).
A kind of fish of a considerable size and much esteemed as food.
Disparaging, carping, captious, fault-finding, hypercritical, finding fault with, an adverse critic, fault-finder. (see múlay).
A workman, peasant, hind, yokel, unskilled or agricultural labourer, farm-hand. (see pógon, púgon, hornaléro).
One who washes clothes; washerwoman, laundress, washerman, laundry-man. (see búnak, labandéra).
Decorator, embellisher, adorner. (see puní).
Stabber, slayer, killer, murderer, gangster, thug, assassin, cut-throat. (see bunô).
A constellation, a cluster of stars.
(B) Shady, thick, dense, leafy (of foliage). (see múrong, madábung, magápà).

Also, too, as well as; well! now! Look here! Nagupúd man ikáw sa íya? Did you also accompany him? Siá malúyag magkádto man. He would like to go too. Man, nagsilíng akó sa ímo nga--. Now, look here, I told you that--. Quite frequently "man" seems to be employed as a mere decorative particle, e.g. Daw alóla man lang inâ sa ímo. That is only a trifling matter for you. Kon amó man lang ang ákon pangabúhì dirí, maáyo pa nga mapaúlì akó sa ákon bánwa. If my life here is to be only this, it would be better for me to return to my home-town. Kon sa isá man ka bágay matúod inâ--. If on the one hand-or-in one respect that is true--. Amó man gihápon. The same as ever, no change or variation, matters stand as before.
(B) See panghimál-i, kalibutáni id. Man-ihí ko kará. How can I know it. I know nothing about it. (see máan).
Snake, serpent, viper. (see sawá).
To call the dog, call the dogs together. (see tókoy, panókoy).
To benumb, cause numbness by a blow or knock. Namán-ol ang síko ko, kay nakasúnggò akó sa díngding. My elbow was benumbed, for I knocked it against the wall.
(B) He says (said) or thinks (thought). (see silíng, níya).
(Sp. maná) Manna.
(B) Low, not high. (see nabâ, manobô).
Shallow, not deep. (nábaw).
(Sp. manada) Flock, herd. (see panóng, hubón).
A kind of small harmless snake.
Rather well-to-do, neither rich nor poor, satisfactory, sufficient. (see dawâdawâ, hingánhingán, dirâdirâ).
Children of a husband or wife by a former wife or husband; step-children.
(B) I say (think) or said (thought). (see maná, silíng, ko).
Prophet, seer, foreteller, prognosticator. (see tágnà).
Musician; musical. (találay, tulálay; see manulálay id.).
Nice, beautiful; delightful, delicious. (námì).
Savoury, tasty, nice, delicious, lovely, palatable, said of food and drinks. (námit).
A kind of rice that is highly esteemed on account of its whiteness and fine flavour. (see arabón).
Protector, helper, upholder, intercessor, patron; lawyer, advocate, attorney-at-law. (see tábang).
Fisher, fisherman. (see panágat, mangingísdà).
Pouncing upon like birds of prey, grabbing, tearing to pieces (as a bird of prey does). Píspis nga mananágit. A bird of prey. (see dágit).
Prophet. (see manalágnà). (tágnà-lágnà).
Tailor, seamstress. (see tahî)
Passenger, traveller on any vehicle on land, sea or in the air. (sakáy; see sumalákay id.).
Usurper, transgressor, encroacher. (see sáklam).
Palatable, tasty, nice, said especially of nuts (nanám; see manámit-tasty (in general).
Eye-witness, spectator, onlooker. (see tán-aw).
Planter, farmer; gardener. (see tanúm).
Domestic animals; meat of animals that live and breed on land.
A critic, one who censures or finds fault with, a fault-finder. (see sawáy).
The eldest sister. Si mánang mo diín? Diín si mánang mo? Where is your eldest sister. (see mánong-eldest brother).
The vocative of mánang.
Toddy-gatherer, tubâ-collector, one whose daily business is to climb a number of coconut palms and to collect the palm-wine. (see tubéro-a seller of, dealer in, tubá).
A kind of bird of prey; a hawk.
See manáda.
See manaól.
(H) Familiarly used for mánang-eldest sister.
Complacent, cheerful, merry, jolly, gay. (nayánáya).
Open, clear, unobstructed, extensive, wide, spacious (said of fields, etc.). (see náyap, mahanáyap, mahanáyak, mahanáhay).
Far away, distant, remote, a long way off. (see nayók-náyok).
Victor, conqueror, winner; victorious, triumphant. (see daúg).

(B) (Sp. mandato) Order, command, mandate, injunction, regulation, precept; leader; ringleader, originator, one who starts or is chiefly responsible for an act. Ikáw gid ang mandátos sinâ. It was you who started that. You are the one who is responsible for that. (see sógò, kasogoán, pangúlo, manugpahítò, kábo, manugdumála).
Aunt; stepmother, foster-mother; dear old woman. (see tíà, tíyà, darâ, áling, bóboy).

(Sp. mandar) To rule, guide, direct, govern, sway, regulate, control, have authority over, hold sway, command, lead. Iámpò ta nga mandoán sang Diós si N.N. sa pagdumála sa áton sing maáyo. Let us pray to God that he may direct N.N. so that he may govern us well. Sín-o ang nagamándò? Who is in charge? Who commands or rules? (see gahúm, dumála, pasunúd, sógò, buót).
(Sp. mando) Authority, office, power, sway, rule, command. (see gahúm, palangakóan, dumála, batúta).
(Sp. mandragora) Mandrake, mandragora.
See manghátì, manghatión-twenty-five centavos each, etc. (see kahátì).
Tourist, sight-seer, traveller; emigrant, home-seeker, one who goes to live or moves to another place. (see malangályaw, mangangáyaw, pangáyaw).
(H) Reaper, harvester, one who reaps rice by means of a "kayóg". (see áni, manganganí, manuganí).
An insect with a very painful sting. See alingáyo, kamaláyo.
Rider, horseman, cavalry. (see kabáyo, kabayó).
Lease-holder, tenant. (see ágsa, agsadór).
One who is-responsible,-in charge,-in authority; official, functionary. (see ákò, palangakóan).
Shell-gatherer, shell-collector; whoremonger, one who runs after girls. (see kalámpay, pangalámpay).
Singer. (see ámba, kantór, kantóra).
Reaper, harvester. See mangalaní.
Eater, feaster. (see káon).
Helper, supporter, assistant, second, upholder, protector. (see ápin, umalapín).
A representative, delegate, senator; proxy, one who presents himself or confronts a situation. (see atúbang, tigpangatubáng).
Fighter, warrior, soldier; martial. (see áway, soldádo).
Thief, etc. See makáwtì, makáwat.
Stranger, foreigner, sojourner, tourist, traveller. See mangalályaw, etc.
A small sea-shell so called. (see búskay, búli, sigáy).
(Sp. manga) Sleeve. (see pakô, pákpak, sóol).
(Sp. mango) The mango-tree and its fruit. (see páhò).

Riches, possessions, property, wealth, assets, capital; to become rich, acquire property, etc. Ang kalabánan sang mga táo nagapaningúhà magmánggad. The majority of men strive to become rich. Nagmánggad siá sa íla nga palatikángan. He got rich in their business. (see pagkabutáng).
(H) Rich, wealthy, well-to-do, possessed of property, propertied, affluent, opulent, man of means. (see mánggad, manggaránon).
Rich, etc. See manggáran. (see pilákan, bangkílan, aligyanán).
(Sp. mango) Penholder, handle, helve, haft (of tools, etc.). (see ápal, kaláptan, pólo, uluyatán).
Trouble-maker, rowdy, gangster, turbulent fellow, ruffian, riotous, revolutionary, disturbing the peace. (see gúbat, huróng, manriríbok, magamó).
To arrange, put in order, sort, assort, classify, manage well. (Perhaps from the Sp. manejar). Manghará ang baráha mo. Arrange your cards in order according to their suits. (see kaláging, húsay).
Twenty-five centavos each, costing twenty-five centavos. Ginabalígyà níya iní sing manghátì. He sells it at twenty-five centavos a piece. (see kahátì, mangahátì).
Worth or costing twenty-five centavos. (see manghátì, kahátì, mangahatión).
(B) Merciful, compassionate, feeling for, commiserative, condoletory, ruthful, pitiful, etc. See malolóy-on. (see ngír-o).
One who judges, a judge, justice. (see hokóm, panghokóm).
A younger brother or sister; not of age, minor; not ripe, unripe, immature, green (of fruits). (see libáyon, kalibáynan, línghod).
A kind of very tasty banana. (see balángon, barángon).
Considerate, thoughtful, careful, solicitous; attentive, mindful, heedful, regardful. (see ngílin).
(B) Setting the teeth on edge, etc. See manílo.

A contr. that often stands for magapangin-, magpangin-and (rarely) for nagapangin-. Indì ka mangintigúlang, kon índì nímo pagduláon ang maláut mo nga kaduyugán. You won't grow old, unless you give up your bad habits. Iníng dakû nga minurô manginbánwa kunína. This large village will finally become a township or Municipality. Sa dílì madúgay manginkabangdánan iní sang íya nga pagkapúto. This, before long, will be the cause of his bankruptcy, will make him bankrupt. N.B. Mangin-is also, but seldom, used to form nouns and adjectives, e.g. manginalámon-a wise man. (see nangin-).
A wise, learned, clever man, a doctor, sage, savant. (see mangin-, álam).
A verbal form of panginbabáe, panginbabáye, but sometimes used as an adjective like palanginbabáe-addicted to women, etc.
One who eats raw meat, etc.; a cannibal. (see kílaw).
Fisherman, fisher, angler. (see ísdà, pangísdà).
A verbal form of panginlaláki, but sometimes used as an adjective like palanginlaláki-addicted to men, etc.
A shell-gatherer, collector of sea-shells; grabber, grafter, boodler. (see pangínhas, pakinháson).
(B) Merciful. See manghír-óhon id. (ngír-o).
(B) Compassionate, merciful. See manghir-óhon.

Troublous, boiling, throbbing, pricking, stinging, stabbing, gnawing, hard to bear or suffer. Mangítngit nga pangabúhì. A troublous or hard life. Mangítngit nga konsiénsya. A conscience that pricks. (see ngítngit, malisúd, mangótngot).
Dark, obscure, black, dusky, ebon, sable, opaque. (see ngitóngitó, maitúm, ilóm, átà, áta, ágtà, madulúm, pitípit).
(B) Jack tree and jack fruit. (see lángkà id.).
A kind of hardwood tree and its valuable timber.
Seeker, one who looks for something. Manglalághap sing palangágdan. A job-hunter, an office-seeker. (see lághap).
Tourist, traveller, one who takes a vacation or travels for pleasure. (see lagúyaw).
One who walks on foot, a footman, foot-soldier, infantry-man; infantry. (see lakát).
One who encroaches upon-, usurps-, wrongfully takes possession of-, another's property. (see láksam).
Bombardier, artilleryman; artillery. (see lantáka).
Searcher, investigator, one of a search party. (see líghot).
A peso of Philippine money. (see písos).

To widen, be or become wide. Kon dugángan magadiótay, kon ibánon nagamángmang. Anó inâ?-Búhò inâ. If something is added, it grows smaller, if something is taken away from it, it grows wider. What is that?-That is a hole. (see wángwang, bángbang).
Rich, having plenty of money. (see mángmang, pilákan, manggáran, manggaránon, bankílan, aligyanán).
Dull, stupid, brainless; an ass, fool. (see tipangág, pangág, pángog, balingág, balingá, búngaw, tampuháw, búang, kólò).
Head, chief, director, manager, leader, boss, spokes-man, ruler, authority, official. (see ólo).
Palpitating, quivering, throbbing (of wounds, the conscience, etc.). (see ngótngot, mangítngit).
Brave, courageous, fearless, reliable, trustworthy, fierce. Mángtas nga idô. A good watchdog. (see mántas).
A charcoal-burner, charcoal-man. (see úling).
Farmer, tiller of the soil, agricultural labourer. (see umá).
One that is attached; supporter, friend, helper, assistant, partner. (see únung).
Debtor, one who owes a debt or borrows money. (see útang).
(Sp. mangostán) Mangosteen.
Preacher, missioner, clergyman. (see wáli).

Open, roomy, spacious; well off, well to do, prosperous; to be well to do, etc. Manháwà na ang íya kahimtángan. He is well off, has some property, is living in easy circumstances. Mangabúdlay kamó sing may kapísan, agúd maluás kamó sa kaimolón kag magmanháwà ang ínyo pangabúhì. Work hard and assiduously to free yourself from poverty and to get on well in life. (see háwà, manwáhà, dawâdawâ, dir-á-dirâ, kaayohán).
(Sp. maní) Peanut, earthnut, groundnut, goober.
A plant that in its leaves resembles the peanut plant.
(Sp. manivela) Steering wheel.
Trim, neat, tidy. See mahípid, mahípig. (see nídnid).
Little, small, tiny, wee, diminutive. (see tikî, maisót, diótay, ikî).
Ticklish, irritating, having a creepy or ticklish feeling, easily tickled; nervous, excited. (see hilás).
(B) Tingling, grating, squeaking, sharp, gritty, setting one's teeth on edge, said of sensations, etc. (see nílo, mangílo, mangiló).
Godmother. (see padríno, panínoy-godfather; madrína).
Agonizing, in one's last agony, on one's death bed. (see tingâ).
Docile, obedient, submissive, submitting, yielding, dutiful, but mostly used in the negative form dìmanínggol-stubborn, disobedient, headstrong, obdurate, intractable. (see tínggol, panínggol).
A potter, one who makes or sells earthenware vessels; manufacturing, industrial. (see díhon).
Watchful, observing, observant, prying, spying; spy, detective, sleuth. Polís nga maniniíd. Secret service man. Detective. (see tíid, maninilág, tíktik, lampitáw).
A thief; pilfering, thievish. (tíkas).
Thief, petty thief, pilferer, sneak. (see tíkmà, maniníkas).
An observer, spy. (panílag).
A kind of a dark-coloured snake growing to a considerable size and very harmful to chickens, eggs, etc., but non-poisonous.
Setting fire to, an incendiary, one who commits arson. (see síndot).
A listener, eavesdropper, one who overhears a conversation, a spy. (see tingád).
Trickling, flowing sparsely or slowly. (see ninít).
Thin, fine, light, flimsy (of paper, cloth, boards, etc.). (see nipís, madámol, madákmol-thick).
(H) Round, spherical, rotund, circular, annular, cylindrical. (see tipólon, matimbúlug, matibúnug).
Lean, thin, spare, lank, emaciated, meagre, gaunt, skinny, slight, slender. (see níwang, mahágpis, kanít, kandínggal, matámbok-fat, stout).
Dim. of maníwang. Rather lean, slightly emaciated.

(Sp. manilla) Manacle, gyve, shackle, handcuff; to fetter; to entangle, get entangled, be caught, become involved (in a rope, sling, etc.). Nagmaníya ang karabáw. The buffalo entangled itself with the tether or rope. (see gápus, gapús, bulíbud).
See mángkà-jackfruit.
A kind of large-eyed (broad-eyed) frog; vermin; a wild boar or pig; wild beasts in general.
See manglalagúyaw-a tourist.
Devouring, swallowing, gobbling up; fierce, bloodthirsty. (see lámon, manunúkub, mananágit).
Spreading, catching, taking, infectious, contagious, epidemic, epidemical. (see latón, malaláton).
Revolutionary, riotous, mutinous, agitator, exciting a commotion or tumult. (see ribók).
A kind of small octopus. (see kugíta-a large octopus).
A large sea shell.
Redeemer, saviour, liberator, rescuer, deliverer. (see luás, mamamáwì, manunúbus).
One who (that which) unbinds, solves, opens, explains or translates something. Manlulúbad sang hámbal. An interpreter. (see lubád).
Flyer, aviator; winged. (see lupád).

A contraction of manungâ. Also: middle-aged, from about thirty-five to fifty-five years of age. Daw anó kamál-am (katigúlang) si Fuláno?-Mánngà (siá). How old is N.N.?-He is middle-aged. (see médya, bída).

(Sp. mano) The hand; the lead, a hand of cards (in card-playing); the right side; direction to a driver of a vehicle to turn to the right or to the side opposite the "sílya". (see kamót, manohán, sílya).
Low, depressed, short, not high or tall. (see nobô, manabâ).
Dim. of manobô. Rather low, rather short, of low stature, a little less than normal in height. Maníwang siá kag manobônóbò. He was lean and rather low in stature.

A prefix denoting occupation with what the root or term implies to which it is attached, e.g. manogarádo-a plougher; manogdumúg-a wrestler; manoghábul-a weaver; manoglála-a basket-weaver, one who makes wickerwork; manogabút-one about, or expected, to arrive; manogkádto-one about to leave or go somewhere, manogtapús-one about to finish or complete (his studies, a job, etc.). N.B. Very frequently the prefix manog-produces a shifting of the accent of the term to which it is attached, e.g. manogdumúg (dúmug); manoghábul (habúl); manogtapús (tápus) and many more. (manug-id.).
A member of a fire-brigade, fireman. (see pálong, súnug).
An object played from the hand in various games, as a ball, stone, marble, card, etc. (see máno).
Fowl, chicken; cock, gamecock; poultry. (see agák, sulúg, mungâ, pisô, sumaláyhaw, kilawát, dumalága, damulága).
Somewhat like or resembling a chicken; squinting slightly.
Low, mean, boorish, uncultured, very common, rough, coarse, rude, vulgar, not fit or proper for educated or refined people. (see bástos).
The eldest brother. (see mánang-the eldest sister).
The vocative of mánong.
(Sp. manojo) A handful; a bunch, batch, string of, rope of, bundle; a bundle of one hundred tobacco leaves on a string, or the like.
(H) Eldest brother (familiar). (see mánong, manóng).
(Sp. mancha) Stain, blotch, blur, taint, spot, blot, blemish, dirt. (see dágtà, bulíng, hígkò, etc.).
(Sp. manzana) Apple.
(Sp. manzanilla) The common chamomile, a medicinal plant.
See amansebádo-one living in concubinage.
Nurse, wet-nurse, children's nurse. (see yáya, sisiwá).
(English: manchester) White cotton cloth, twill, drill, Manchester goods or wares.
(Sp. manso) Tame, domestic, domesticated, gentle, meek, willing, broken in, well trained, subdued, tractable. (see mahagúp, mabúot, antâ).
(Sp. manta) A woollen blanket; shawl, travelling rug. (see hábul, abláy, kúnop, kápay).
Reliable, etc. (of watch-dogs). See mángtas id.
(Sp. manteca) Lard, fat, dripping. (see támbok).
(Sp. mantequilla) Butter.
(Sp. mantel) Table-cloth, altar-cloth, table-cover. (see tabón).
(Sp. mantellina) Mantilla, a woman's head-shawl, woman's veil. (see kúnop, kúmbung, takuróng, tákdong, kúdong).

(Sp. mantener) To maintain, keep up, hold out, support, keep alive, manage to go on. Nagamantenér gid lang silá sang íla pangabúhì. They are just managing to keep alive, they are supporting themselves rather poorly or with difficulty. Mantenehón mo ánay ang kalát, kay kuháon ko pa ang tigíb. Hold the rope in position, for I am going to fetch the chisel. Komústa kamó?-Nagamantenér kamí. How are you?-We are getting along pretty well. Nagaduhádúha akó kon makamantenér siá dídto sing maláwig nga tión. I wonder (doubt), whether he will be able to support himself there (remain there) for any length of time. Mantenér lang. It will do-for the present,-to go on with. It is only-a make-shift,-a temporary substitute, or the like.
See mantenér.
A ghost. See mantíw.
Bewitched, charmed, wonderful. (see mantíw).
A bugbear, a ghost supposed to be of gigantic proportions and of terrible aspect; jinnee, jinn.
Bewitched, etc. See mantihón.
(Sp. manto) A head-covering, head-shawl (for women). (see mantelyína).
A ghost. See mantíw.
Preying upon, devouring, ravening, rapacious, catching and tearing to pieces. (see subád-sibád, síbà, manúkub).
See manog-.
Butcher, slaughterer, dealer in meat. (see íhaw).
Fisher, fisherman, angler, fishmonger or dealer in fish, seller of fish. (see ísdà).
(B) Daughter-in-law. (see umágad-son-in-law; in some places manúgang and umágad are used promiscuously for son-in-law and daughter-in-law). (see dúgang, ágad).
Doing well, recovering, getting well, improving (of sick persons); promising, likely to turn out well (of crops, etc.). (see áyo, marayádon).
Buyer, purchaser, customer. (see bakál, súkì).
Seller, salesman, saleswoman, dispenser, vender, vendor, retailer, dealer, merchant. (see balígyà).
Dentist. (see bánsil).
Watch, watchman, guard, keeper, sentry, sentinel, shepherd, custodian, observer; tutor, warder, warden, guardian. (see bántay).
One who is an adept at working various designs into cloth. An expert in arranging and adapting the thread of the warp for making multicoloured designs. (see bibít).
Maker, artificer, craftsman, manufacturer, creator, builder, constructer, constructor. (búhat). (see magbubúhat).
Doctor, medical man, physician, healer, leech. (bulúng).
A singer of Christmas carols. (see daígon).
Governor, director, administrator, manager, ruler, boss. (dumála).
An expert in removing foreign bodies from the eye, eye-cleaner, oculist. (see gáhid).
Hair dresser, barber. (gúnting).
Masseur, masseuse, one who practises massage. (see hílot).
A palmister, fortune-teller, chiromancer, one who practises palmistry. (see pálad, himálad).
Collector-, gatherer-, seller-, of firewood; dealer in wood. (see káhoy).
A sawyer, one who saws wood. (see lagárì).
Preacher, adviser, counsellor, admonisher. (see láygay).
Care-taker; nurse. Manuglíbang sang kabatáan, sang mga masakít, etc. A children' nurse, an infirmarian, etc. (see libáng).
Debater, disputant, controversialist. (báis).
Propagator, disseminator, distributer, agent. (see lápnag).
A circus-master, an acrobat, tumbler. (sírko-Sp. circo).
One who pushes or presses forward. Manugsiúg sang tigbató. A type-setter. (see síug).
Author, writer, a literary man. (see sulát, magsusúlat, manunúlat).
Investigator, inspector, examiner. Manugsusipuód. Manugsusipuodnanon. Provincial Inspector. (see súsi).
Tailor, cutter. (see tábas, sástre).
Prophet, seer, fore-teller, predictor. (see tágnà, manalágnà, mananágnà).
Manager, care-taker, administrator. (tátap).
Messenger, harbinger, bringer of tidings, angel. (túndà).
Messenger; angel. (see manunúndà, manugtúndà, anhél).
(Probably from the Sp. tumbar) A stunner, surprising, amazing, overwhelming, overpowering.
One who is a frequent caller or likes to visit from house to house. (panumbálay).
A farmer, tiller of the soil, peasant; rustic, rude, uncultured. (see umá, umánhon).
A half, one half each. (see tungâ, mánngà).
A kind of vine whose bitter juice is used as an antiseptic in cleaning wounds, etc.
Guide, leader. (see tóytoy).
A disturber; disturbing, interrupting, interfering with, causing a disturbance. (see túblag).
Redeemer, saviour, deliverer, liberator. (see manlulúas, mamamáwì, tubús).
An unwelcome visitor, a parasite, sycophant. (see panudángsudáng).
Teacher, etc. See manunúon, maéstro. (see túdlò, panúdlo).
Seer, prophet, propounder of riddles, riddle maker, riddle solver; wise, sage. (see túgma).
Tearing to pieces, pouncing upon, devouring, preying, (beast) of prey. (see tubúk).
A writer, author. See magsusúlat, manugsúlat.
A tempter; the devil. (see suláy, panuláy).
Accuser, plaintiff. Manunúmbung puodnánon. Provincial Fiscal. (see súmbung).
Teacher, professor, master, tutor, instructor. (see toón, magtotóon, magtutúon).
Plotter, gangster, murderer, conspirator, one who intends to harm, or to wreak vengeance upon, others. (see tuyô).
To go on well, prosper, make progress, be well-to-do. (see manháwà).

An exclamation of remonstrance, or disappointment, etc. Manyági, kay nagahípus ang bátà, ginapahibî mo! Good heavens, as the baby is quiet, don't make it cry! Manyági, kay nagapahimúyong ang alimángo sa búhò, ginkúot mo; tî, kóndì ginkagát níya ikáw. There now, you disturbed with your finger the crab at rest in its hole; of course it bit you and it serves you right. (see yádi, yádan).

(B) Greedy, voracious, ravenous, wolfish, gluttonous. The verb is minaóg-to be greedy, eat greedily. Maóg siá nga táo. He is a greedy man. He is a voracious eater. Indì ka magminaóg. Don't be greedy. (see hákug, dalók, dinalók).

(Sp. mapa) A map, plan, drawing, topographic outline; to map, map out, make a map. Mapáha iníng papél. Use this paper to draw a plan on. Mapáhi ang ákon dútà. Make a map of my lands. Mapáhi akó sang ákon talámnan. Make me a map of my fields. Buás ugáling pagasóklon kag pagamapáhan ko ang ímo nga dútà. Not just now, but to-morrow I will measure your grounds and draw a map of them.

A prefix composed of "ma" and "pa-". Sán-o mo mapabúhat ang ímo bág-o nga baláy? When shall you be able to have your new home built? "mapa-" frequently stands for "magapa-", e.g. Sán-o ka mapamanílà (magapamanílà)? When are you going to Manila? Ang mga matárung mapalángit, ang mga mamatáy sa salâ nga ikamatáy mapainpiérno. The just will go to heaven, those that die in mortal sin will go to hell. (see nagapa-, naga-, pa-).
Bitter, acrid, biting, piquant, pungent; cruel, severe, painful, poignant. (pa-ít).
Hot, stuffy, sultry, close, sweltry, oppressive. (páang). (see mabóhot, magín-ot).
Negligent, careless, letting things take their course without any serious reflection or effort at remedying the state of affairs, putting off, procrastinating, (see pabuyánbúyan).
(H) Amenable to persuasion or bribery, easily led, easily won over by argument or bribes. (dalá).
Sharp, cutting, caustic, sarcastic, ironic, mordent, biting, pointed (of speech); to be or become sharp, etc. (see padás, maparás, magíska).
One easily swayed or carried along, not steadfast, not firm of character, unreliable, vacillating. (see dalá, padalá).
Firm, steady, strong, solid, stable, unshakable, stanch, staunch. (see pág-on, malíg-on, salalígan, mabákud).
Strong, firm, solid, robust. (see págrus, mapág-on, mabákud).
Quick, agile, nimble, swift. (págsi). (see mapágsik, malígsi).
See mapágsi. (págsik-págsi).
Open, frank, candid, plain spoken. (see paháyag).
Changeable, mutable, variable, unstaid, inconstant, not reliable or trustworthy, fickle. (see paháylo).
Patient, meek, tolerant, submissive, resigned, gentle, long-suffering, bearing with. (see paílub).
See the following mapainubúson.
Humble, lowly, submissive, self-effacing, unassuming, modest, meek. (see ubús, paubús).
See mapailúbon.
(H) Abstinent, abstemious, frugal, self-denying, temperate or moderate in eating and drinking. (úmud).
Weak, slow; dull, stupid, obtuse, backward, (pákok; see malúya, mabúndul, malúyò, kagúng, kalóng).
(H) Postponing, dilatory, putting off, procrastinating, letting things pass by, paying no attention to, heedless. (lígad).
Wiping out, destroying, obliterating, rubbing out, removing all trace of, erasing. (see pánas).
Generous, liberal, munificent, free, open-handed; giver, giving. (see hátag, maálwan).
(H) Circumspect, prudent, watchful, wary, chary, cautious. Ang táo nga mapanginlamánon malayô sa katalágman. A cautious man is far removed from danger. Forewarned, forearmed. (see panginláman).
Urinous, smelling-of urine,-like urine. (see pángsot).
See mapanghatágon.
Observant, watchful, open-eyed, alive to, awake to, vigilant, wide awake, guarded, on the lookout. (see panílag).
(B) Assiduous, diligent, with zeal or application. (see pántok, mapísan, maúkud, mabákas, matútum).
(H) See mapadás-cutting of speech, etc.
Thankful, grateful, indebted to, obliged, under obligation. (see salámat, pasalámat).
Partial, one-sided, inequitable, giving preference to, prejudiced, narrow-minded. (see labí).
Thoughtful, regardful, considerate, kind. (see pasunáid).
Open, plain, clear, unobstructed, said of land and fields. (pátag). (see mahanáyak, mahanáyap).
Forgiving, indulgent, lenient, tolerant, forbearing, ready to pardon, forgetful of wrongs or injuries, not given to revenge or retaliation. (patáwad).
Credulous, gullible, easily believing any story or report, easily taken in. (páti).
(B) Tough, hard, difficult to manage. (pátol; see mahúnit, mahúnlit, maáwot).
Prolific, productive, fertile, fruitful, frugiferous, fecund, yielding a good crop. (see patubás, palatúbson).
Productive, etc. See mapinatubóon.
Considerate, thoughtful, mindful of, having regard or consideration for, conscientious. (see patugsíling).
Negligent, careless, dilatory, procrastinating. (see patumbáyà).
Negligent, unconcerned, careless, heedless. (patumbáya; see mapabuyánbuyánon).
Selfish, egoistic, pleasing oneself, self-indulgent, worldly-minded. (see patúyang).
Humble, etc. See mapainubúson, mapainubsánon.
Clumsy, cumbrous, unwieldy, awkward to carry on account of bulky size or great length, as a large drum, a bird-cage, arm-chair, a long pole, flag-staff, etc. (see páya, mabángkag, magámbal).
One who is very particular about his food, fastidious, dainty, difficult to please. (see pidâ).
Weak, frail, feeble, collapsible. (see pígaw, malúya, mahúyang).
Harsh, oppressive, exploiting, cruel. (see pígus, malúpig).
Harsh, etc. See mapígus, malupígon.
Choosing, fastidious, exacting, selecting, particular about one's food, dress, etc.; finical, finikin, finicking, difficult to please or satisfy, nice in the matter of food, etc. (see pílì, mapidâ).
Sticky, adhesive, viscous, gummy, cohesive, gluey, glutinous, clammy, adhering to. (see pilít).
Insisting, persistent, urging, pressing, importunate; sticking to. (see pílit, pilít).
Clogged, contracted, narrow of aperture, difficult to breathe, asthmatic, choked (of the windpipe, etc.). (see pín-ot).
Lasting, enduring, permanent, constant, persevering. (see dáyon).
Obliging, pleasing, considerate, thoughtful, ingratiating, tactful, regardful. (see buút, hamúot, pahamúot).
Patient, etc. See mapailúbon.
Doting, petting, caressing, fondling, cherishing, kind, kindly, tender, affectionate. (see palánggà).
Devout, pious, a man of prayer. (see pangadî).
Mindful, regardful. Dílì (dî) mapinasapayánon-indifferent, careless, thoughtless. (see sapayán, waláy, sapayán, pagkadilìmapinasapayanón).
Insulting, affronting, deriding, mocking, scoffing, blaspheming, blasphemous, scurrilous, gibing, abusive, jeering, vilifying. (see pasipála).

Filling, absorbing, taking in, devouring, absorbent, stuffing, cramming; one who learns well or has a good memory; one who takes things to heart, sensitive, full of feeling, impressionable. (see sulúd, pasulúd).
Thoughtful, etc. See mapasunaíron.
Credulous, gullible, unsuspecting, easily deceived or tricked. (see páti, mapatípatíhon).
Founding, establishing, erecting, laying the foundations of, instituting; inventing, making up (a story, lie, etc.). (see pátok).
Imaginative, inventive, creative, illusory, fictitious; an adept in getting up plausible stories, or the like. (see patôpátò).
Productive, fertile, good (of soil, etc.). (see túbò).
See mapatumbayáon.
Self-indulgent, etc. See mapatuyángon.
(H) Abstemious, abstinent, mortifying, mortified, self-denying. (see paúmud).
Cruel, pitiless, inhuman, savage, ferocious, fierce, brutal, destitute of mercy or compassion, harsh, atrocious, tyrannical, unjustly severe. (see píntas, mabangís, mabarís).
Useful, of use, of utility, of some good or service, serviceable, profitable, gainful, remunerative, advantageous. (see pulús, mapulús, mapuslánon).
Strict, close, narrow, contracted, straitened, dense, crowded, packed, pressed together, hard-pressed; hard, difficult, severe. (see píot).
Diligent, assiduous, sedulous, hard-working, zealous, industrious, active, energetic, with application. (see písan, maíd-id, matúl-id, maúkud, mabákas).
Hard, hardened, clotty, clotted, cloddy; lumpy, coagulated, full of clods or lumps (of earth, sand, etc.); dry, brittle, hard to swallow (of bread, etc.). (see púg-a).
Red, reddish, ruddy, rufous, florid, sanguine, rosy, incarnadine, carroty, fiery, copper-coloured, crimson, flushed. (see pulá).
Waking, watching, watchful, wakeful, keeping awake, awake, keeping watch or vigil, vigilant, assiduous, not sleepy or lazy. (see puláw, mapuláwon).
See mapúlaw. Also: Wanting little sleep, staying up long, keeping late hours, sleepless.
See mapinuslánon-useful, etc.
Lonely, solitary, isolated, dreary, desolate, dismal. (púng-aw).
Weak, feeble, frail, debile. (pungáy; see malumíng, malúya, mapígaw).
Strong, robust; loud (of voice). (see purús).
See mapinuslánon-useful, etc.
(B) Thick, not thin or slender. (púsug; see madámol id.).
White, snowy, chalky, hoar, hoary, blanched; pure, unsullied, untarnished, candid, uncontaminated, snow-white. (putî).
Dirty, ugly, nasty, abominable, sullied, soiled. (see raíng, mahígkò, maláw-ay, magím-ang, kalaímnan, marígkam, marísmò).
(B) The mole-cricket. See malámalá.
(Sp. maravilla) A kind of flowering plant, marigold; deep pink colour.
Tasty, succulent, delectable, dainty, nice, toothsome, savoury, of good flavour (of fruits and tubers); opposed to maganás-insipid. (see rabó).

Spotted, soiled, disfigured, blotched, blotchy, stained, bloodstained; full of pustules or eruptions (of skin-diseases). Maragáng ang báyò níya sing dugô. His jacket is blood-stained. Maragáng (nagamaragáng) siá sang katúl. His body is covered with eruptions of the skin-disease called katúl. (see ragáng, pamaragáng).
(B) Thick (of paint, or the like). (see rágas, madámol).
Creaking, cracking, squeaking. (see ragíting).
(B) Sticky, viscous, adhesive, stiff. Mabúdlay ang paglakát sa maragkót nga lalaó. Walking through sticky mud is tiresome. (see ragkót, mapilít).
(B) Slightly feverish, etc. See malágnat.
Crisp, short. (see ragomó, mahágpok).
Story, history, event, incident, anecdote, chronicle, record. (see histórya).
Historical, eventful, momentous, memorable. Maragtásnon nga hitabû. An historical event. Maragtásnon nga túig. An eventful year.
Mediocre, neither poor nor rich, neither much nor little, middle-class. (see hingánhingán, dawâdawâ, dirâdirâ).
Quick, swift, very agile, nimble, lithe, lithesome. (see raháyráhay, mapágsik, malígsi, maábtik, madásig, kisáy).
(B) Many, plenty, galore, abundant, abounding. (see rakô, dúro, madámù).
The male of the singgálong (fox; civet cat).
(B) Liable to attract-, to become infested with-, ants called lásgà, particularly said of eatables. (see masulubáyon).

(B) To be wide awake, be fully aware of, to grasp, comprehend, understand, take in. Warâ akó kamarámad kang ginkoón na. (Walâ akó makahangúp (makamarásmas) sang ginsilíng níya). I don't (did not, didn't) understand what he says (said). Karámad kaw kará? (Makasáyod, makahibaló ka sinâ?). Can you understand it? Do you know that? (see malámad, marásmas, hibalú, sáyod, balintúnod, áto, hántup, hangúp).
(B) Cold; stiff. (see ramíg, malamíg, matúgnaw).
(B) A ghost, spectre, etc. See malánhig.
(B) Stinking, smelling, having a bad smell, giving off a stench, of an evil or obnoxious smell or odour. (see rapúg, mabahô, mabáhò, makalolóod, makangingíl-ad).
(B) Daring, bold, defiant, impertinent, audacious, insolent, froward; cunning, resourceful. (see rárang, makáhas, masúpug, maaháng, malálang).

(B) Good, well, etc. See maáyo. Dílì marása ang íya památì (pagbátì). His health is not good. He is sick. Marása gid ang íya nga batásan. His behaviour (character) is excellent. His manners are engaging. (see rása).

To be wide (fully) awake, be awake to, to grasp, comprehend, understand, take in, take. Walâ siá makamarásmas sang ákon nga gin silíng. He could not understand what I said. Namarasmasán níya ang tanán nga ginpaháyag ni Fuláno. He comprehended all that N.N. expounded. Namarasmasán akó sang dídto na akó sa baláy. I recovered my senses when I got to the house. (see marámad, mádmad, hangúp, hántup, balintúnod, áto, sáyod, másngà).
(B) Getting well or better; promising. See manugáyo. (see ayád).
(B) See malayô-distant, far away, etc.
(Sp. marga, margajita) Pyrites, mispickel; marl.
A kind of flowering plant, the common daisy.
See amargóso.
Disturbing the peace, rebellious, riotous, tumultuous, turbulent, disorderly, revolutionary, mutinous. (ribók).
(B) Thick, stout, round, plump, fat of arms, calves, cheeks, etc. (ribúok). (see matibúnog, matipúlon, manipólon).
(B) See maribúok. (ribusól).
(Sp. marido) Husband. (see bána).
Hot, sultry, stuffy, sweltry, close; disturbed, upset, perplexed, confused, excited through overwork or through having too many things to attend to. (rigáhot). (see magín-ot, mabóhot, gomón).
Dirty, filthy, nasty, nauseating. (see rígkam, mahígkò, makalolóod, makangilíl-ad, raíng).
Haunted, weird, dreary, desolate, depressing, lonely, lonesome, inspiring fear, uncanny, said particularly of lonely places. (see ríit).
Complicated, mingled, combined, confused, involved. (rikót). (see gomón). Marikót nga pangabúdlay. Complicated work that requires great patience, etc.
(B) Dim. of marímis. Rather sweet, sweetish.
(B) Sweet, sugary, syrupy. (see rímis, matám-is, dólse).

(B) Hidden, secret, difficult to find, out of the way, concealed, not open to view or inspection. Marírong nga lugár ang tinagóan níya sang ákon líbro. He has hidden my book in a secret place or hidden nook. (see maríit).
(B) Dirty, soiled, stained, old and torn. (see rísmò, mahígkò, etc.).

(Sp. marca) Mark, sign, brand, trade-mark, standard; to mark, sign, brand. Markahí ang karabáw. Brand the buffalo. Bákli akó sing agás nga márka manók. Buy me some kerosene of the Cock brand. (see pát-in, doón, timáan).
(Sp. marques, marquesa) Marquis, marquess; marchioness, marquise.
(Sp. marmol) Marble. Batungdáan nga mármol (bukáy). A marble monument. (see bató, nga, bukáy).

The rice-flower; to flower (of rice). Ang humáy nagamarô na. The rice is now flowering or in bloom. Sa duhá ka simána magamarô ang humáy sa ákon talámnan. Within two weeks the rice on my field will be in flower. Namaroán na akó sang ákon humáy. My rice has flowered, blossomed.
(B) Wild, untamed. (see simarón id.).
A kind of small fish.
(Sp. marfil) Ivory.
(Sp. Marzo) March. (see dagangbúlan).
A large earthen jar somewhat resembling a tádyaw, but more cylindrical in shape.
(Sp. Martes) Tuesday.
(Sp. martillo) Hammer, mallet. (see palapâ, palô).
(Sp. martir) Martyr. (see tigbatás).
(B) The East. (see murúd-an, sidlangán).
(H) Ever. Dílì nga más-a-never. (see mugís).
(H) To waste, squander, throw away, spend to no purpose. (see kamásà, uyáng, úsik, pilák).
(Sp. masa) Dough, mass, lump; to knead. Masáha ang arína. Knead the flour. Masáhi akó sing isá ka sáko nga arína. Knead one sack of flour for me. (see lamás, malasahón).
(Sp. maza) The hub, nave of a wheel.
(H) Inconvenient, awkward, unmanageable, unwieldy, unsuitable (through being too long, said of sticks, poles, etc., that are too long for a given purpose). (see maságway, mapáya).
Cheerful, jolly, merry, gleeful, blithe, blithesome, mirthful, animated, lively, gay, cheery, sprightly, high-spirited. (see sádya, makalilípay, makalulúyag, makawiwíli, malipáyon, malipayón).
(H) Dark, shaded, dim, dark-coloured, brown, dun, obscure, not very light. (see sagíl-om, itúm, ilómlóm, dulúm).
Taking care of, rearing, bringing up. (see sagúd).
Awkward, clumsy, inconvenient through being too long, or the like. (see masábad, magámbal, mabángkag).
Sick, ill, infirm, ailing, unwell, poorly, sore, out of sorts, seedy, painful, aching, poignant, smarting, hurting, excruciating; sharp, harsh, rough, cutting (of speech). (see sakít).
Dim. of masakít. Slightly ill, indisposed, rather sore, a little painful, paining a little, not quite well, a little out of sorts.
Also: Injured, spoilt, rotten, worm-eaten (of fruits). (see torakón).
Sickly, invalid, unhealthy, having poor health, inclined, or liable, to be often sick; causing pain, painful; sharp, cutting (of speech). (see masakít).
Keeping one very busy, engrossing, causing or giving much work, bustling, hustling, very much occupied, busy, engaged. (see sákò).
Disagreeing, at variance, quarrelling, falling out, at logger-heads, having a difference with. (see sál-ag).
(H) Erring, mistaken, making a-mistake,-blunder,-mess of, blundering, doing a thing wrong, committing a fault or blunder. (see sayúp, masinaláypon).
Pleasing, pleasant, cheerful. (see alikáya, masádya).
Thick, stout, big; near delivery, pregnant, at the last stage of child-bearing. (see samból).

Often, ofttimes, often-times, recurrent, many a time, frequent, many times; again and again, over and over again, repeatedly. Sing masamí áton mapanilágan--. Often we can observe--. (see samí, masúnsun, himánhimán, makadámù).
Interfering, disturbing, bothering, causing annoyance or making oneself a nuisance. (sámok).
Glimmering, crepuscular, faint light, said of twilight; half-light, dim, obscure. (sanáaw).
Clear, bright, light, broad daylight, illuminating, glaring, strong, dazzling; manifest, evident. (see sánag, dayág).
Wide, broad, of large breadth, ample, extended, vast. (see sángkad, malápad, mahanáhay, etc.).
Vehement, fierce, heavy, violent (of fighting, war, etc.). (sángsang). (see hinugúng, sugúng).

Enduring, lasting, continuous, permanent, persisting, abiding, perpetual; extending, advancing, progressing. Masányog siá sing panghunâhúnà. He is liberal-minded, broad-minded, advanced or progressive in his ideas or way of thinking. (see sányog).

Rough, difficult of passage; not easy to swallow. Masápnot ang kán-on nga maitúm, labí na gid, kon walâ sing tinóla. Black rice is difficult to swallow, especially, if there is no side-dish with sauce. Masápnot iníng dálan sa paggúyud, sing kawáyan. This road is difficult to get through when hauling bamboo. (sápnot).
Hard, difficult, tiresome, said of work, life etc.; clumsy, awkward of speech. (sariwáol).
To feast, attend a banquet, eat much or to one's heart's content. (see páskwa, tábad, laód, pasáy, páskon).
Disgusting, loathsome, antipathetic, improper, unbecoming, exciting aversion or dislike. (see sáw-a).
Abominable, loathsome, stinking, emitting a bad smell. (see sáwhung, bahô, makataláka).
Often, frequently; frequent. (see sáyo, masúnsun, masamí, makadámù).
Continuous, continual, constant, always. (dáyon, daláyon).
Easy, facile. (see mahapús, mahulás).
(Sp. maceta) Flower-pot. (see masíta).
(Sp. demasiado) Excessive, more than enough, very much, too much, overdone. (see támà, lám-ag).
Shining, dazzling, very bright, like sunlight, sparkling, glittering, gleaming, glowing, scintillating, beaming, vivid, brilliant, resplendent, refulgent, effulgent. (sídlak).
Shining; bright, splendid, clear, etc. See masídlak.
See masídlak. (sílaw).
See under nasig-.
Bright, brilliant, good, shining, powerful, vivid, dazzling, shedding-, casting-, light, giving much light, said of a lamp or the like. (síga).
A prefix denoting equality of condition, e.g. masigkatáo-a man like ourselves, a fellow-man, neighbour. (see isigka-).
(H) See masídlak id.
See masídlaw id.
(H) Dazzling white, shining with a white lustre, very bright. (see masídlak, masílaw). (sílì).
Far-reaching, resounding, sonorous, lusty, reverberating, loud, carrying far, said of sounds and voices. (see sílik, malágsing, matágsing, masulánting, matúnug).
Sympathetic, regardful, considerate, thoughtful, affectionate, compassionate; emotional, sentimental. (see sín-it, kasín-it).
(B) Shining, polished, burnished, furbished, bright, shiny, gleaming, glossy, said of smooth surfaces that have been burnished. (see silíng, mahíning, masílì).
(B) Solitary, desolate, dismal, lonely, dreary, secluded. (sím-ong). (see mapúng-aw id.).
A frequent church-goer; devout, pious, religious, a man of prayer. (see símba, simbáhan, silimbáhon, mainampóon).
Discontented, displeased, unsatisfied, grumbling on account of having received less than others, envious, spiteful. (sabít).
Cheerful, jolly, etc. See masádya. (see maluyagón).
Transparent, translucent, pellucid, translucid, transmitting light, crystal. (sinág).
Taking care of, etc. See masagúron.
Supporting, helpful, assisting, looking after, taking care of. (see sákdag, maampínon, mainapínon).
Erring, etc. See masaláypon. (see sayúp).
Trustful, confiding, confident, hopeful, full of trust or confidence. (see sálig, salalígan).
Accomplished, well trained, practised, expert, adept, experienced; giving or providing a good training. (see sampáton).
Heedful, mindful, attentive, taking notice of, attending to, careful to observe or attend to; sensitive. (see sapák).
Generous, hospitable, taking care of, giving shelter and food, sympathetic. (see sapópo).
Praising, exalting, giving honour or praise to. (see saúlug).
Clear, transparent, pellucid, crystal. (see sínaw, matín-aw).
Very warm, hot, ardent, aglow, burning, white-hot, fiery, incandescent, said of the passions as well as of the temperature of substances. (see síngkal).
Hot, fiery, excited. Masíngkì siá sing panimúot. He is very hot-tempered. (see síngkì, masíngkal).
Adoring, worshipping, church-going; one who adores, worships or frequently goes to church; pious, a man of prayer. (see símba).
Sorry, sad, desolate, dismal, dejected, mournful, doleful, dolorous, distressed, dreary, sorrowful. (see subô, masubô).
Conform, conformable, agreeing, willing, ready, complying, compliant, obliging, obedient, docile, yielding. (see sugút).
Obedient, dutiful, submissive, docile, yielding, complying with orders. (see sunúd).
See masinulúndon-obedient, etc.
(B) Dense, overgrown, jungle-like, full of high grass or underbrush. (see siók).
(H) Dense, etc. See masiók.
Avenging, vengeful, resentful, revengeful, vindictive, retaliating, spiteful, mischievous, malicious. (see sípat).
Sharp, keen (of eyes); wasteful, squandering, prodigal. (see makilitán-on, buhahâ, mausíkon).
Close-, near-, together, tied closely, strung or bound together. (see sípong).
(B) Narrow, of little breadth or extent, limited, circumscribed, not wide or broad. (see sipót, makitíd).
(B) See masílì-shining, glossy, lustrous, bright.
See masariwáol. Masiriwáol is more in use.
(B) Dim, obscure, getting dark, fading light, twilight, crepuscular, gloaming, said of nightfall. (sirúm).
(Sp. maceta) Flower-pot. (see masetéra). Also: Plants and flowers set out in flower-pots.
(Sp. mascabado) Unrefined sugar, muscovado.
(Sp. mascar) Tobacco-leaves used for chewing together with betel-nut, lime and búyò-leaves.
(Sp. máscara) Mask, disguise, face-mask; masquerade.
(Sp. por más que) Even if, though, although, notwithstanding. (see bisán).
To be or become aware of, know, understand. See namaslután. (see marásmas, malámad).

(B) Clear, bright, said of light or sight. Dílì másna iníng kínki, kay may bíro ang túbo. This lamp is not bright, because the chimney is sooty. Dílì na másna ang panúluk ko, kay tigúlang na man akó. My sight is getting dim, for I am quite old. (see masánag).

To know, understand. Indì siá makamásngà magbása kag magsulát. He does not know how to read and write. Walâ siá sing namasngaán nahanungúd sináng mga butáng. He hasn't an inkling of those matters. (see hibaló, balintúnod, marásmas, etc.).
(Sp. mazo) A mallet, a heavy hammer, sledge-hammer, mall, maul, beetle.
Nauseating, sickening, revolting, exciting a feeling of loathing, uninviting, unappetizing, applied especially to food cooked in too much fat. (see somó, makasolómo, mabútlà, masúm-od).
(Sp. mason) Freemason.
(Sp. masoneria) Freemasonry.
A convulsive choking fit that often attacks young children and may easily end in death, unless help is rendered at once.
See máslut-to be aware of, etc.
Sad, sorrowful, mournful, dejected, downcast, heart-sick, doleful, melancholic, woe-begone, moping, glum, forlorn, desolate, downhearted, despondent, depressed, unhappy. (see subô, masinulúb-on).
(H) See masagíl-om id.
Far-reaching, sonorous, loud, etc. (see malágsing, masílik, matágsing).
(B) Fresh, refreshed, comfortable, vigorous, well. (see súlhay, raháyráhay, présko).
Attracting ants, etc. (see subáy, maralasgáon).
Current, swift, rapid, strong, applied to running water; rushing. (sulúg).
Twisted, complicated, involved, entangled.
See masulukisák. (sulukusák-sulukisák).
Following, imitating; obedient, etc. See masinulúndon.
See makasolómo-disgusting, etc. (see súm-od).
Frequent, many times, many a time, often. (súnsun). (see masamí, makadámù).
Following, succeeding, coming after, ensuing, next. (see sunúd, madasón).
Weak, easy to conquer or overcome. (see súpil, dalág-on, mapígaw, malúya).
Daring, audacious, bold, defiant, impertinent, reckless, impudent, insolent, foolhardy, rash, venturesome, brave, violent. (see súpug, makáhas, maaháng, maísug, masurísol).
See masúpug.
See masulukisák-complicated, etc.
Exact, precise, careful, thorough, searching. (see súsi, maíd-id, matúl-id, mapísan, maúkud).
Writer; correspondent (of a newspaper, etc.); author, literary man. (see sulát).
From matá. See máthan id.

Something in sight, at hand, something that turns up, ready for use, way of earning a livelihood. Walâ siá sing mát-an kag sáp-an. There is (was) nothing (no means, work, help, etc.) in sight for his need and he has (had) nowhere to go to for shelter or protection. (see matá, palangitán-an, paaliwánsan, dalángpan, aláypan, pangítà).
(B) Family, blood relation. (see bátà, himatâ).

Eye, orb, sight, vision; hole (of a needle), loop (for a hook), etc.; eyelet; bud or shoot (of potatoes, cuttings of sugar cane, etc.); mesh (of a net); to awake, open the eyes; to keep vigil, remain awake. Nagmatá na siá? Is he already awake? Magmatá na ikáw. Wake up. Open your eyes. Rise (up). Ginpamatá akó níla. They woke me up. Pamatahá (památha) siá. Wake him. Namatahán (namáthan) ko ang amó nga gamú. That noise woke me. I was roused from sleep by that noise. Nagamatá gid siá magtoón, bisán kon gáb-i na. He keeps himself awake for study till late at night. He studies till late at night. (see búgtaw, puláw).
Dim. of matá-eye. Also: the thin membrane surrounding maize-kernels near the part attached to the cob; the eye, bud, shoot (of a plant or tuber).
High, tall, lofty, towering, exalted in altitude or dignity. (see táas, matatáas, malántyog, matág-as).
Proud, self-conscious, insolent, haughty, overbearing, arrogant, bumptious, stuck-up, supercilious, overweening. (táas).
Light, mild (of tobacco, beverage, etc.) (see táb-ang, dalísay, maísug-strong).
Impeding, hampering, hindering, obstructing, interfering, disturbing. (see táblaw).
Thick, fat, plump, chubby, stout, round, muscular, buxom, fleshy (of arms, legs, etc.). (see tábnul, matíbsul, matibúnog, maribúok, maribusól).
A kind of banana similar to kadísnon and anonóo and eaten either raw or boiled.
Straight, straight-forward, direct, right, rectilinear, honest, frank. (tádlung).
Any common day, every day, a working day.
(H) High. See matáas id. tág-as).
Sinking down, falling to the bottom, descending; weighty, ponderous, heavy (of weight); grave, serious, tactful (of speech). (see tágbong, mabúg-at, malígdong, maúgdang).
Far-reaching, resounding, ringing, sonorous, reverberating, loud, shrill, piercing (of voices and sounds). (see tágsing, malágsing, masílik, masulánting, matúnug, malániog).
Grateful, thankful, mindful of, making a proper return for favours received. (see bálus, matinagubalúson).
Apprehensive, suspicious, fearful, afraid, in suspense, in danger or peril; risky, hazardous. (see táhap).

Nice, beautiful; quiet, tranquil, peaceful. Matahímik ang pagtúlug siníng bátà. This baby sleeps nicely. Matahímik ang pagsinalayó sináng mga táo. Those people live peacefully together. (see matahúm, matáwhay, malinóng).
(B) Respectful, reverent, reverential, deferential, courteous; generous, liberal. (see táhud, matinahóron, maálwan, palanghátag, paraná-o).
Beautiful, beauteous, seemly, bonny, good-looking, sightly, pretty, handsome, fine, charming, comely, nice, lovely, splendid. (see tahúm, maányag, maayóáyo, maámbong, madálig, magayón, mamahî)
Nice, funny, queer. Matahúm kaáyo nga paghokóm iní! This is a nice way of administering justice!
(B) Pilfering, stealing. (see takáb, maniníkas, makáwat, matákaw).
(B) Thief; stealing. See makáwat. (see tákaw, maniníkas, maniníkmà, kawtían, kawatán).
Apathetic, etc. See matinalák-on.
Unobstructed, smooth, slippery, easy of passage, easily swallowed. (see talás, matánlas).
Cowardly, coward, craven, scared, timid, white-livered, poltroon, craven. (see tálaw).
Sharp-pointed. See matalíwis.

Easy to split, separable; disjointed, spaced wide apart. Ang sibúkaw matálhà. Sebucao-wood is easy to split. Sapan-wood cleaves-easily,-readily. Iníng súlud matálhà sing ngípon. This reed (of a weaving loom) has its teeth spaced wide apart. (see tálhà, malakâ).
(H) Sharp-pointed, acute, prickly, barbed. (talíwis).
(H) Sharp-edged, keen, cutting. (talúm).
Also: difficult to digest (of food). (matarúm id.).
Quiet, tranquil, calm, comfortable, undisturbed; straight on, continuous; pure unsullied. (talúnsay).
Attentive, regardful, intent on, considerate, observant, taking care of or paying attention to. (talupangúd). (see tamúd).

Sweet, sugary, syrupy, delectable (of food and drink); delightful, delicious, pleasant (of music, smells and feelings); kind, gentle, tender (of speech, disposition and sentiments); pleasing, beautiful, nice, pretty (to see). (tám-is). (see marímis).
Overmuch, excessive, too much, more than enough, immoderate, exorbitant, preposterous. (támà). (see lám-ag, lakás, masiádo, demasiádo).
Slow, lazy, indolent, sluggish, idle, slothful, otiose, slack, inert, listless, drone. (see támad, tamarán, ligoyán).
Fat, obese, plump, fleshy, stout, corpulent. (támbok).

Aiming well, a marksman, a good shot, an adept shooter or hitter; exact, precise, perfectly adapted or fit for. Iníng súlud waló (ka búgkos) nga matándà. This reed (of a weaving loom) is exactly adjusted (adapted) for eight (small bundles of yarn, i.e. stripes, to the span (dángaw). This is a reed of exactly eight (stripes to the span). (see tándà, ígò).
Marking, noting, taking stock, observing well, taking note of or paying much attention to. (see tándà, matinandáon).
Handy, practical, expeditious, zealous, diligent. (see tándus, mapísan, mabúhat, makarî, maábtik, etc.).
Wonderful, miraculous, extraordinary, marvellous, strange, surprising, astonishing; one who wonders or is surprised. (see tanhágà, makatitingála, makatalanhágà).
Smooth, slippery, easy to swallow. (see matalás, madánlug).
