Nagpanagubílin siá sa ákon sa pagbántay sing maáyo sang íya baláy, kay siá íya makádto sa Ilóngílong. He left orders to me to guard his house well, for he himself is going to Iloilo. Ginpanagubilínan (Ginpanagubínlan) níya kamí sa pagbuligáy kag pagtabangáy. He admonished us (He entreated us on his deathbed) to help and succour each other. (see bílin).
Freq. of sagúd-to take care of, etc.
Freq. of sagúdsud-to draggle, shuffle.
To reel, stagger, stumble, sway to and fro, as a drunkard or drunken person. (see dulíngdúling, panayódò).
Freq. of tagúntun-to spread, extend. See panagónton id.
Thunder; to thunder. (see dagúob).
To be full of-, covered with-, "tagústos".
(B) Shame, confusion, abasement, humiliation; to be ashamed, feel shame, be abashed or confounded, be confused or disconcerted with a feeling of guilt or inferiority. (see huyâ).
Form, shape, figure, outline; be in the form or shape of--. (see dágway).
Freq. of ságyad-to fell (a tree); to beat (gold, etc.).
To catch fish with the ságyap-net.

To put forth suckers or offshoots from the roots of the parent-stem, especially applied to bananas. Iníng mga ságing nagapanáhà sing madámù. These bananas have many offshoots. (see sáhà). panahâ, Freq. of tahâ-to respect, honour, revere, etc.
Freq. of táhap-to be afraid, apprehensive, shy, timid, have reverential fear, etc. (see panághap).
(B) Form or shape of one's forehead. (see dahî, pangágtang).

Freq. of tahî-to sew, stitch, etc. The style-, manner-, method-, of sewing; to sew, be a tailor or seamstress, be a dressmaker. Ang pagpanahî amó ang íya ginakabuhían. She lives by sewing. She earns her living as a seamstress (costumier, costumer).
Freq. of tahíntáhin. To dress well, go about in clean and tidy clothes, to be spick and span, to arrange well-one's dress,-one's hair,-one's general appearance.

Season, time, period of time, epoch; climate. Sa karón nga panahón. At the present-time,-juncture,-occasion, in these times, under the present circumstances. Sang panahón sang ribók. At the time of the Revolution. (see túig, dág-on, panág-on, tión, tiémpo).
To leaf, form leaves, grow-, put forth-, shoot out-, shoot forth-, produce-, leaves. (see dáhon).
Gambling, gaming; to gamble, game, be a gambler. (see tahór).

Freq. of sahót-to attend to pay attention to, regard, consider, have consideration or regard for. Often used sarcastically in the meaning of: to keep aloof from, do not meddle or interfere, or the like. Panahót (sahót) ka sinâ. Leave that alone. Don't bother about it. (see sapák, dipára, tamúd, panahâ).
Freq. of tahúp-to sift, separate the rounded (hulled, husked) rice from the chaff.
Freq. of sákà-to go up-a ladder,-a flight of stairs, or the like; to rise (of prices).
Freq. of taká-to loathe, etc.
(B) Freq. of takáb-to pilfer, steal.
A rise (in the price of a thing); to rise. (see sákà).

Freq. of sakár (Sp. sacar) To seek to get, try to obtain, covet, desire. Nagapanakár gid siá nga manganák sang bátà ni Fuláno. He wishes to have the honour of being godfather to N.N.'s child. Nakapanakár siá sa íya mga ginikánan nga mamiésta dídto. He obtained (got) leave from his parents to attend the feast there. (see ahâ).
To go on land, to land, go away from the sea, leave the sea-coast or the bank of a river, go up country. (see tákas).
(B) Freq. of tákaw-to steal, rob, pilfer, etc. (see pangáwat).
Journey, trip, travelling, sailing, going (by boat); to sail, boat, go, travel, journey (by boat). (see sakáy, sakayán, salákyan, sumalákay, sakayánon).
Freq. of tákga-to promise. Ang mga pinanákga (ipinanákga) ni Hesukrísto. The promises of (made by) Jesus Christ.
Fever, epidemic of fever; to have fever, contract a fever, suffer from malaria. (see tákig).
Freq. of sákit, sakít-to pain, etc.
Freq. of sáklam-to encroach upon, etc.
Freq. of táklas-to climb, etc.
Freq. of sáklit-to bind together, etc.
Freq. of sákot. Ingredient, condiment, mixture, seasoning; to mix, mingle. (see lakót).
Freq. of sáksi-to be a witness, to testify.
Testimony; to give testimony as a witness. (see sáksi).
Freq. of dakúp-to catch, etc. (see pangdakúp).
Freq. of takúp-to cover, etc.
Freq. of takús-to measure, etc. (see panókol).
To run away, flee, disperse, disappear. (see tál-as).
(B) Freq. of sálà-to leave behind. Ginpanálà nánda sa baláy ni Fuláno ang mga tabungós nga sinúdlan kang mga turulán-on. They left behind the baskets filled with vegetables in N.N.'s house.
Freq. of dalá-to carry, etc. See pandalá.

Freq. of salâ. To confess, own to a fault, acknowledge a mistake, admit being in the wrong, say "salâ ko".-It is my fault, I am to blame. My mistake. Frequently this panalâ is almost identical in meaning with súmpà, panúmpà-to swear, take an oath, declare under oath. "Salâ ko" may also mean (according to the context): If what I say is not true, I am a liar (am committing the sin of telling lies).
To glean, gather rice, wheat, etc., left after the harvest. (see panagílò, panígput, pamíngkong).

Crying, mourning, sighing, weeping, lamentation, lament; utterance, expression; to sigh, mourn, cry, weep, grieve, moan, bemoan, wail, bewail, keen, lament; to utter, express, give expression to (one's feelings, thoughts, etc.). Nagpanalabíton siá sa dakû nga kalisúd nga inmabút sa íya. She uttered lamentations because of the great calamity that had befallen her. (see panalambíton, sámbit).
Answer, retort, repartee, (severe) reply; to answer back, retort, reply. (see sabát, panabát).
Freq. of dalága. To go after-, look for-, a girl, try to meet girls, seek the society of young women. (see pamulán).
Freq. of dalágan-to run, etc. Madásig (mahínay) siá sing panalágan. He is a fast (slow) runner.
Rare, seldom, scarce; rarely, scarcely. Inâ malakâ pa sa panalágsa. That almost never happens. That will scarcely ever happen. (see talágsa).
Rare, seldom, scarce; difficult to find or to obtain. (see panalágsa, maíwat, mahínà).
See panalabíton-to sigh, etc.
To grow or gather salápi-a second crop from the roots of the first.
To be a coward, act dastardly or cowardly. (see tálaw).
Freq. of daláwat-to buy cereals.

To soak, drench, immerse, dip, plunge, put into a liquid; put to the test, examine, investigate; examination, investigation. Iníng mga butáng dápat nga usisáon sa isá ka dayág nga panaláwsaw. This matter should be investigated by a public hearing-or-in open trial. Nakapanagámsam kag nakapanaláwsaw siá sang maluíb nga pamatásan sang kalibútan. She has tasted and experienced the treacherous ways of the world. (see sáwsaw).
To make one's way along a river-bank, a mountain-ridge, etc. where there is no beaten track. (see látay, táytay).

Floor, shelf, ledge; story (of a house); platform. Ang ákon estánte may ápat ka panálgan. My book case has four shelves. Magapatíndog silá, konó, sing bág-o nga baláy nga may ánum ka panálgan. They are going to erect, it is rumoured, a new house of six stories. (see salúg).
(B) To walk along a ridge, along a river bank, etc. (see panaríbay, panaláytay, panalíbtib).
To walk along a steep river bank or along a precipice (particularly in order to avoid crossing a deep river).
Freq. of sálig-to expect, trust, have confidence, etc.
To make (form into) a chain; to put in chains. (see talikalâ).
To cup the hands behind the ears in order to hear the better, to prick up the ears. (see talínga).
Freq. of talíthi-mizzle, drizzle, etc.

Freq. of salô-to catch a ball, fruit dropped from a tree, or the like. Nagapanalô silá sang mga páhò nga ginahúlug ni Fuláno. They are catching with their hands the mangoes dropped (from the tree) by N.N.

Freq. of sálo-to sit down to a common meal, etc. Also: comradeship, companionship, equality; to be equal to or a match for. Walâ gid kamí sing panálo sa íla. We are no match for them. We are inferior to them. There is no fellowship or equality between us and them.
Freq. of tálo. An even chance, opportunity, luck; to have an even chance to win, come out victorious (in gambling, etc.). (see bagít).
Dim. and Freq. of sálo. To sit down to a common meal, to feast, banquet, etc.; a banquet, feast, dinner. (panarósáro id.).
To be a parasite, act as a hanger-on, sponge upon-, frequent the tables of-, the rich, etc. (see paniróngsiróng, panarósaró).
To be greedy, etc. See dalók, dinalók.

Twilight, dusk; to shine feebly or mildly, to glimmer, to shed-, give-, afford-, a feeble light. Nagapanalóndong ang búlan. The moon is shining feebly, is giving a dim light. Nagpanalóndong ang kasisídmon. The evening light faded, was failing. Evening twilight set in. The shades of evening gathered.
See panalóndong, panalúngdung.
To forge-, hammer-, work-, iron or other metal at a forge; be a smith. Maálam siá magpanálsal. He knows to work metals. (see sálsal, panalsálon).
Way or manner of working iron. Dílì maáyo sing panalsálon iníng pánday. This smith (artisan) is not good at working iron, iron-work.
Form or shape of a floor; to lay-, put in-, a floor. (see salúg, panálgan).
Freq. of sálug-to fish-, catch fish-, with the hand.
Freq. of salúgsug-to enter, penetrate, pierce.
See panalóndong-twilight, etc.
Freq. of salúpsup-to enter deep, penetrate. (see panalúgsug).
Freq. of tám-is-to be sweet, etc. Sweetmeat, confection. Also: to be pleased with, take pleasure in, gloat over, be delighted with, take delight in. (see hinám-is).
Panama; a kind of hat; a hat made of Panama-grass.
Freq of sámay. Also: to make fabrics called "sinamáy".
Freq. of támay-to contemn, despise.

A superstitious practice of fishermen consisting in the ceremony of putting some of the "small fry" of the first catch in a tin. The tin containing the fish is then placed on a small raft and send adrift. It may be considered a kind of sacrifice to Neptune, the heathen sea-god. Also verb. Indì ka magkáon sing dánglay, parótpot ukón sápsap nga pinanambián. Don't eat dánglay-, parótpot-or sápsap-fish that have been offered to the sea-god. (panámbì is probably derived from támbì, because the raft with the tin of fish on it somewhat resembles a kitchen-balcony called támbì).
To shelve; to dismiss, reject, despise. See the foregoing.
Freq. of támbong-to be present at, attend.
Freq. of dámgo-to dream. Also: To ponder, ruminate, muse, imagine, build castles in the air, to day-dream. (see ginaóng).
Freq. of damílit-to take one's leave, depart, say goodbye.
To shield, use a shield, protect oneself or others as with a shield. (see tamíng-shield).
To conceive, Freq. of the obsolete sámkon. Nanámkon-or-nagpanámkon siá. She conceived.
Freq. of támpà-to slap, strike, beat; a blow, slap of the open hand.
Face, front, frontage, facade; to confront, face. (see támpad, tamparán).
To bury one's face in one's hands; to grieve, mourn, be down in-the mouth,-the dumps. (see tampoáy).
Freq. of sámpok-to rush upon, fight (of cocks, etc.); to beat or strike against. Nagpanámpok siá sa (sang) íya dúghan. He struck (beat) his breast (as a sign of guilt, compunction, etc.).
Freq. of támpok. To fill up a hole; to set a precious stone in a ring, etc. (see panáp-ok).
Freq. of sámput-to arrive, come upon the scene.
Freq. of tamúd-to look down; to consider, reflect.
Dim. of panamúd.
(H) Freq. of tán-aw-to see, look at, inspect, behold, view. Dílì na maáyo ang íya panán-aw. His eyes are impaired, he does not see well any longer.
Sight, eyesight, vision, faculty of seeing; view, scene, sight (i.e. something seen). (see tán-aw, panán-aw, panan-áwon).
Sight, view, look, gaze; scenic show, what can be, or is to be, seen. (see talan-áwon).
Dim. of panán-aw. (see panulúktúluk, pangalágkalág).
Freq. of tándà-to sign, mark, note, etc.
Freq. of sándig-to lean against (for support), etc.
Freq. of sáng-ul-to hang on, hook in, etc.
Freq. of tangâ-to look up, lift one's eyes.
To develop or grow branches, to branch out. (see sangá).
Dim. of panangâ. Also: to loiter, linger, tarry; to gape or stare idly about.
Consent, assent, acquiescence; to consent, nod assent, agree to, approve of. (see tángdò).
Freq. of sánggot. To use-, apply-, a "sánggot"; to be a-toddy-gatherer,-toddy-collector,-mananggíti.
To look for, seek, search after, try to get or obtain. (see pangítà, lághap, ságap).
Freq. of sánghid-to test, etc.
Freq. of tángis-to cry, weep, etc.
To equip, furnish, make (get) ready, prepare, provide, supply, have or get a supply (of furniture, tools, arms, ships, etc.). (see sángkap, kasangkápan).
Freq. of tángkup. To finish, terminate, complete, close.
Freq. of tánglà-to look up (upwards), raise one's eyes, etc. Also: to be on the lookout for, seek, try to obtain or engage (workmen, farm-hands, etc.).

An example, instance, illustration; to give an example, to illustrate, cite a case or explain by means of an example or a parable; for instance. Hunâhunáon ta panánglit nga--. Let us imagine, for instance, that--. Saráng ikáw makapanánglit sang ímo nga ginpaháyag? Saráng mo mapananglitán ang ímo nga ginpaháyag? Can you illustrate what you have said by an example? Can you explain your statement by a comparison? Ang kabúhì sang táo ginapanánglit sa asó nga umalági. The life of man is compared to passing smoke. (see sánglit, kahalimbáwà, ábi, súbung).
Example, likeness, comparison, simile, similitude, figure, parable, case, illustration, analogy. (see sánglit, panánglit, katúlad, kahalimbáwà, kaángay, kaanggídánggid, súbung).
See pananglítan.
Freq. of sángsang-to be or become vehement, violent, etc.
Freq. of tángsò-to become loose, etc.
Freq. of tángtang-to fall, drop; to jingle, tink.
Freq. of tángub-to fill, cover or take in all, complete, finish. Nanángub na kaáyo ang madalúm nga dágway sang kagab-íhon. The dark form of night had completely covered all things.
Freq. of tángway-to buy a drink, etc.
Dealing in drinks or refreshments, the buying and selling of drinks, etc. (see tángway, panángway).
To fish (catch fish) with a net called sángyà.
Freq. of sántik-to strike or knock against something hard.
Freq. of tánum; tanúm-to plant rice; plant (in general), etc.
Freq. of tányag-to offer (for sale, etc.).
To fish-with,-in-, a small fish-trap called taón.
Freq. of táp-ok-to fill up a hole, etc. (see panámpok).
Freq. of tápa-to dry meat, etc.

Sometimes used instead of panapát, e.g. Nanápa siá nga índì na gid magsakáy sa sakayán, kay makaisá nadiotayán lang siá (kag) malúnud. He made a resolution not to travel any more by boat, because once he was nearly drowned.
The (trapeziform) side of a roof. (see panólong-the triangular end of a roof).
Freq. of sapák-to mind, care for, attend to.

Inkling, thought, idea, knowledge; to know (mostly used with "walâ"). Walâ gid siá sing panápang kon diín siá mapakádto. He had not an inkling (did not care) of where he was going to. Walâ gid silá panápang kon anó ang íla madangátan. They have no idea of what is in store for them. They don't (didn't) care for the consequences.
Freq. of tapás-to hew down, fell (trees, etc.). Panápson nínyo ang mga káhoy dídto sa bánglid. Cut down the trees there on the slope. (see púkan, pamulúd).

Freq. of dápat-to use, apply, etc. Anó nga bulúng ang ginpanápat sa íya sang manugbúlung? What remedies did the doctor apply to him? Also: to wear an amulet, or the like. Ang babáylan nagapanápat gihápon sa íya láwas kon magkádto siá sa búkid. The sorcerer always wears an amulet when he goes to the mountain. Anó karón ang íya ginadalá nga panápat? What kind of an amulet does he wear now? What sort of an outfit has he got now?
Freq. of tapát-to purpose, resolve, determine, make a resolution, be determined to, make up one's mind, be bent (set) upon.
Freq. of sapó-to find, come upon by chance, find out.
(B) The sense of smell; to smell. (see dapóg, sínghot, panimáhò, panínghot).
Clothes, clothing, dress, raiment, garment, costume, attire, garb, vesture, vestment, wearing apparel, wear, robe. (see sapút, panapút, ulús, naúg, bíste).
To turn as red as a red tapulánga-flower, i.e. to be ashamed, or the like.
Freq. of tapúngol-to belabour with one's fist, beat, punch, pommel, thrash. (see súmbag, pókpok, búngbung, ómol, patók).
Extreme, complete, consummate, utter, last, perfect; to be extreme, etc. (see tápus).

To dress-, vest-, array-, drape-, robe-, enrobe-, attire-, garb-, apparel-, deck out-, oneself, to don-, put on-, assume-, wear-, clothes. Nagpanapút siá sing mapulá. She wore a red dress. She was dressed in red. Magpanapút kamó sing maúgdang (malígdong). Dress decently. (see sapút, panápton).
To fish with a net called "sápyod".

(B) To start weaving, commence actual weaving after completing all preliminary work on the loom. Panarahí (Panád-i) ang háblon mo. Begin (start, commence, set to, set about) weaving the cloth (for everything is ready).
See panáda.
To cook or warm over a slow fire; to warm oneself at a fire.
(B) See panalága-to take a walk in order to meet girls, etc.
See panará.
See panará. (see aráng).
Freq. of kalángkang-to spread out one's fingers, to extend the fingers convulsively, etc.

To walk along the edge or ridge of, to go by (along) the-side,-edge,-border,-margin of, pick one's way at the side of, march parallel to, or along, the border of. (see panaláytay, pangalíhid, panalíbay, pangríbay).
Freq. of sarót-to be or become difficult, trying, troublous, wretched.
Freq. of sárot-ugly, bad, miserable.
Erased, wiped out, obliterated, rubbed out, expunged, cancelled, effaced, blotted out, etc. (see pánas).

To rub out, erase, wipe out, delete, scratch out, obliterate, scrape out, efface, expunge, blot-, take-, strike-, wash-, sponge-, out, draw the pen through, apply the sponge. Panása ang íya sinulát sa pisára. Wipe off the blackboard what he has written. Ipánas sa pisára iníng lapát. Use this cloth to clean the slate with. Panási ang papél sang sinulát. Erase the writing from the paper. Panása ang tinalíkdan kag bag-ohá ang ímo pangabúhì. Obliterate-, wipe out-, blot out-, (from your memory) the past and begin a new life.
Joking, jesting, fun; to joke, jest, make fun. (see tsásko, langás, lahóg).
Freq. of sátsat-to answer back, retort, etc. (see sagátsat, panagátsat).
Freq. of daúg-to win, conquer, overcome, etc.

To come-, get-, go-, down, descend, go downstairs, go down a ladder, leave the house, descend from a tree, dismount from-, get off-, a horse, etc.; to bring down, take or fetch down. Manáug ka. Come down. Go down. Leave the house. Papanaúga ang síya. Bring down the chair. Papanaúga siá. Make him come (get) down. Panaúgi siá. Go down to him. Papanaúgi siá sing síya. Bring (fetch) down a chair for him. Nanáug (Nagpanáug) na ang mga dumulúaw. The visitors have gone down, i.e. have left the house. The visitors have gone, have left. Nanáug siá sa salákyan. He left (got out of) the vehicle. (see náug).
Freq. of sáut, saútsáut-to dance.

(B) To go, walk, travel, hike, go on foot, tramp, trudge, march, foot it. Panáwi siá dídto sa umá. Go to him there at the farm. Anó ang pagabút mo dirí, pánaw lang ukón sakáy? How did you come here, walking or riding? (see lakát).
Freq. of tawág-to call, request or order to appear, to call upon in prayer.
Freq. of táwag-to proclaim, call out the names; roll-call, the giving (reading) out of a list of names.
Freq. of dáwhat-to accept, take in one's hand. (see pangáb-ot, panáb-ut).

(H) Form-, shape-, cast-, of one's face, physiognomy; face, cover or title-page of a book, magazine, etc.; page (of a book); to display or exhibit the best side of a thing. (see pauyahón, pánid-leaf (of a book, etc.).
Freq. of sáwsaw-to dip in, soak in; to fathom, examine.
Freq. of dáyà-to cheat, deceive, defraud, etc. (pandáyà id.).
Freq. of tayâ-to bet, wager.
Freq. of táyà-to hold a weapon in such a way as to be ready for attack or defense.
(B) Freq. of táyod-to stand still, etc.
(B) To lounge, loiter, stand about idly. (see panindógtíndog).
To reel, sway, totter, stagger, as a drunken person, walk with body bent or stooping, be unsteady on one's legs. (see panayódoy id.).
See panayódò.
Freq. of sáysay-to explain, give an exposition of, etc.
Explanation, exposition, clear statement; to give an explanation, give out a statement. (see sáy-*say).
Now and then pand-is used instead of pan-in words beginning with d, e. g. pandakúp, pandála, pandáyà, etc. etc. See pan-.

To show off, give oneself airs, be proud or ostentatious. Nakapándag siá, kay nangasáwa sing manggaránon. He is carrying his head high, because he has married a rich woman. Also: to live peacefully, lead a steady or settled life, settle down, have no worry.
Freq. of dágas-to pluck, pick (fruit, etc.). (panágas id.).
(B) See panahî, pangágtang-shape of one's forehead.
Contrivance, machination. See pandihútan id.
Short, stocky, squat, squab, dumpy, stumpy, podgy, stubby, low of stature and bulky or stout in comparison. Pándak nga táo. A thick, short, stocky man. (see tipúngkò, búdul, karibúd).
Short, stocky, etc. See pándak.
Freq. of dakúp-to arrest, take, seize, etc. (see panakúp).
Freq. of dála-to bear (a child), to be pregnant, etc. (see pangmábdus, pamúsung, pamábdus).

Freq. of dalá-to carry, bring, fetch, etc. Ginpandalá níla sa Manílà ang tanán níla nga kasangkápan. They brought their whole outfit (all their goods and chattels) to Manila. Indì amó inâ ang pandalá sang kínke; subúnga siní. That is not the way of carrying a lamp; do it like this.
Freq. of damóg-to feed a pig or dog, etc.
The screw pine, a cactus-like plant growing to a considerable size. Its fibre is made into doormats, etc. (pángdan id.).
A kind of Filipino dance.
Carpenter, artisan, craftsman, handicraftsman, skilled workman, joiner, smith, wright, operative; to be or become a carpenter, etc. (see pamánday).
Freq. of dáyà-to cheat, etc. (panáyà id.).
(Sp. panderete) A small tambourine.
Contrivance, machination, means, management, making, scheme. (see pandahútan, pahítò, padíhut, padihútan, patúga).
(Sp. pandilla) Party, gang, set, faction. (see hubón, panóng).

(B) To be compared with, likened to, made an example of, be exposed to criticism, be held up as a warning to others. Kon magságad ka panábad (sang panábad) pagapandinganán ikáw sa kay Tíban Bádù ukón sa kay Nánà Inkì. If you have the habit of going to every feast you will be likened to "Stephan, the Feaster" or to "Mama Inkì". Also used as noun: bad example, type to be avoided, model (sort) not to be imitated. (see papánding).
(Sp. pan de sal) Bread, ordinary bread. (see panisál, tinápay).

Stocks to secure the feet (legs) of a criminal, lunatic, etc.; to put in the stocks, to pillory. Napandogán siá. He was put in the stocks. Pandogí siá. Put him in the stocks. Ipapándog ko iníng búang. I'll have this madman put in the stocks. I'll see to it that this madman is put in the stocks.
To knuckle, etc. (See panokól, dokól).

Hood, awning, canopy, detachable roof, tilt, any light cover for the head (against sun or rain); helmet, topi, topee, hat; the bowl of a ladle, spoon, etc. Ang pándong sang kalésa. The roof of the rig (calesa). Ang pándong sang luág. The bowl of the ladle.
To ordain, order, nominate, appoint, command. (see bílin, tógon, sógò).
To roll a cigar, etc. See panúbla, dúbla.
Freq. of duhá-dúha-to doubt, etc.
To darken, become obscure, etc. See palandulúm, dulúm.
To proceed, go to, approach, go in the direction of. See panúlung, dúlung.
To loll, rest in a careless attitude, sit or lie lazily with the head pillowed on the arm or the like, lie like a log. (see dúngkul, dungkulán-a log).
Feast, festival, solemnity, celebration, Feast of the Patron-Saint of a parish or town. Hiwáton níla, kunó, ang íla pándut sa--. They are going to celebrate their feast, it is said, on--.
Freq. of duyâduyâ. Also: to relax, do (eat, etc.) slowly, weakly, or the like. (see dwáldwál).
Pang-is at times interchangeable with pan-in words beginning with s or d, e.g. pangsagúp (panagúp, sagúp); pangdakúp (pandakúp, panakúp, dakúp), etc. See pan-, pand-.
Plain, ugly, distorted, dark and marked with smallpox, etc., said of the face. Páng-al siá sing guyá. He has an ugly face.
To gnaw, nibble, bite off piece by piece. (see kíbkib, kítkit, áp-ap, áb-ab, páng-os, háng-it).
To bite or gnaw off bit by bit (piece by piece), especially applied to nibbling sugar-cane stalks. Pang-osá ang tubó. Eat the sugar-cane by biting off a bit at a time. (see páng-it, háng-it).
Inexperienced, stupid, dull, backward. (see pángog, pungág).
Hook, fire-hook; the small hook used for putting the threads of the warp through the reed in a weaving loom.
Now and then used instead of pang-, e.g. pangalíntak (líntak); pangalabá (labá); pangamálus (málus), etc.
Freq. of kaáyo-to mend, repair, etc.
Freq. of káb-ot-to reach, make a long arm, etc. (see panáwhat, panáb-ot).

Form or shape of one's shoulder (abága) Also: to shoulder, undergo, tackle, handle, manage. Walâ siá sing igkasángkol sa pagpangabága sang amó nga palangakoán. He has not the ability to shoulder the duties of such an office. Pílit na gid nga magkangíl-ad kamí sang íya pagpangabága (sang íya mga pangabága) sang íya mga katungdánan. We are now forced to-repudiate his way of performing his duties,-be disgusted with his manner of carrying out his obligation.
To wave a fan, to fan oneself. (see abaníko, panguyáb).
Freq. of ábat-to follow, call back, summon. (see pangápas).
To exclaim "abáw!". (The English equivalent is a prolonged "Oh" or "Awe!").

Freq. of kabáy. To wish, desire, ask for, hanker after, covet, long for, crave. Ginapangabáy ko nga--. I wish that--. Ginapangabáy ko sa ímo ang isá ka mahamungayáon nga bág-ong túig. I wish you a happy new year. Nagpangabáy (nangabáy) siá nga--. He desired that--. Indì ka magpangabáy (mangabáy) sa íya sing maláin. Don't wish him any evil. Don't curse (imprecate) him.
To ride on horseback, mount a horse. (see kabáyo, kabayó).
Freq. of kábis-to pay in full, pay off a debt, settle an account, square a bill, or the like.
Dim. of pangábis. Also: to excel, be superior, surpass, give a very good account of oneself. Iníng bátà nagapangabískábis sa tanán nga bágay. This boy excels in everything.
Freq. of kabúd-to cling to, encircle, coil round, wind round, trail over, be trained up, grow around an object, as a vine, creeper, trailing plant, etc.
Dim. of pangabúd.

Freq. of búdlay. Hard work, toil, drudgery, exertion, work in general, labour; to work hard, labour, exert oneself, toil, toil and moil, drudge. Nangabúdlay (Nagpangabúdlay) siá sing dakû, ápang awát man lang ang tanán níya nga paningúhà. He worked hard indeed, but all his labour was (his exertions were) in vain. Ang matámad magpangabúdlay (mangabúdlay) dílì takús nga pakán-on. He who is too lazy to work does not deserve to be fed.
Life, living, living conditions; to live. (see kabúhì, búhì, buhî).
Livelihood, living, means of-sustenance,-subsistence,-support. (see kabuhián).
To rummage, ransack, disarrange things in search. (see abúkay).
Freq. of abút-to arrive.
Freq. of ábut-to catch up with, reach, overtake.
To make friends, be friendly with. Hirúpi kag pangabyána siá sing maáyo. Try and make her acquaintance, and befriend her. (see ábyan).
To pray, say one's prayers. Magpangadî-or-mangadî ka. Pray. Say your prayers. Pangadiá ang "Amáy námon". Say the "Our Father".

To cause pain and swelling in the joints, said of wounds, burns, scratches, etc. that have become infected. Ang pilás sang túdlò sang íya kamót nagpangádlay sang íya bútkon-or-Ginpangadlayán ang íya bútkon tungúd sang pilás sang túdlò sang íya kamót. The wound in his finger has infected his arm (causing swellings in the elbow and armpit). Ginapangadlayán ang íya hítà gíkan sa hubág sa íya tiíl. He has a swelling in the groin due to the ulcer on his foot.
Freq. of kádto-to go, etc.
Dim. of pangádto. To go (pass) to and fro, roam or walk-about,-from place to place.
Freq. of kádwas-to take hold of or catch with outstretched arm and with the palm of the hand turned downward.
Oblivious, forgetful, wandering in mind, not quite normal, not all there, distracted, dreamy, wool-gathering. (see pungág).
Freq. of ágad. To serve, be a servant or employee. Especially: to serve for an intended wife in the house of her parents.

Freq. of agálon. To seek a master or owner, look for an employment, or the like, hunt for a job, try to find an employer. Ang idô nagapangagálon. The dog is looking for its master. Magpangagálon (Mangagálon) ka kon walâ ka sing palamúgnan. Go and look for somebody who will give you a job, who will employ you (as a cook, servant, errand-boy, washerwoman, etc.), if you are out of work (if you have no position, if you are unemployed).
Freq. of agám. Also; to grasp (do, handle, manage) well, to be careful or circumspect.
Drying, withering, fading; to dry up, wither, shrivel, fade. (see kagáng).
Freq. of ágas. The healing process of smallpox, measless, etc.; to heal, form scabs.
Freq. of kagát-to bite, snap, etc.
Freq. of ágaw. Usurpation, forceful appropriation, expropriation, dispossession; to take by force, usurp, etc.
Freq. of ágda. To invite, etc.; invitation-card. Magpabálhag ka sing mga pangágda. Have some invitation cards printed.
Freq. of kághà-to grieve, be in sorrow, etc.
Freq. of ági-to go or pass by, etc.
Tenancy, tenantry, tenure, lease, leasehold, tenure by lease; to work or till land belonging to another for part of the produce, to be a tenant or leaseholder. (see ágsa).
Form or shape of one's forehead, etc. (see ágtang, panahî).
(B) See pangádto-to go, etc. from kádto, kágtò, ágtò.
Freq. of ahás-to dare, etc. (see pangáhas).
Freq. of káhas-to dare, be impertinent, audacious, bold.

(B) Freq. of kahíg. Shape, form and use of one's legs, especially applied to game (fighting) cocks. Iníng sulúg maáyo sing pangahíg. This cock has fine legs, is strong or expert in the use of its legs, can use its legs to good purpose.
Freq. of káhig-to scratch with the feet as chickens looking for food.
Freq. of káhoy. To fetch or gather firewood, collect fuel. Mangáhoy (magpangáhoy) kamó dídto sa bakólod. Go and gather firewood there on the hill.
Freq. of kaingín-jungle fire, etc.
Freq. of ák-ak-to tear or strip off.
Freq. of áka-to be much resorted to or much in demand.
Freq. of kâkâ-to be full to the bursting point.
Freq. of káka-to gather, scrape together.
Freq. of kakáak-to cackle.
Freq. of kákak-to cackle. (see pangakáak).
Freq. of kakás-to pull or tear down, tear in pieces.
(H) The Freq. of ákig-to be or become angry, etc. Nangákig (Nagpangákig) silá. They got angry, grew angry, waxed hot.
Freq. of ákò-to be able, to undertake a work and its responsibility.
Prayer, oration; to pray, beseech, ask in prayer, to call upon in prayer. Freq. of alába.
Place of prayer, oratory; altar. (see pangalába, halarán).

To steal garden-and farm-produce during the night preceding All Souls' Day, the thieves pretending to be souls of the departed. Many ignorant people believe that the souls in purgatory walk abroad at that time to visit their former haunts. Pangalagá lang ang íya mga ságing. Steal his bananas on the eve of All Souls' Day. Pinangalagán níla kagáb-i ang ákon kalubihán. Last night they visited my coco-nut-plantation and stole coco-nuts, etc. (kalág).

Freq. of kalág-kalág. Also: to examine, search, try to find, look over a room, road, etc. for lost articles or the like. Pangalágkalagón mo ang kwárta nga nadúlà. Look for the lost money. Try to find the lost money. Pangalágkalagán mo ang dálan, básì pa lang nga makítà nímo ang síngsing nga nawígit (nagkawígit). Keep a sharp lookout on the way (look everywhere on the road), perhaps you will find the ring you dropped. (see pangítà, panulúktúluk).
Freq. of kaláging-to arrange well; to drill.
To cook, hold the pan, have "an iron in the fire", have "an axe to grind", have something to gain. (see kaláhà).
To wear jewels (jewelry, jewelery). (see aláhas).
To look for, or gather, river-crabs; to go in search of pleasure. (see kalámpay).
To hesitate, doubt, be-undecided,-in doubt,-uncertain, not to know exactly what to say or do. (alángálang).

To go in search of an amulet; to wear a talisman, amulet, charm in the superstitious belief that it will protect the wearer in danger, preserve him from disease, keep him out of harm, etc. (see antíngánting, pinangálap).
To cling to, adhere to, creep up, wind or circle around as a vine or creeper. (Freq. of kalápkap, kápkap; see pangabúd).
Grip, hold; influence, power, sway. (see pangalápkap).
Grasp, grip, handle, heft; business, occupation. Maáyo siá sing pangalápton. He is a good-, an experienced-, worker. He is an old hand
To tremble, shake; suffer from the gapes (the disease "alátay" (arátay)) that often causes great havoc amongst poultry.
Freq. of aláw-to treat visitors, offer them smokes, etc.; to be hospitable, entertain a guest.
Freq. of kaláwat-to go to-, to receive-, Holy Communion.
Freq. of álay-to be stiff, tired, etc. Rigidity, stiffness, tiredness (of limbs, etc.) through overexertion, or the like; to be or become stiff, etc.
Freq. of kaláyo. To attend to the-fire,-hearth,-cooking. Kamó lang ang matánum, kay akó sing ákon mangaláyo. You go and plant rice, I for my part will look after (attend to) the cooking.
See pangalihít-to throw aside, shelve, etc.
Security, bond, bail, surety; assurance; to be or give security, stand bail, etc. (see líg-on, palíg-on).
Freq. of alíhid-to go along the side or edge of, pick one's way along the margin (edge, border) of.
To throw aside, shelve, put in the corner, discard; pay no attention to, neglect, disregard. (see lihít, ahígahíg, ihígihíg).
A probe; a sponge. (see kalikóg).
Freq. of kalíkog-to poke, probe (a wound, etc.).

(B) To handle, grasp or take with the hand, to actually lay hands upon. Sín-o siníng mga makáwat ang nagpangalíma (nangalíma) sang pílak? Which of these thieves did actually take the money, did the actual stealing of the money, did personally lay hands on the money? Maáyo siá mangalíma. He has deft hands, knows how to use his hands well. (see pangamót).
(B) The way one speaks, quality of one's voice (in speaking); to speak. (see límog, pangatingúg, paníngug, paningúg, panlímug-quality of one's voice in singing).

To wash or rinse out one's mouth, to gargle. Pangalimúg (magpangalimúg, mangalimúg) ka ánay sing túbig. First wash out your mouth. Ari ang túbig nga inogpangalimúg (ipangalimúg). Here is the water for rinsing out the mouth with.
To click the tongue. Indì ka magpangalíntak. Don't click your tongue. Pinangalintakán akó níya. He clicked his tongue at me. (see líntak).
To amuse oneself, rejoice, exult, be glad, joyful, jolly, cheerful, merry, gay. (see lípay, kalípay, palangalipáyan).

Freq. of alísbong-odour, smell, etc.; to emit or exhale an odour, smells, scents, odoriferous vapours, etc. Nagapangalísbong ang mga mahumút nga búlak sa pamulákan. The fragrant flowers are filling the garden with their odours (sweet smell, sweetness).
Freq. of lisúd, kalisúd. To worry, grieve, sorrow, to be-in distress,-in trouble, have-difficulties,-worries,-troubles,-a hard time of it, be hard put to it.
Freq. of kalít-to do at once, quickly, by anticipation, promptly, to take time by the forelock, avail oneself of an opportunity.
Freq. of almidón. To starch. Sagád siá mangalabá kag mangalmidón sang mga panápton. She is an expert at washing and starching clothes.
Freq. of kalókos-to tuck up.
Freq. of kalós-to scratch. Ang kuríng nagapangalós. The cat (is scratching) scratches. (see pangarós, which is more commonly used).
Freq. of kálot-to scratch lightly, to relieve an itch by rubbing or scratching.
Dim. of pangálot. Nagapangalótkálot siá sang íya ólo. He is scratching his head.
Freq. of áloy-to pretend to be sick, etc.
To grow old and pass away, to leave the world, to die, succumb. Nangálpò siá nga walâ makakítà sing áwto. He grew old and passed away without ever having so much as seen an automobile.
Freq. of álpot. Prostitution, harlotry, whoredom; the meretricious conduct, arts and wiles of bawds and lewd women; to practise prostitution, etc.
Freq. of álsa-to raise, lift, hoist, heave; to receive or take on credit.
Freq. of kalúgmò-to cover oneself with, enwrap oneself in. (see pangulúmbut, pangulámbut).
Freq. of kalúmbut. To wrap oneself up in (a blanket, etc.). (see pangalúgmò, panimúlon).

To be retiring, timid, shy, bashful, reserved, aloof, to keep away from social gatherings or entertainments as one having a cold or feeling indisposed. Indì ka magpangalúpò (mangalúpò) sa mga katipúnan. Don't be too retiring at social gatherings. (see lupô, likáw).
To visit or go to another place in search of work, to emigrate, etc. See pangáyaw id.
An uneasy sensation in the skin (that inclines one to scratch the affected part), itch; to itch (as of a healing wound, etc.). (see málus).

Freq. of áman. Preparation, caution, circumspection, foresight, forethought, prudence; to prepare, get ready, be cautious or circumspect, make previous arrangement for, be careful, etc. (see panghíkot, panghímos, panigáon).
Freq. of áman-to add, throw in without charge, allow for discount, etc.
To gather tomatoes; to become as red as a ripe tomato, to blush. (see kamátis).
Freq. of ámbon-to gather clouds around, be covered with clouds. Nagapangámbon ang mga búkid. The mountains are covered with clouds.
Freq. of kámias-to make a scratching or clawing motion with the hands or paws, as a dog jumping on its master and caressing him with its paws, etc.
To go or travel-north,-northward,-northwards,-towards the North,-in a northerly direction. Nagapangamíhan ang mga gál-um. The clouds are travelling northwards. (see amíhan, amínhan).
Freq. of ámion-to be odoriferous, spread agreeable scents or diffuse pleasant odours.
Sense of touch; to touch. (see kámlot).
Freq. of amóma-to regale, treat, give food to, serve with, serve out to, be hospitable, entertain; present with, make a gift of (fruits, eatables, etc.).
Freq. of kamúskamús-to live from hand to mouth, to have barely enough to live on. (see abátabát).
Freq. of ámot-to contribute towards a fund, etc.

Freq. of kamót. To handle, grasp or take hold of with the hand, to take in hand, to manage; quality or use of one's hand. Maáyo sing pangamót iníng tigduág, magsusúlat, etc. This painter, writer, etc. is skillful in the use of his brush, pen, etc. (see pangalíma).

Freq. of ámpò. Request, petition; surrender; to ask, pray, beg, beseech, supplicate, intercede for, implore, plead, entreat, petition; to ask for mercy, yield, surrender. Kon walâ silá mangámpò áyhan naúrut silá magkalamatáy. If they had not surrendered they would probably have been killed.
Prayer, orison, invocation; to pray, invoke, say-, offer up-, a prayer. Pangamúyò ka (Magpangamúyò, mangamúyò ka). Pray. Say a prayer. Say your prayers. Offer up a prayer. (see pangadî).
See pangámion-a sweet smell, etc.
Delivery, birth; to give birth to; to beget, procreate, bring forth, have-offspring,-a child,-issue; to be godfather or godmother to a child at baptism or confirmation. (see anák).
Freq. of kánaw-to glisten, shine, etc. Freq. of ánaw-to flood, deluge.
Dim. of pangánaw. Also: to fill to overflowing, become brimful, to brim, brim over (of tears). (see kanáw-kanáw).
First-born; firstling, first-fruits. (ánay). (see subáng).
Freq. of kanáy-kánay-to blow softly, gently; to abate, get mild or even-tempered.
To moan, sigh, grieve, wail, mourn, groan, lament, keen, whimper, whine. (see dúhoy). Also noun: a moan, etc.
Caus. of ngánga-to open (the mouth).
To cart, transport or convey by cart, to be a carter. (see kánggà). Also: Freq. of ánggà-to pet, fondle.
From pangánga. Pangángha siá sang íya bâbâ. Let him open his mouth.
Freq. of kángkang. To open one's hand with the fingers spread wide apart; to sprawl, spread the legs or open the-claw,-pincer,-pincher, said of crabs, lobsters, etc.
(B) Freq. of ángkat-to get on credit; to get loose, separate; to challenge, defy.
To be godfather or godmother. Ang pinanángkon ni Fuláno. N.N.'s godchild. (see anák, ángkon). Also: Freq. of ángkon-to acquire, etc.
Freq. of áni-to harvest rice, to cut rice with the kayóg, etc.

Freq. of anínaw. To look into a mirror and see the reflection; to picture to oneself, practise crystal gazing, seem to foresee, have prescience-foreboding,-foreknowledge,-second sight,-forewarning. Daw ginpanganínaw ko nga dáan ang maabután siníng bátà. I seemed to know beforehand what was in store for this child.
Freq. of ánit-to flay, skin, etc. Kon mangánit kitá sa ibán, anítan man kitá. If we flay others, we shall be flayed ourselves i.e. The evil done by us to others will recoil on ourselves.
Freq. of ánod-to float, etc. Also: Cloud. (see gál-um, ámbon, alopó-op, dámpug).
Freq. of kanógon-to bewail, be sorry for, to exclaim "kanógon"-"What a pity!".
Freq. of kánta-to sing. Freq. of ánta-smell of burnt food.
(Probably from the Sp. ante) To show off, wish to be first or foremost, like to be in the front rank; to exert oneself, make great efforts. (see palangánti).
To act like a weather-cock or dog-vane. (see kánti).

To long, crave, desire vehemently, be-anxious-eager,-avid,-keen, for a fight and the like. Nagapangánti siá sa pakigáway, pagdúmug, etc. He longs for a fight, is anxious to wrestle, etc. (see the following pangánti).
(H) Freq. of ántod-the smell of burnt food; to burn and emit a corresponding smell.

Freq. of káon-to eat, take food, etc. Nagapangáon-or-nagapangináon silá. They are taking food, are having a meal. Ang mga gál-um nagapangináon pa. The clouds are eating still, i.e. are gathering or increasing in size (a sign of coming rain).
Freq. of ápas-to follow, call back. (see pangábat, sunúd).
Freq. of kápay-blanket. To use a blanket, wrap oneself up in a blanket.
To use wings; cover oneself as with wings. (see kapáy).
Freq. of ápin-to help, assist, protect, defend, be a partner, take sides with.
To grope, feel one's way like a blind man. (see kápkap).
Freq. of áplag-to spread, disperse.
To draw near, come close to, in order to be noticed or petted as a dog coming near its master.
To have grandchildren; be a grandfather, grandmother. (apó).
(B) Freq. of kárà-to vituperate, scold, chide in rude language, etc.
Dim. of pangárà. Also: to twitter, utter tremulous, broken sounds.
Freq. of karáb-kárab-to flame, flare up, burn lustily; to crackle (of fire).
To wail, sigh, moan, groan, fret, say "aragóy"-oh! ah! ow! in complaining of pain or grief. (see pangháyhay, pangharóy, pangandúhoy).
Freq. of karánda-to do quickly; to scamp, to perform carelessly, etc.
To warm oneself, etc. See panarán, panaráng id. (aráng).
To shout; bark; cry out aloud; to talk nonsense, prattle. (see úwang, sínggit, únggal, ngálngal, ngásal, lásang, lamádà).
To scratch as a cat, chicken, etc. (see pangalós, pangarós, karós).

Freq. of karáskas-to tear, pull off, etc. Also: to exert oneself very much, strive with might and main. Nagapangaráskas silá sa pagsákà sa maáyo sing sóhol nga palangakóan. They are making great efforts to attain (rise to) a well-paid position. (see káskas, panikasúg, pamarúg-ot, etc.).
Freq. of areglár-to arrange, etc. Also: to dress well, to be neat and tidy, be spick and span. (see panahíntáhin).
Freq. of arímo-to lean-, rely-, upon.
To wear earrings. (arítos).
(B) To be shy, restrained in one's behaviour, feel ill at ease (as a stranger in unknown surroundings). (see pangirákirá).
Freq. of karóskos-to scratch, use claws or nails in tearing, etc.
See pangálot.
Freq. of aróy. To complain of pain, say "aróy". (see pangaragóy).
Freq. of karóy-to starch yarn, etc. previous to weaving.
Extraordinary, wonderful, uncommon, astonishing, exceptional. (see tanhágà, pasahî, makatilingála).
Freq. kása-to hunt.
To engage in a legal fight, have a case in court, appeal to the law, carry on a legal prosecution. (see kasábà).
Marriage, wedlock, matrimony, nuptials, wedding; to take-, marry-, wed-, a wife, to marry, wed, be joined in matrimony, be-, get-, married. (see asáwa, asawá).
Freq. of kasáy-kásay-to convalesce, get better, improve in health.

An intoxicating drink prepared from rice, rice-beer. The pangásì is usually sipped by means of a small tube and served only on special occasions as at a marriage-feast, etc. Superstitious practitioners (babáylan) use the pangásì at their yearly assemblies near their "sacred places" called by them the "halígi sang kalibútan".
To abominate, abhor, loathe, exclaim "asíg" of which the English equivalents are ugh! faugh! foh!
Heart, condition or quality of one's heart, mind, feeling, sentiments, aspirations. (see kasíng-kásing, panagiposóon).
Freq. of ásoy-to explain, expose, make clear, expound, elucidate.

A dish prepared from dried and cut-up dágmay-leaves mixed with crabs, shrimps, chili, etc. Himói akó sing pangát. Prepare me a dish of pangát. Nakakáon kamí dídto sing pangát (pinangát). We ate there a dish of pangát. (see pinangát).
Freq. of kátay-to form in line, etc.
Freq. of atí-to raid, rob, plunder, ransack.

Freq. of káti-to provoke; to lure, entice, allure, catch birds, etc. by means of a lure (katián). Ginbutangán níla ang siáy sing katián sa pagpangáti sing iláhas. They put a lure into the siáy-trap, in order to catch wild chickens.
Freq. of tíngug-voice; to voice, speak, etc.
Freq. of áto. To see the point, to understand; to look for the end or key of a thread, rope, etc.
Freq. of atóp-to make a roof, to roof in, put a roof on.
(H) Freq. of átsi-to sneeze. Dî mo akó pagpangatsihán. Don't sneeze at me. (see bahaón, pamahaón).

Freq. of atúbang. To confront, face, stand-in front of,-before,-in presence of, present oneself before. Mangatúbang ka sing maísug sa mga kalisdánan sang pagpangabúhì. Bravely face the difficulties of life. Nangatúbang siá sa támpad sang íya káaway. He confronted his enemy face to face.
Freq. of áwà. To be compassionate, have mercy, take pity on, sympathize with, commiserate with, condole with, to pity, to take-mercy-,-compassion-, on (upon).
Freq. of áwas-to overflow, flow out over the rim, flow-, run-, well-, brim-, pour-, spill-, over the edge (brim, rim).
Freq. of káwas-to go or step over the side of, etc.
(H) Freq. of káwat-to steal, etc. (see panákaw, tákaw, paníkas).
Freq. of awát-to keep occupied, hinder, detain, etc.
Adultery; to commit adultery, (see láyì, pangláyì, kawátan-lover, correspondent, adulterer).
(H) Freq. of áway-to fight, quarrel, etc.
Freq. of káwhi. To pick one's ears, use a piece of smooth bamboo, etc. to clean one's ears of wax.
(B) Freq. of káwit. To hook, seize with a hook, crook, pole and hook; to catch, tear, lacerate, rend, said of thorns, briars and the like catching in one's clothes in passing, etc. (see paníngit).
(H) Freq. of káwit-to gather with pole and hook, etc.
To perform light work, etc. See pangawótkáwot id.

Light work, an easy job, as various household duties, etc.; to perform household duties, do some easy (light) work, be busy, be occupied, be neither idle nor engaged in heavy work that requires great physical exertions. Nagapangawótkáwot siá sa sulúd sang baláy. She is occupied with her household duties. Walâ siá pagpangawótkáwot. She does nothing. She is idle (lazy). Pangawótkáwot man. Do something. Occupy yourself with some easy work. Be not so idle.

A temporary resident, sojourner, migrating, migratory, wandering; to migrate, sojourn or dwell in a place temporarily or as a stranger, go to live somewhere else with the intention of coming back within a longer or shorter period to one's old place of abode. Píspis nga pangáyaw. A migratory bird. A bird of passage. Ang mga pumulúyò nga pangáyaw. Temporary residents. Visitors. Travellers. Guests. Madámù nga mga mamumugón ang nagapangáyaw sa tuígtúig sa Négros nga Nakatúndan. Many workmen go yearly to Occidental Negros for a season. Ginapangayáwan man lang siníng mga táo ang áton bánwa. These people are staying here in our town only for a time. (see pangályaw).
Freq. of áyaw-to be sufficient, to satisfy, etc.
(H) Freq. of áyo-to be or get well, etc.

To ask, beg, request, solicit. Mangáyò (Magpangáyò) ka kag pagahatágan ikáw. Ask and you shall receive. Pangayóa sa íya ang ímo kinahánglan. Beg of him to grant you what you need. Ginpangayóan akó níya sing isá ka gántang nga humáy. He asked me for a ganta of rice. Anó ang ginapangáyò mo? What are you asking for? What do you want? (see ayô).
To haggle, higgle, bargain, ask, request (help, money, etc.; see kayô, ayô).
To live-, behave-, act-, like a drone or parasite. (see kayô).
To contract the limbs convulsively, spasmodically, as people suffering from cramps, epileptic fits, etc.
Freq. of kayúgpus-to shrivel, shrink.
Freq. of kayúmkum-to dwindle, shrivel. (see pangayúgpus).
See pangayúgpus-to dwindle, etc. (see kúpus).
Freq. of buút-to will, etc. See pamuút.
Freq. of dakúp-to catch, arrest, etc.
Freq. of dalasâ-to run over, collide with, etc.
The screw pine. See pándan id.
Freq. of dánghos. To strive after, look for, seek, try hard to obtain, be anxious about, be very busy or occupied. (see sákò, dúlup).
Freq. of dápit-to invite. Ang mga pinangdápit. The (invited) guests.
Freq. of dóhol-to reach, hand, etc.
Freq. of duhá-dúha-to doubt, etc.

Freq. and Dim. of dóhol. To reach up, to reach or pass to others, spread, hand over, retail. Ang kartéro amó ang nagapangduhólduhól sang mga sulát sa kabalayán. The postman delivers the letters from house to house.
To sigh, etc. See dúhoy, pangandúhoy.
To look into a mirror, use-, stand before-, a mirror. (see espého).
To eradicate, pull out, uproot. (see gábut).
Freq. of gáid-to bind, fasten, etc. (see pánggid).
A fyke, fish-trap. (see páta, báw-an, etc.).
To grow thin, small, slender; to become lean, emaciated, etc. (see gamáy).
To lay or put one's hand upon. Panggambayí ang íya abága. Put your hand on his shoulders.

To plant, sow, especially to plant seeds by hand in holes made by a stick, etc. Ipánggas ang maís. Plant the corn. Panggasí sing maís ang talámnan nga naányan na. Plant corn in the field from which the rice has been harvested. Ang mga ginikánan dápat magpánggas sang bínhì sang maáyo nga pamatásan sa lanúbò nga tagiposóon sang íla mga bátà. Parents should sow the seed of good conduct (manners) in the young hearts of their children. Walâ kamí sing humáy nga pinánggas, kóndì tinánum lang. We have no rice grown directly from the seeds, but only rice from transplanted seedlings. Ang pamánggas ángay sa mga bánglid, ápang ang panánum sa saláma nga wayáng. Seed-planting is suitable on slopes, but seedling-planting on level plains.
Freq. of gasód-to retort, give a rough answer.
To secure, fasten, tie, bind. Kon magsinutíl ikáw liwán ipánggid ko ikáw sa bánkò kag hanóton. If you are naughty again I'll tie you down on a bench and give you a whipping. (see higót, góos, gápus).
A game at cards; to play panggínggi.
Place (room, house, table, etc.) where panggínggi is played.

Uneducated, illiterate, ill-bred, low, mean, base, rude, unlettered, unschooled, uncultured, a term of contempt applied chiefly to white men. Ang ibán nga mga bukáy nga nagabút dirí sa áton mga panggópánggo gid lámang. Some of the whites that have come here to us are really very low-class people. A, panggópánggo lang siá. Ah, he is only an ill-bred white, a low-cast white man.
To catch fish, crabs, etc. by means of one's apron or skirt (a primitive method of fishing in rivers and shallow waters).
See panggwâ-to go outside, etc.
Freq. of gúsnit-to tear, rend, etc.
Face, countenance, physiognomy, cast or expression of face. Magayón siá sing pangguyáhon. Her face is (was) beautiful. (see guyá, nawóng).
Freq. of gwâ-to go outside, etc.
The same as panh-in words beginning with "h", e.g. panghímos-panhímos (hímos); panghápit-panhápit (hápit). See pan-.
To swell; to ripen, change colour. (see hábal, habál).
Freq. of hágyò-to gesticulate; swing one's arms.
Freq. of haláwhaw-to be taken unawares, to express surprise or astonishment.

Freq. of hamút. To be odoriferous, perfumed, sweet-smelling, scented, aromatic, to have a sweet smell, etc., to give-, give off-, breathe-, exhale-, emit-, diffuse-, a sweet-, pleasant-, delicious-, smell,-odour,-aroma,-scent,-perfume. (see pangámyon).
Freq. of hamóy. To wash one's face, to move the palm of the hand down one's face as after a swim or bath.
Vindication, justification, argument, defence, self-defence; to vindicate, justify, prove to be right. (see tárung, matárung, katarúngan).

Freq. of hangdálhángdal, handálhándal. To go in search of a buyer, to visit from house to house in order to dispose of a pawn or of something for sale. Dúro gid ang panghangdálhángdal ko sa pagbalígyà sang ákon báka. I had to go from place to place in trying to find a buyer for my cow or ox. Ipapanghangdálhángdal mo ang ímo báboy, básì may mabakál. Try to dispose of your pig, perhaps someone would like to buy it. Pinanghangdálhangdalán ko ang madámù nga mga baláy, ápang walâ sing may lúyag sa pagbakál sang ákon umá. I have been to many houses in search of a buyer, but there is none who wants to buy my land. Nagapanghangdálhángdal silá sing pílak nga ilimós sa minatáy. They are looking for money to pay the funeral fees for the person that died.

To go in search of, look for, try to find, get or obtain whatever one needs by going from house to house, etc. Nagapanghánglas siá sing kwárta, kán-on, wásay, etc. He is in search of money, rice, a hatchet, etc.
To moan, sigh, complain, ejaculate, say or shout "haróy" (alas!). (see haróy).
To trick, cheat, fool, bamboozle, cozen. (see hásò).
Freq. of hatúd-to deliver, hand over.
Freq. of háw-ad-to take out of, snatch away from.
Form or shape of a person's waist or hips. (see háwak).
Freq. of háwan-to make clear of obstacles, etc.
See pangháw-ad. (háwas-háw-ad).
Freq. of háyhay-to sigh, moan, say "háy", "aháy". "Heigh-ho!" in pain or distress.
To congratulate, felicitate, wish good luck, call blessed, praise. (buláhan).
(H) To make for the edge or side of; to edge away from, go aside or away from. (higád).
To touch, feel; grope one's way. (see híkap).
Freq. of híkog-to commit suicide (by hanging, etc.).
Freq. of híkot-to prepare, get ready, make arrangements for. (see panghímos).
(H) To wash one's head and face. (Freq. of lám-os).
To weed, weed out, pull up weeds, clear of weeds. (hilamón).
Freq. and Dim. of hiláw. Also: to change colour, betray-fear,-shyness,-disgust.
To do something coldly, half-heartedly, merely to keep up appearances, particularly applied to a forced smile or laugh. (see hiláw, pakuláhaw).
Freq. of hilód-hílod. To wriggle, stir, writhe; to wriggle and twist in rubbing off dirt whilst bathing, etc.
See panghimalóod-to loathe, etc.
(H) Blessing, congratulation; to bless, invoke a blessing upon, call blessed, praise, exalt; to congratulate, wish another-joy,-happiness,-well. (see maáyo, pakamaáyo-to approve, etc.).

(H) The imperative passive of panghibaló (Freq. of hibaló)-to know, understand, but used in the same meaning as pamál-i, which see. Panghimál-i ni Pédro sang panglútò sing pagkáon. Peter knows nothing about cooking, has no inkling as to how prepare a meal. (see kalibutáni).
(H) Curse, imprecation; to curse, invoke a curse upon, call cursed, imprecate, execrate, condemn, wish evil to. (see maláut, panóloy).

Loathing, abomination, detestation; to loathe, abominate, abhor, detest. Ginapanghimalóod níya ang batásan ni Fuláno. He abominates N.N.'s conduct. Nagapanghimalóod siá siníng pagkáon. He detests this food. (see lóod).
Freq. of hímos. To prepare, get ready, provide, see to beforehand, make arrangements for; preparation, previous arrangement, provision.
To make great efforts, do one's best, struggle hard, exert oneself, strive with might and main. (see purús, himúd-os, paningúhà).
To clean the eyes of mucus. (see mútà).
(H) To wash one's hands, etc. Freq. of hináw.
To make use of an opportunity, do at once, take advantage of, make "hay while the sun shines". (see kalít).
To commit suicide, hang oneself; suicide. (see hingápus, híkog).
Freq. of hípus. To be silent, taciturn, quiet, etc.
Freq. of hísà-to envy, spite, grudge, bear ill-will; to beat, thrash, hurt.

To clean the mouth of remnants of food after a meal by means of the tongue. Kay walâ kitá sing túbig nga ilímnon magapanghiwángì lang kitá. As we have no drinking water, let us clean our mouths with our tongue.
Freq. of hokóm-to judge, etc.
(H) Freq. of hubág-to swell, become bloated, swollen; a swelling.
To be in the neighbourhood of, loiter, linger, tarry, stand around. (see hubáy-hubáy).
Freq. of húgas-to rinse, wash. To clean one's feet, etc. with water.
To soak, steep in. (see húgum).
Freq. of hulám-to borrow, etc. Walâ siá madagtaí sang mga pinanghulamán nga batásan sang mga dumulóong. He was untouched by (kept himself aloof from) customs borrowed from foreigners.
Freq. of huláwid-to entangle, etc.
Freq. of hunâhúnà-thought; to think, reflect, consider, deliberate, etc. Ang panghunâhúnà nga binanwahánon. Civic spirit, public opinion, political thinking (speculation).
Freq. of húnong-to quiet, calm, placate, abate, mitigate, allay, soothe, pacify, assuage.
To swell up, get flabby or bloated. Nagpanghunúng ang íya guyá. His face-became bloated,-became swollen,-swelled up.
Freq. of huráp-us-to solicit help, etc.
Freq. of húsay-to arrange, set in order, square up, settle; to comb the hair.
Freq. of húy-ab-to yawn, gape, open the mouth drowsily or lazily.
Freq. of húyab-to run off quickly, scamper off, run about pell-mell.
To be or become pale, pallid, wan; to change colour, be surprised, taken aback. (see huyús).
A kind of plant (tree) with medicinal properties. Atsára nga pángi. A kind of pickles prepared from the pángi-plant.
To strut, walk pompously or ostentatiously, swagger, walk with a lofty, proud gait or with affected dignity. (see kiáykíay).

(B) To behave like a stranger, be shy, timid, quiet, bashful. Kon magdúaw ka sa íla índì ka mangibáibá. If you pay them a visit, don't act as if you were a stranger, as if you were not on familiar terms with them.
To diminish, decrease, take away from. (see íban).
(H) See pangibáibá.
Freq. of íbok-to move, stir, writhe, twist, squirm, twitch; to root (of pigs).
Freq. of íbug-to desire, crave, lust after, have a passion for, covet.
Congratulation, best wishes; to congratulate, felicitate. (see pangibúlan, panghibuláhan, panghimaáyo).
To congratulate. Nagapangibúlan akó sa ímo-or-ginapangibuláhan ko ikáw. I congratulate you. (see pangibuláhan, panghibuláhan).
Freq. and Caus. of ngídlis. To shock, surprise; be shocked, surprised, taken aback, in fear or terror.
Freq. of kigí-strip (hemp, etc.).
To urinate, make (pass) water. (see íhì).
Freq. of ikláhag-to stumble, etc.
To wag the tail, etc. Freq. of íkog-tail.
To eat sliced coconut-meat soaked in toddy. Nangilábò silá sa íla nga píknik. At their picnic they ate sliced coconut-meat mixed with toddy. (see kilábò).
Freq. of kílag-to look about curiously, etc.
Freq. of kilála-to be acquainted with, etc. May napangilál-an akó dídto. I have an acquaintance there.
To shine, sparkle, glisten, twinkle. (see kilángkílang, kilánkílan, bádlak, sílak, sílì, ínggat, etc.).

Freq. of kilás. To make a sudden jerk or movement as if electrified, shake, tremble, receive a shock through fear, excitement, etc. Nagapangilás ang íya láwas. He (His body) is shaking all over with fear.
Lightning, flashes of lightning; to lighten. May pangilát. Nagapangilát. There is lightning. Lightning is flashing.
Form or shape of one's eyebrows. (see kílay).

To raise the eyebrows, give the hint, wink at, signal to another by moving the eyebrows. Nagapangiláyay silá. They are-winking at each other,-signalling to each other with their eyebrows. (see kílay).
Side, edge, border, rim, margin, brink, verge; to be or go at the side of. (see kílid).
Freq. of ílis-to change, etc.

To scrape or rub with a rough fish-skin, to rub and make smooth with the skin of a crocodile, etc., to smooth as with glass paper; to cause a creepy, uncanny sensation, to shock, take aback. Pinangilkigán siá kag nagbátyag sing dakû gid nga kahádluk. A creepy sensation stole over him and he felt great fear. (see kílkig).

To show signs of joy and pleasure, welcome with delight, receive with gladness; to strive to please or be of service, as an inferior or a (contrite) culprit, try to placate, as an offender the one offended. (see aráyaráy).
To zigzag, stagger, reel, totter, as a drunken man. (see panayódò, panayódoy, dulíngdúling).
Freq. of ilóm-to darken, blacken, etc. (see panagíl-om, pangitúm).
Form or shape of nose, way of carrying one's nose. Hímpit siá sing pangilóng. He has a perfect type of nose. The shape of his nose is beautiful. (see ilóng).
Motherhood, maternity, matronhood; to be a mother. (see ilóy).
To offer flowers to the Blessed Virgin during the month of May; the offering of such flowers.
Freq. of ímon-to be jealous, envious. Magapangimonáy silá. They are jealous of each other.

A prefix expressing mostly the idea of becoming, or being changed into, what the root implies. For magapangin-and magpangin-"mangin-is often used and for nagpangin-"nangin-". Pagpanginímol-to become poor. Nanginímol siá. He became poor. Iníng diótay nga tanúm manginkáhoy (magapanginkáhoy) kunína. This small plant will finally grow or develop into a tree. Indì ka na maginúm, kay manginhubúg ikáw. Don't drink any more, or you will become fuddled. Manginmatáy siá ánay sang sa magbúhat sinâ. He would rather die than do that. He prefers death to doing that. Nanginsúbung siá sa (sang)--. He became like--.

To ask for assistance, help, recommendation, etc. Manginahán kitá sa kay Fuláno, agúd madángat ta ang áton ginakinahánglan sa pangúlopuód. Let us ask for N.N.'s recommendation, so that we may obtain what we want from the Provincial Governor. (see pangarímo).
Freq. of kinámkínam. To smack one's lips; try the taste of. Kon íya makítà iní manginám-kínam siá gid. When he sees this he will smack his lips (with pleasure).
Eating, feasting (of many); to feast, banquet, eat. (see káon).
To augment, gather force or strength, increase, add to. (see dúgang, sárga).
To gather or collect shell-fish. (see pakinháson).
Place where shell-fish (pakinháson) are often found.
To put the arms akimbo, i.e. with the elbows pointing outwards, and the hands resting on the hips. (háwak). (see paninghawák).
Freq. of ínit-to wax hot, get angry, have one's blood boiling with rage or passion. Kon makabatî siá sinâ, magapangínit gid ang íya láwas sa kaákig. If he hears of it, he will be boiling with rage.
To be apprehensive of danger, be wary and cautious, fear. Nagapanginláman siá nga--. He is full-of apprehension that--,-of fear, lest--.
To die, do away with oneself, choose to die, give one's life willingly. Manginmatáy akó, ápang dílì gid akó magbúhat sinâ. I will rather die than do that. (see patáy, matáy).
To slip out, escape. (see palús, panimúdlus).

To put the blame on, hold responsible, make answer for, accuse, lay the guilt upon. Ginapanginsálà níla sinâ yádtong mga ponoán nga--. They put the blame for it on those officials that--. Ikáw gid ang ákon pagapanginsaláon, kon--. I'll hold you responsible, if--. I'll call you to account, if--. (see sumálà).
To take out from a hidden recess, get from a known hiding place. Panginsápwa lang dídto ang agás. Just get the petroleum from where you know it is kept. (see sapó).

Disappointment, chagrin, vexation, annoyance; to be grieved, hurt, disappointed, displeased, vexed, annoyed; to be in a complaining or bad humour. Nagapanginsawâ ang kálag níya, kay walâ magdúaw sa íya si Fuláno. He complains (is in a bad humour), because N.N. has not visited him. Manginsawâ siá kon índì mo siá pagagdahón. He will feel hurt, if you do not invite him. (see panaginsáwà).
To deny, disown, repudiate, say "no", contradict, disavow, belie, refuse to admit an imputation, or the like; denial, disavowal, repudiation, etc. (see wálà, walâ).

To be avaricious, covetous of more, be (inordinately) eager to increase one's possessions, to be selfish or greedy; to be anxious to take advantage of, to avail oneself of an opportunity. (see pangunyádî, himulús).
Freq. of kipí-kípì-to tuck up, gather round, etc.
See panagíp-ol id. (see pangímon).
To evacuate, void the bowels. (see ípot, pamús-on).

To be shy, bashful, self-conscious, ill at ease, to move about restrainedly, appear to be under some restraint. Iníng táo kon magsákà sa baláy walâ sing pangirákirá. When this man comes for a visit, he moves about quite freely, unrestrainedly, makes himself at home. Kon magdúaw ka sa íya índì ka mangirákirá, kay índì siá kaúyon sang pangirákirá. When you pay him a visit, be at your ease, for he does not like a shy, bashful or self-conscious behaviour.
Freq. of isdà. To fish, catch fish, ply the trade of a fisherman, go out fishing. Mangísdà kitá. Let us go fishing. Nagapangísdà silá sa báybay. They are out fishing on the beach. (see panágat).
Freq. of kisó. To wrinkle, crease, form plaits or folds in garments, etc.
Dim. of pangisó. Also: to hang down, fall down in folds (of drapery, dresses, etc.).

Freq. of ísug. To be brave, fearless, dauntless, bold, violent, strong, unyielding, vehement. Nangísug (nagpangísug) silá sa pagtámpad sa mga kaáway. They were full of courage to face their enemies. Mangísug (Magpangísug) ka kag dílì ka magpatubalíng. Be brave and don't give way (don't yield).
Corner angle, ridge. Atpi ang pangitâ. Cover the ridge with some roofing material.

Freq. of kítà. To seek, look for, search for, try to find; to get a livelihood, work or do business for one's living; livelihood, sustenance, means or mode of one's life, business, employment, engagement, occupation. Mangítà ka sing manók. Look for some chicken. Pangitái akó sing páhò. Try to get some mangoes for me. Ginpangítà níya ang nadúlà nga síngsing túbtub nga íya nakítà. He sought for the lost ring till he found it. Anó ang íya pangítà? What does he do for a living? How is he employed? What is his business? Ang mangítà makakítà. Those who seek shall find.
Freq. of itî-droppings; to void the bowels (of birds, etc.).
Freq. of ítik-to tickle.
Freq. of ítok-to tickle.
To darken, blacken, etc. (see itúm, pangilóm).

To economize, curtail-, check-, curb-, cut down-, one's expenditures, to refrain from spending as much as usual; to avoid, turn away from, keep aloof from. Nagapangiyáw siá karón sa paghinguyáng, kay maíwat kaáyo ang kwárta. He spends little at present, for money is very scarce. Ginapangiyawán lang námon karón ang pagtíg-ang, kay nakulángan kamí sing humáy, kag ang tigaláni malayô pa. We are cooking only a little rice at present, for we have run short and the harvest is still far off. Magpangiyáw (mangiyáw) ka sa pagpatúyang mo sing pílak, kay kon dílì mapúto ka sa dílì madúgay. Refrain from spending money so freely, for otherwise you will be bankrupt before long. Pangiyawí siá. Keep aloof from him. Nagapangiyáw siá, kay may útang siá sa ákon. He avoids me, because he is in debt to me. (see paúmud, likáw).
Frog, toad. (see pakâ, pánkà).

To ask information, question, interrogate, inquire. Pangkotá siá kon diín ang íya agálon. Ask him where his master is. Napángkot na siá sing makadámù, ápang walâ siá pagsúgid sang ginpángkot sa íya. He has been asked (already) many times, but-does not tell what is asked of him,-has not answered the questions put to him. Anó ang igapángkot mo sa íya? What are you going to ask him (about)? (see pamángkot, pamangkotánon, pakiána, pangutána).

Pangl-very often stands for panl-in the frequentative forms of words beginning with the letter "l", so much so that both are used indiscriminately for the same word, e.g. panglibák, panlibák; panglápas, panlápas; panglángbas, panlángbas, etc.
To cry, weep, wail, sob, lament, complain, mourn or sigh aloud; to cry out, say or speak in a loud voice. (see panalambíton).
Freq. of lábnot-to draw, pull out.
Freq. of lághap-to seek, look for, search for, etc.
To throw down in disorder, strew, spread, sow. (see lághit).
To travel up and down a country, wander, journey, go sight-seeing or on business through a district, etc. (see lagúlad).
Freq. of lagúyaw-to divert oneself, beguile the time, travel, spend a holiday, take a vacation.
Diversion, vacation, holiday, travel; to spend a holiday or travel for recreation.
Freq. of lahús-to pass through, filter, etc. Also: to put in an appearance, pay a visit, call on a friend, come just for a chat or gossip, or the like. (see panumbálay).
To go-by foot,-on foot,-afoot, to foot it, to march, walk, hike, tramp, trudge, wend (one's way); way or manner of one's walking. (see lakát).
(H) March, way, path, course, track, journey, road to be travelled over; to travel, to be on one's way, march on, proceed on one's journey.
To tear or pull down, tear in pieces. (see lalás).
To inundate, overflow, overrun. (see lámbas).
See panglámbas. (lánas-lámbas).
An eruptive skin-disease; to develop (form, produce) blisters, pustules, or the like. (see láp-ok).
To be-, go-, pass-, reach-, over, to overflow, inundate, to rise higher or above. (see lapáw).
To pierce, pass through, perforate, transfix, make a hole through. (see lapús).
To make pictures, portraits, photoes, to take-photoes,-likenesses, to follow the profession of a portrait-painter or photographer; the art-, calling-, of painter, photographer, etc. (see laráwan).
To gather, collect, put together, assemble. (see lárip).
Freq. of latón-to spread, infect, etc.
Form or shape of one's body. See panglawasón.
Form, shape, size or growth of one's body. Maáyo siá sing panglawasón. He is well built. He has a well developed body. He is well developed. (see láwas).
To catch fish with a net called "láya".
Adultery; to commit adultery. (see láyì, pangawátan).
To give lessons, instruct, teach, hold class. (see leksyón, toón, panoón).
To look around with curiosity, turn the eyes in every direction. (see lisílísi).
Freq. of libáng. Also: Diarrhoea; to have diarrhoea, suffer from looseness of the bowels.
Dim. of planglibáng. Also: to do odd jobs, to have nothing to do in particular and consequently to while away the time in various occupations of little moment.
Lavatory, privy, W.C.; cess-pool.
Dim. of panglíbod, the Freq. of líbod-to peddle, etc.
Freq. of líbut-to go, (pass) round, etc.
Freq. of lígad-to go (pass) by, etc.

To gather or look for mushrooms called "lígbos"; to be in consternation, be affrighted, get a shock, have one's hair stand on end. Nagapanglígbos ang íya láwas. He is full of consternation. Nanglígbos (Nagpanglígbos) siá kag nagpalaníndog ang íya bohók. He was affrighted and his hair stood on end.
Freq. of líghot-to seek, search for, look for, try to find or get hold of. (see panglághap, pangítà).
To be a loafer, idler, vagabond; to idle, stroll, roam about, rove. (see landólándo, lagáwlágaw, lihôlihô).
See pangalimúg-to rinse out or wash one's mouth, etc.
Diversion, amusement, distraction; to divert-, amuse-, distract-, oneself, to beguile-, while away-, the time, go out in search of amusement or recreation. (see lingáw, lingáwlíngaw, paliwálíwa).
To smack one's lips or click one's tongue. See pangalíntak id.
Freq. of líntì-lightning. To lighten, to flash lightning; to curse, swear, etc.
To go or wander from place to place, walk about aimlessly. (see litálíta).
Freq. of liwálíwa. (see paliwálíwa).
December. (see disiémbre).
November. (see nobiémbre).

To rummage, disturb, disorder, disarrange, throw into disorder, toss about papers, books, clothes, etc. in trying to find or get hold of what one wants. Indì ka magságad panglugás sináng mga pagkítan. Don't be always throwing those papers into disorder. (see pangabúkay, balúskay, balúkhay).
To search, reconnoitre, investigate, examine. (see lúghut).
Freq. of luhúd-to kneel, etc. See panluhúd.
To overturn, lay low, blow down, uproot. (see lúka).
To be or become wet, moist, soaked, soiled, stained. (see lumáw, lumáwan, palumáwlumáw).
To grow pale, turn pale, blanch, etc. See lún-ad. Sang pagkabatî níya sinâ nanglún-ad (nagpanglún-ad, nagpalanglún-ad) siá. When he heard that he grew pale. (see palanglúspad, lápsì).
Freq. of lupók. Also: to form (develop) cracks, fissures, or the like.
Freq. of lutá-to dislocate. (see lúak).
To cook; cooking. (see lútò).
To overcome, subdue, vanquish, keep down, oppress. (see lútos).
Freq. of lúyà-to tire, become tired, grow tired, weary, fatigued.
To weaken, become weak, feeble. Nagapanglúya na siá. He is getting weak. Tigúlang na siá kag nagapalanglúya ang íya mga túhud. He is old now and his knees are getting weak. (see lúya).
Freq. of luyáw. To divert oneself, take a holiday, travel for recreation. (see panglagúyaw, paliwálíwa, dayándáyan, panglingáwlíngaw).

Freq. of matá-the eye; to wake, awake, etc. Also: Form, shape, colour, of one's eyes; the expression of the eyes. Matalúm ang íya pangmatá. Matalúm siá sing pangmatá. He has sharp eyes. His look is penetrating. Malúya na ang íya pangmatá. His eyesight is now weak. (see pamatá).
Freq. of matáy. To kill, etc. (see patáy).
Foolish, stupid; a fool, ass, stupid fellow; to be a fool or act like one. (see kalúndong, bulálo, búngaw, tampuháw, bat-ólan, kólò, kolôkolô, balingág, tipangág, mangô).
To listen, be an eavesdropper. (see paníngad).
To form new shoots, new leaves, etc. See ógbos.
See pangóga and both probably derived from an expert eavesdropper called "Ogo"-Hugo.
To gather mushrooms. (see óhong).
Freq. of kokót-to shell beans, etc. Mangokót kamó sing kadiós sa panyága náton. Shell some cadios-peas for our dinner.

Freq. of ólo. Head, head-master, ruler, leader, chief, commander; to be master, to rule or govern. Sín-o ang nagapangólo dirí? Who is master here? May mga púngsud nga ginapangolóhan sang isá ka hárì. There are nations ruled over by a king. Pangólo-bánwa. Municipal President. Pangólo-puód. Provincial Governor. Pangólo-púngsud. National Governor or President, Governor General, President of a Nation. Pangólo-kasapulán. Board of Directors. Directing (Governing) Board. Pangólo'ng mga dinalán. Leading article, leader, head-lines; editorial.
Government, administration, management. (ólo).
Trade, commerce; to engage in trade or commerce, be a merchant or trader. (From the Sp. comercio).

(Freq. of the Sp. contra) Opposition, resistance, enmity; opponent, antagonist, rival; to resist, oppose, make opposition to. Nagapangóntra silá. They are enemies. They are opposed to each other. Indì mo silá pagpangontrahón. Do not oppose them. Don't go against them. Iníng manók walâ sing pangóntra. This cock has no rival. (see súmpung, bátok, pamalábag).
Freq. of kóot, kúut-to grope, put one's hand in, etc.
The cut or make of clothes, tailoring; to cut out clothes, to tailor. Iníng manugtábas maáyo gid sing pangórte. This tailor is an expert at cutting out (clothes). (From the Sp. corte).
Spoilt, rotten, putrid, musty, rancid (of foodstuff). See pán-os id.
Very flat-nosed. (see kurapâ).
To touch, establish physical-, come in-, contact with. Napángot ang duhá ka bóla (pálo). The two balls (masts) touched each other. (see ángot, angót, doót).
Touching, in contact with (as balls in the game of billiards, etc.).
Freq. of kótkot-to dig, etc.
River bank, river side; edge, border, rim, any steep bank. (see bíbì, bígki, binít, kílid).
To gather, collect, heap together, assemble (beginning with the objects that are nearest). (see típon).
(B) To go along the bank of a river, the ridge of a mountain and the like. (see panaláytay, panalíbay, panaríbay).
The smell of urine; to smell like urine. (see ángso, pánsot, id.).
To turn upside down, upset; perplex, confuse. (see sulî).

Freq. of kúbung. Also: To walk very carefully or gingerly (as over sharp stones or the like). Nagapangúbung lang siá, kay matalíwis ang mga bató kag naánad siá sa sapátos kag índì man siá makabatás maglápak sang súra. He is walking very carefully, for the stones are sharp and he is accustomed to wear boots and he cannot bear stepping on the young and prickly cogon-shoots.
To grasp or hold another's hand, walk hand in hand. Nagapangúbung silá, kay madánlug ang dálan. They are walking hand in hand, because the road is slippery.
Freq. of kúdlit-to make a line or stroke, sign, mark with a pencil, pen, brush, pointed instrument, etc.
See pángog-foolish, etc.
Freq. of ugá-to dry, be or become dry, etc.
Freq. of kúghad, úghad-to hawk and spit. Indì ka mangúghad, kay maláw-ay. Don't hawk and spit, for it is unbecoming, ugly, a dirty habit.
Freq. of kúhà-to take, etc. Pinanguháan (ginpanguháan) akó níya sing tátlo ka mángmang. He took three pesos away from me.
Freq. of kúhit-to nudge, etc.
Freq. of úl-ul-to be stiff, painful, etc. (see palangúl-ul).
(H) To cover oneself with, or wrap oneself up in, a blanket, etc. (see kulámbot, panimúlon).
To request a favour, oblige oneself, ask for help or assistance. (see líhog, pakitábang (from paki-and tábang).
To use toilet paper. (see úli, ulí).
See pangólo.
See pangulámbut.

Agriculture, tillage, tilth, husbandry, cultivation, culture, farming; a piece of land, especially corn-or rice-land; to till, cultivate-, labour-, the soil, be a farmer. Walâ siá sing pangúma karón nga túig. He has no corn-land (rice-land) this year. Nagapangúma (Mangungúma) siá. He is a farmer. Yádtong mga bakólod saráng pa mapangúma. Those hills can be cultivated yet. (see umá).
Farm, field, ground, land, soil fit for tillage. (see palangúmhan).
To look for-, fetch-, (green) fodder for horses, cattle, etc. (see kúmpay).
(Probably from the Sp. competir). To strive, contend, compete with, vie; insist on, be determined or resolute. (see paindísíndis, panikasúg).
Freq. of kúmus-to squeeze, compress with the hand. Pinangúmus nga sulát, papél, etc. A crumpled letter, a piece of crumpled paper, etc.
Freq. of úna-to do-, come-, go-, first, before, in front, to head, precede, lead; be-ahead,-in advance,-in the van; the article (grammar). Ang pangúna nga "ang". The article "ang".
Dim. of pangúna. Also: To start, begin, commence.
To go ahead, lead, be in front, precede; the one in front, what is before or ahead, the forepart. Ang tiíl nga pangúnhan sang báka. The forelegs or front legs of the cow.
To wear or put on a cloak or coat; to cover, cloak. (see kúnop).
Growth, development (of flesh, meat, muscles, etc.); to form (grow, develop) flesh, etc., particularly applied to all kinds of tubers (see unúd).
Freq. of únut-to fall out, shed (of hair).

(B) To be very selfish or greedy, seek one's own advantage, to overreach. Dî mo siá pagpangunyadían (pagpanginyawátan). Don't overreach him. Don't cheat him out of money, goods, etc. (see panginyáwat).
Freq. of upúd-to go along with, accompany, etc.
Freq. of kúpus-to contract, shrink, shrivel. (see palangúpus).
Caus. of ngúrab-to growl, grumble, murmur.
(B) To clutch, grasp, seize, take hold of. Pangurábtan mo ang hilamón kag gabúton. Take hold of the grass and pull it up.
To wrinkle one's brow, etc. (see kurínot, kurinót).
Caus. of ngúrub-to show the teeth, to snarl, gnarl (of dogs, etc.). Pangurúba ang idô kon maglígad silá. Make the dog show its teeth when they pass by.
Freq. of kúrug, kúdug-to tremble, shiver, quake. (see palangúrug).
Trembling, shivering, shaking, quaking; to tremble, shiver, shake, quake. (see kúdug, kúrug, pangúrug).
To make the sign of the cross or bless oneself. (see krus).
(H) Freq. of úrut-to finish, make an end of, etc.
Freq. of kurútay-to call the chickens together.
Sense of taste, taste; to taste. (see kúsam).
Freq. of usísà. Investigation, examination, search, research; to investigate, examine, search.

Freq. of kusúg. To make great efforts, exert oneself, strive, apply force, show strength; to grow stiff. Nagapangusúg siá sa paghíwat sang amó nga kasadyáhan. He is making great efforts in preparation for that solemnity, festivity, rejoicing. (see palangusúg).
To be firm, robust, strong, brave, valiant; to use or apply force, insist on. (see kúsug).
Dim. of pangúsug, pangusúg.
To arrest, put in prison, put in a place of safety or security. (see kútà).
(H) To gather-, fetch-, look for-, vegetables. (see útan, panuláon).
